400     def deconstruct(self):
401         """
402         Return enough information to recreate the field as a 4-tuple:
403 
404          * The name of the field on the model, if contribute_to_class() has
405            been run.
406          * The import path of the field, including the class:e.g.
407            django.db.models.IntegerField This should be the most portable
408            version, so less specific may be better.
409          * A list of positional arguments.
410          * A dict of keyword arguments.
411 
412         Note that the positional or keyword arguments must contain values of
413         the following types (including inner values of collection types):
414 
415          * None, bool, str, int, float, complex, set, frozenset, list, tuple,
416            dict
417          * UUID
418          * datetime.datetime (naive), datetime.date
419          * top-level classes, top-level functions - will be referenced by their
420            full import path
421          * Storage instances - these have their own deconstruct() method
422 
423         This is because the values here must be serialized into a text format
424         (possibly new Python code, possibly JSON) and these are the only types
425         with encoding handlers defined.
426 
427         There's no need to return the exact way the field was instantiated this
428         time, just ensure that the resulting field is the same - prefer keyword
429         arguments over positional ones, and omit parameters with their default
430         values.
431         """
432         # Short-form way of fetching all the default parameters
433         keywords = {}
434         possibles = {
435             "verbose_name": None,
436             "primary_key": False,
437             "max_length": None,
438             "unique": False,
439             "blank": False,
440             "null": False,
441             "db_index": False,
442             "default": NOT_PROVIDED,
443             "editable": True,
444             "serialize": True,
445             "unique_for_date": None,
446             "unique_for_month": None,
447             "unique_for_year": None,
448             "choices": None,
449             "help_text": '',
450             "db_column": None,
451             "db_tablespace": None,
452             "auto_created": False,
453             "validators": [],
454             "error_messages": None,
455         }
456         attr_overrides = {
457             "unique": "_unique",
458             "error_messages": "_error_messages",
459             "validators": "_validators",
460             "verbose_name": "_verbose_name",
461             "db_tablespace": "_db_tablespace",
462         }
463         equals_comparison = {"choices", "validators"}
464         for name, default in possibles.items():
465             value = getattr(self, attr_overrides.get(name, name))
466             # Unroll anything iterable for choices into a concrete list
467             if name == "choices" and isinstance(value, collections.abc.Iterable):
468                 value = list(value)
469             # Do correct kind of comparison
470             if name in equals_comparison:
471                 if value != default:
472                     keywords[name] = value
473             else:
474                 if value is not default:
475                     keywords[name] = value
476         # Work out path - we shorten it for known Django core fields
477         path = "%s.%s" % (self.__class__.__module__, self.__class__.__qualname__)
478         if path.startswith("django.db.models.fields.related"):
479             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields.related", "django.db.models")
480         elif path.startswith("django.db.models.fields.files"):
481             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields.files", "django.db.models")
482         elif path.startswith("django.db.models.fields.proxy"):
483             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields.proxy", "django.db.models")
484         elif path.startswith("django.db.models.fields"):
485             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields", "django.db.models")
486         # Return basic info - other fields should override this.
487         return (self.name, path, [], keywords)
488

531     def __reduce__(self):
532         """
533         Pickling should return the model._meta.fields instance of the field,
534         not a new copy of that field. So, use the app registry to load the
535         model and then the field back.

540             # instance. The code below will create a new empty instance of
541             # class self.__class__, then update its dict with self.__dict__

578     def run_validators(self, value):
579         if value in self.empty_values:
580             return
581 
582         errors = []
583         for v in self.validators:
584             try:
585                 v(value)
586             except exceptions.ValidationError as e:
587                 if hasattr(e, 'code') and e.code in self.error_messages:
588                     e.message = self.error_messages[e.code]
589                 errors.extend(e.error_list)

594     def validate(self, value, model_instance):
595         """
596         Validate value and raise ValidationError if necessary. Subclasses
597         should override this to provide validation logic.
598         """
599         if not self.editable:
600             # Skip validation for non-editable fields.
601             return
602 
603         if self.choices is not None and value not in self.empty_values:
604             for option_key, option_value in self.choices:
605                 if isinstance(option_value, (list, tuple)):
606                     # This is an optgroup, so look inside the group for
607                     # options.
608                     for optgroup_key, optgroup_value in option_value:
609                         if value == optgroup_key:
610                             return
611                 elif value == option_key:
612                     return
613             raise exceptions.ValidationError(
614                 self.error_messages['invalid_choice'],
615                 code='invalid_choice',
616                 params={'value': value},
617             )
618 
619         if value is None and not self.null:
620             raise exceptions.ValidationError(self.error_messages['null'], code='null')
621 
622         if not self.blank and value in self.empty_values:
623             raise exceptions.ValidationError(self.error_messages['blank'], code='blank')

632         self.validate(value, model_instance)
633         self.run_validators(value)
634         return value

651     def db_type(self, connection):
652         """
653         Return the database column data type for this field, for the provided
654         connection.
655         """
656         # The default implementation of this method looks at the
657         # backend-specific data_types dictionary, looking up the field by its
658         # "internal type".
659         #
660         # A Field class can implement the get_internal_type() method to specify
661         # which *preexisting* Django Field class it's most similar to -- i.e.,
662         # a custom field might be represented by a TEXT column type, which is
663         # the same as the TextField Django field type, which means the custom
664         # field's get_internal_type() returns 'TextField'.
665         #
666         # But the limitation of the get_internal_type() / data_types approach
667         # is that it cannot handle database column types that aren't already
668         # mapped to one of the built-in Django field types. In this case, you
669         # can implement db_type() instead of get_internal_type() to specify
670         # exactly which wacky database column type you want to use.
671         data = self.db_type_parameters(connection)
672         try:
673             return connection.data_types[self.get_internal_type()] % data
674         except KeyError:
675             return None

809     def get_choices(self, include_blank=True, blank_choice=BLANK_CHOICE_DASH, limit_choices_to=None, ordering=()):

811         Return choices with a default blank choices included, for use
812         as <select> choices for this field.

814         if self.choices is not None:

817                 blank_defined = any(choice in ('', None) for choice, _ in self.flatchoices)

51         if (f.has_default() and
52                 form[f.name].field.widget.value_omitted_from_data(form.data, form.files, form.add_prefix(f.name))):
53             continue
54         # Defer saving file-type fields until after the other fields, so a
55         # callable upload_to can use the values from other fields.
56         if isinstance(f, models.FileField):
57             file_field_list.append(f)
58         else:
59             f.save_form_data(instance, cleaned_data[f.name])
60 
61     for f in file_field_list:
62         f.save_form_data(instance, cleaned_data[f.name])
63 
64     return instance

69 def model_to_dict(instance, fields=None, exclude=None):
70     """
71     Return a dict containing the data in ``instance`` suitable for passing as
72     a Form's ``initial`` keyword argument.
73 
74     ``fields`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, return only the
75     named.
76 
77     ``exclude`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, exclude the
78     named from the returned dict, even if they are listed in the ``fields``
79     argument.
80     """
81     opts = instance._meta
82     data = {}
83     for f in chain(opts.concrete_fields, opts.private_fields, opts.many_to_many):
84         if not getattr(f, 'editable', False):
85             continue
86         if fields is not None and f.name not in fields:
87             continue
88         if exclude and f.name in exclude:
89             continue
90         data[f.name] = f.value_from_object(instance)
91     return data

97         limit_choices_to = formfield.get_limit_choices_to()
98         if limit_choices_to is not None:

102 def fields_for_model(model, fields=None, exclude=None, widgets=None,
103                      formfield_callback=None, localized_fields=None,
104                      labels=None, help_texts=None, error_messages=None,
105                      field_classes=None, *, apply_limit_choices_to=True):
106     """
107     Return a dictionary containing form fields for the given model.
108 
109     ``fields`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, return only the
110     named fields.
111 
112     ``exclude`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, exclude the
113     named fields from the returned fields, even if they are listed in the
114     ``fields`` argument.
115 
116     ``widgets`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a widget.
117 
118     ``formfield_callback`` is a callable that takes a model field and returns
119     a form field.
120 
121     ``localized_fields`` is a list of names of fields which should be localized.
122 
123     ``labels`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a label.
124 
125     ``help_texts`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a help text.
126 
127     ``error_messages`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a
128     dictionary of error messages.
129 
130     ``field_classes`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a form
131     field class.
132 
133     ``apply_limit_choices_to`` is a boolean indicating if limit_choices_to
134     should be applied to a field's queryset.
135     """
136     field_dict = {}
137     ignored = []
138     opts = model._meta
139     # Avoid circular import
140     from django.db.models.fields import Field as ModelField
141     sortable_private_fields = [f for f in opts.private_fields if isinstance(f, ModelField)]
142     for f in sorted(chain(opts.concrete_fields, sortable_private_fields, opts.many_to_many)):
143         if not getattr(f, 'editable', False):
144             if (fields is not None and f.name in fields and
145                     (exclude is None or f.name not in exclude)):
146                 raise FieldError(
147                     "'%s' cannot be specified for %s model form as it is a non-editable field" % (
148                         f.name, model.__name__)
149                 )
150             continue
151         if fields is not None and f.name not in fields:
152             continue
153         if exclude and f.name in exclude:
154             continue
155 
156         kwargs = {}
157         if widgets and f.name in widgets:
158             kwargs['widget'] = widgets[f.name]
159         if localized_fields == ALL_FIELDS or (localized_fields and f.name in localized_fields):
160             kwargs['localize'] = True
161         if labels and f.name in labels:
162             kwargs['label'] = labels[f.name]
163         if help_texts and f.name in help_texts:
164             kwargs['help_text'] = help_texts[f.name]
165         if error_messages and f.name in error_messages:
166             kwargs['error_messages'] = error_messages[f.name]
167         if field_classes and f.name in field_classes:
168             kwargs['form_class'] = field_classes[f.name]
169 
170         if formfield_callback is None:
171             formfield = f.formfield(**kwargs)
172         elif not callable(formfield_callback):
173             raise TypeError('formfield_callback must be a function or callable')
174         else:
175             formfield = formfield_callback(f, **kwargs)
176 
177         if formfield:
178             if apply_limit_choices_to:
179                 apply_limit_choices_to_to_formfield(formfield)
180             field_dict[f.name] = formfield
181         else:
182             ignored.append(f.name)
183     if fields:
184         field_dict = {
185             f: field_dict.get(f) for f in fields
186             if (not exclude or f not in exclude) and f not in ignored
187         }
188     return field_dict
189

199         self.help_texts = getattr(options, 'help_texts', None)

204 class ModelFormMetaclass(DeclarativeFieldsMetaclass):
205     def __new__(mcs, name, bases, attrs):
206         base_formfield_callback = None
207         for b in bases:
208             if hasattr(b, 'Meta') and hasattr(b.Meta, 'formfield_callback'):
209                 base_formfield_callback = b.Meta.formfield_callback
210                 break
211 
212         formfield_callback = attrs.pop('formfield_callback', base_formfield_callback)
213 
214         new_class = super(ModelFormMetaclass, mcs).__new__(mcs, name, bases, attrs)
215 
216         if bases == (BaseModelForm,):
217             return new_class
218 
219         opts = new_class._meta = ModelFormOptions(getattr(new_class, 'Meta', None))
220 
221         # We check if a string was passed to `fields` or `exclude`,
222         # which is likely to be a mistake where the user typed ('foo') instead
223         # of ('foo',)
224         for opt in ['fields', 'exclude', 'localized_fields']:
225             value = getattr(opts, opt)
226             if isinstance(value, str) and value != ALL_FIELDS:
227                 msg = ("%(model)s.Meta.%(opt)s cannot be a string. "
228                        "Did you mean to type: ('%(value)s',)?" % {
229                            'model': new_class.__name__,
230                            'opt': opt,
231                            'value': value,
232                        })
233                 raise TypeError(msg)
234 
235         if opts.model:
236             # If a model is defined, extract form fields from it.
237             if opts.fields is None and opts.exclude is None:
238                 raise ImproperlyConfigured(
239                     "Creating a ModelForm without either the 'fields' attribute "
240                     "or the 'exclude' attribute is prohibited; form %s "
241                     "needs updating." % name
242                 )
243 
244             if opts.fields == ALL_FIELDS:
245                 # Sentinel for fields_for_model to indicate "get the list of
246                 # fields from the model"
247                 opts.fields = None
248 
249             fields = fields_for_model(
250                 opts.model, opts.fields, opts.exclude, opts.widgets,
251                 formfield_callback, opts.localized_fields, opts.labels,
252                 opts.help_texts, opts.error_messages, opts.field_classes,
253                 # limit_choices_to will be applied during ModelForm.__init__().
254                 apply_limit_choices_to=False,
255             )
256 
257             # make sure opts.fields doesn't specify an invalid field
258             none_model_fields = {k for k, v in fields.items() if not v}
259             missing_fields = none_model_fields.difference(new_class.declared_fields)
260             if missing_fields:
261                 message = 'Unknown field(s) (%s) specified for %s'
262                 message = message % (', '.join(missing_fields),
263                                      opts.model.__name__)
264                 raise FieldError(message)
265             # Override default model fields with any custom declared ones
266             # (plus, include all the other declared fields).
267             fields.update(new_class.declared_fields)
268         else:
269             fields = new_class.declared_fields
270 
271         new_class.base_fields = fields
272 
273         return new_class
274

276 class BaseModelForm(BaseForm):
277     def __init__(self, data=None, files=None, auto_id='id_%s', prefix=None,
278                  initial=None, error_class=ErrorList, label_suffix=None,
279                  empty_permitted=False, instance=None, use_required_attribute=None,
280                  renderer=None):
281         opts = self._meta
282         if opts.model is None:
283             raise ValueError('ModelForm has no model class specified.')
284         if instance is None:
285             # if we didn't get an instance, instantiate a new one
286             self.instance = opts.model()
287             object_data = {}
288         else:
289             self.instance = instance
290             object_data = model_to_dict(instance, opts.fields, opts.exclude)
291         # if initial was provided, it should override the values from instance
292         if initial is not None:
293             object_data.update(initial)
294         # self._validate_unique will be set to True by BaseModelForm.clean().
295         # It is False by default so overriding self.clean() and failing to call
296         # super will stop validate_unique from being called.
297         self._validate_unique = False
298         super().__init__(
299             data, files, auto_id, prefix, object_data, error_class,
300             label_suffix, empty_permitted, use_required_attribute=use_required_attribute,
301             renderer=renderer,
302         )
303         for formfield in self.fields.values():
304             apply_limit_choices_to_to_formfield(formfield)
305 
306     def _get_validation_exclusions(self):
307         """
308         For backwards-compatibility, exclude several types of fields from model
309         validation. See tickets #12507, #12521, #12553.
310         """
311         exclude = []
312         # Build up a list of fields that should be excluded from model field
313         # validation and unique checks.
314         for f in self.instance._meta.fields:
315             field = f.name
316             # Exclude fields that aren't on the form. The developer may be
317             # adding these values to the model after form validation.
318             if field not in self.fields:
319                 exclude.append(f.name)
320 
321             # Don't perform model validation on fields that were defined
322             # manually on the form and excluded via the ModelForm's Meta
323             # class. See #12901.
324             elif self._meta.fields and field not in self._meta.fields:
325                 exclude.append(f.name)
326             elif self._meta.exclude and field in self._meta.exclude:
327                 exclude.append(f.name)
328 
329             # Exclude fields that failed form validation. There's no need for
330             # the model fields to validate them as well.
331             elif field in self._errors:
332                 exclude.append(f.name)
333 
334             # Exclude empty fields that are not required by the form, if the
335             # underlying model field is required. This keeps the model field
336             # from raising a required error. Note: don't exclude the field from
337             # validation if the model field allows blanks. If it does, the blank
338             # value may be included in a unique check, so cannot be excluded
339             # from validation.
340             else:
341                 form_field = self.fields[field]
342                 field_value = self.cleaned_data.get(field)
343                 if not f.blank and not form_field.required and field_value in form_field.empty_values:
344                     exclude.append(f.name)
345         return exclude
346 
347     def clean(self):
348         self._validate_unique = True
349         return self.cleaned_data
350 
351     def _update_errors(self, errors):
352         # Override any validation error messages defined at the model level
353         # with those defined at the form level.
354         opts = self._meta
355 
356         # Allow the model generated by construct_instance() to raise
357         # ValidationError and have them handled in the same way as others.
358         if hasattr(errors, 'error_dict'):
359             error_dict = errors.error_dict
360         else:
361             error_dict = {NON_FIELD_ERRORS: errors}
362 
363         for field, messages in error_dict.items():
364             if (field == NON_FIELD_ERRORS and opts.error_messages and
365                     NON_FIELD_ERRORS in opts.error_messages):
366                 error_messages = opts.error_messages[NON_FIELD_ERRORS]
367             elif field in self.fields:
368                 error_messages = self.fields[field].error_messages
369             else:
370                 continue
371 
372             for message in messages:
373                 if (isinstance(message, ValidationError) and
374                         message.code in error_messages):
375                     message.message = error_messages[message.code]
376 
377         self.add_error(None, errors)
378 
379     def _post_clean(self):
380         opts = self._meta
381 
382         exclude = self._get_validation_exclusions()
383 
384         # Foreign Keys being used to represent inline relationships
385         # are excluded from basic field value validation. This is for two
386         # reasons: firstly, the value may not be supplied (#12507; the
387         # case of providing new values to the admin); secondly the
388         # object being referred to may not yet fully exist (#12749).
389         # However, these fields *must* be included in uniqueness checks,
390         # so this can't be part of _get_validation_exclusions().
391         for name, field in self.fields.items():
392             if isinstance(field, InlineForeignKeyField):
393                 exclude.append(name)
394 
395         try:
396             self.instance = construct_instance(self, self.instance, opts.fields, opts.exclude)
397         except ValidationError as e:
398             self._update_errors(e)
399 
400         try:
401             self.instance.full_clean(exclude=exclude, validate_unique=False)
402         except ValidationError as e:
403             self._update_errors(e)
404 
405         # Validate uniqueness if needed.
406         if self._validate_unique:
407             self.validate_unique()
408 
409     def validate_unique(self):
410         """
411         Call the instance's validate_unique() method and update the form's
412         validation errors if any were raised.
413         """
414         exclude = self._get_validation_exclusions()
415         try:
416             self.instance.validate_unique(exclude=exclude)
417         except ValidationError as e:
418             self._update_errors(e)
419 
420     def _save_m2m(self):
421         """
422         Save the many-to-many fields and generic relations for this form.
423         """
424         cleaned_data = self.cleaned_data
425         exclude = self._meta.exclude
426         fields = self._meta.fields
427         opts = self.instance._meta
428         # Note that for historical reasons we want to include also
429         # private_fields here. (GenericRelation was previously a fake
430         # m2m field).
431         for f in chain(opts.many_to_many, opts.private_fields):
432             if not hasattr(f, 'save_form_data'):
433                 continue
434             if fields and f.name not in fields:
435                 continue
436             if exclude and f.name in exclude:
437                 continue
438             if f.name in cleaned_data:
439                 f.save_form_data(self.instance, cleaned_data[f.name])
440 
441     def save(self, commit=True):
442         """
443         Save this form's self.instance object if commit=True. Otherwise, add
444         a save_m2m() method to the form which can be called after the instance
445         is saved manually at a later time. Return the model instance.
446         """
447         if self.errors:
448             raise ValueError(
449                 "The %s could not be %s because the data didn't validate." % (
450                     self.instance._meta.object_name,
451                     'created' if self.instance._state.adding else 'changed',
452                 )
453             )
454         if commit:
455             # If committing, save the instance and the m2m data immediately.
456             self.instance.save()
457             self._save_m2m()
458         else:
459             # If not committing, add a method to the form to allow deferred
460             # saving of m2m data.
461             self.save_m2m = self._save_m2m
462         return self.instance
463 
464     save.alters_data = True
465

471 def modelform_factory(model, form=ModelForm, fields=None, exclude=None,
472                       formfield_callback=None, widgets=None, localized_fields=None,
473                       labels=None, help_texts=None, error_messages=None,
474                       field_classes=None):
475     """
476     Return a ModelForm containing form fields for the given model.
477 
478     ``fields`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, include only
479     the named fields in the returned fields. If omitted or '__all__', use all
480     fields.
481 
482     ``exclude`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, exclude the
483     named fields from the returned fields, even if they are listed in the
484     ``fields`` argument.
485 
486     ``widgets`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a widget.
487 
488     ``localized_fields`` is a list of names of fields which should be localized.
489 
490     ``formfield_callback`` is a callable that takes a model field and returns
491     a form field.
492 
493     ``labels`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a label.
494 
495     ``help_texts`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a help text.
496 
497     ``error_messages`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a
498     dictionary of error messages.
499 
500     ``field_classes`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a form
501     field class.
502     """
503     # Create the inner Meta class. FIXME: ideally, we should be able to
504     # construct a ModelForm without creating and passing in a temporary
505     # inner class.
506 
507     # Build up a list of attributes that the Meta object will have.
508     attrs = {'model': model}
509     if fields is not None:
510         attrs['fields'] = fields
511     if exclude is not None:
512         attrs['exclude'] = exclude
513     if widgets is not None:
514         attrs['widgets'] = widgets
515     if localized_fields is not None:
516         attrs['localized_fields'] = localized_fields
517     if labels is not None:
518         attrs['labels'] = labels
519     if help_texts is not None:
520         attrs['help_texts'] = help_texts
521     if error_messages is not None:
522         attrs['error_messages'] = error_messages
523     if field_classes is not None:
524         attrs['field_classes'] = field_classes
525 
526     # If parent form class already has an inner Meta, the Meta we're
527     # creating needs to inherit from the parent's inner meta.
528     bases = (form.Meta,) if hasattr(form, 'Meta') else ()
529     Meta = type('Meta', bases, attrs)
530     if formfield_callback:
531         Meta.formfield_callback = staticmethod(formfield_callback)
532     # Give this new form class a reasonable name.
533     class_name = model.__name__ + 'Form'
534 
535     # Class attributes for the new form class.
536     form_class_attrs = {
537         'Meta': Meta,
538         'formfield_callback': formfield_callback
539     }
540 
541     if (getattr(Meta, 'fields', None) is None and
542             getattr(Meta, 'exclude', None) is None):
543         raise ImproperlyConfigured(
544             "Calling modelform_factory without defining 'fields' or "
545             "'exclude' explicitly is prohibited."
546         )
547 
548     # Instantiate type(form) in order to use the same metaclass as form.
549     return type(form)(class_name, (form,), form_class_attrs)

554 class BaseModelFormSet(BaseFormSet):
555     """
556     A ``FormSet`` for editing a queryset and/or adding new objects to it.
557     """
558     model = None
559 
560     # Set of fields that must be unique among forms of this set.
561     unique_fields = set()
562 
563     def __init__(self, data=None, files=None, auto_id='id_%s', prefix=None,
564                  queryset=None, *, initial=None, **kwargs):
565         self.queryset = queryset
566         self.initial_extra = initial
567         super().__init__(**{'data': data, 'files': files, 'auto_id': auto_id, 'prefix': prefix, **kwargs})
568 
569     def initial_form_count(self):
570         """Return the number of forms that are required in this FormSet."""
571         if not self.is_bound:
572             return len(self.get_queryset())
573         return super().initial_form_count()
574 
575     def _existing_object(self, pk):
576         if not hasattr(self, '_object_dict'):
577             self._object_dict = {o.pk: o for o in self.get_queryset()}
578         return self._object_dict.get(pk)
579 
580     def _get_to_python(self, field):
581         """
582         If the field is a related field, fetch the concrete field's (that
583         is, the ultimate pointed-to field's) to_python.
584         """
585         while field.remote_field is not None:
586             field = field.remote_field.get_related_field()
587         return field.to_python
588 
589     def _construct_form(self, i, **kwargs):
590         pk_required = i < self.initial_form_count()
591         if pk_required:
592             if self.is_bound:
593                 pk_key = '%s-%s' % (self.add_prefix(i), self.model._meta.pk.name)
594                 try:
595                     pk = self.data[pk_key]
596                 except KeyError:
597                     # The primary key is missing. The user may have tampered
598                     # with POST data.
599                     pass
600                 else:
601                     to_python = self._get_to_python(self.model._meta.pk)
602                     try:
603                         pk = to_python(pk)
604                     except ValidationError:
605                         # The primary key exists but is an invalid value. The
606                         # user may have tampered with POST data.
607                         pass
608                     else:
609                         kwargs['instance'] = self._existing_object(pk)
610             else:
611                 kwargs['instance'] = self.get_queryset()[i]
612         elif self.initial_extra:
613             # Set initial values for extra forms
614             try:
615                 kwargs['initial'] = self.initial_extra[i - self.initial_form_count()]
616             except IndexError:
617                 pass
618         form = super()._construct_form(i, **kwargs)
619         if pk_required:
620             form.fields[self.model._meta.pk.name].required = True
621         return form
622 
623     def get_queryset(self):
624         if not hasattr(self, '_queryset'):
625             if self.queryset is not None:
626                 qs = self.queryset
627             else:
628                 qs = self.model._default_manager.get_queryset()
629 
630             # If the queryset isn't already ordered we need to add an
631             # artificial ordering here to make sure that all formsets
632             # constructed from this queryset have the same form order.
633             if not qs.ordered:
634                 qs = qs.order_by(self.model._meta.pk.name)
635 
636             # Removed queryset limiting here. As per discussion re: #13023
637             # on django-dev, max_num should not prevent existing
638             # related objects/inlines from being displayed.
639             self._queryset = qs
640         return self._queryset
641 
642     def save_new(self, form, commit=True):
643         """Save and return a new model instance for the given form."""
644         return form.save(commit=commit)
645 
646     def save_existing(self, form, instance, commit=True):
647         """Save and return an existing model instance for the given form."""
648         return form.save(commit=commit)
649 
650     def delete_existing(self, obj, commit=True):
651         """Deletes an existing model instance."""
652         if commit:
653             obj.delete()
654 
655     def save(self, commit=True):
656         """
657         Save model instances for every form, adding and changing instances
658         as necessary, and return the list of instances.
659         """
660         if not commit:
661             self.saved_forms = []
662 
663             def save_m2m():
664                 for form in self.saved_forms:
665                     form.save_m2m()
666             self.save_m2m = save_m2m
667         return self.save_existing_objects(commit) + self.save_new_objects(commit)
668 
669     save.alters_data = True
670 
671     def clean(self):
672         self.validate_unique()
673 
674     def validate_unique(self):
675         # Collect unique_checks and date_checks to run from all the forms.
676         all_unique_checks = set()
677         all_date_checks = set()
678         forms_to_delete = self.deleted_forms
679         valid_forms = [form for form in self.forms if form.is_valid() and form not in forms_to_delete]
680         for form in valid_forms:
681             exclude = form._get_validation_exclusions()
682             unique_checks, date_checks = form.instance._get_unique_checks(exclude=exclude)
683             all_unique_checks.update(unique_checks)
684             all_date_checks.update(date_checks)
685 
686         errors = []
687         # Do each of the unique checks (unique and unique_together)
688         for uclass, unique_check in all_unique_checks:
689             seen_data = set()
690             for form in valid_forms:
691                 # Get the data for the set of fields that must be unique among the forms.
692                 row_data = (
693                     field if field in self.unique_fields else form.cleaned_data[field]
694                     for field in unique_check if field in form.cleaned_data
695                 )
696                 # Reduce Model instances to their primary key values
697                 row_data = tuple(
698                     d._get_pk_val() if hasattr(d, '_get_pk_val')
699                     # Prevent "unhashable type: list" errors later on.
700                     else tuple(d) if isinstance(d, list)
701                     else d for d in row_data
702                 )
703                 if row_data and None not in row_data:
704                     # if we've already seen it then we have a uniqueness failure
705                     if row_data in seen_data:
706                         # poke error messages into the right places and mark
707                         # the form as invalid
708                         errors.append(self.get_unique_error_message(unique_check))
709                         form._errors[NON_FIELD_ERRORS] = self.error_class([self.get_form_error()])
710                         # remove the data from the cleaned_data dict since it was invalid
711                         for field in unique_check:
712                             if field in form.cleaned_data:
713                                 del form.cleaned_data[field]
714                     # mark the data as seen
715                     seen_data.add(row_data)
716         # iterate over each of the date checks now
717         for date_check in all_date_checks:
718             seen_data = set()
719             uclass, lookup, field, unique_for = date_check
720             for form in valid_forms:
721                 # see if we have data for both fields
722                 if (form.cleaned_data and form.cleaned_data[field] is not None and
723                         form.cleaned_data[unique_for] is not None):
724                     # if it's a date lookup we need to get the data for all the fields
725                     if lookup == 'date':
726                         date = form.cleaned_data[unique_for]
727                         date_data = (date.year, date.month, date.day)
728                     # otherwise it's just the attribute on the date/datetime
729                     # object
730                     else:
731                         date_data = (getattr(form.cleaned_data[unique_for], lookup),)
732                     data = (form.cleaned_data[field],) + date_data
733                     # if we've already seen it then we have a uniqueness failure
734                     if data in seen_data:
735                         # poke error messages into the right places and mark
736                         # the form as invalid
737                         errors.append(self.get_date_error_message(date_check))
738                         form._errors[NON_FIELD_ERRORS] = self.error_class([self.get_form_error()])
739                         # remove the data from the cleaned_data dict since it was invalid
740                         del form.cleaned_data[field]
741                     # mark the data as seen
742                     seen_data.add(data)
743 
744         if errors:
745             raise ValidationError(errors)

749             return gettext("Please correct the duplicate data for %(field)s.") % {
750                 "field": unique_check[0],
751             }
752         else:
753             return gettext("Please correct the duplicate data for %(field)s, which must be unique.") % {
754                 "field": get_text_list(unique_check, _("and")),

759             "Please correct the duplicate data for %(field_name)s "
760             "which must be unique for the %(lookup)s in %(date_field)s."
761         ) % {
762             'field_name': date_check[2],

770     def save_existing_objects(self, commit=True):
771         self.changed_objects = []
772         self.deleted_objects = []
773         if not self.initial_forms:
774             return []
775 
776         saved_instances = []
777         forms_to_delete = self.deleted_forms
778         for form in self.initial_forms:
779             obj = form.instance
780             # If the pk is None, it means either:
781             # 1. The object is an unexpected empty model, created by invalid
782             #    POST data such as an object outside the formset's queryset.
783             # 2. The object was already deleted from the database.
784             if obj.pk is None:
785                 continue
786             if form in forms_to_delete:
787                 self.deleted_objects.append(obj)
788                 self.delete_existing(obj, commit=commit)
789             elif form.has_changed():
790                 self.changed_objects.append((obj, form.changed_data))
791                 saved_instances.append(self.save_existing(form, obj, commit=commit))
792                 if not commit:
793                     self.saved_forms.append(form)
794         return saved_instances

796     def save_new_objects(self, commit=True):
797         self.new_objects = []
798         for form in self.extra_forms:
799             if not form.has_changed():
800                 continue
801             # If someone has marked an add form for deletion, don't save the
802             # object.
803             if self.can_delete and self._should_delete_form(form):
804                 continue
805             self.new_objects.append(self.save_new(form, commit=commit))
806             if not commit:
807                 self.saved_forms.append(form)
808         return self.new_objects

810     def add_fields(self, form, index):
811         """Add a hidden field for the object's primary key."""
812         from django.db.models import AutoField, OneToOneField, ForeignKey
813         self._pk_field = pk = self.model._meta.pk
814         # If a pk isn't editable, then it won't be on the form, so we need to
815         # add it here so we can tell which object is which when we get the
816         # data back. Generally, pk.editable should be false, but for some
817         # reason, auto_created pk fields and AutoField's editable attribute is
818         # True, so check for that as well.
819 
820         def pk_is_not_editable(pk):
821             return (
822                 (not pk.editable) or (pk.auto_created or isinstance(pk, AutoField)) or (
823                     pk.remote_field and pk.remote_field.parent_link and
824                     pk_is_not_editable(pk.remote_field.model._meta.pk)
825                 )
826             )
827         if pk_is_not_editable(pk) or pk.name not in form.fields:
828             if form.is_bound:
829                 # If we're adding the related instance, ignore its primary key
830                 # as it could be an auto-generated default which isn't actually
831                 # in the database.
832                 pk_value = None if form.instance._state.adding else form.instance.pk
833             else:
834                 try:
835                     if index is not None:
836                         pk_value = self.get_queryset()[index].pk
837                     else:
838                         pk_value = None
839                 except IndexError:
840                     pk_value = None
841             if isinstance(pk, (ForeignKey, OneToOneField)):
842                 qs = pk.remote_field.model._default_manager.get_queryset()
843             else:
844                 qs = self.model._default_manager.get_queryset()
845             qs = qs.using(form.instance._state.db)
846             if form._meta.widgets:
847                 widget = form._meta.widgets.get(self._pk_field.name, HiddenInput)
848             else:
849                 widget = HiddenInput
850             form.fields[self._pk_field.name] = ModelChoiceField(qs, initial=pk_value, required=False, widget=widget)

886                  save_as_new=False, prefix=None, queryset=None, **kwargs):
887         if instance is None:
888             self.instance = self.fk.remote_field.model()

890             self.instance = instance

892         if queryset is None:
893             queryset = self.model._default_manager

895             qs = queryset.filter(**{self.fk.name: self.instance})
896         else:
897             qs = queryset.none()

900 
901         # Add the generated field to form._meta.fields if it's defined to make
902         # sure validation isn't skipped on that field.
903         if self.form._meta.fields and self.fk.name not in self.form._meta.fields:
904             if isinstance(self.form._meta.fields, tuple):

918             if mutable is not None:
919                 form.data._mutable = True

921             # creating new instances
922             form.data[form.add_prefix(self._pk_field.name)] = None

924             form.data[form.add_prefix(self.fk.name)] = None
925             if mutable is not None:
926                 form.data._mutable = mutable
927 
928         # Set the fk value here so that the form can do its validation.
929         fk_value = self.instance.pk
930         if self.fk.remote_field.field_name != self.fk.remote_field.model._meta.pk.name:
931             fk_value = getattr(self.instance, self.fk.remote_field.field_name)
932             fk_value = getattr(fk_value, 'pk', fk_value)

940     def save_new(self, form, commit=True):

942         # form (it may have been saved after the formset was originally
943         # instantiated).

947     def add_fields(self, form, index):
948         super().add_fields(form, index)

950             name = self._pk_field.name
951             kwargs = {'pk_field': True}
952         else:
953             # The foreign key field might not be on the form, so we poke at the
954             # Model field to get the label, since we need that for error messages.

957                 'label': getattr(form.fields.get(name), 'label', capfirst(self.fk.verbose_name))

960         # The InlineForeignKeyField assumes that the foreign key relation is
961         # based on the parent model's pk. If this isn't the case, set to_field

972                 to_field = self.instance._meta.pk
973             if to_field.has_default():
974                 setattr(self.instance, to_field.attname, None)

979         unique_check = [field for field in unique_check if field != self.fk.name]
980         return super().get_unique_error_message(unique_check)

983 def _get_foreign_key(parent_model, model, fk_name=None, can_fail=False):
984     """
985     Find and return the ForeignKey from model to parent if there is one
986     (return None if can_fail is True and no such field exists). If fk_name is
987     provided, assume it is the name of the ForeignKey field. Unless can_fail is
988     True, raise an exception if there isn't a ForeignKey from model to
989     parent_model.
990     """
991     # avoid circular import
992     from django.db.models import ForeignKey
993     opts = model._meta
994     if fk_name:
995         fks_to_parent = [f for f in opts.fields if f.name == fk_name]
996         if len(fks_to_parent) == 1:
997             fk = fks_to_parent[0]
998             if not isinstance(fk, ForeignKey) or \
999                     (fk.remote_field.model != parent_model and
1000                      fk.remote_field.model not in parent_model._meta.get_parent_list()):
1001                 raise ValueError(
1002                     "fk_name '%s' is not a ForeignKey to '%s'." % (fk_name, parent_model._meta.label)
1003                 )
1004         elif not fks_to_parent:
1005             raise ValueError(
1006                 "'%s' has no field named '%s'." % (model._meta.label, fk_name)
1007             )
1008     else:
1009         # Try to discover what the ForeignKey from model to parent_model is
1010         fks_to_parent = [
1011             f for f in opts.fields
1012             if isinstance(f, ForeignKey) and (
1013                 f.remote_field.model == parent_model or
1014                 f.remote_field.model in parent_model._meta.get_parent_list()
1015             )
1016         ]
1017         if len(fks_to_parent) == 1:
1018             fk = fks_to_parent[0]
1019         elif not fks_to_parent:
1020             if can_fail:
1021                 return
1022             raise ValueError(
1023                 "'%s' has no ForeignKey to '%s'." % (
1024                     model._meta.label,
1025                     parent_model._meta.label,
1026                 )
1027             )
1028         else:
1029             raise ValueError(
1030                 "'%s' has more than one ForeignKey to '%s'." % (
1031                     model._meta.label,
1032                     parent_model._meta.label,
1033                 )
1034             )
1035     return fk
1036

1038 def inlineformset_factory(parent_model, model, form=ModelForm,
1039                           formset=BaseInlineFormSet, fk_name=None,
1040                           fields=None, exclude=None, extra=3, can_order=False,
1041                           can_delete=True, max_num=None, formfield_callback=None,

1048     ``fk_name`` must be provided if ``model`` has more than one ``ForeignKey``

1069         'localized_fields': localized_fields,
1070         'labels': labels,
1071         'help_texts': help_texts,
1072         'error_messages': error_messages,
1073         'field_classes': field_classes,
1074     }
1075     FormSet = modelformset_factory(model, **kwargs)
1076     FormSet.fk = fk

1211         presented by this object. Subclasses can override this method to

1216     def _get_choices(self):
1217         # If self._choices is set, then somebody must have manually set
1218         # the property self.choices. In this case, just return self._choices.

1220             return self._choices

1222         # Otherwise, execute the QuerySet in self.queryset to determine the
1223         # choices dynamically. Return a fresh ModelChoiceIterator that has not been
1224         # consumed. Note that we're instantiating a new ModelChoiceIterator *each*

1258         data_value = data if data is not None else ''
1259         return str(self.prepare_value(initial_value)) != str(data_value)

As part of startup django validates the ModelAdmin's list_display list/tuple for correctness (django.admin.contrib.checks._check_list_display). Having upgraded django from 2.07 to 2.2.1 I found that a ModelAdmin with a list display that used to pass the checks and work fine in admin now fails validation, preventing django from starting. A PositionField from the django-positions library triggers this bug, explanation why follows.
from django.db import models
from position.Fields import PositionField
class Thing(models.Model)
 number = models.IntegerField(default=0)
 order = PositionField()
from django.contrib import admin
from .models import Thing
@admin.register(Thing)
class ThingAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin)
 list_display = ['number', 'order']
Under 2.2.1 this raises an incorrect admin.E108 message saying "The value of list_display[1] refers to 'order' which is not a callable...".
Under 2.0.7 django starts up successfully.
If you change 'number' to 'no_number' or 'order' to 'no_order' then the validation correctly complains about those.
The reason for this bug is commit ​https://github.com/django/django/commit/47016adbf54b54143d4cf052eeb29fc72d27e6b1 which was proposed and accepted as a fix for bug https://code.djangoproject.com/ticket/28490. The problem is while it fixed that bug it broke the functionality of _check_list_display_item in other cases. The rationale for that change was that after field=getattr(model, item) field could be None if item was a descriptor returning None, but subsequent code incorrectly interpreted field being None as meaning getattr raised an AttributeError. As this was done after trying field = model._meta.get_field(item) and that failing that meant the validation error should be returned. However, after the above change if hasattr(model, item) is false then we no longer even try field = model._meta.get_field(item) before returning an error. The reason hasattr(model, item) is false in the case of a PositionField is its get method throws an exception if called on an instance of the PositionField class on the Thing model class, rather than a Thing instance.
For clarity, here are the various logical tests that _check_list_display_item needs to deal with and the behaviour before the above change, after it, and the correct behaviour (which my suggested patch exhibits). Note this is assuming the first 2 tests callable(item) and hasattr(obj, item) are both false (corresponding to item is an actual function/lambda rather than string or an attribute of ThingAdmin).
hasattr(model, item) returns True or False (which is the same as seeing if getattr(model, item) raises AttributeError)
model._meta.get_field(item) returns a field or raises FieldDoesNotExist

def _check_list_display_item(self, obj, item, label):

		return []

						obj=obj.__class__,
						id='admin.E108',

		if isinstance(field, models.ManyToManyField):
			return [
				checks.Error(
					"The value of '%s' must not be a ManyToManyField." % label,
					obj=obj.__class__,
					id='admin.E109',

791     def _check_list_filter_item(self, obj, item, label):
792         """
793         Check one item of `list_filter`, i.e. check if it is one of three options:
794         1. 'field' -- a basic field filter, possibly w/ relationships (e.g.
795            'field__rel')
796         2. ('field', SomeFieldListFilter) - a field-based list filter class
797         3. SomeListFilter - a non-field list filter class
798         """
799 
800         from django.contrib.admin import ListFilter, FieldListFilter
801 
802         if callable(item) and not isinstance(item, models.Field):
803             # If item is option 3, it should be a ListFilter...
804             if not _issubclass(item, ListFilter):
805                 return must_inherit_from(parent='ListFilter', option=label,
806                                          obj=obj, id='admin.E113')
807             # ...  but not a FieldListFilter.
808             elif issubclass(item, FieldListFilter):
809                 return [
810                     checks.Error(
811                         "The value of '%s' must not inherit from 'FieldListFilter'." % label,
812                         obj=obj.__class__,
813                         id='admin.E114',
814                     )
815                 ]
816             else:
817                 return []
818         elif isinstance(item, (tuple, list)):
819             # item is option #2

158 def parse_http_date(date):
159     """
160     Parse a date format as specified by HTTP RFC7231 section 7.1.1.1.

162     The three formats allowed by the RFC are accepted, even if only the first
163     one is still in widespread use.

384 def _url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme(url, allowed_hosts, require_https=False):
385     # Chrome considers any URL with more than two slashes to be absolute, but
386     # urlparse is not so flexible. Treat any url with three slashes as unsafe.
387     if url.startswith('///'):
388         return False
389     try:
390         url_info = _urlparse(url)
391     except ValueError:  # e.g. invalid IPv6 addresses
392         return False
393     # Forbid URLs like http:///example.com - with a scheme, but without a hostname.
394     # In that URL, example.com is not the hostname but, a path component. However,
395     # Chrome will still consider example.com to be the hostname, so we must not
396     # allow this syntax.
397     if not url_info.netloc and url_info.scheme:
398         return False
399     # Forbid URLs that start with control characters. Some browsers (like
400     # Chrome) ignore quite a few control characters at the start of a
401     # URL and might consider the URL as scheme relative.
402     if unicodedata.category(url[0])[0] == 'C':
403         return False

406     if not url_info.scheme and url_info.netloc:
407         scheme = 'http'
408     valid_schemes = ['https'] if require_https else ['http', 'https']
409     return ((not url_info.netloc or url_info.netloc in allowed_hosts) and

44 class Field:
45     widget = TextInput  # Default widget to use when rendering this type of Field.
46     hidden_widget = HiddenInput  # Default widget to use when rendering this as "hidden".
47     default_validators = []  # Default set of validators
48     # Add an 'invalid' entry to default_error_message if you want a specific
49     # field error message not raised by the field validators.
50     default_error_messages = {
51         'required': _('This field is required.'),
52     }
53     empty_values = list(validators.EMPTY_VALUES)
54 
55     def __init__(self, *, required=True, widget=None, label=None, initial=None,
56                  help_text='', error_messages=None, show_hidden_initial=False,
57                  validators=(), localize=False, disabled=False, label_suffix=None):
58         # required -- Boolean that specifies whether the field is required.
59         #             True by default.
60         # widget -- A Widget class, or instance of a Widget class, that should
61         #           be used for this Field when displaying it. Each Field has a
62         #           default Widget that it'll use if you don't specify this. In
63         #           most cases, the default widget is TextInput.
64         # label -- A verbose name for this field, for use in displaying this
65         #          field in a form. By default, Django will use a "pretty"
66         #          version of the form field name, if the Field is part of a
67         #          Form.
68         # initial -- A value to use in this Field's initial display. This value
69         #            is *not* used as a fallback if data isn't given.
70         # help_text -- An optional string to use as "help text" for this Field.
71         # error_messages -- An optional dictionary to override the default
72         #                   messages that the field will raise.
73         # show_hidden_initial -- Boolean that specifies if it is needed to render a
74         #                        hidden widget with initial value after widget.
75         # validators -- List of additional validators to use
76         # localize -- Boolean that specifies if the field should be localized.
77         # disabled -- Boolean that specifies whether the field is disabled, that
78         #             is its widget is shown in the form but not editable.
79         # label_suffix -- Suffix to be added to the label. Overrides
80         #                 form's label_suffix.
81         self.required, self.label, self.initial = required, label, initial
82         self.show_hidden_initial = show_hidden_initial
83         self.help_text = help_text
84         self.disabled = disabled
85         self.label_suffix = label_suffix
86         widget = widget or self.widget
87         if isinstance(widget, type):
88             widget = widget()
89         else:
90             widget = copy.deepcopy(widget)
91 
92         # Trigger the localization machinery if needed.
93         self.localize = localize
94         if self.localize:
95             widget.is_localized = True
96 
97         # Let the widget know whether it should display as required.
98         widget.is_required = self.required
99 
100         # Hook into self.widget_attrs() for any Field-specific HTML attributes.
101         extra_attrs = self.widget_attrs(widget)
102         if extra_attrs:
103             widget.attrs.update(extra_attrs)
104 
105         self.widget = widget
106 
107         messages = {}
108         for c in reversed(self.__class__.__mro__):
109             messages.update(getattr(c, 'default_error_messages', {}))
110         messages.update(error_messages or {})
111         self.error_messages = messages
112 
113         self.validators = [*self.default_validators, *validators]
114 
115         super().__init__()
116 
117     def prepare_value(self, value):
118         return value
119 
120     def to_python(self, value):
121         return value
122 
123     def validate(self, value):
124         if value in self.empty_values and self.required:
125             raise ValidationError(self.error_messages['required'], code='required')
126 
127     def run_validators(self, value):
128         if value in self.empty_values:
129             return
130         errors = []
131         for v in self.validators:
132             try:
133                 v(value)
134             except ValidationError as e:
135                 if hasattr(e, 'code') and e.code in self.error_messages:
136                     e.message = self.error_messages[e.code]
137                 errors.extend(e.error_list)
138         if errors:
139             raise ValidationError(errors)
140 
141     def clean(self, value):
142         """
143         Validate the given value and return its "cleaned" value as an
144         appropriate Python object. Raise ValidationError for any errors.
145         """
146         value = self.to_python(value)
147         self.validate(value)
148         self.run_validators(value)
149         return value
150 
151     def bound_data(self, data, initial):
152         """
153         Return the value that should be shown for this field on render of a
154         bound form, given the submitted POST data for the field and the initial
155         data, if any.
156 
157         For most fields, this will simply be data; FileFields need to handle it
158         a bit differently.
159         """
160         if self.disabled:
161             return initial
162         return data
163 
164     def widget_attrs(self, widget):
165         """
166         Given a Widget instance (*not* a Widget class), return a dictionary of
167         any HTML attributes that should be added to the Widget, based on this
168         Field.
169         """
170         return {}
171 
172     def has_changed(self, initial, data):
173         """Return True if data differs from initial."""
174         # Always return False if the field is disabled since self.bound_data
175         # always uses the initial value in this case.
176         if self.disabled:
177             return False
178         try:
179             data = self.to_python(data)
180             if hasattr(self, '_coerce'):
181                 return self._coerce(data) != self._coerce(initial)
182         except ValidationError:
183             return True
184         # For purposes of seeing whether something has changed, None is
185         # the same as an empty string, if the data or initial value we get
186         # is None, replace it with ''.
187         initial_value = initial if initial is not None else ''
188         data_value = data if data is not None else ''
189         return initial_value != data_value
190 
191     def get_bound_field(self, form, field_name):
192         """
193         Return a BoundField instance that will be used when accessing the form
194         field in a template.
195         """
196         return BoundField(form, self, field_name)
197 
198     def __deepcopy__(self, memo):
199         result = copy.copy(self)
200         memo[id(self)] = result
201         result.widget = copy.deepcopy(self.widget, memo)
202         result.validators = self.validators[:]
203         return result

206 class CharField(Field):
207     def __init__(self, *, max_length=None, min_length=None, strip=True, empty_value='', **kwargs):
208         self.max_length = max_length
209         self.min_length = min_length
210         self.strip = strip
211         self.empty_value = empty_value
212         super().__init__(**kwargs)
213         if min_length is not None:
214             self.validators.append(validators.MinLengthValidator(int(min_length)))
215         if max_length is not None:
216             self.validators.append(validators.MaxLengthValidator(int(max_length)))
217         self.validators.append(validators.ProhibitNullCharactersValidator())
218 
219     def to_python(self, value):
220         """Return a string."""
221         if value not in self.empty_values:
222             value = str(value)
223             if self.strip:
224                 value = value.strip()
225         if value in self.empty_values:
226             return self.empty_value
227         return value
228 
229     def widget_attrs(self, widget):
230         attrs = super().widget_attrs(widget)
231         if self.max_length is not None and not widget.is_hidden:
232             # The HTML attribute is maxlength, not max_length.
233             attrs['maxlength'] = str(self.max_length)
234         if self.min_length is not None and not widget.is_hidden:
235             # The HTML attribute is minlength, not min_length.
236             attrs['minlength'] = str(self.min_length)
237         return attrs

240 class IntegerField(Field):
241     widget = NumberInput
242     default_error_messages = {
243         'invalid': _('Enter a whole number.'),
244     }
245     re_decimal = re.compile(r'\.0*\s*$')
246 
247     def __init__(self, *, max_value=None, min_value=None, **kwargs):
248         self.max_value, self.min_value = max_value, min_value
249         if kwargs.get('localize') and self.widget == NumberInput:
250             # Localized number input is not well supported on most browsers
251             kwargs.setdefault('widget', super().widget)
252         super().__init__(**kwargs)
253 
254         if max_value is not None:
255             self.validators.append(validators.MaxValueValidator(max_value))
256         if min_value is not None:
257             self.validators.append(validators.MinValueValidator(min_value))
258 
259     def to_python(self, value):
260         """
261         Validate that int() can be called on the input. Return the result
262         of int() or None for empty values.
263         """
264         value = super().to_python(value)
265         if value in self.empty_values:
266             return None
267         if self.localize:
268             value = formats.sanitize_separators(value)
269         # Strip trailing decimal and zeros.
270         try:
271             value = int(self.re_decimal.sub('', str(value)))
272         except (ValueError, TypeError):
273             raise ValidationError(self.error_messages['invalid'], code='invalid')
274         return value
275 
276     def widget_attrs(self, widget):
277         attrs = super().widget_attrs(widget)
278         if isinstance(widget, NumberInput):
279             if self.min_value is not None:
280                 attrs['min'] = self.min_value
281             if self.max_value is not None:
282                 attrs['max'] = self.max_value
283         return attrs

321 class DecimalField(IntegerField):
322     default_error_messages = {
323         'invalid': _('Enter a number.'),
324     }
325 
326     def __init__(self, *, max_value=None, min_value=None, max_digits=None, decimal_places=None, **kwargs):
327         self.max_digits, self.decimal_places = max_digits, decimal_places
328         super().__init__(max_value=max_value, min_value=min_value, **kwargs)
329         self.validators.append(validators.DecimalValidator(max_digits, decimal_places))
330 
331     def to_python(self, value):
332         """
333         Validate that the input is a decimal number. Return a Decimal
334         instance or None for empty values. Ensure that there are no more
335         than max_digits in the number and no more than decimal_places digits
336         after the decimal point.
337         """
338         if value in self.empty_values:
339             return None
340         if self.localize:
341             value = formats.sanitize_separators(value)
342         value = str(value).strip()
343         try:
344             value = Decimal(value)
345         except DecimalException:
346             raise ValidationError(self.error_messages['invalid'], code='invalid')
347         return value
348 
349     def validate(self, value):
350         super().validate(value)
351         if value in self.empty_values:
352             return
353         if not value.is_finite():
354             raise ValidationError(self.error_messages['invalid'], code='invalid')
355 
356     def widget_attrs(self, widget):
357         attrs = super().widget_attrs(widget)
358         if isinstance(widget, NumberInput) and 'step' not in widget.attrs:
359             if self.decimal_places is not None:
360                 # Use exponential notation for small values since they might
361                 # be parsed as 0 otherwise. ref #20765
362                 step = str(Decimal(1).scaleb(-self.decimal_places)).lower()
363             else:
364                 step = 'any'
365             attrs.setdefault('step', step)
366         return attrs

467 class DurationField(Field):
468     default_error_messages = {
469         'invalid': _('Enter a valid duration.'),
470         'overflow': _('The number of days must be between {min_days} and {max_days}.')
471     }
472 
473     def prepare_value(self, value):
474         if isinstance(value, datetime.timedelta):
475             return duration_string(value)
476         return value
477 
478     def to_python(self, value):
479         if value in self.empty_values:
480             return None
481         if isinstance(value, datetime.timedelta):
482             return value
483         try:
484             value = parse_duration(str(value))
485         except OverflowError:
486             raise ValidationError(self.error_messages['overflow'].format(
487                 min_days=datetime.timedelta.min.days,
488                 max_days=datetime.timedelta.max.days,
489             ), code='overflow')
490         if value is None:
491             raise ValidationError(self.error_messages['invalid'], code='invalid')
492         return value

527 class FileField(Field):
528     widget = ClearableFileInput
529     default_error_messages = {
530         'invalid': _("No file was submitted. Check the encoding type on the form."),
531         'missing': _("No file was submitted."),
532         'empty': _("The submitted file is empty."),
533         'max_length': ngettext_lazy(
534             'Ensure this filename has at most %(max)d character (it has %(length)d).',
535             'Ensure this filename has at most %(max)d characters (it has %(length)d).',
536             'max'),
537         'contradiction': _('Please either submit a file or check the clear checkbox, not both.')
538     }
539 
540     def __init__(self, *, max_length=None, allow_empty_file=False, **kwargs):
541         self.max_length = max_length
542         self.allow_empty_file = allow_empty_file
543         super().__init__(**kwargs)
544 
545     def to_python(self, data):
546         if data in self.empty_values:
547             return None
548 
549         # UploadedFile objects should have name and size attributes.
550         try:
551             file_name = data.name
552             file_size = data.size
553         except AttributeError:
554             raise ValidationError(self.error_messages['invalid'], code='invalid')
555 
556         if self.max_length is not None and len(file_name) > self.max_length:
557             params = {'max': self.max_length, 'length': len(file_name)}
558             raise ValidationError(self.error_messages['max_length'], code='max_length', params=params)
559         if not file_name:
560             raise ValidationError(self.error_messages['invalid'], code='invalid')
561         if not self.allow_empty_file and not file_size:
562             raise ValidationError(self.error_messages['empty'], code='empty')
563 
564         return data
565 
566     def clean(self, data, initial=None):
567         # If the widget got contradictory inputs, we raise a validation error
568         if data is FILE_INPUT_CONTRADICTION:
569             raise ValidationError(self.error_messages['contradiction'], code='contradiction')
570         # False means the field value should be cleared; further validation is
571         # not needed.
572         if data is False:
573             if not self.required:
574                 return False
575             # If the field is required, clearing is not possible (the widget
576             # shouldn't return False data in that case anyway). False is not
577             # in self.empty_value; if a False value makes it this far
578             # it should be validated from here on out as None (so it will be
579             # caught by the required check).
580             data = None
581         if not data and initial:
582             return initial
583         return super().clean(data)
584 
585     def bound_data(self, data, initial):
586         if data in (None, FILE_INPUT_CONTRADICTION):
587             return initial
588         return data
589 
590     def has_changed(self, initial, data):
591         return not self.disabled and data is not None

594 class ImageField(FileField):
595     default_validators = [validators.validate_image_file_extension]
596     default_error_messages = {
597         'invalid_image': _(
598             "Upload a valid image. The file you uploaded was either not an "
599             "image or a corrupted image."
600         ),
601     }
602 
603     def to_python(self, data):
604         """
605         Check that the file-upload field data contains a valid image (GIF, JPG,
606         PNG, etc. -- whatever Pillow supports).
607         """
608         f = super().to_python(data)
609         if f is None:
610             return None
611 
612         from PIL import Image
613 
614         # We need to get a file object for Pillow. We might have a path or we might
615         # have to read the data into memory.
616         if hasattr(data, 'temporary_file_path'):
617             file = data.temporary_file_path()
618         else:
619             if hasattr(data, 'read'):
620                 file = BytesIO(data.read())
621             else:
622                 file = BytesIO(data['content'])
623 
624         try:
625             # load() could spot a truncated JPEG, but it loads the entire
626             # image in memory, which is a DoS vector. See #3848 and #18520.
627             image = Image.open(file)
628             # verify() must be called immediately after the constructor.
629             image.verify()
630 
631             # Annotating so subclasses can reuse it for their own validation
632             f.image = image
633             # Pillow doesn't detect the MIME type of all formats. In those
634             # cases, content_type will be None.
635             f.content_type = Image.MIME.get(image.format)
636         except Exception as exc:
637             # Pillow doesn't recognize it as an image.
638             raise ValidationError(
639                 self.error_messages['invalid_image'],
640                 code='invalid_image',
641             ) from exc
642         if hasattr(f, 'seek') and callable(f.seek):
643             f.seek(0)
644         return f
645 
646     def widget_attrs(self, widget):
647         attrs = super().widget_attrs(widget)
648         if isinstance(widget, FileInput) and 'accept' not in widget.attrs:
649             attrs.setdefault('accept', 'image/*')
650         return attrs

653 class URLField(CharField):
654     widget = URLInput
655     default_error_messages = {
656         'invalid': _('Enter a valid URL.'),
657     }
658     default_validators = [validators.URLValidator()]
659 
660     def __init__(self, **kwargs):
661         super().__init__(strip=True, **kwargs)
662 
663     def to_python(self, value):
664 
665         def split_url(url):
666             """
667             Return a list of url parts via urlparse.urlsplit(), or raise
668             ValidationError for some malformed URLs.
669             """
670             try:
671                 return list(urlsplit(url))
672             except ValueError:
673                 # urlparse.urlsplit can raise a ValueError with some
674                 # misformatted URLs.
675                 raise ValidationError(self.error_messages['invalid'], code='invalid')
676 
677         value = super().to_python(value)
678         if value:
679             url_fields = split_url(value)
680             if not url_fields[0]:
681                 # If no URL scheme given, assume http://
682                 url_fields[0] = 'http'
683             if not url_fields[1]:
684                 # Assume that if no domain is provided, that the path segment
685                 # contains the domain.
686                 url_fields[1] = url_fields[2]
687                 url_fields[2] = ''
688                 # Rebuild the url_fields list, since the domain segment may now
689                 # contain the path too.
690                 url_fields = split_url(urlunsplit(url_fields))
691             value = urlunsplit(url_fields)
692         return value
693

696     widget = CheckboxInput

<issue>
docutils reports an error rendering view docstring when the first line is not empty
Description
	
Currently admindoc works correctly only with docstrings where the first line is empty, and all Django docstrings are formatted in this way.
However usually the docstring text starts at the first line, e.g.:
def test():
	"""test tests something.
	"""
and this cause an error:
Error in "default-role" directive:
no content permitted.
.. default-role:: cmsreference
The culprit is this code in trim_docstring:
indent = min(len(line) - len(line.lstrip()) for line in lines if line.lstrip())
The problem is that the indentation of the first line is 0.
The solution is to skip the first line:
indent = min(len(line) - len(line.lstrip()) for line in lines[1:] if line.lstrip())
Thanks.

</issue>

154 def replace_named_groups(pattern):
155     r"""
156     Find named groups in `pattern` and replace them with the group name. E.g.,
157     1. ^(?P<a>\w+)/b/(\w+)$ ==> ^<a>/b/(\w+)$
158     2. ^(?P<a>\w+)/b/(?P<c>\w+)/$ ==> ^<a>/b/<c>/$
159     3. ^(?P<a>\w+)/b/(\w+) ==> ^<a>/b/(\w+)
160     4. ^(?P<a>\w+)/b/(?P<c>\w+) ==> ^<a>/b/<c>
161     """
162     named_group_indices = [
163         (m.start(0), m.end(0), m.group(1))
164         for m in named_group_matcher.finditer(pattern)
165     ]
166     # Tuples of (named capture group pattern, group name).
167     group_pattern_and_name = []
168     # Loop over the groups and their start and end indices.
169     for start, end, group_name in named_group_indices:
170         # Handle nested parentheses, e.g. '^(?P<a>(x|y))/b'.
171         unmatched_open_brackets, prev_char = 1, None
172         for idx, val in enumerate(pattern[end:]):
173             # Check for unescaped `(` and `)`. They mark the start and end of a
174             # nested group.
175             if val == '(' and prev_char != '\\':
176                 unmatched_open_brackets += 1
177             elif val == ')' and prev_char != '\\':
178                 unmatched_open_brackets -= 1
179             prev_char = val
180             # If brackets are balanced, the end of the string for the current
181             # named capture group pattern has been reached.
182             if unmatched_open_brackets == 0:
183                 group_pattern_and_name.append((pattern[start:end + idx + 1], group_name))
184                 break
185 
186     # Replace the string for named capture groups with their group names.
187     for group_pattern, group_name in group_pattern_and_name:
188         pattern = pattern.replace(group_pattern, group_name)
189     return pattern
