1341     def build_filter(
1342         self,
1343         filter_expr,
1344         branch_negated=False,
1345         current_negated=False,
1346         can_reuse=None,
1347         allow_joins=True,
1348         split_subq=True,
1349         reuse_with_filtered_relation=False,
1350         check_filterable=True,
1351     ):
1352         """
1353         Build a WhereNode for a single filter clause but don't add it
1354         to this Query. Query.add_q() will then add this filter to the where
1355         Node.
1356 
1357         The 'branch_negated' tells us if the current branch contains any
1358         negations. This will be used to determine if subqueries are needed.
1359 
1360         The 'current_negated' is used to determine if the current filter is
1361         negated or not and this will be used to determine if IS NULL filtering
1362         is needed.
1363 
1364         The difference between current_negated and branch_negated is that
1365         branch_negated is set on first negation, but current_negated is
1366         flipped for each negation.
1367 
1368         Note that add_filter will not do any negating itself, that is done
1369         upper in the code by add_q().
1370 
1371         The 'can_reuse' is a set of reusable joins for multijoins.
1372 
1373         If 'reuse_with_filtered_relation' is True, then only joins in can_reuse
1374         will be reused.
1375 
1376         The method will create a filter clause that can be added to the current
1377         query. However, if the filter isn't added to the query then the caller
1378         is responsible for unreffing the joins used.
1379         """
1380         if isinstance(filter_expr, dict):
1381             raise FieldError("Cannot parse keyword query as dict")
1382         if isinstance(filter_expr, Q):
1383             return self._add_q(
1384                 filter_expr,
1385                 branch_negated=branch_negated,
1386                 current_negated=current_negated,
1387                 used_aliases=can_reuse,
1388                 allow_joins=allow_joins,
1389                 split_subq=split_subq,
1390                 check_filterable=check_filterable,
1391             )
1392         if hasattr(filter_expr, "resolve_expression"):
1393             if not getattr(filter_expr, "conditional", False):
1394                 raise TypeError("Cannot filter against a non-conditional expression.")
1395             condition = filter_expr.resolve_expression(self, allow_joins=allow_joins)
1396             if not isinstance(condition, Lookup):
1397                 condition = self.build_lookup(["exact"], condition, True)
1398             return WhereNode([condition], connector=AND), []
1399         arg, value = filter_expr
1400         if not arg:
1401             raise FieldError("Cannot parse keyword query %r" % arg)
1402         lookups, parts, reffed_expression = self.solve_lookup_type(arg)
1403 
1404         if check_filterable:
1405             self.check_filterable(reffed_expression)
1406 
1407         if not allow_joins and len(parts) > 1:
1408             raise FieldError("Joined field references are not permitted in this query")
1409 
1410         pre_joins = self.alias_refcount.copy()
1411         value = self.resolve_lookup_value(value, can_reuse, allow_joins)
1412         used_joins = {
1413             k for k, v in self.alias_refcount.items() if v > pre_joins.get(k, 0)
1414         }
1415 
1416         if check_filterable:
1417             self.check_filterable(value)
1418 
1419         if reffed_expression:
1420             condition = self.build_lookup(lookups, reffed_expression, value)
1421             return WhereNode([condition], connector=AND), []
1422 
1423         opts = self.get_meta()
1424         alias = self.get_initial_alias()
1425         allow_many = not branch_negated or not split_subq
1426 
1427         try:
1428             join_info = self.setup_joins(
1429                 parts,
1430                 opts,
1431                 alias,
1432                 can_reuse=can_reuse,
1433                 allow_many=allow_many,
1434                 reuse_with_filtered_relation=reuse_with_filtered_relation,
1435             )
1436 
1437             # Prevent iterator from being consumed by check_related_objects()
1438             if isinstance(value, Iterator):
1439                 value = list(value)
1440             self.check_related_objects(join_info.final_field, value, join_info.opts)
1441 
1442             # split_exclude() needs to know which joins were generated for the
1443             # lookup parts
1444             self._lookup_joins = join_info.joins
1445         except MultiJoin as e:
1446             return self.split_exclude(filter_expr, can_reuse, e.names_with_path)
1447 
1448         # Update used_joins before trimming since they are reused to determine
1449         # which joins could be later promoted to INNER.
1450         used_joins.update(join_info.joins)
1451         targets, alias, join_list = self.trim_joins(
1452             join_info.targets, join_info.joins, join_info.path
1453         )
1454         if can_reuse is not None:
1455             can_reuse.update(join_list)
1456 
1457         if join_info.final_field.is_relation:
1458             # No support for transforms for relational fields
1459             num_lookups = len(lookups)
1460             if num_lookups > 1:
1461                 raise FieldError(
1462                     "Related Field got invalid lookup: {}".format(lookups[0])
1463                 )
1464             if len(targets) == 1:
1465                 col = self._get_col(targets[0], join_info.final_field, alias)
1466             else:
1467                 col = MultiColSource(
1468                     alias, targets, join_info.targets, join_info.final_field
1469                 )
1470         else:
1471             col = self._get_col(targets[0], join_info.final_field, alias)
1472 
1473         condition = self.build_lookup(lookups, col, value)
1474         lookup_type = condition.lookup_name
1475         clause = WhereNode([condition], connector=AND)
1476 
1477         require_outer = (
1478             lookup_type == "isnull" and condition.rhs is True and not current_negated
1479         )
1480         if (
1481             current_negated
1482             and (lookup_type != "isnull" or condition.rhs is False)
1483             and condition.rhs is not None
1484         ):
1485             require_outer = True
1486             if lookup_type != "isnull":
1487                 # The condition added here will be SQL like this:
1488                 # NOT (col IS NOT NULL), where the first NOT is added in
1489                 # upper layers of code. The reason for addition is that if col
1490                 # is null, then col != someval will result in SQL "unknown"
1491                 # which isn't the same as in Python. The Python None handling
1492                 # is wanted, and it can be gotten by
1493                 # (col IS NULL OR col != someval)
1494                 #   <=>
1495                 # NOT (col IS NOT NULL AND col = someval).
1496                 if (
1497                     self.is_nullable(targets[0])
1498                     or self.alias_map[join_list[-1]].join_type == LOUTER
1499                 ):
1500                     lookup_class = targets[0].get_lookup("isnull")
1501                     col = self._get_col(targets[0], join_info.targets[0], alias)
1502                     clause.add(lookup_class(col, False), AND)
1503                 # If someval is a nullable column, someval IS NOT NULL is
1504                 # added.
1505                 if isinstance(value, Col) and self.is_nullable(value.target):
1506                     lookup_class = value.target.get_lookup("isnull")
1507                     clause.add(lookup_class(value, False), AND)
1508         return clause, used_joins if not require_outer else ()
1509 
1510     def add_filter(self, filter_lhs, filter_rhs):
1511         self.add_q(Q((filter_lhs, filter_rhs)))

1513     def add_q(self, q_object):
1514         """
1515         A preprocessor for the internal _add_q(). Responsible for doing final
1516         join promotion.
1517         """
1518         # For join promotion this case is doing an AND for the added q_object
1519         # and existing conditions. So, any existing inner join forces the join
1520         # type to remain inner. Existing outer joins can however be demoted.
1521         # (Consider case where rel_a is LOUTER and rel_a__col=1 is added - if
1522         # rel_a doesn't produce any rows, then the whole condition must fail.
1523         # So, demotion is OK.
1524         existing_inner = {
1525             a for a in self.alias_map if self.alias_map[a].join_type == INNER
1526         }
1527         clause, _ = self._add_q(q_object, self.used_aliases)
1528         if clause:
1529             self.where.add(clause, AND)
1530         self.demote_joins(existing_inner)

1532     def build_where(self, filter_expr):

1538     def _add_q(
1539         self,
1540         q_object,
1541         used_aliases,
1542         branch_negated=False,
1543         current_negated=False,
1544         allow_joins=True,
1545         split_subq=True,
1546         check_filterable=True,
1547     ):
1548         """Add a Q-object to the current filter."""
1549         connector = q_object.connector
1550         current_negated = current_negated ^ q_object.negated
1551         branch_negated = branch_negated or q_object.negated
1552         target_clause = WhereNode(connector=connector, negated=q_object.negated)
1553         joinpromoter = JoinPromoter(
1554             q_object.connector, len(q_object.children), current_negated
1555         )
1556         for child in q_object.children:
1557             child_clause, needed_inner = self.build_filter(
1558                 child,
1559                 can_reuse=used_aliases,
1560                 branch_negated=branch_negated,
1561                 current_negated=current_negated,
1562                 allow_joins=allow_joins,
1563                 split_subq=split_subq,
1564                 check_filterable=check_filterable,
1565             )
1566             joinpromoter.add_votes(needed_inner)
1567             if child_clause:
1568                 target_clause.add(child_clause, connector)
1569         needed_inner = joinpromoter.update_join_types(self)
1570         return target_clause, needed_inner
1571 
1572     def build_filtered_relation_q(
1573         self, q_object, reuse, branch_negated=False, current_negated=False
1574     ):
1575         """Add a FilteredRelation object to the current filter."""
1576         connector = q_object.connector
1577         current_negated ^= q_object.negated
1578         branch_negated = branch_negated or q_object.negated
1579         target_clause = WhereNode(connector=connector, negated=q_object.negated)
1580         for child in q_object.children:
1581             if isinstance(child, Node):
1582                 child_clause = self.build_filtered_relation_q(
1583                     child,
1584                     reuse=reuse,
1585                     branch_negated=branch_negated,
1586                     current_negated=current_negated,
1587                 )
1588             else:
1589                 child_clause, _ = self.build_filter(
1590                     child,
1591                     can_reuse=reuse,
1592                     branch_negated=branch_negated,
1593                     current_negated=current_negated,
1594                     allow_joins=True,
1595                     split_subq=False,
1596                     reuse_with_filtered_relation=True,
1597                 )
1598             target_clause.add(child_clause, connector)
1599         return target_clause

1601     def add_filtered_relation(self, filtered_relation, alias):
1602         filtered_relation.alias = alias
1603         lookups = dict(get_children_from_q(filtered_relation.condition))
1604         relation_lookup_parts, relation_field_parts, _ = self.solve_lookup_type(
1605             filtered_relation.relation_name
1606         )
1607         if relation_lookup_parts:
1608             raise ValueError(
1609                 "FilteredRelation's relation_name cannot contain lookups "
1610                 "(got %r)." % filtered_relation.relation_name
1611             )
1612         for lookup in chain(lookups):
1613             lookup_parts, lookup_field_parts, _ = self.solve_lookup_type(lookup)
1614             shift = 2 if not lookup_parts else 1
1615             lookup_field_path = lookup_field_parts[:-shift]
1616             for idx, lookup_field_part in enumerate(lookup_field_path):
1617                 if len(relation_field_parts) > idx:
1618                     if relation_field_parts[idx] != lookup_field_part:
1619                         raise ValueError(
1620                             "FilteredRelation's condition doesn't support "
1621                             "relations outside the %r (got %r)."
1622                             % (filtered_relation.relation_name, lookup)
1623                         )
1624                 else:
1625                     raise ValueError(
1626                         "FilteredRelation's condition doesn't support nested "
1627                         "relations deeper than the relation_name (got %r for "
1628                         "%r)." % (lookup, filtered_relation.relation_name)
1629                     )
1630         self._filtered_relations[filtered_relation.alias] = filtered_relation

1632     def names_to_path(self, names, opts, allow_many=True, fail_on_missing=False):
1633         """
1634         Walk the list of names and turns them into PathInfo tuples. A single
1635         name in 'names' can generate multiple PathInfos (m2m, for example).
1636 
1637         'names' is the path of names to travel, 'opts' is the model Options we
1638         start the name resolving from, 'allow_many' is as for setup_joins().
1639         If fail_on_missing is set to True, then a name that can't be resolved
1640         will generate a FieldError.
1641 
1642         Return a list of PathInfo tuples. In addition return the final field
1643         (the last used join field) and target (which is a field guaranteed to
1644         contain the same value as the final field). Finally, return those names
1645         that weren't found (which are likely transforms and the final lookup).
1646         """
1647         path, names_with_path = [], []
1648         for pos, name in enumerate(names):
1649             cur_names_with_path = (name, [])
1650             if name == "pk":
1651                 name = opts.pk.name
1652 
1653             field = None
1654             filtered_relation = None
1655             try:
1656                 if opts is None:
1657                     raise FieldDoesNotExist
1658                 field = opts.get_field(name)
1659             except FieldDoesNotExist:
1660                 if name in self.annotation_select:
1661                     field = self.annotation_select[name].output_field
1662                 elif name in self._filtered_relations and pos == 0:
1663                     filtered_relation = self._filtered_relations[name]
1664                     if LOOKUP_SEP in filtered_relation.relation_name:
1665                         parts = filtered_relation.relation_name.split(LOOKUP_SEP)
1666                         filtered_relation_path, field, _, _ = self.names_to_path(
1667                             parts,
1668                             opts,
1669                             allow_many,
1670                             fail_on_missing,
1671                         )
1672                         path.extend(filtered_relation_path[:-1])
1673                     else:
1674                         field = opts.get_field(filtered_relation.relation_name)
1675             if field is not None:
1676                 # Fields that contain one-to-many relations with a generic
1677                 # model (like a GenericForeignKey) cannot generate reverse
1678                 # relations and therefore cannot be used for reverse querying.
1679                 if field.is_relation and not field.related_model:
1680                     raise FieldError(
1681                         "Field %r does not generate an automatic reverse "
1682                         "relation and therefore cannot be used for reverse "
1683                         "querying. If it is a GenericForeignKey, consider "
1684                         "adding a GenericRelation." % name
1685                     )
1686                 try:
1687                     model = field.model._meta.concrete_model
1688                 except AttributeError:
1689                     # QuerySet.annotate() may introduce fields that aren't
1690                     # attached to a model.
1691                     model = None
1692             else:
1693                 # We didn't find the current field, so move position back
1694                 # one step.
1695                 pos -= 1
1696                 if pos == -1 or fail_on_missing:
1697                     available = sorted(
1698                         [
1699                             *get_field_names_from_opts(opts),
1700                             *self.annotation_select,
1701                             *self._filtered_relations,
1702                         ]
1703                     )
1704                     raise FieldError(
1705                         "Cannot resolve keyword '%s' into field. "
1706                         "Choices are: %s" % (name, ", ".join(available))
1707                     )
1708                 break
1709             # Check if we need any joins for concrete inheritance cases (the
1710             # field lives in parent, but we are currently in one of its
1711             # children)
1712             if opts is not None and model is not opts.model:
1713                 path_to_parent = opts.get_path_to_parent(model)
1714                 if path_to_parent:
1715                     path.extend(path_to_parent)
1716                     cur_names_with_path[1].extend(path_to_parent)
1717                     opts = path_to_parent[-1].to_opts
1718             if hasattr(field, "path_infos"):
1719                 if filtered_relation:
1720                     pathinfos = field.get_path_info(filtered_relation)
1721                 else:
1722                     pathinfos = field.path_infos
1723                 if not allow_many:
1724                     for inner_pos, p in enumerate(pathinfos):
1725                         if p.m2m:
1726                             cur_names_with_path[1].extend(pathinfos[0 : inner_pos + 1])
1727                             names_with_path.append(cur_names_with_path)
1728                             raise MultiJoin(pos + 1, names_with_path)
1729                 last = pathinfos[-1]
1730                 path.extend(pathinfos)
1731                 final_field = last.join_field
1732                 opts = last.to_opts
1733                 targets = last.target_fields
1734                 cur_names_with_path[1].extend(pathinfos)
1735                 names_with_path.append(cur_names_with_path)
1736             else:
1737                 # Local non-relational field.
1738                 final_field = field
1739                 targets = (field,)
1740                 if fail_on_missing and pos + 1 != len(names):
1741                     raise FieldError(
1742                         "Cannot resolve keyword %r into field. Join on '%s'"
1743                         " not permitted." % (names[pos + 1], name)
1744                     )
1745                 break
1746         return path, final_field, targets, names[pos + 1 :]

1748     def setup_joins(
1749         self,
1750         names,
1751         opts,
1752         alias,
1753         can_reuse=None,
1754         allow_many=True,
1755         reuse_with_filtered_relation=False,
1756     ):
1757         """
1758         Compute the necessary table joins for the passage through the fields
1759         given in 'names'. 'opts' is the Options class for the current model
1760         (which gives the table we are starting from), 'alias' is the alias for
1761         the table to start the joining from.
1762 
1763         The 'can_reuse' defines the reverse foreign key joins we can reuse. It
1764         can be None in which case all joins are reusable or a set of aliases
1765         that can be reused. Note that non-reverse foreign keys are always
1766         reusable when using setup_joins().
1767 
1768         The 'reuse_with_filtered_relation' can be used to force 'can_reuse'
1769         parameter and force the relation on the given connections.
1770 
1771         If 'allow_many' is False, then any reverse foreign key seen will
1772         generate a MultiJoin exception.
1773 
1774         Return the final field involved in the joins, the target field (used
1775         for any 'where' constraint), the final 'opts' value, the joins, the
1776         field path traveled to generate the joins, and a transform function
1777         that takes a field and alias and is equivalent to `field.get_col(alias)`
1778         in the simple case but wraps field transforms if they were included in
1779         names.
1780 
1781         The target field is the field containing the concrete value. Final
1782         field can be something different, for example foreign key pointing to
1783         that value. Final field is needed for example in some value
1784         conversions (convert 'obj' in fk__id=obj to pk val using the foreign
1785         key field for example).
1786         """
1787         joins = [alias]
1788         # The transform can't be applied yet, as joins must be trimmed later.
1789         # To avoid making every caller of this method look up transforms
1790         # directly, compute transforms here and create a partial that converts
1791         # fields to the appropriate wrapped version.
1792 
1793         def final_transformer(field, alias):
1794             if not self.alias_cols:
1795                 alias = None
1796             return field.get_col(alias)
1797 
1798         # Try resolving all the names as fields first. If there's an error,
1799         # treat trailing names as lookups until a field can be resolved.
1800         last_field_exception = None
1801         for pivot in range(len(names), 0, -1):
1802             try:
1803                 path, final_field, targets, rest = self.names_to_path(
1804                     names[:pivot],
1805                     opts,
1806                     allow_many,
1807                     fail_on_missing=True,
1808                 )
1809             except FieldError as exc:
1810                 if pivot == 1:
1811                     # The first item cannot be a lookup, so it's safe
1812                     # to raise the field error here.
1813                     raise
1814                 else:
1815                     last_field_exception = exc
1816             else:
1817                 # The transforms are the remaining items that couldn't be
1818                 # resolved into fields.
1819                 transforms = names[pivot:]
1820                 break
1821         for name in transforms:
1822 
1823             def transform(field, alias, *, name, previous):
1824                 try:
1825                     wrapped = previous(field, alias)
1826                     return self.try_transform(wrapped, name)
1827                 except FieldError:
1828                     # FieldError is raised if the transform doesn't exist.
1829                     if isinstance(final_field, Field) and last_field_exception:
1830                         raise last_field_exception
1831                     else:
1832                         raise
1833 
1834             final_transformer = functools.partial(
1835                 transform, name=name, previous=final_transformer
1836             )
1837         # Then, add the path to the query's joins. Note that we can't trim
1838         # joins at this stage - we will need the information about join type
1839         # of the trimmed joins.
1840         for join in path:
1841             if join.filtered_relation:
1842                 filtered_relation = join.filtered_relation.clone()
1843                 table_alias = filtered_relation.alias
1844             else:
1845                 filtered_relation = None
1846                 table_alias = None
1847             opts = join.to_opts
1848             if join.direct:
1849                 nullable = self.is_nullable(join.join_field)
1850             else:
1851                 nullable = True
1852             connection = self.join_class(
1853                 opts.db_table,
1854                 alias,
1855                 table_alias,
1856                 INNER,
1857                 join.join_field,
1858                 nullable,
1859                 filtered_relation=filtered_relation,
1860             )
1861             reuse = can_reuse if join.m2m or reuse_with_filtered_relation else None
1862             alias = self.join(
1863                 connection,
1864                 reuse=reuse,
1865                 reuse_with_filtered_relation=reuse_with_filtered_relation,
1866             )
1867             joins.append(alias)
1868             if filtered_relation:
1869                 filtered_relation.path = joins[:]
1870         return JoinInfo(final_field, targets, opts, joins, path, final_transformer)
1871 
1872     def trim_joins(self, targets, joins, path):
1873         """
1874         The 'target' parameter is the final field being joined to, 'joins'
1875         is the full list of join aliases. The 'path' contain the PathInfos
1876         used to create the joins.
1877 
1878         Return the final target field and table alias and the new active
1879         joins.
1880 
1881         Always trim any direct join if the target column is already in the
1882         previous table. Can't trim reverse joins as it's unknown if there's
1883         anything on the other side of the join.
1884         """
1885         joins = joins[:]
1886         for pos, info in enumerate(reversed(path)):
1887             if len(joins) == 1 or not info.direct:
1888                 break
1889             if info.filtered_relation:
1890                 break
1891             join_targets = {t.column for t in info.join_field.foreign_related_fields}
1892             cur_targets = {t.column for t in targets}
1893             if not cur_targets.issubset(join_targets):
1894                 break
1895             targets_dict = {
1896                 r[1].column: r[0]
1897                 for r in info.join_field.related_fields
1898                 if r[1].column in cur_targets
1899             }
1900             targets = tuple(targets_dict[t.column] for t in targets)
1901             self.unref_alias(joins.pop())
1902         return targets, joins[-1], joins

1904     @classmethod
1905     def _gen_cols(cls, exprs, include_external=False):
1906         for expr in exprs:
1907             if isinstance(expr, Col):
1908                 yield expr
1909             elif include_external and callable(
1910                 getattr(expr, "get_external_cols", None)
1911             ):
1912                 yield from expr.get_external_cols()
1913             elif hasattr(expr, "get_source_expressions"):
1914                 yield from cls._gen_cols(
1915                     expr.get_source_expressions(),
1916                     include_external=include_external,
1917                 )

1923     def resolve_ref(self, name, allow_joins=True, reuse=None, summarize=False):
1924         annotation = self.annotations.get(name)
1925         if annotation is not None:
1926             if not allow_joins:
1927                 for alias in self._gen_col_aliases([annotation]):
1928                     if isinstance(self.alias_map[alias], Join):
1929                         raise FieldError(
1930                             "Joined field references are not permitted in this query"
1931                         )
1932             if summarize:
1933                 # Summarize currently means we are doing an aggregate() query
1934                 # which is executed as a wrapped subquery if any of the
1935                 # aggregate() elements reference an existing annotation. In
1936                 # that case we need to return a Ref to the subquery's annotation.
1937                 if name not in self.annotation_select:
1938                     raise FieldError(
1939                         "Cannot aggregate over the '%s' alias. Use annotate() "
1940                         "to promote it." % name
1941                     )
1942                 return Ref(name, self.annotation_select[name])
1943             else:
1944                 return annotation
1945         else:
1946             field_list = name.split(LOOKUP_SEP)
1947             annotation = self.annotations.get(field_list[0])
1948             if annotation is not None:
1949                 for transform in field_list[1:]:
1950                     annotation = self.try_transform(annotation, transform)
1951                 return annotation
1952             join_info = self.setup_joins(
1953                 field_list, self.get_meta(), self.get_initial_alias(), can_reuse=reuse
1954             )
1955             targets, final_alias, join_list = self.trim_joins(
1956                 join_info.targets, join_info.joins, join_info.path
1957             )
1958             if not allow_joins and len(join_list) > 1:
1959                 raise FieldError(
1960                     "Joined field references are not permitted in this query"
1961                 )
1962             if len(targets) > 1:
1963                 raise FieldError(
1964                     "Referencing multicolumn fields with F() objects isn't supported"
1965                 )
1966             # Verify that the last lookup in name is a field or a transform:
1967             # transform_function() raises FieldError if not.
1968             transform = join_info.transform_function(targets[0], final_alias)
1969             if reuse is not None:
1970                 reuse.update(join_list)
1971             return transform

1973     def split_exclude(self, filter_expr, can_reuse, names_with_path):
1974         """
1975         When doing an exclude against any kind of N-to-many relation, we need
1976         to use a subquery. This method constructs the nested query, given the
1977         original exclude filter (filter_expr) and the portion up to the first
1978         N-to-many relation field.
1979 
1980         For example, if the origin filter is ~Q(child__name='foo'), filter_expr
1981         is ('child__name', 'foo') and can_reuse is a set of joins usable for
1982         filters in the original query.
1983 
1984         We will turn this into equivalent of:
1985             WHERE NOT EXISTS(
1986                 SELECT 1
1987                 FROM child
1988                 WHERE name = 'foo' AND child.parent_id = parent.id
1989                 LIMIT 1
1990             )
1991         """
1992         # Generate the inner query.
1993         query = self.__class__(self.model)
1994         query._filtered_relations = self._filtered_relations
1995         filter_lhs, filter_rhs = filter_expr
1996         if isinstance(filter_rhs, OuterRef):
1997             filter_rhs = OuterRef(filter_rhs)
1998         elif isinstance(filter_rhs, F):
1999             filter_rhs = OuterRef(filter_rhs.name)
2000         query.add_filter(filter_lhs, filter_rhs)
2001         query.clear_ordering(force=True)
2002         # Try to have as simple as possible subquery -> trim leading joins from
2003         # the subquery.
2004         trimmed_prefix, contains_louter = query.trim_start(names_with_path)
2005 
2006         col = query.select[0]
2007         select_field = col.target
2008         alias = col.alias
2009         if alias in can_reuse:
2010             pk = select_field.model._meta.pk
2011             # Need to add a restriction so that outer query's filters are in effect for
2012             # the subquery, too.
2013             query.bump_prefix(self)
2014             lookup_class = select_field.get_lookup("exact")
2015             # Note that the query.select[0].alias is different from alias
2016             # due to bump_prefix above.
2017             lookup = lookup_class(pk.get_col(query.select[0].alias), pk.get_col(alias))
2018             query.where.add(lookup, AND)
2019             query.external_aliases[alias] = True
2020 
2021         lookup_class = select_field.get_lookup("exact")
2022         lookup = lookup_class(col, ResolvedOuterRef(trimmed_prefix))
2023         query.where.add(lookup, AND)
2024         condition, needed_inner = self.build_filter(Exists(query))
2025 
2026         if contains_louter:
2027             or_null_condition, _ = self.build_filter(
2028                 ("%s__isnull" % trimmed_prefix, True),
2029                 current_negated=True,
2030                 branch_negated=True,
2031                 can_reuse=can_reuse,
2032             )
2033             condition.add(or_null_condition, OR)
2034             # Note that the end result will be:
2035             # (outercol NOT IN innerq AND outercol IS NOT NULL) OR outercol IS NULL.
2036             # This might look crazy but due to how IN works, this seems to be
2037             # correct. If the IS NOT NULL check is removed then outercol NOT
2038             # IN will return UNKNOWN. If the IS NULL check is removed, then if
2039             # outercol IS NULL we will not match the row.
2040         return condition, needed_inner

2050     def set_limits(self, low=None, high=None):
2051         """
2052         Adjust the limits on the rows retrieved. Use low/high to set these,
2053         as it makes it more Pythonic to read and write. When the SQL query is
2054         created, convert them to the appropriate offset and limit values.
2055 
2056         Apply any limits passed in here to the existing constraints. Add low
2057         to the current low value and clamp both to any existing high value.
2058         """
2059         if high is not None:
2060             if self.high_mark is not None:
2061                 self.high_mark = min(self.high_mark, self.low_mark + high)
2062             else:
2063                 self.high_mark = self.low_mark + high
2064         if low is not None:
2065             if self.high_mark is not None:
2066                 self.low_mark = min(self.high_mark, self.low_mark + low)
2067             else:
2068                 self.low_mark = self.low_mark + low
2069 
2070         if self.low_mark == self.high_mark:
2071             self.set_empty()

2175     def add_ordering(self, *ordering):
2176         """
2177         Add items from the 'ordering' sequence to the query's "order by"
2178         clause. These items are either field names (not column names) --
2179         possibly with a direction prefix ('-' or '?') -- or OrderBy
2180         expressions.

2188                     continue

2190                     item = item[1:]

2196                 # FieldError will be raise if it's not.
2197                 self.names_to_path(item.split(LOOKUP_SEP), self.model._meta)
2198             elif not hasattr(item, "resolve_expression"):

2201                 raise FieldError(
2202                     "Using an aggregate in order_by() without also including "
2203                     "it in annotate() is not allowed: %s" % item
2204                 )
2205         if errors:
2206             raise FieldError("Invalid order_by arguments: %s" % errors)
2207         if ordering:
2208             self.order_by += ordering

2210             self.default_ordering = False

2228     def set_group_by(self, allow_aliases=True):

2233         return data. If the database backend supports grouping by the
2234         primary key, and the query would be equivalent, the optimization
2235         will be made automatically.

2237         # Column names from JOINs to check collisions with aliases.
2238         if allow_aliases:
2239             column_names = set()
2240             seen_models = set()
2241             for join in list(self.alias_map.values())[1:]:  # Skip base table.
2242                 model = join.join_field.related_model
2243                 if model not in seen_models:
2244                     column_names.update(
2245                         {field.column for field in model._meta.local_concrete_fields}
2246                     )

2250         if self.annotation_select:
2251             for alias, annotation in self.annotation_select.items():
2252                 if not allow_aliases or alias in column_names:
2253                     alias = None

2258     def add_select_related(self, fields):

2260         Set up the select_related data structure so that we only select

2262         self.select_related=True).

2265             field_dict = {}

2267             field_dict = self.select_related

2613         """
2614         Change join types so that the generated query is as efficient as
2615         possible, but still correct. So, change as many joins as possible

2617         results from the query.

2619         to_promote = set()

2622         # similarly to (a OR b) for join promotion.
2623         for table, votes in self.votes.items():

2626             # valid results. Consider the case where a model with rel_a and

2646             if self.effective_connector == AND or (

2652             # Now, we first generate the OR clause, and promote joins for it

392     def _get_path_info_with_parent(self, filtered_relation):
393         """
394         Return the path that joins the current model through any parent models.
395         The idea is that if you have a GFK defined on a parent model then we
396         need to join the parent model first, then the child model.
397         """
398         # With an inheritance chain ChildTag -> Tag and Tag defines the
399         # GenericForeignKey, and a TaggedItem model has a GenericRelation to
400         # ChildTag, then we need to generate a join from TaggedItem to Tag
401         # (as Tag.object_id == TaggedItem.pk), and another join from Tag to
402         # ChildTag (as that is where the relation is to). Do this by first
403         # generating a join to the parent model, then generating joins to the
404         # child models.
405         path = []
406         opts = self.remote_field.model._meta.concrete_model._meta
407         parent_opts = opts.get_field(self.object_id_field_name).model._meta
408         target = parent_opts.pk
409         path.append(
410             PathInfo(
411                 from_opts=self.model._meta,
412                 to_opts=parent_opts,
413                 target_fields=(target,),
414                 join_field=self.remote_field,
415                 m2m=True,
416                 direct=False,
417                 filtered_relation=filtered_relation,
418             )
419         )
420         # Collect joins needed for the parent -> child chain. This is easiest
421         # to do if we collect joins for the child -> parent chain and then
422         # reverse the direction (call to reverse() and use of
423         # field.remote_field.get_path_info()).
424         parent_field_chain = []
425         while parent_opts != opts:
426             field = opts.get_ancestor_link(parent_opts.model)
427             parent_field_chain.append(field)
428             opts = field.remote_field.model._meta
429         parent_field_chain.reverse()
430         for field in parent_field_chain:
431             path.extend(field.remote_field.path_infos)
432         return path

1 """
2 Accessors for related objects.
3 
4 When a field defines a relation between two models, each model class provides
5 an attribute to access related instances of the other model class (unless the
6 reverse accessor has been disabled with related_name='+').
7 
8 Accessors are implemented as descriptors in order to customize access and
9 assignment. This module defines the descriptor classes.
10 
11 Forward accessors follow foreign keys. Reverse accessors trace them back. For
12 example, with the following models::
13 
14     class Parent(Model):
15         pass
16 
17     class Child(Model):
18         parent = ForeignKey(Parent, related_name='children')
19 
20  ``child.parent`` is a forward many-to-one relation. ``parent.children`` is a
21 reverse many-to-one relation.
22 
23 There are three types of relations (many-to-one, one-to-one, and many-to-many)
24 and two directions (forward and reverse) for a total of six combinations.
25 
26 1. Related instance on the forward side of a many-to-one relation:
27    ``ForwardManyToOneDescriptor``.
28 
29    Uniqueness of foreign key values is irrelevant to accessing the related
30    instance, making the many-to-one and one-to-one cases identical as far as
31    the descriptor is concerned. The constraint is checked upstream (unicity
32    validation in forms) or downstream (unique indexes in the database).
33 
34 2. Related instance on the forward side of a one-to-one
35    relation: ``ForwardOneToOneDescriptor``.
36 
37    It avoids querying the database when accessing the parent link field in
38    a multi-table inheritance scenario.
39 
40 3. Related instance on the reverse side of a one-to-one relation:
41    ``ReverseOneToOneDescriptor``.
42 
43    One-to-one relations are asymmetrical, despite the apparent symmetry of the
44    name, because they're implemented in the database with a foreign key from
45    one table to another. As a consequence ``ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`` is
46    slightly different from ``ForwardManyToOneDescriptor``.
47 
48 4. Related objects manager for related instances on the reverse side of a
49    many-to-one relation: ``ReverseManyToOneDescriptor``.
50 
51    Unlike the previous two classes, this one provides access to a collection
52    of objects. It returns a manager rather than an instance.
53 
54 5. Related objects manager for related instances on the forward or reverse
55    sides of a many-to-many relation: ``ManyToManyDescriptor``.
56 
57    Many-to-many relations are symmetrical. The syntax of Django models
58    requires declaring them on one side but that's an implementation detail.
59    They could be declared on the other side without any change in behavior.
60    Therefore the forward and reverse descriptors can be the same.
61 
62    If you're looking for ``ForwardManyToManyDescriptor`` or
63    ``ReverseManyToManyDescriptor``, use ``ManyToManyDescriptor`` instead.
64 """

144             },
145         )

153     def get_prefetch_queryset(self, instances, queryset=None):
154         if queryset is None:
155             queryset = self.get_queryset()
156         queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])
157 
158         rel_obj_attr = self.field.get_foreign_related_value
159         instance_attr = self.field.get_local_related_value
160         instances_dict = {instance_attr(inst): inst for inst in instances}
161         related_field = self.field.foreign_related_fields[0]
162         remote_field = self.field.remote_field
163 
164         # FIXME: This will need to be revisited when we introduce support for
165         # composite fields. In the meantime we take this practical approach to
166         # solve a regression on 1.6 when the reverse manager in hidden
167         # (related_name ends with a '+'). Refs #21410.
168         # The check for len(...) == 1 is a special case that allows the query
169         # to be join-less and smaller. Refs #21760.
170         if remote_field.is_hidden() or len(self.field.foreign_related_fields) == 1:
171             query = {
172                 "%s__in"
173                 % related_field.name: {instance_attr(inst)[0] for inst in instances}
174             }
175         else:
176             query = {"%s__in" % self.field.related_query_name(): instances}
177         queryset = queryset.filter(**query)
178 
179         # Since we're going to assign directly in the cache,
180         # we must manage the reverse relation cache manually.
181         if not remote_field.multiple:
182             for rel_obj in queryset:
183                 instance = instances_dict[rel_obj_attr(rel_obj)]
184                 remote_field.set_cached_value(rel_obj, instance)
185         return (
186             queryset,
187             rel_obj_attr,
188             instance_attr,
189             True,
190             self.field.get_cache_name(),
191             False,
192         )
193 
194     def get_object(self, instance):

196         # Assuming the database enforces foreign keys, this won't fail.
197         return qs.get(self.field.get_reverse_related_filter(instance))

199     def __get__(self, instance, cls=None):
200         """
201         Get the related instance through the forward relation.
202 
203         With the example above, when getting ``child.parent``:
204 
205         - ``self`` is the descriptor managing the ``parent`` attribute
206         - ``instance`` is the ``child`` instance
207         - ``cls`` is the ``Child`` class (we don't need it)
208         """
209         if instance is None:
210             return self
211 
212         # The related instance is loaded from the database and then cached
213         # by the field on the model instance state. It can also be pre-cached
214         # by the reverse accessor (ReverseOneToOneDescriptor).
215         try:
216             rel_obj = self.field.get_cached_value(instance)
217         except KeyError:
218             has_value = None not in self.field.get_local_related_value(instance)
219             ancestor_link = (
220                 instance._meta.get_ancestor_link(self.field.model)
221                 if has_value
222                 else None
223             )
224             if ancestor_link and ancestor_link.is_cached(instance):
225                 # An ancestor link will exist if this field is defined on a
226                 # multi-table inheritance parent of the instance's class.
227                 ancestor = ancestor_link.get_cached_value(instance)
228                 # The value might be cached on an ancestor if the instance
229                 # originated from walking down the inheritance chain.
230                 rel_obj = self.field.get_cached_value(ancestor, default=None)
231             else:
232                 rel_obj = None
233             if rel_obj is None and has_value:
234                 rel_obj = self.get_object(instance)
235                 remote_field = self.field.remote_field
236                 # If this is a one-to-one relation, set the reverse accessor
237                 # cache on the related object to the current instance to avoid
238                 # an extra SQL query if it's accessed later on.
239                 if not remote_field.multiple:
240                     remote_field.set_cached_value(rel_obj, instance)
241             self.field.set_cached_value(instance, rel_obj)
242 
243         if rel_obj is None and not self.field.null:
244             raise self.RelatedObjectDoesNotExist(
245                 "%s has no %s." % (self.field.model.__name__, self.field.name)
246             )
247         else:
248             return rel_obj
249 
250     def __set__(self, instance, value):
251         """
252         Set the related instance through the forward relation.
253 
254         With the example above, when setting ``child.parent = parent``:
255 
256         - ``self`` is the descriptor managing the ``parent`` attribute
257         - ``instance`` is the ``child`` instance
258         - ``value`` is the ``parent`` instance on the right of the equal sign
259         """
260         # An object must be an instance of the related class.
261         if value is not None and not isinstance(
262             value, self.field.remote_field.model._meta.concrete_model
263         ):
264             raise ValueError(
265                 'Cannot assign "%r": "%s.%s" must be a "%s" instance.'
266                 % (
267                     value,
268                     instance._meta.object_name,
269                     self.field.name,
270                     self.field.remote_field.model._meta.object_name,
271                 )
272             )
273         elif value is not None:
274             if instance._state.db is None:
275                 instance._state.db = router.db_for_write(
276                     instance.__class__, instance=value
277                 )
278             if value._state.db is None:
279                 value._state.db = router.db_for_write(
280                     value.__class__, instance=instance
281                 )
282             if not router.allow_relation(value, instance):
283                 raise ValueError(
284                     'Cannot assign "%r": the current database router prevents this '
285                     "relation." % value
286                 )
287 
288         remote_field = self.field.remote_field
289         # If we're setting the value of a OneToOneField to None, we need to clear
290         # out the cache on any old related object. Otherwise, deleting the
291         # previously-related object will also cause this object to be deleted,
292         # which is wrong.
293         if value is None:
294             # Look up the previously-related object, which may still be available
295             # since we've not yet cleared out the related field.
296             # Use the cache directly, instead of the accessor; if we haven't
297             # populated the cache, then we don't care - we're only accessing
298             # the object to invalidate the accessor cache, so there's no
299             # need to populate the cache just to expire it again.
300             related = self.field.get_cached_value(instance, default=None)
301 
302             # If we've got an old related object, we need to clear out its
303             # cache. This cache also might not exist if the related object
304             # hasn't been accessed yet.
305             if related is not None:
306                 remote_field.set_cached_value(related, None)
307 
308             for lh_field, rh_field in self.field.related_fields:
309                 setattr(instance, lh_field.attname, None)
310 
311         # Set the values of the related field.
312         else:
313             for lh_field, rh_field in self.field.related_fields:
314                 setattr(instance, lh_field.attname, getattr(value, rh_field.attname))
315 
316         # Set the related instance cache used by __get__ to avoid an SQL query
317         # when accessing the attribute we just set.
318         self.field.set_cached_value(instance, value)
319 
320         # If this is a one-to-one relation, set the reverse accessor cache on
321         # the related object to the current instance to avoid an extra SQL
322         # query if it's accessed later on.
323         if value is not None and not remote_field.multiple:
324             remote_field.set_cached_value(value, instance)
325 
326     def __reduce__(self):
327         """
328         Pickling should return the instance attached by self.field on the
329         model, not a new copy of that descriptor. Use getattr() to retrieve
330         the instance directly from the model.
331         """
332         return getattr, (self.field.model, self.field.name)

335 class ForwardOneToOneDescriptor(ForwardManyToOneDescriptor):
336     """
337     Accessor to the related object on the forward side of a one-to-one relation.
338 
339     In the example::
340 
341         class Restaurant(Model):
342             place = OneToOneField(Place, related_name='restaurant')
343 
344     ``Restaurant.place`` is a ``ForwardOneToOneDescriptor`` instance.
345     """
346 
347     def get_object(self, instance):
348         if self.field.remote_field.parent_link:
349             deferred = instance.get_deferred_fields()
350             # Because it's a parent link, all the data is available in the
351             # instance, so populate the parent model with this data.
352             rel_model = self.field.remote_field.model
353             fields = [field.attname for field in rel_model._meta.concrete_fields]
354 
355             # If any of the related model's fields are deferred, fallback to
356             # fetching all fields from the related model. This avoids a query
357             # on the related model for every deferred field.
358             if not any(field in fields for field in deferred):
359                 kwargs = {field: getattr(instance, field) for field in fields}
360                 obj = rel_model(**kwargs)
361                 obj._state.adding = instance._state.adding
362                 obj._state.db = instance._state.db
363                 return obj
364         return super().get_object(instance)
365 
366     def __set__(self, instance, value):
367         super().__set__(instance, value)
368         # If the primary key is a link to a parent model and a parent instance
369         # is being set, update the value of the inherited pk(s).
370         if self.field.primary_key and self.field.remote_field.parent_link:
371             opts = instance._meta
372             # Inherited primary key fields from this object's base classes.
373             inherited_pk_fields = [
374                 field
375                 for field in opts.concrete_fields
376                 if field.primary_key and field.remote_field
377             ]
378             for field in inherited_pk_fields:
379                 rel_model_pk_name = field.remote_field.model._meta.pk.attname
380                 raw_value = (
381                     getattr(value, rel_model_pk_name) if value is not None else None
382                 )
383                 setattr(instance, rel_model_pk_name, raw_value)
384

501         With the example above, when setting ``place.restaurant = restaurant``:

503         - ``self`` is the descriptor managing the ``restaurant`` attribute

513         if value is None:

531                     instance._meta.object_name,
532                     self.related.get_accessor_name(),
533                     self.related.related_model._meta.object_name,
534                 )
535             )

537             if instance._state.db is None:
538                 instance._state.db = router.db_for_write(
539                     instance.__class__, instance=value
540                 )
541             if value._state.db is None:
542                 value._state.db = router.db_for_write(
543                     value.__class__, instance=instance
544                 )

630 def create_reverse_many_to_one_manager(superclass, rel):
631     """
632     Create a manager for the reverse side of a many-to-one relation.
633 
634     This manager subclasses another manager, generally the default manager of
635     the related model, and adds behaviors specific to many-to-one relations.
636     """
637 
638     class RelatedManager(superclass, AltersData):
639         def __init__(self, instance):
640             super().__init__()
641 
642             self.instance = instance
643             self.model = rel.related_model
644             self.field = rel.field
645 
646             self.core_filters = {self.field.name: instance}
647 
648         def __call__(self, *, manager):
649             manager = getattr(self.model, manager)
650             manager_class = create_reverse_many_to_one_manager(manager.__class__, rel)
651             return manager_class(self.instance)
652 
653         do_not_call_in_templates = True
654 
655         def _check_fk_val(self):
656             for field in self.field.foreign_related_fields:
657                 if getattr(self.instance, field.attname) is None:
658                     raise ValueError(
659                         f'"{self.instance!r}" needs to have a value for field '
660                         f'"{field.attname}" before this relationship can be used.'
661                     )
662 
663         def _apply_rel_filters(self, queryset):
664             """
665             Filter the queryset for the instance this manager is bound to.
666             """
667             db = self._db or router.db_for_read(self.model, instance=self.instance)
668             empty_strings_as_null = connections[
669                 db
670             ].features.interprets_empty_strings_as_nulls
671             queryset._add_hints(instance=self.instance)
672             if self._db:
673                 queryset = queryset.using(self._db)
674             queryset._defer_next_filter = True
675             queryset = queryset.filter(**self.core_filters)
676             for field in self.field.foreign_related_fields:
677                 val = getattr(self.instance, field.attname)
678                 if val is None or (val == "" and empty_strings_as_null):
679                     return queryset.none()
680             if self.field.many_to_one:
681                 # Guard against field-like objects such as GenericRelation
682                 # that abuse create_reverse_many_to_one_manager() with reverse
683                 # one-to-many relationships instead and break known related
684                 # objects assignment.
685                 try:
686                     target_field = self.field.target_field
687                 except FieldError:
688                     # The relationship has multiple target fields. Use a tuple
689                     # for related object id.
690                     rel_obj_id = tuple(
691                         [
692                             getattr(self.instance, target_field.attname)
693                             for target_field in self.field.path_infos[-1].target_fields
694                         ]
695                     )
696                 else:
697                     rel_obj_id = getattr(self.instance, target_field.attname)
698                 queryset._known_related_objects = {
699                     self.field: {rel_obj_id: self.instance}
700                 }
701             return queryset
702 
703         def _remove_prefetched_objects(self):
704             try:
705                 self.instance._prefetched_objects_cache.pop(
706                     self.field.remote_field.get_cache_name()
707                 )
708             except (AttributeError, KeyError):
709                 pass  # nothing to clear from cache
710 
711         def get_queryset(self):
712             # Even if this relation is not to pk, we require still pk value.
713             # The wish is that the instance has been already saved to DB,
714             # although having a pk value isn't a guarantee of that.
715             if self.instance.pk is None:
716                 raise ValueError(
717                     f"{self.instance.__class__.__name__!r} instance needs to have a "
718                     f"primary key value before this relationship can be used."
719                 )
720             try:
721                 return self.instance._prefetched_objects_cache[
722                     self.field.remote_field.get_cache_name()
723                 ]
724             except (AttributeError, KeyError):
725                 queryset = super().get_queryset()
726                 return self._apply_rel_filters(queryset)
727 
728         def get_prefetch_queryset(self, instances, queryset=None):
729             if queryset is None:
730                 queryset = super().get_queryset()
731 
732             queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])
733             queryset = queryset.using(queryset._db or self._db)
734 
735             rel_obj_attr = self.field.get_local_related_value
736             instance_attr = self.field.get_foreign_related_value
737             instances_dict = {instance_attr(inst): inst for inst in instances}
738             queryset = _filter_prefetch_queryset(queryset, self.field.name, instances)
739 
740             # Since we just bypassed this class' get_queryset(), we must manage
741             # the reverse relation manually.
742             for rel_obj in queryset:
743                 if not self.field.is_cached(rel_obj):
744                     instance = instances_dict[rel_obj_attr(rel_obj)]
745                     setattr(rel_obj, self.field.name, instance)
746             cache_name = self.field.remote_field.get_cache_name()
747             return queryset, rel_obj_attr, instance_attr, False, cache_name, False
748 
749         def add(self, *objs, bulk=True):
750             self._check_fk_val()
751             self._remove_prefetched_objects()
752             db = router.db_for_write(self.model, instance=self.instance)
753 
754             def check_and_update_obj(obj):
755                 if not isinstance(obj, self.model):
756                     raise TypeError(
757                         "'%s' instance expected, got %r"
758                         % (
759                             self.model._meta.object_name,
760                             obj,
761                         )
762                     )
763                 setattr(obj, self.field.name, self.instance)
764 
765             if bulk:
766                 pks = []
767                 for obj in objs:
768                     check_and_update_obj(obj)
769                     if obj._state.adding or obj._state.db != db:
770                         raise ValueError(
771                             "%r instance isn't saved. Use bulk=False or save "
772                             "the object first." % obj
773                         )
774                     pks.append(obj.pk)
775                 self.model._base_manager.using(db).filter(pk__in=pks).update(
776                     **{
777                         self.field.name: self.instance,
778                     }
779                 )
780             else:
781                 with transaction.atomic(using=db, savepoint=False):
782                     for obj in objs:
783                         check_and_update_obj(obj)
784                         obj.save()
785 
786         add.alters_data = True
787 
788         def create(self, **kwargs):
789             self._check_fk_val()
790             kwargs[self.field.name] = self.instance
791             db = router.db_for_write(self.model, instance=self.instance)
792             return super(RelatedManager, self.db_manager(db)).create(**kwargs)
793 
794         create.alters_data = True
795

946     the related model, and adds behaviors specific to many-to-many relations.

958                 self.prefetch_cache_name = rel.field.name
959                 self.source_field_name = rel.field.m2m_field_name()
960                 self.target_field_name = rel.field.m2m_reverse_field_name()
961                 self.symmetrical = rel.symmetrical

963                 self.model = rel.related_model
964                 self.query_field_name = rel.field.name
965                 self.prefetch_cache_name = rel.field.related_query_name()
966                 self.source_field_name = rel.field.m2m_reverse_field_name()
967                 self.target_field_name = rel.field.m2m_field_name()

972

976             self.core_filters = {}

979                 core_filter_key = "%s__%s" % (self.query_field_name, rh_field.name)
980                 self.core_filters[core_filter_key] = getattr(instance, rh_field.attname)

996                     "a many-to-many relationship can be used."
997                     % instance.__class__.__name__

1009         def _build_remove_filters(self, removed_vals):

1020                     [(self.target_field_name, self.related_val)]

1024                         [(f"{self.source_field_name}__in", removed_vals)]

1283             # user-defined intermediary models as they could have other fields

1299                 can_ignore_conflicts,

1304         def _add_items(

1308             # target_field_name: the PK fieldname in join table for the target object

1311             if not objs:

1314             through_defaults = dict(resolve_callables(through_defaults or {}))

1316             db = router.db_for_write(self.through, instance=self.instance)
1317             can_ignore_conflicts, must_send_signals, can_fast_add = self._get_add_plan(
1318                 db, source_field_name
1319             )
1320             if can_fast_add:
1321                 self.through._default_manager.using(db).bulk_create(
1322                     [
1323                         self.through(
1324                             **{
1325                                 "%s_id" % source_field_name: self.related_val[0],
1326                                 "%s_id" % target_field_name: target_id,
1327                             }
1328                         )
1329                         for target_id in target_ids
1330                     ],
1331                     ignore_conflicts=True,
1332                 )

1335             missing_target_ids = self._get_missing_target_ids(
1336                 source_field_name, target_field_name, db, target_ids
1337             )

1339                 if must_send_signals:
1340                     signals.m2m_changed.send(
1341                         sender=self.through,
1342                         action="pre_add",
1343                         instance=self.instance,
1344                         reverse=self.reverse,
1345                         model=self.model,
1346                         pk_set=missing_target_ids,
1347                         using=db,
1348                     )

1350                 self.through._default_manager.using(db).bulk_create(
1351                     [
1352                         self.through(
1353                             **through_defaults,
1354                             **{
1355                                 "%s_id" % source_field_name: self.related_val[0],
1356                                 "%s_id" % target_field_name: target_id,
1357                             },
1358                         )

1360                     ],
1361                     ignore_conflicts=can_ignore_conflicts,
1362                 )
1363 
1364                 if must_send_signals:
1365                     signals.m2m_changed.send(
1366                         sender=self.through,
1367                         action="post_add",
1368                         instance=self.instance,
1369                         reverse=self.reverse,
1370                         model=self.model,
1371                         pk_set=missing_target_ids,
1372                         using=db,
1373                     )

1375         def _remove_items(self, source_field_name, target_field_name, *objs):
1376             # source_field_name: the PK colname in join table for the source object
1377             # target_field_name: the PK colname in join table for the target object
1378             # *objs - objects to remove. Either object instances, or primary
1379             # keys of object instances.
1380             if not objs:
1381                 return

1387                     fk_val = self.target_field.get_foreign_related_value(obj)[0]

1390                     old_ids.add(obj)
1391 
1392             db = router.db_for_write(self.through, instance=self.instance)
1393             with transaction.atomic(using=db, savepoint=False):
1394                 # Send a signal to the other end if need be.
1395                 signals.m2m_changed.send(
1396                     sender=self.through,
1397                     action="pre_remove",
1398                     instance=self.instance,
1399                     reverse=self.reverse,
1400                     model=self.model,
1401                     pk_set=old_ids,

1407                         **{"%s__in" % self.target_field.target_field.attname: old_ids}
1408                     )

569     def aggregate(self, *args, **kwargs):
570         """
571         Return a dictionary containing the calculations (aggregation)
572         over the current queryset.
573 
574         If args is present the expression is passed as a kwarg using
575         the Aggregate object's default alias.
576         """
577         if self.query.distinct_fields:
578             raise NotImplementedError("aggregate() + distinct(fields) not implemented.")
579         self._validate_values_are_expressions(
580             (*args, *kwargs.values()), method_name="aggregate"
581         )
582         for arg in args:
583             # The default_alias property raises TypeError if default_alias
584             # can't be set automatically or AttributeError if it isn't an
585             # attribute.
586             try:
587                 arg.default_alias
588             except (AttributeError, TypeError):
589                 raise TypeError("Complex aggregates require an alias")
590             kwargs[arg.default_alias] = arg
591 
592         query = self.query.chain()
593         for (alias, aggregate_expr) in kwargs.items():
594             query.add_annotation(aggregate_expr, alias, is_summary=True)
595             annotation = query.annotations[alias]
596             if not annotation.contains_aggregate:
597                 raise TypeError("%s is not an aggregate expression" % alias)
598             for expr in annotation.get_source_expressions():
599                 if (
600                     expr.contains_aggregate
601                     and isinstance(expr, Ref)
602                     and expr.refs in kwargs
603                 ):
604                     name = expr.refs
605                     raise exceptions.FieldError(
606                         "Cannot compute %s('%s'): '%s' is an aggregate"
607                         % (annotation.name, name, name)
608                     )
609         return query.get_aggregation(self.db, kwargs)

633         keyword arguments.

637                 "Calling QuerySet.get(...) with filters after %s() is not "
638                 "supported." % self.query.combinator

688     def _check_bulk_create_options(
689         self, ignore_conflicts, update_conflicts, update_fields, unique_fields
690     ):
691         if ignore_conflicts and update_conflicts:
692             raise ValueError(
693                 "ignore_conflicts and update_conflicts are mutually exclusive."
694             )
695         db_features = connections[self.db].features
696         if ignore_conflicts:
697             if not db_features.supports_ignore_conflicts:
698                 raise NotSupportedError(
699                     "This database backend does not support ignoring conflicts."
700                 )
701             return OnConflict.IGNORE
702         elif update_conflicts:
703             if not db_features.supports_update_conflicts:
704                 raise NotSupportedError(
705                     "This database backend does not support updating conflicts."
706                 )
707             if not update_fields:
708                 raise ValueError(
709                     "Fields that will be updated when a row insertion fails "
710                     "on conflicts must be provided."
711                 )
712             if unique_fields and not db_features.supports_update_conflicts_with_target:
713                 raise NotSupportedError(
714                     "This database backend does not support updating "
715                     "conflicts with specifying unique fields that can trigger "
716                     "the upsert."
717                 )
718             if not unique_fields and db_features.supports_update_conflicts_with_target:
719                 raise ValueError(
720                     "Unique fields that can trigger the upsert must be provided."
721                 )
722             # Updating primary keys and non-concrete fields is forbidden.
723             update_fields = [self.model._meta.get_field(name) for name in update_fields]
724             if any(not f.concrete or f.many_to_many for f in update_fields):
725                 raise ValueError(
726                     "bulk_create() can only be used with concrete fields in "
727                     "update_fields."
728                 )
729             if any(f.primary_key for f in update_fields):
730                 raise ValueError(
731                     "bulk_create() cannot be used with primary keys in "
732                     "update_fields."
733                 )
734             if unique_fields:
735                 unique_fields = [
736                     self.model._meta.get_field(name) for name in unique_fields
737                 ]
738                 if any(not f.concrete or f.many_to_many for f in unique_fields):
739                     raise ValueError(
740                         "bulk_create() can only be used with concrete fields "
741                         "in unique_fields."
742                     )
743             return OnConflict.UPDATE
744         return None
745 
746     def bulk_create(
747         self,
748         objs,
749         batch_size=None,
750         ignore_conflicts=False,
751         update_conflicts=False,
752         update_fields=None,
753         unique_fields=None,
754     ):
755         """
756         Insert each of the instances into the database. Do *not* call
757         save() on each of the instances, do not send any pre/post_save
758         signals, and do not set the primary key attribute if it is an
759         autoincrement field (except if features.can_return_rows_from_bulk_insert=True).
760         Multi-table models are not supported.
761         """
762         # When you bulk insert you don't get the primary keys back (if it's an
763         # autoincrement, except if can_return_rows_from_bulk_insert=True), so
764         # you can't insert into the child tables which references this. There
765         # are two workarounds:
766         # 1) This could be implemented if you didn't have an autoincrement pk
767         # 2) You could do it by doing O(n) normal inserts into the parent
768         #    tables to get the primary keys back and then doing a single bulk
769         #    insert into the childmost table.
770         # We currently set the primary keys on the objects when using
771         # PostgreSQL via the RETURNING ID clause. It should be possible for
772         # Oracle as well, but the semantics for extracting the primary keys is
773         # trickier so it's not done yet.
774         if batch_size is not None and batch_size <= 0:
775             raise ValueError("Batch size must be a positive integer.")
776         # Check that the parents share the same concrete model with the our
777         # model to detect the inheritance pattern ConcreteGrandParent ->
778         # MultiTableParent -> ProxyChild. Simply checking self.model._meta.proxy
779         # would not identify that case as involving multiple tables.
780         for parent in self.model._meta.get_parent_list():
781             if parent._meta.concrete_model is not self.model._meta.concrete_model:
782                 raise ValueError("Can't bulk create a multi-table inherited model")
783         if not objs:
784             return objs
785         opts = self.model._meta
786         if unique_fields:
787             # Primary key is allowed in unique_fields.
788             unique_fields = [
789                 opts.pk.name if name == "pk" else name for name in unique_fields
790             ]
791         on_conflict = self._check_bulk_create_options(
792             ignore_conflicts,
793             update_conflicts,
794             update_fields,
795             unique_fields,
796         )
797         self._for_write = True
798         fields = opts.concrete_fields
799         objs = list(objs)
800         self._prepare_for_bulk_create(objs)
801         with transaction.atomic(using=self.db, savepoint=False):
802             objs_with_pk, objs_without_pk = partition(lambda o: o.pk is None, objs)
803             if objs_with_pk:
804                 returned_columns = self._batched_insert(
805                     objs_with_pk,
806                     fields,
807                     batch_size,
808                     on_conflict=on_conflict,
809                     update_fields=update_fields,
810                     unique_fields=unique_fields,
811                 )
812                 for obj_with_pk, results in zip(objs_with_pk, returned_columns):
813                     for result, field in zip(results, opts.db_returning_fields):
814                         if field != opts.pk:
815                             setattr(obj_with_pk, field.attname, result)
816                 for obj_with_pk in objs_with_pk:
817                     obj_with_pk._state.adding = False
818                     obj_with_pk._state.db = self.db
819             if objs_without_pk:
820                 fields = [f for f in fields if not isinstance(f, AutoField)]
821                 returned_columns = self._batched_insert(
822                     objs_without_pk,
823                     fields,
824                     batch_size,
825                     on_conflict=on_conflict,
826                     update_fields=update_fields,
827                     unique_fields=unique_fields,
828                 )
829                 connection = connections[self.db]
830                 if (
831                     connection.features.can_return_rows_from_bulk_insert
832                     and on_conflict is None
833                 ):
834                     assert len(returned_columns) == len(objs_without_pk)
835                 for obj_without_pk, results in zip(objs_without_pk, returned_columns):
836                     for result, field in zip(results, opts.db_returning_fields):
837                         setattr(obj_without_pk, field.attname, result)
838                     obj_without_pk._state.adding = False
839                     obj_without_pk._state.db = self.db
840 
841         return objs
842
