393     def margins(self, *margins, x=None, y=None, z=None, tight=True):
394         """
395         Convenience method to set or retrieve autoscaling margins.
396 
397         signatures::
398             margins()
399 
400         returns xmargin, ymargin, zmargin
401 
402         ::
403 
404             margins(margin)
405 
406             margins(xmargin, ymargin, zmargin)
407 
408             margins(x=xmargin, y=ymargin, z=zmargin)
409 
410             margins(..., tight=False)
411 
412         All forms above set the xmargin, ymargin and zmargin
413         parameters. All keyword parameters are optional.  A single
414         positional argument specifies xmargin, ymargin and zmargin.
415         Passing both positional and keyword arguments for xmargin,
416         ymargin, and/or zmargin is invalid.
417 
418         The *tight* parameter
419         is passed to :meth:`autoscale_view`, which is executed after
420         a margin is changed; the default here is *True*, on the
421         assumption that when margins are specified, no additional
422         padding to match tick marks is usually desired.  Setting
423         *tight* to *None* will preserve the previous setting.
424 
425         Specifying any margin changes only the autoscaling; for example,
426         if *xmargin* is not None, then *xmargin* times the X data
427         interval will be added to each end of that interval before
428         it is used in autoscaling.
429 
430         .. versionadded :: 1.1.0
431             This function was added, but not tested. Please report any bugs.
432         """
433         if margins and x is not None and y is not None and z is not None:
434             raise TypeError('Cannot pass both positional and keyword '
435                             'arguments for x, y, and/or z.')
436         elif len(margins) == 1:
437             x = y = z = margins[0]
438         elif len(margins) == 3:
439             x, y, z = margins
440         elif margins:
441             raise TypeError('Must pass a single positional argument for all '
442                             'margins, or one for each margin (x, y, z).')
443 
444         if x is None and y is None and z is None:
445             if tight is not True:
446                 cbook._warn_external(f'ignoring tight={tight!r} in get mode')
447             return self._xmargin, self._ymargin, self._zmargin
448 
449         if x is not None:
450             self.set_xmargin(x)
451         if y is not None:
452             self.set_ymargin(y)
453         if z is not None:
454             self.set_zmargin(z)
455 
456         self.autoscale_view(
457             tight=tight, scalex=(x is not None), scaley=(y is not None),
458             scalez=(z is not None)
459         )
460

492     def auto_scale_xyz(self, X, Y, Z=None, had_data=None):
493         # This updates the bounding boxes as to keep a record as to what the
494         # minimum sized rectangular volume holds the data.
495         X = np.reshape(X, -1)
496         Y = np.reshape(Y, -1)
497         self.xy_dataLim.update_from_data_xy(
498             np.column_stack([X, Y]), not had_data)
499         if Z is not None:
500             Z = np.reshape(Z, -1)
501             self.zz_dataLim.update_from_data_xy(
502                 np.column_stack([Z, Z]), not had_data)
503         # Let autoscale_view figure out how to use this data.
504         self.autoscale_view()

506     def autoscale_view(self, tight=None, scalex=True, scaley=True,
507                              scalez=True):
508         """
509         Autoscale the view limits using the data limits.
510         See :meth:`matplotlib.axes.Axes.autoscale_view` for documentation.
511         Note that this function applies to the 3D axes, and as such
512         adds the *scalez* to the function arguments.
513 
514         .. versionchanged :: 1.1.0
515             Function signature was changed to better match the 2D version.
516             *tight* is now explicitly a kwarg and placed first.
517 
518         .. versionchanged :: 1.2.1
519             This is now fully functional.
520 
521         """
522         if not self._ready:
523             return
524 
525         # This method looks at the rectangular volume (see above)
526         # of data and decides how to scale the view portal to fit it.
527         if tight is None:
528             # if image data only just use the datalim
529             _tight = self._tight or (
530                 len(self.images) > 0
531                 and len(self.lines) == len(self.patches) == 0)
532         else:
533             _tight = self._tight = bool(tight)
534 
535         if scalex and self._autoscaleXon:
536             self._shared_x_axes.clean()
537             x0, x1 = self.xy_dataLim.intervalx
538             xlocator = self.xaxis.get_major_locator()
539             x0, x1 = xlocator.nonsingular(x0, x1)
540             if self._xmargin > 0:
541                 delta = (x1 - x0) * self._xmargin
542                 x0 -= delta
543                 x1 += delta
544             if not _tight:
545                 x0, x1 = xlocator.view_limits(x0, x1)
546             self.set_xbound(x0, x1)
547 
548         if scaley and self._autoscaleYon:
549             self._shared_y_axes.clean()
550             y0, y1 = self.xy_dataLim.intervaly
551             ylocator = self.yaxis.get_major_locator()
552             y0, y1 = ylocator.nonsingular(y0, y1)
553             if self._ymargin > 0:
554                 delta = (y1 - y0) * self._ymargin
555                 y0 -= delta
556                 y1 += delta
557             if not _tight:
558                 y0, y1 = ylocator.view_limits(y0, y1)
559             self.set_ybound(y0, y1)
560 
561         if scalez and self._autoscaleZon:
562             self._shared_z_axes.clean()
563             z0, z1 = self.zz_dataLim.intervalx
564             zlocator = self.zaxis.get_major_locator()
565             z0, z1 = zlocator.nonsingular(z0, z1)
566             if self._zmargin > 0:
567                 delta = (z1 - z0) * self._zmargin
568                 z0 -= delta
569                 z1 += delta
570             if not _tight:
571                 z0, z1 = zlocator.view_limits(z0, z1)
572             self.set_zbound(z0, z1)
573

589     def set_xlim3d(self, left=None, right=None, emit=True, auto=False,
590                    *, xmin=None, xmax=None):
591         """
592         Set 3D x limits.
593 
594         See :meth:`matplotlib.axes.Axes.set_xlim` for full documentation.
595 
596         """
597         if right is None and np.iterable(left):
598             left, right = left
599         if xmin is not None:
600             cbook.warn_deprecated('3.0', name='`xmin`',
601                                   alternative='`left`', obj_type='argument')
602             if left is not None:
603                 raise TypeError('Cannot pass both `xmin` and `left`')
604             left = xmin
605         if xmax is not None:
606             cbook.warn_deprecated('3.0', name='`xmax`',
607                                   alternative='`right`', obj_type='argument')
608             if right is not None:
609                 raise TypeError('Cannot pass both `xmax` and `right`')
610             right = xmax
611 
612         self._process_unit_info(xdata=(left, right))
613         left = self._validate_converted_limits(left, self.convert_xunits)
614         right = self._validate_converted_limits(right, self.convert_xunits)
615 
616         old_left, old_right = self.get_xlim()
617         if left is None:
618             left = old_left
619         if right is None:
620             right = old_right
621 
622         if left == right:
623             cbook._warn_external(
624                 f"Attempting to set identical left == right == {left} results "
625                 f"in singular transformations; automatically expanding.")
626         left, right = self.xaxis.get_major_locator().nonsingular(left, right)
627         left, right = self.xaxis.limit_range_for_scale(left, right)
628         self.xy_viewLim.intervalx = (left, right)
629 
630         if auto is not None:
631             self._autoscaleXon = bool(auto)
632 
633         if emit:
634             self.callbacks.process('xlim_changed', self)
635             # Call all of the other x-axes that are shared with this one
636             for other in self._shared_x_axes.get_siblings(self):
637                 if other is not self:
638                     other.set_xlim(self.xy_viewLim.intervalx,
639                                             emit=False, auto=auto)
640                     if other.figure != self.figure:
641                         other.figure.canvas.draw_idle()
642         self.stale = True
643         return left, right
644     set_xlim = set_xlim3d

704     def set_zlim3d(self, bottom=None, top=None, emit=True, auto=False,

706         """
707         Set 3D z limits.
708 
709         See :meth:`matplotlib.axes.Axes.set_ylim` for full documentation
710 
711         """
712         if top is None and np.iterable(bottom):
713             bottom, top = bottom
714         if zmin is not None:
715             cbook.warn_deprecated('3.0', name='`zmin`',
716                                   alternative='`bottom`', obj_type='argument')
717             if bottom is not None:
718                 raise TypeError('Cannot pass both `zmin` and `bottom`')
719             bottom = zmin

722                                   alternative='`top`', obj_type='argument')
723             if top is not None:

728         bottom = self._validate_converted_limits(bottom, self.convert_zunits)
729         top = self._validate_converted_limits(top, self.convert_zunits)
730 
731         old_bottom, old_top = self.get_zlim()
732         if bottom is None:
733             bottom = old_bottom
734         if top is None:
735             top = old_top
736 
737         if bottom == top:

739                 f"Attempting to set identical bottom == top == {bottom} "
740                 f"results in singular transformations; automatically "
741                 f"expanding.")
742         bottom, top = self.zaxis.get_major_locator().nonsingular(bottom, top)

746         if auto is not None:

748 
749         if emit:
750             self.callbacks.process('zlim_changed', self)
751             # Call all of the other y-axes that are shared with this one
752             for other in self._shared_z_axes.get_siblings(self):

755                                             emit=False, auto=auto)

986         ----------

989 
990         """
991         if proj_type == 'persp':
992             self._projection = proj3d.persp_transformation

998     def get_proj(self):
999         """
1000         Create the projection matrix from the current viewing position.
1001 
1002         elev stores the elevation angle in the z plane
1003         azim stores the azimuth angle in the x,y plane
1004 
1005         dist is the distance of the eye viewing point from the object
1006         point.
1007 
1008         """
1009         relev, razim = np.pi * self.elev/180, np.pi * self.azim/180
1010 
1011         xmin, xmax = self.get_xlim3d()
1012         ymin, ymax = self.get_ylim3d()
1013         zmin, zmax = self.get_zlim3d()
1014 
1015         # transform to uniform world coordinates 0-1.0,0-1.0,0-1.0
1016         worldM = proj3d.world_transformation(xmin, xmax,
1017                                              ymin, ymax,
1018                                              zmin, zmax)
1019 
1020         # look into the middle of the new coordinates
1021         R = np.array([0.5, 0.5, 0.5])
1022 
1023         xp = R[0] + np.cos(razim) * np.cos(relev) * self.dist
1024         yp = R[1] + np.sin(razim) * np.cos(relev) * self.dist
1025         zp = R[2] + np.sin(relev) * self.dist
1026         E = np.array((xp, yp, zp))
1027 
1028         self.eye = E
1029         self.vvec = R - E
1030         self.vvec = self.vvec / np.linalg.norm(self.vvec)
1031 
1032         if abs(relev) > np.pi/2:
1033             # upside down
1034             V = np.array((0, 0, -1))
1035         else:
1036             V = np.array((0, 0, 1))
1037         zfront, zback = -self.dist, self.dist
1038 
1039         viewM = proj3d.view_transformation(E, R, V)
1040         projM = self._projection(zfront, zback)
1041         M0 = np.dot(viewM, worldM)
1042         M = np.dot(projM, M0)
1043         return M
1044

1148     def format_coord(self, xd, yd):
1149         """
1150         Given the 2D view coordinates attempt to guess a 3D coordinate.
1151         Looks for the nearest edge to the point and then assumes that
1152         the point is at the same z location as the nearest point on the edge.
1153         """
1154 
1155         if self.M is None:
1156             return ''
1157 
1158         if self.button_pressed in self._rotate_btn:
1159             return 'azimuth={:.0f} deg, elevation={:.0f} deg '.format(
1160                 self.azim, self.elev)
1161             # ignore xd and yd and display angles instead
1162 
1163         # nearest edge
1164         p0, p1 = min(self.tunit_edges(),
1165                      key=lambda edge: proj3d._line2d_seg_dist(
1166                          edge[0], edge[1], (xd, yd)))
1167 
1168         # scale the z value to match
1169         x0, y0, z0 = p0
1170         x1, y1, z1 = p1
1171         d0 = np.hypot(x0-xd, y0-yd)
1172         d1 = np.hypot(x1-xd, y1-yd)
1173         dt = d0+d1
1174         z = d1/dt * z0 + d0/dt * z1
1175 
1176         x, y, z = proj3d.inv_transform(xd, yd, z, self.M)
1177 
1178         xs = self.format_xdata(x)
1179         ys = self.format_ydata(y)
1180         zs = self.format_zdata(z)
1181         return 'x=%s, y=%s, z=%s' % (xs, ys, zs)

1183     def _on_move(self, event):
1184         """Mouse moving
1185 
1186         button-1 rotates by default.  Can be set explicitly in mouse_init().
1187         button-3 zooms by default.  Can be set explicitly in mouse_init().
1188         """
1189 
1190         if not self.button_pressed:
1191             return
1192 
1193         if self.M is None:
1194             return
1195 
1196         x, y = event.xdata, event.ydata
1197         # In case the mouse is out of bounds.
1198         if x is None:
1199             return
1200 
1201         dx, dy = x - self.sx, y - self.sy
1202         w = self._pseudo_w
1203         h = self._pseudo_h
1204         self.sx, self.sy = x, y
1205 
1206         # Rotation
1207         if self.button_pressed in self._rotate_btn:
1208             # rotate viewing point
1209             # get the x and y pixel coords
1210             if dx == 0 and dy == 0:
1211                 return
1212             self.elev = art3d._norm_angle(self.elev - (dy/h)*180)
1213             self.azim = art3d._norm_angle(self.azim - (dx/w)*180)
1214             self.get_proj()
1215             self.stale = True
1216             self.figure.canvas.draw_idle()
1217 
1218 #        elif self.button_pressed == 2:
1219             # pan view
1220             # project xv,yv,zv -> xw,yw,zw
1221             # pan
1222 #            pass
1223 
1224         # Zoom
1225         elif self.button_pressed in self._zoom_btn:
1226             # zoom view
1227             # hmmm..this needs some help from clipping....
1228             minx, maxx, miny, maxy, minz, maxz = self.get_w_lims()
1229             df = 1-((h - dy)/h)
1230             dx = (maxx-minx)*df
1231             dy = (maxy-miny)*df
1232             dz = (maxz-minz)*df
1233             self.set_xlim3d(minx - dx, maxx + dx)
1234             self.set_ylim3d(miny - dy, maxy + dy)
1235             self.set_zlim3d(minz - dz, maxz + dz)
1236             self.get_proj()
1237             self.figure.canvas.draw_idle()

1542     def plot_surface(self, X, Y, Z, *args, norm=None, vmin=None,
1543                      vmax=None, lightsource=None, **kwargs):
1544         """
1545         Create a surface plot.
1546 
1547         By default it will be colored in shades of a solid color, but it also
1548         supports color mapping by supplying the *cmap* argument.
1549 
1550         .. note::
1551 
1552            The *rcount* and *ccount* kwargs, which both default to 50,
1553            determine the maximum number of samples used in each direction.  If
1554            the input data is larger, it will be downsampled (by slicing) to
1555            these numbers of points.
1556 
1557         Parameters
1558         ----------
1559         X, Y, Z : 2d arrays
1560             Data values.
1561 
1562         rcount, ccount : int
1563             Maximum number of samples used in each direction.  If the input
1564             data is larger, it will be downsampled (by slicing) to these
1565             numbers of points.  Defaults to 50.
1566 
1567             .. versionadded:: 2.0
1568 
1569         rstride, cstride : int
1570             Downsampling stride in each direction.  These arguments are
1571             mutually exclusive with *rcount* and *ccount*.  If only one of
1572             *rstride* or *cstride* is set, the other defaults to 10.
1573 
1574             'classic' mode uses a default of ``rstride = cstride = 10`` instead
1575             of the new default of ``rcount = ccount = 50``.
1576 
1577         color : color-like
1578             Color of the surface patches.
1579 
1580         cmap : Colormap
1581             Colormap of the surface patches.
1582 
1583         facecolors : array-like of colors.
1584             Colors of each individual patch.
1585 
1586         norm : Normalize
1587             Normalization for the colormap.
1588 
1589         vmin, vmax : float
1590             Bounds for the normalization.
1591 
1592         shade : bool
1593             Whether to shade the facecolors. Defaults to True. Shading is
1594             always disabled when `cmap` is specified.
1595 
1596         lightsource : `~matplotlib.colors.LightSource`
1597             The lightsource to use when `shade` is True.
1598 
1599         **kwargs
1600             Other arguments are forwarded to `.Poly3DCollection`.
1601         """
1602 
1603         had_data = self.has_data()
1604 
1605         if Z.ndim != 2:
1606             raise ValueError("Argument Z must be 2-dimensional.")
1607         if np.any(np.isnan(Z)):
1608             cbook._warn_external(
1609                 "Z contains NaN values. This may result in rendering "
1610                 "artifacts.")
1611 
1612         # TODO: Support masked arrays
1613         X, Y, Z = np.broadcast_arrays(X, Y, Z)
1614         rows, cols = Z.shape
1615 
1616         has_stride = 'rstride' in kwargs or 'cstride' in kwargs
1617         has_count = 'rcount' in kwargs or 'ccount' in kwargs
1618 
1619         if has_stride and has_count:
1620             raise ValueError("Cannot specify both stride and count arguments")
1621 
1622         rstride = kwargs.pop('rstride', 10)
1623         cstride = kwargs.pop('cstride', 10)
1624         rcount = kwargs.pop('rcount', 50)
1625         ccount = kwargs.pop('ccount', 50)
1626 
1627         if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']:
1628             # Strides have priority over counts in classic mode.
1629             # So, only compute strides from counts
1630             # if counts were explicitly given
1631             compute_strides = has_count
1632         else:
1633             # If the strides are provided then it has priority.
1634             # Otherwise, compute the strides from the counts.
1635             compute_strides = not has_stride
1636 
1637         if compute_strides:
1638             rstride = int(max(np.ceil(rows / rcount), 1))
1639             cstride = int(max(np.ceil(cols / ccount), 1))
1640 
1641         if 'facecolors' in kwargs:
1642             fcolors = kwargs.pop('facecolors')
1643         else:
1644             color = kwargs.pop('color', None)
1645             if color is None:
1646                 color = self._get_lines.get_next_color()
1647             color = np.array(mcolors.to_rgba(color))
1648             fcolors = None
1649 
1650         cmap = kwargs.get('cmap', None)
1651         shade = kwargs.pop('shade', cmap is None)
1652         if shade is None:
1653             cbook.warn_deprecated(
1654                 "3.1",
1655                 message="Passing shade=None to Axes3D.plot_surface() is "
1656                         "deprecated since matplotlib 3.1 and will change its "
1657                         "semantic or raise an error in matplotlib 3.3. "
1658                         "Please use shade=False instead.")
1659 
1660         # evenly spaced, and including both endpoints
1661         row_inds = list(range(0, rows-1, rstride)) + [rows-1]
1662         col_inds = list(range(0, cols-1, cstride)) + [cols-1]
1663 
1664         colset = []  # the sampled facecolor
1665         polys = []
1666         for rs, rs_next in zip(row_inds[:-1], row_inds[1:]):
1667             for cs, cs_next in zip(col_inds[:-1], col_inds[1:]):
1668                 ps = [
1669                     # +1 ensures we share edges between polygons
1670                     cbook._array_perimeter(a[rs:rs_next+1, cs:cs_next+1])
1671                     for a in (X, Y, Z)
1672                 ]
1673                 # ps = np.stack(ps, axis=-1)
1674                 ps = np.array(ps).T
1675                 polys.append(ps)
1676 
1677                 if fcolors is not None:
1678                     colset.append(fcolors[rs][cs])
1679 
1680         # note that the striding causes some polygons to have more coordinates
1681         # than others
1682         polyc = art3d.Poly3DCollection(polys, *args, **kwargs)
1683 
1684         if fcolors is not None:
1685             if shade:
1686                 colset = self._shade_colors(
1687                     colset, self._generate_normals(polys), lightsource)
1688             polyc.set_facecolors(colset)
1689             polyc.set_edgecolors(colset)
1690         elif cmap:
1691             # doesn't vectorize because polys is jagged
1692             avg_z = np.array([ps[:, 2].mean() for ps in polys])
1693             polyc.set_array(avg_z)
1694             if vmin is not None or vmax is not None:
1695                 polyc.set_clim(vmin, vmax)
1696             if norm is not None:
1697                 polyc.set_norm(norm)
1698         else:
1699             if shade:
1700                 colset = self._shade_colors(
1701                     color, self._generate_normals(polys), lightsource)
1702             else:
1703                 colset = color
1704             polyc.set_facecolors(colset)
1705 
1706         self.add_collection(polyc)
1707         self.auto_scale_xyz(X, Y, Z, had_data)
1708 
1709         return polyc
1710 
1711     def _generate_normals(self, polygons):
1712         """
1713         Takes a list of polygons and return an array of their normals.
1714 
1715         Normals point towards the viewer for a face with its vertices in
1716         counterclockwise order, following the right hand rule.
1717 
1718         Uses three points equally spaced around the polygon.
1719         This normal of course might not make sense for polygons with more than
1720         three points not lying in a plane, but it's a plausible and fast
1721         approximation.
1722 
1723         Parameters
1724         ----------
1725         polygons: list of (M_i, 3) array_like, or (..., M, 3) array_like
1726             A sequence of polygons to compute normals for, which can have
1727             varying numbers of vertices. If the polygons all have the same
1728             number of vertices and array is passed, then the operation will
1729             be vectorized.
1730 
1731         Returns
1732         -------
1733         normals: (..., 3) array_like
1734             A normal vector estimated for the polygon.
1735 
1736         """
1737         if isinstance(polygons, np.ndarray):
1738             # optimization: polygons all have the same number of points, so can
1739             # vectorize
1740             n = polygons.shape[-2]
1741             i1, i2, i3 = 0, n//3, 2*n//3
1742             v1 = polygons[..., i1, :] - polygons[..., i2, :]
1743             v2 = polygons[..., i2, :] - polygons[..., i3, :]
1744         else:
1745             # The subtraction doesn't vectorize because polygons is jagged.
1746             v1 = np.empty((len(polygons), 3))
1747             v2 = np.empty((len(polygons), 3))
1748             for poly_i, ps in enumerate(polygons):
1749                 n = len(ps)
1750                 i1, i2, i3 = 0, n//3, 2*n//3
1751                 v1[poly_i, :] = ps[i1, :] - ps[i2, :]
1752                 v2[poly_i, :] = ps[i2, :] - ps[i3, :]
1753         return np.cross(v1, v2)
1754 
1755     def _shade_colors(self, color, normals, lightsource=None):
1756         """
1757         Shade *color* using normal vectors given by *normals*.
1758         *color* can also be an array of the same length as *normals*.
1759         """
1760         if lightsource is None:
1761             # chosen for backwards-compatibility
1762             lightsource = LightSource(azdeg=225, altdeg=19.4712)
1763 
1764         with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
1765             shade = ((normals / np.linalg.norm(normals, axis=1, keepdims=True))
1766                      @ lightsource.direction)
1767         mask = ~np.isnan(shade)
1768 
1769         if mask.any():
1770             # convert dot product to allowed shading fractions
1771             in_norm = Normalize(-1, 1)
1772             out_norm = Normalize(0.3, 1).inverse
1773 
1774             def norm(x):
1775                 return out_norm(in_norm(x))
1776 
1777             shade[~mask] = 0
1778 
1779             color = mcolors.to_rgba_array(color)
1780             # shape of color should be (M, 4) (where M is number of faces)
1781             # shape of shade should be (M,)
1782             # colors should have final shape of (M, 4)
1783             alpha = color[:, 3]
1784             colors = norm(shade)[:, np.newaxis] * color
1785             colors[:, 3] = alpha
1786         else:
1787             colors = np.asanyarray(color).copy()
1788 
1789         return colors
1790 
1791     def plot_wireframe(self, X, Y, Z, *args, **kwargs):
1792         """
1793         Plot a 3D wireframe.
1794 
1795         .. note::
1796 
1797            The *rcount* and *ccount* kwargs, which both default to 50,
1798            determine the maximum number of samples used in each direction.  If
1799            the input data is larger, it will be downsampled (by slicing) to
1800            these numbers of points.
1801 
1802         Parameters
1803         ----------
1804         X, Y, Z : 2d arrays
1805             Data values.
1806 
1807         rcount, ccount : int
1808             Maximum number of samples used in each direction.  If the input
1809             data is larger, it will be downsampled (by slicing) to these
1810             numbers of points.  Setting a count to zero causes the data to be
1811             not sampled in the corresponding direction, producing a 3D line
1812             plot rather than a wireframe plot.  Defaults to 50.
1813 
1814             .. versionadded:: 2.0
1815 
1816         rstride, cstride : int
1817             Downsampling stride in each direction.  These arguments are
1818             mutually exclusive with *rcount* and *ccount*.  If only one of
1819             *rstride* or *cstride* is set, the other defaults to 1.  Setting a
1820             stride to zero causes the data to be not sampled in the
1821             corresponding direction, producing a 3D line plot rather than a
1822             wireframe plot.
1823 
1824             'classic' mode uses a default of ``rstride = cstride = 1`` instead
1825             of the new default of ``rcount = ccount = 50``.
1826 
1827         **kwargs
1828             Other arguments are forwarded to `.Line3DCollection`.
1829         """
1830 
1831         had_data = self.has_data()
1832         if Z.ndim != 2:
1833             raise ValueError("Argument Z must be 2-dimensional.")
1834         # FIXME: Support masked arrays
1835         X, Y, Z = np.broadcast_arrays(X, Y, Z)
1836         rows, cols = Z.shape
1837 
1838         has_stride = 'rstride' in kwargs or 'cstride' in kwargs
1839         has_count = 'rcount' in kwargs or 'ccount' in kwargs
1840 
1841         if has_stride and has_count:
1842             raise ValueError("Cannot specify both stride and count arguments")
1843 
1844         rstride = kwargs.pop('rstride', 1)
1845         cstride = kwargs.pop('cstride', 1)
1846         rcount = kwargs.pop('rcount', 50)
1847         ccount = kwargs.pop('ccount', 50)
1848 
1849         if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']:
1850             # Strides have priority over counts in classic mode.
1851             # So, only compute strides from counts
1852             # if counts were explicitly given
1853             if has_count:
1854                 rstride = int(max(np.ceil(rows / rcount), 1)) if rcount else 0
1855                 cstride = int(max(np.ceil(cols / ccount), 1)) if ccount else 0
1856         else:
1857             # If the strides are provided then it has priority.
1858             # Otherwise, compute the strides from the counts.
1859             if not has_stride:
1860                 rstride = int(max(np.ceil(rows / rcount), 1)) if rcount else 0
1861                 cstride = int(max(np.ceil(cols / ccount), 1)) if ccount else 0
1862 
1863         # We want two sets of lines, one running along the "rows" of
1864         # Z and another set of lines running along the "columns" of Z.
1865         # This transpose will make it easy to obtain the columns.
1866         tX, tY, tZ = np.transpose(X), np.transpose(Y), np.transpose(Z)
1867 
1868         if rstride:
1869             rii = list(range(0, rows, rstride))
1870             # Add the last index only if needed
1871             if rows > 0 and rii[-1] != (rows - 1):
1872                 rii += [rows-1]
1873         else:
1874             rii = []
1875         if cstride:
1876             cii = list(range(0, cols, cstride))
1877             # Add the last index only if needed
1878             if cols > 0 and cii[-1] != (cols - 1):
1879                 cii += [cols-1]
1880         else:
1881             cii = []
1882 
1883         if rstride == 0 and cstride == 0:
1884             raise ValueError("Either rstride or cstride must be non zero")
1885 
1886         # If the inputs were empty, then just
1887         # reset everything.
1888         if Z.size == 0:
1889             rii = []
1890             cii = []
1891 
1892         xlines = [X[i] for i in rii]
1893         ylines = [Y[i] for i in rii]
1894         zlines = [Z[i] for i in rii]
1895 
1896         txlines = [tX[i] for i in cii]
1897         tylines = [tY[i] for i in cii]
1898         tzlines = [tZ[i] for i in cii]
1899 
1900         lines = ([list(zip(xl, yl, zl))
1901                   for xl, yl, zl in zip(xlines, ylines, zlines)]
1902                 + [list(zip(xl, yl, zl))
1903                    for xl, yl, zl in zip(txlines, tylines, tzlines)])
1904 
1905         linec = art3d.Line3DCollection(lines, *args, **kwargs)
1906         self.add_collection(linec)
1907         self.auto_scale_xyz(X, Y, Z, had_data)
1908 
1909         return linec
1910 
1911     def plot_trisurf(self, *args, color=None, norm=None, vmin=None, vmax=None,
1912                      lightsource=None, **kwargs):
1913         """
1914         Plot a triangulated surface.
1915 
1916         The (optional) triangulation can be specified in one of two ways;
1917         either::
1918 
1919           plot_trisurf(triangulation, ...)
1920 
1921         where triangulation is a :class:`~matplotlib.tri.Triangulation`
1922         object, or::
1923 
1924           plot_trisurf(X, Y, ...)
1925           plot_trisurf(X, Y, triangles, ...)
1926           plot_trisurf(X, Y, triangles=triangles, ...)
1927 
1928         in which case a Triangulation object will be created.  See
1929         :class:`~matplotlib.tri.Triangulation` for a explanation of
1930         these possibilities.
1931 
1932         The remaining arguments are::
1933 
1934           plot_trisurf(..., Z)
1935 
1936         where *Z* is the array of values to contour, one per point
1937         in the triangulation.
1938 
1939         Parameters
1940         ----------
1941         X, Y, Z : array-like
1942             Data values as 1D arrays.
1943         color
1944             Color of the surface patches.
1945         cmap
1946             A colormap for the surface patches.
1947         norm : Normalize
1948             An instance of Normalize to map values to colors.
1949         vmin, vmax : scalar, optional, default: None
1950             Minimum and maximum value to map.

1953             always disabled when *cmap* is specified.
1954         lightsource : `~matplotlib.colors.LightSource`
1955             The lightsource to use when *shade* is True.

2018     def _3d_extend_contour(self, cset, stride=5):
2019         '''
2020         Extend a contour in 3D by creating
2021         '''
2022 
2023         levels = cset.levels
2024         colls = cset.collections
2025         dz = (levels[1] - levels[0]) / 2
2026 
2027         for z, linec in zip(levels, colls):
2028             paths = linec.get_paths()
2029             if not paths:
2030                 continue
2031             topverts = art3d._paths_to_3d_segments(paths, z - dz)
2032             botverts = art3d._paths_to_3d_segments(paths, z + dz)
2033 
2034             color = linec.get_color()[0]
2035 
2036             polyverts = []
2037             normals = []
2038             nsteps = np.round(len(topverts[0]) / stride)
2039             if nsteps <= 1:
2040                 if len(topverts[0]) > 1:
2041                     nsteps = 2
2042                 else:
2043                     continue
2044 
2045             stepsize = (len(topverts[0]) - 1) / (nsteps - 1)
2046             for i in range(int(np.round(nsteps)) - 1):
2047                 i1 = int(np.round(i * stepsize))
2048                 i2 = int(np.round((i + 1) * stepsize))
2049                 polyverts.append([topverts[0][i1],
2050                     topverts[0][i2],
2051                     botverts[0][i2],
2052                     botverts[0][i1]])
2053 
2054             # all polygons have 4 vertices, so vectorize
2055             polyverts = np.array(polyverts)
2056             normals = self._generate_normals(polyverts)
2057 
2058             colors = self._shade_colors(color, normals)
2059             colors2 = self._shade_colors(color, normals)
2060             polycol = art3d.Poly3DCollection(polyverts,
2061                                              facecolors=colors,
2062                                              edgecolors=colors2)
2063             polycol.set_sort_zpos(z)
2064             self.add_collection3d(polycol)
2065 
2066         for col in colls:
2067             self.collections.remove(col)

2416     def bar3d(self, x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, color=None,
2417               zsort='average', shade=True, *args, **kwargs):
2418         """Generate a 3D barplot.
2419 
2420         This method creates three dimensional barplot where the width,
2421         depth, height, and color of the bars can all be uniquely set.
2422 
2423         Parameters
2424         ----------
2425         x, y, z : array-like
2426             The coordinates of the anchor point of the bars.
2427 
2428         dx, dy, dz : scalar or array-like
2429             The width, depth, and height of the bars, respectively.
2430 
2431         color : sequence of valid color specifications, optional
2432             The color of the bars can be specified globally or
2433             individually. This parameter can be:
2434 
2435               - A single color value, to color all bars the same color.
2436               - An array of colors of length N bars, to color each bar
2437                 independently.
2438               - An array of colors of length 6, to color the faces of the
2439                 bars similarly.
2440               - An array of colors of length 6 * N bars, to color each face
2441                 independently.
2442 
2443             When coloring the faces of the boxes specifically, this is
2444             the order of the coloring:
2445 
2446               1. -Z (bottom of box)
2447               2. +Z (top of box)
2448               3. -Y
2449               4. +Y
2450               5. -X
2451               6. +X
2452 
2453         zsort : str, optional
2454             The z-axis sorting scheme passed onto `~.art3d.Poly3DCollection`
2455 
2456         shade : bool, optional (default = True)
2457             When true, this shades the dark sides of the bars (relative
2458             to the plot's source of light).
2459 
2460         **kwargs
2461             Any additional keyword arguments are passed onto
2462             `~.art3d.Poly3DCollection`.
2463 
2464         Returns
2465         -------
2466         collection : `~.art3d.Poly3DCollection`
2467             A collection of three dimensional polygons representing
2468             the bars.
2469         """
2470 
2471         had_data = self.has_data()
2472 
2473         x, y, z, dx, dy, dz = np.broadcast_arrays(
2474             np.atleast_1d(x), y, z, dx, dy, dz)
2475         minx = np.min(x)
2476         maxx = np.max(x + dx)
2477         miny = np.min(y)
2478         maxy = np.max(y + dy)
2479         minz = np.min(z)
2480         maxz = np.max(z + dz)
2481 
2482         # shape (6, 4, 3)
2483         # All faces are oriented facing outwards - when viewed from the
2484         # outside, their vertices are in a counterclockwise ordering.
2485         cuboid = np.array([
2486             # -z
2487             (
2488                 (0, 0, 0),
2489                 (0, 1, 0),
2490                 (1, 1, 0),
2491                 (1, 0, 0),
2492             ),
2493             # +z
2494             (
2495                 (0, 0, 1),
2496                 (1, 0, 1),
2497                 (1, 1, 1),
2498                 (0, 1, 1),
2499             ),
2500             # -y
2501             (
2502                 (0, 0, 0),
2503                 (1, 0, 0),
2504                 (1, 0, 1),
2505                 (0, 0, 1),
2506             ),
2507             # +y
2508             (
2509                 (0, 1, 0),
2510                 (0, 1, 1),
2511                 (1, 1, 1),
2512                 (1, 1, 0),
2513             ),
2514             # -x
2515             (
2516                 (0, 0, 0),
2517                 (0, 0, 1),
2518                 (0, 1, 1),
2519                 (0, 1, 0),
2520             ),
2521             # +x
2522             (
2523                 (1, 0, 0),
2524                 (1, 1, 0),
2525                 (1, 1, 1),
2526                 (1, 0, 1),
2527             ),
2528         ])
2529 
2530         # indexed by [bar, face, vertex, coord]
2531         polys = np.empty(x.shape + cuboid.shape)
2532 
2533         # handle each coordinate separately
2534         for i, p, dp in [(0, x, dx), (1, y, dy), (2, z, dz)]:
2535             p = p[..., np.newaxis, np.newaxis]
2536             dp = dp[..., np.newaxis, np.newaxis]
2537             polys[..., i] = p + dp * cuboid[..., i]
2538 
2539         # collapse the first two axes
2540         polys = polys.reshape((-1,) + polys.shape[2:])
2541 
2542         facecolors = []
2543         if color is None:
2544             color = [self._get_patches_for_fill.get_next_color()]
2545 
2546         if len(color) == len(x):
2547             # bar colors specified, need to expand to number of faces
2548             for c in color:
2549                 facecolors.extend([c] * 6)
2550         else:
2551             # a single color specified, or face colors specified explicitly
2552             facecolors = list(mcolors.to_rgba_array(color))
2553             if len(facecolors) < len(x):
2554                 facecolors *= (6 * len(x))
2555 
2556         if shade:
2557             normals = self._generate_normals(polys)
2558             sfacecolors = self._shade_colors(facecolors, normals)
2559         else:
2560             sfacecolors = facecolors
2561 
2562         col = art3d.Poly3DCollection(polys,
2563                                      zsort=zsort,
2564                                      facecolor=sfacecolors,
2565                                      *args, **kwargs)
2566         self.add_collection(col)
2567 
2568         self.auto_scale_xyz((minx, maxx), (miny, maxy), (minz, maxz), had_data)
2569 
2570         return col

ax.clear() adds extra ticks, un-hides shared-axis tick labels
### Bug report

**Bug summary**

When using shared axes (e.g. from `plt.subplots(2, 2, sharex=True, sharey=True)`), calling `ax.clear()` causes ticks and tick labels to be shown that should be hidden. The axes are still linked, though (e.g. adjusting the plotting range on one subplot adjusts the others as well). This is a behavior change between matplotlib 3.4.1 and 3.4.2.

**Code for reproduction**

This code produces different results with matplotlib 3.4.1 and 3.4.2:

```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, sharex=True, sharey=True)

x = np.arange(0.0, 2*np.pi, 0.01)
y = np.sin(x)

for ax in axes.flatten():
    ax.clear()
    ax.plot(x, y)
```

This example is of course silly, but I use the general pattern when making animations with FuncAnimation, where my plotting function is a complex module which doesn't facilitate blitting, so I clear and re-use the axes for each frame of the animation.

**Actual outcome**

This is the plot produced with matplotlib 3.4.2:

![matplotlib-3 4 2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23462789/126717195-a974fcf6-52d6-465b-841e-4f8172964dcd.png)

The presence of tick labels that should be hidden by virtue of the shared axes is the clearest problem in this plot, but there are also ticks that appear along the top and right side of each subplot which are not present in the example below (and not part of the default plotting style, IIRC).

The top and right-side ticks also appear when not using multiple subplots, so I think the shared-axis aspect reveals another symptom but is not a core part of this bug.

If the `ax.clear()` call is removed, the plot produced with matplotlib 3.4.2 appears identical to the 3.4.1 plot below.

**Expected outcome**

This is the plot produced with matplotlib 3.4.1:

![matplotlib-3 4 1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23462789/126717203-e755c628-0e32-4a7d-80a0-90c1a3ca6eb7.png)

347     def _apply_params(self, **kw):
348         for name, target in [("gridOn", self.gridline),
349                              ("tick1On", self.tick1line),
350                              ("tick2On", self.tick2line),
351                              ("label1On", self.label1),
352                              ("label2On", self.label2)]:
353             if name in kw:
354                 target.set_visible(kw.pop(name))
355         if any(k in kw for k in ['size', 'width', 'pad', 'tickdir']):
356             self._size = kw.pop('size', self._size)
357             # Width could be handled outside this block, but it is
358             # convenient to leave it here.
359             self._width = kw.pop('width', self._width)
360             self._base_pad = kw.pop('pad', self._base_pad)
361             # _apply_tickdir uses _size and _base_pad to make _pad, and also
362             # sets the ticklines markers.
363             self._apply_tickdir(kw.pop('tickdir', self._tickdir))
364             for line in (self.tick1line, self.tick2line):
365                 line.set_markersize(self._size)
366                 line.set_markeredgewidth(self._width)
367             # _get_text1_transform uses _pad from _apply_tickdir.
368             trans = self._get_text1_transform()[0]
369             self.label1.set_transform(trans)
370             trans = self._get_text2_transform()[0]
371             self.label2.set_transform(trans)
372         tick_kw = {k: v for k, v in kw.items() if k in ['color', 'zorder']}
373         if 'color' in kw:
374             tick_kw['markeredgecolor'] = kw['color']
375         self.tick1line.set(**tick_kw)
376         self.tick2line.set(**tick_kw)
377         for k, v in tick_kw.items():
378             setattr(self, '_' + k, v)
379 
380         if 'labelrotation' in kw:
381             self._set_labelrotation(kw.pop('labelrotation'))
382             self.label1.set(rotation=self._labelrotation[1])
383             self.label2.set(rotation=self._labelrotation[1])
384 
385         label_kw = {k[5:]: v for k, v in kw.items()
386                     if k in ['labelsize', 'labelcolor']}
387         self.label1.set(**label_kw)
388         self.label2.set(**label_kw)
389 
390         grid_kw = {k[5:]: v for k, v in kw.items()
391                    if k in _gridline_param_names}
392         self.gridline.set(**grid_kw)

568 class _LazyTickList:
569     """
570     A descriptor for lazy instantiation of tick lists.
571 
572     See comment above definition of the ``majorTicks`` and ``minorTicks``
573     attributes.
574     """
575 
576     def __init__(self, major):
577         self._major = major
578 
579     def __get__(self, instance, cls):
580         if instance is None:
581             return self
582         else:
583             # instance._get_tick() can itself try to access the majorTicks
584             # attribute (e.g. in certain projection classes which override
585             # e.g. get_xaxis_text1_transform).  In order to avoid infinite
586             # recursion, first set the majorTicks on the instance to an empty
587             # list, then create the tick and append it.
588             if self._major:
589                 instance.majorTicks = []
590                 tick = instance._get_tick(major=True)
591                 instance.majorTicks.append(tick)
592                 return instance.majorTicks
593             else:
594                 instance.minorTicks = []
595                 tick = instance._get_tick(major=False)
596                 instance.minorTicks.append(tick)
597                 return instance.minorTicks

882     @staticmethod
883     def _translate_tick_kw(kw):
884         # The following lists may be moved to a more accessible location.
885         kwkeys = ['size', 'width', 'color', 'tickdir', 'pad',
886                   'labelsize', 'labelcolor', 'zorder', 'gridOn',
887                   'tick1On', 'tick2On', 'label1On', 'label2On',
888                   'length', 'direction', 'left', 'bottom', 'right', 'top',
889                   'labelleft', 'labelbottom', 'labelright', 'labeltop',
890                   'labelrotation'] + _gridline_param_names
891         kwtrans = {}
892         if 'length' in kw:
893             kwtrans['size'] = kw.pop('length')
894         if 'direction' in kw:
895             kwtrans['tickdir'] = kw.pop('direction')
896         if 'rotation' in kw:
897             kwtrans['labelrotation'] = kw.pop('rotation')
898         if 'left' in kw:
899             kwtrans['tick1On'] = kw.pop('left')
900         if 'bottom' in kw:
901             kwtrans['tick1On'] = kw.pop('bottom')
902         if 'right' in kw:
903             kwtrans['tick2On'] = kw.pop('right')
904         if 'top' in kw:
905             kwtrans['tick2On'] = kw.pop('top')
906         if 'labelleft' in kw:
907             kwtrans['label1On'] = kw.pop('labelleft')
908         if 'labelbottom' in kw:
909             kwtrans['label1On'] = kw.pop('labelbottom')
910         if 'labelright' in kw:
911             kwtrans['label2On'] = kw.pop('labelright')
912         if 'labeltop' in kw:
913             kwtrans['label2On'] = kw.pop('labeltop')
914         if 'colors' in kw:
915             c = kw.pop('colors')
916             kwtrans['color'] = c
917             kwtrans['labelcolor'] = c
918         # Maybe move the checking up to the caller of this method.
919         for key in kw:
920             if key not in kwkeys:
921                 raise ValueError(
922                     "keyword %s is not recognized; valid keywords are %s"
923                     % (key, kwkeys))
924         kwtrans.update(kw)
925         return kwtrans

1033     def _update_ticks(self):
1034         """
1035         Update ticks (position and labels) using the current data interval of
1036         the axes.  Return the list of ticks that will be drawn.
1037         """
1038         major_locs = self.get_majorticklocs()
1039         major_labels = self.major.formatter.format_ticks(major_locs)
1040         major_ticks = self.get_major_ticks(len(major_locs))
1041         self.major.formatter.set_locs(major_locs)
1042         for tick, loc, label in zip(major_ticks, major_locs, major_labels):
1043             tick.update_position(loc)
1044             tick.set_label1(label)
1045             tick.set_label2(label)
1046         minor_locs = self.get_minorticklocs()
1047         minor_labels = self.minor.formatter.format_ticks(minor_locs)
1048         minor_ticks = self.get_minor_ticks(len(minor_locs))
1049         self.minor.formatter.set_locs(minor_locs)
1050         for tick, loc, label in zip(minor_ticks, minor_locs, minor_labels):
1051             tick.update_position(loc)
1052             tick.set_label1(label)
1053             tick.set_label2(label)
1054         ticks = [*major_ticks, *minor_ticks]
1055 
1056         view_low, view_high = self.get_view_interval()
1057         if view_low > view_high:
1058             view_low, view_high = view_high, view_low
1059 
1060         interval_t = self.get_transform().transform([view_low, view_high])
1061 
1062         ticks_to_draw = []
1063         for tick in ticks:
1064             try:
1065                 loc_t = self.get_transform().transform(tick.get_loc())
1066             except AssertionError:
1067                 # transforms.transform doesn't allow masked values but
1068                 # some scales might make them, so we need this try/except.
1069                 pass
1070             else:
1071                 if mtransforms._interval_contains_close(interval_t, loc_t):
1072                     ticks_to_draw.append(tick)
1073 
1074         return ticks_to_draw
1075

1078         return ([tick.label1.get_window_extent(renderer)
1079                  for tick in ticks if tick.label1.get_visible()],
1080                 [tick.label2.get_window_extent(renderer)

1083     def get_tightbbox(self, renderer, *, for_layout_only=False):
1084         """
1085         Return a bounding box that encloses the axis. It only accounts
1086         tick labels, axis label, and offsetText.
1087 
1088         If *for_layout_only* is True, then the width of the label (if this
1089         is an x-axis) or the height of the label (if this is a y-axis) is
1090         collapsed to near zero.  This allows tight/constrained_layout to ignore
1091         too-long labels when doing their layout.
1092         """
1093         if not self.get_visible():
1094             return
1095 
1096         ticks_to_draw = self._update_ticks()
1097 
1098         self._update_label_position(renderer)
1099 
1100         # go back to just this axis's tick labels
1101         ticklabelBoxes, ticklabelBoxes2 = self._get_tick_bboxes(
1102                     ticks_to_draw, renderer)
1103 
1104         self._update_offset_text_position(ticklabelBoxes, ticklabelBoxes2)
1105         self.offsetText.set_text(self.major.formatter.get_offset())
1106 
1107         bboxes = [
1108             *(a.get_window_extent(renderer)
1109               for a in [self.offsetText]
1110               if a.get_visible()),
1111             *ticklabelBoxes,
1112             *ticklabelBoxes2,
1113         ]
1114         # take care of label
1115         if self.label.get_visible():
1116             bb = self.label.get_window_extent(renderer)
1117             # for constrained/tight_layout, we want to ignore the label's
1118             # width/height because the adjustments they make can't be improved.
1119             # this code collapses the relevant direction
1120             if for_layout_only:
1121                 if self.axis_name == "x" and bb.width > 0:
1122                     bb.x0 = (bb.x0 + bb.x1) / 2 - 0.5
1123                     bb.x1 = bb.x0 + 1.0
1124                 if self.axis_name == "y" and bb.height > 0:
1125                     bb.y0 = (bb.y0 + bb.y1) / 2 - 0.5
1126                     bb.y1 = bb.y0 + 1.0
1127             bboxes.append(bb)
1128         bboxes = [b for b in bboxes
1129                   if 0 < b.width < np.inf and 0 < b.height < np.inf]
1130         if bboxes:
1131             return mtransforms.Bbox.union(bboxes)
1132         else:
1133             return None

1451     def _update_axisinfo(self):

1453         Check the axis converter for the stored units to see if the
1454         axis info needs to be updated.

1461         if info is None:

1464            self.major.locator != info.majloc and self.isDefault_majloc:

1472            self.major.formatter != info.majfmt and self.isDefault_majfmt:

1488     def convert_units(self, x):
1489         # If x is natively supported by Matplotlib, doesn't need converting
1490         if munits._is_natively_supported(x):
1491             return x

1493         if self.converter is None:
1494             self.converter = munits.registry.get_converter(x)

1496         if self.converter is None:
1497             return x
1498         try:
1499             ret = self.converter.convert(x, self.units, self)
1500         except Exception as e:
1501             raise munits.ConversionError('Failed to convert value(s) to axis '
1502                                          f'units: {x!r}') from e

1673     def set_ticklabels(self, ticklabels, *, minor=False, **kwargs):
1674         r"""
1675         Set the text values of the tick labels.
1676 
1677         .. admonition:: Discouraged
1678 
1679             The use of this method is discouraged, because of the dependency
1680             on tick positions. In most cases, you'll want to use
1681             ``set_[x/y]ticks(positions, labels)`` instead.
1682 
1683             If you are using this method, you should always fix the tick
1684             positions before, e.g. by using `.Axis.set_ticks` or by explicitly
1685             setting a `~.ticker.FixedLocator`. Otherwise, ticks are free to
1686             move and the labels may end up in unexpected positions.
1687 
1688         Parameters
1689         ----------
1690         ticklabels : sequence of str or of `.Text`\s
1691             Texts for labeling each tick location in the sequence set by
1692             `.Axis.set_ticks`; the number of labels must match the number of
1693             locations.
1694         minor : bool
1695             If True, set minor ticks instead of major ticks.
1696         **kwargs
1697             Text properties.
1698 
1699         Returns
1700         -------
1701         list of `.Text`\s
1702             For each tick, includes ``tick.label1`` if it is visible, then
1703             ``tick.label2`` if it is visible, in that order.
1704         """
1705         ticklabels = [t.get_text() if hasattr(t, 'get_text') else t
1706                       for t in ticklabels]
1707         locator = (self.get_minor_locator() if minor
1708                    else self.get_major_locator())
1709         if isinstance(locator, mticker.FixedLocator):
1710             # Passing [] as a list of ticklabels is often used as a way to
1711             # remove all tick labels, so only error for > 0 ticklabels
1712             if len(locator.locs) != len(ticklabels) and len(ticklabels) != 0:
1713                 raise ValueError(
1714                     "The number of FixedLocator locations"
1715                     f" ({len(locator.locs)}), usually from a call to"
1716                     " set_ticks, does not match"
1717                     f" the number of ticklabels ({len(ticklabels)}).")
1718             tickd = {loc: lab for loc, lab in zip(locator.locs, ticklabels)}
1719             func = functools.partial(self._format_with_dict, tickd)
1720             formatter = mticker.FuncFormatter(func)
1721         else:
1722             formatter = mticker.FixedFormatter(ticklabels)
1723 
1724         if minor:
1725             self.set_minor_formatter(formatter)
1726             locs = self.get_minorticklocs()
1727             ticks = self.get_minor_ticks(len(locs))
1728         else:
1729             self.set_major_formatter(formatter)
1730             locs = self.get_majorticklocs()
1731             ticks = self.get_major_ticks(len(locs))
1732 
1733         ret = []
1734         for pos, (loc, tick) in enumerate(zip(locs, ticks)):
1735             tick.update_position(loc)
1736             tick_label = formatter(loc, pos)
1737             # deal with label1
1738             tick.label1.set_text(tick_label)
1739             tick.label1.update(kwargs)
1740             # deal with label2
1741             tick.label2.set_text(tick_label)
1742             tick.label2.update(kwargs)
1743             # only return visible tick labels
1744             if tick.label1.get_visible():
1745                 ret.append(tick.label1)
1746             if tick.label2.get_visible():
1747                 ret.append(tick.label2)
1748 
1749         self.stale = True
1750         return ret
1751

1972 def _make_getset_interval(method_name, lim_name, attr_name):

1974     Helper to generate ``get_{data,view}_interval`` and
1975     ``set_{data,view}_interval`` implementations.

1982     def setter(self, vmin, vmax, ignore=False):
1983         # docstring inherited.
1984         if ignore:
1985             setattr(getattr(self.axes, lim_name), attr_name, (vmin, vmax))
1986         else:
1987             oldmin, oldmax = getter(self)
1988             if oldmin < oldmax:
1989                 setter(self, min(vmin, vmax, oldmin), max(vmin, vmax, oldmax),
1990                        ignore=True)
1991             else:
1992                 setter(self, max(vmin, vmax, oldmin), min(vmin, vmax, oldmax),
1993                        ignore=True)
1994         self.stale = True
1995 
1996     getter.__name__ = f"get_{method_name}_interval"
1997     setter.__name__ = f"set_{method_name}_interval"
1998

375             dt = dt.replace(microsecond=0) + datetime.timedelta(seconds=1)
376         else:
377             dt = dt.replace(microsecond=ms)
378 
379     return dt

416 def date2num(d):
417     """
418     Convert datetime objects to Matplotlib dates.
419 
420     Parameters
421     ----------
422     d : `datetime.datetime` or `numpy.datetime64` or sequences of these
423 
424     Returns
425     -------
426     float or sequence of floats
427         Number of days since the epoch.  See `.get_epoch` for the
428         epoch, which can be changed by :rc:`date.epoch` or `.set_epoch`.  If
429         the epoch is "1970-01-01T00:00:00" (default) then noon Jan 1 1970
430         ("1970-01-01T12:00:00") returns 0.5.
431 
432     Notes
433     -----
434     The Gregorian calendar is assumed; this is not universal practice.
435     For details see the module docstring.
436     """
437     if hasattr(d, "values"):
438         # this unpacks pandas series or dataframes...
439         d = d.values
440 
441     # make an iterable, but save state to unpack later:
442     iterable = np.iterable(d)
443     if not iterable:
444         d = [d]
445 
446     d = np.asarray(d)
447     # convert to datetime64 arrays, if not already:
448     if not np.issubdtype(d.dtype, np.datetime64):
449         # datetime arrays
450         if not d.size:
451             # deals with an empty array...
452             return d
453         tzi = getattr(d[0], 'tzinfo', None)
454         if tzi is not None:
455             # make datetime naive:
456             d = [dt.astimezone(UTC).replace(tzinfo=None) for dt in d]
457             d = np.asarray(d)
458         d = d.astype('datetime64[us]')
459 
460     d = _dt64_to_ordinalf(d)
461 
462     return d if iterable else d[0]

465 def julian2num(j):
466     """
467     Convert a Julian date (or sequence) to a Matplotlib date (or sequence).
468 
469     Parameters
470     ----------
471     j : float or sequence of floats
472         Julian dates (days relative to 4713 BC Jan 1, 12:00:00 Julian
473         calendar or 4714 BC Nov 24, 12:00:00, proleptic Gregorian calendar).
474 
475     Returns
476     -------
477     float or sequence of floats
478         Matplotlib dates (days relative to `.get_epoch`).
479     """
480     ep = np.datetime64(get_epoch(), 'h').astype(float) / 24.
481     ep0 = np.datetime64('0000-12-31T00:00:00', 'h').astype(float) / 24.
482     # Julian offset defined above is relative to 0000-12-31, but we need
483     # relative to our current epoch:
484     dt = JULIAN_OFFSET - ep0 + ep
485     return np.subtract(j, dt)  # Handles both scalar & nonscalar j.

564 def drange(dstart, dend, delta):
565     """
566     Return a sequence of equally spaced Matplotlib dates.
567 
568     The dates start at *dstart* and reach up to, but not including *dend*.
569     They are spaced by *delta*.
570 
571     Parameters
572     ----------
573     dstart, dend : `~datetime.datetime`
574         The date limits.
575     delta : `datetime.timedelta`
576         Spacing of the dates.
577 
578     Returns
579     -------
580     `numpy.array`
581         A list floats representing Matplotlib dates.
582 
583     """
584     f1 = date2num(dstart)
585     f2 = date2num(dend)
586     step = delta.total_seconds() / SEC_PER_DAY
587 
588     # calculate the difference between dend and dstart in times of delta
589     num = int(np.ceil((f2 - f1) / step))
590 
591     # calculate end of the interval which will be generated
592     dinterval_end = dstart + num * delta
593 
594     # ensure, that an half open interval will be generated [dstart, dend)
595     if dinterval_end >= dend:
596         # if the endpoint is greater than dend, just subtract one delta
597         dinterval_end -= delta
598         num -= 1
599 
600     f2 = date2num(dinterval_end)  # new float-endpoint
601     return np.linspace(f1, f2, num + 1)

642 class ConciseDateFormatter(ticker.Formatter):
643     """
644     A `.Formatter` which attempts to figure out the best format to use for the
645     date, and to make it as compact as possible, but still be complete. This is
646     most useful when used with the `AutoDateLocator`::
647 
648     >>> locator = AutoDateLocator()
649     >>> formatter = ConciseDateFormatter(locator)
650 
651     Parameters
652     ----------
653     locator : `.ticker.Locator`
654         Locator that this axis is using.
655 
656     tz : str or `~datetime.tzinfo`, default: :rc:`timezone`
657         Passed to `.dates.num2date`.
658 
659     formats : list of 6 strings, optional
660         Format strings for 6 levels of tick labelling: mostly years,
661         months, days, hours, minutes, and seconds.  Strings use
662         the same format codes as `~datetime.datetime.strftime`.  Default is
663         ``['%Y', '%b', '%d', '%H:%M', '%H:%M', '%S.%f']``
664 
665     zero_formats : list of 6 strings, optional
666         Format strings for tick labels that are "zeros" for a given tick
667         level.  For instance, if most ticks are months, ticks around 1 Jan 2005
668         will be labeled "Dec", "2005", "Feb".  The default is
669         ``['', '%Y', '%b', '%b-%d', '%H:%M', '%H:%M']``
670 
671     offset_formats : list of 6 strings, optional
672         Format strings for the 6 levels that is applied to the "offset"
673         string found on the right side of an x-axis, or top of a y-axis.
674         Combined with the tick labels this should completely specify the
675         date.  The default is::
676 
677             ['', '%Y', '%Y-%b', '%Y-%b-%d', '%Y-%b-%d', '%Y-%b-%d %H:%M']
678 
679     show_offset : bool, default: True
680         Whether to show the offset or not.
681 
682     usetex : bool, default: :rc:`text.usetex`
683         To enable/disable the use of TeX's math mode for rendering the results
684         of the formatter.
685 
686     Examples
687     --------
688     See :doc:`/gallery/ticks/date_concise_formatter`
689 
690     .. plot::
691 
692         import datetime
693         import matplotlib.dates as mdates
694 
695         base = datetime.datetime(2005, 2, 1)
696         dates = np.array([base + datetime.timedelta(hours=(2 * i))
697                           for i in range(732)])
698         N = len(dates)
699         np.random.seed(19680801)
700         y = np.cumsum(np.random.randn(N))
701 
702         fig, ax = plt.subplots(constrained_layout=True)
703         locator = mdates.AutoDateLocator()
704         formatter = mdates.ConciseDateFormatter(locator)
705         ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(locator)
706         ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
707 
708         ax.plot(dates, y)
709         ax.set_title('Concise Date Formatter')
710 
711     """
712 
713     def __init__(self, locator, tz=None, formats=None, offset_formats=None,
714                  zero_formats=None, show_offset=True, *, usetex=None):
715         """
716         Autoformat the date labels.  The default format is used to form an
717         initial string, and then redundant elements are removed.
718         """
719         self._locator = locator
720         self._tz = tz
721         self.defaultfmt = '%Y'
722         # there are 6 levels with each level getting a specific format
723         # 0: mostly years,  1: months,  2: days,
724         # 3: hours, 4: minutes, 5: seconds
725         if formats:
726             if len(formats) != 6:
727                 raise ValueError('formats argument must be a list of '
728                                  '6 format strings (or None)')
729             self.formats = formats
730         else:
731             self.formats = ['%Y',  # ticks are mostly years
732                             '%b',          # ticks are mostly months
733                             '%d',          # ticks are mostly days
734                             '%H:%M',       # hrs
735                             '%H:%M',       # min
736                             '%S.%f',       # secs
737                             ]
738         # fmt for zeros ticks at this level.  These are
739         # ticks that should be labeled w/ info the level above.
740         # like 1 Jan can just be labelled "Jan".  02:02:00 can
741         # just be labeled 02:02.
742         if zero_formats:
743             if len(zero_formats) != 6:
744                 raise ValueError('zero_formats argument must be a list of '
745                                  '6 format strings (or None)')
746             self.zero_formats = zero_formats
747         elif formats:
748             # use the users formats for the zero tick formats
749             self.zero_formats = [''] + self.formats[:-1]
750         else:
751             # make the defaults a bit nicer:
752             self.zero_formats = [''] + self.formats[:-1]
753             self.zero_formats[3] = '%b-%d'
754 
755         if offset_formats:
756             if len(offset_formats) != 6:
757                 raise ValueError('offset_formats argument must be a list of '
758                                  '6 format strings (or None)')
759             self.offset_formats = offset_formats
760         else:
761             self.offset_formats = ['',
762                                    '%Y',
763                                    '%Y-%b',
764                                    '%Y-%b-%d',
765                                    '%Y-%b-%d',
766                                    '%Y-%b-%d %H:%M']
767         self.offset_string = ''
768         self.show_offset = show_offset
769         self._usetex = (usetex if usetex is not None else
770                         mpl.rcParams['text.usetex'])
771 
772     def __call__(self, x, pos=None):
773         formatter = DateFormatter(self.defaultfmt, self._tz,
774                                   usetex=self._usetex)
775         return formatter(x, pos=pos)
776 
777     def format_ticks(self, values):
778         tickdatetime = [num2date(value, tz=self._tz) for value in values]
779         tickdate = np.array([tdt.timetuple()[:6] for tdt in tickdatetime])
780 
781         # basic algorithm:
782         # 1) only display a part of the date if it changes over the ticks.
783         # 2) don't display the smaller part of the date if:
784         #    it is always the same or if it is the start of the
785         #    year, month, day etc.
786         # fmt for most ticks at this level
787         fmts = self.formats
788         # format beginnings of days, months, years, etc.
789         zerofmts = self.zero_formats
790         # offset fmt are for the offset in the upper left of the
791         # or lower right of the axis.
792         offsetfmts = self.offset_formats
793         show_offset = self.show_offset
794 
795         # determine the level we will label at:
796         # mostly 0: years,  1: months,  2: days,
797         # 3: hours, 4: minutes, 5: seconds, 6: microseconds
798         for level in range(5, -1, -1):
799             if len(np.unique(tickdate[:, level])) > 1:
800                 if level < 2:
801                     show_offset = False
802                 break
803             elif level == 0:
804                 # all tickdate are the same, so only micros might be different
805                 # set to the most precise (6: microseconds doesn't exist...)
806                 level = 5
807 
808         # level is the basic level we will label at.
809         # now loop through and decide the actual ticklabels
810         zerovals = [0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0]
811         labels = [''] * len(tickdate)
812         for nn in range(len(tickdate)):
813             if level < 5:
814                 if tickdate[nn][level] == zerovals[level]:
815                     fmt = zerofmts[level]
816                 else:
817                     fmt = fmts[level]
818             else:
819                 # special handling for seconds + microseconds
820                 if (tickdatetime[nn].second == tickdatetime[nn].microsecond
821                         == 0):
822                     fmt = zerofmts[level]
823                 else:
824                     fmt = fmts[level]
825             labels[nn] = tickdatetime[nn].strftime(fmt)
826 
827         # special handling of seconds and microseconds:
828         # strip extra zeros and decimal if possible.
829         # this is complicated by two factors.  1) we have some level-4 strings
830         # here (i.e. 03:00, '0.50000', '1.000') 2) we would like to have the
831         # same number of decimals for each string (i.e. 0.5 and 1.0).
832         if level >= 5:
833             trailing_zeros = min(
834                 (len(s) - len(s.rstrip('0')) for s in labels if '.' in s),
835                 default=None)
836             if trailing_zeros:
837                 for nn in range(len(labels)):
838                     if '.' in labels[nn]:
839                         labels[nn] = labels[nn][:-trailing_zeros].rstrip('.')
840 
841         if show_offset:
842             # set the offset string:
843             self.offset_string = tickdatetime[-1].strftime(offsetfmts[level])
844             if self._usetex:
845                 self.offset_string = _wrap_in_tex(self.offset_string)
846         else:
847             self.offset_string = ''
848 
849         if self._usetex:
850             return [_wrap_in_tex(l) for l in labels]
851         else:
852             return labels
853 
854     def get_offset(self):
855         return self.offset_string
856 
857     def format_data_short(self, value):
858         return num2date(value, tz=self._tz).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')

861 class AutoDateFormatter(ticker.Formatter):
862     """
863     A `.Formatter` which attempts to figure out the best format to use.  This
864     is most useful when used with the `AutoDateLocator`.
865 
866     `.AutoDateFormatter` has a ``.scale`` dictionary that maps tick scales (the
867     interval in days between one major tick) to format strings; this dictionary
868     defaults to ::
869 
870         self.scaled = {
871             DAYS_PER_YEAR: rcParams['date.autoformat.year'],
872             DAYS_PER_MONTH: rcParams['date.autoformat.month'],
873             1: rcParams['date.autoformat.day'],
874             1 / HOURS_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformat.hour'],
875             1 / MINUTES_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformat.minute'],
876             1 / SEC_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformat.second'],
877             1 / MUSECONDS_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformat.microsecond'],
878         }
879 
880     The formatter uses the format string corresponding to the lowest key in
881     the dictionary that is greater or equal to the current scale.  Dictionary
882     entries can be customized::
883 
884         locator = AutoDateLocator()
885         formatter = AutoDateFormatter(locator)
886         formatter.scaled[1/(24*60)] = '%M:%S' # only show min and sec
887 
888     Custom callables can also be used instead of format strings.  The following
889     example shows how to use a custom format function to strip trailing zeros
890     from decimal seconds and adds the date to the first ticklabel::
891 
892         def my_format_function(x, pos=None):
893             x = matplotlib.dates.num2date(x)
894             if pos == 0:
895                 fmt = '%D %H:%M:%S.%f'
896             else:
897                 fmt = '%H:%M:%S.%f'
898             label = x.strftime(fmt)
899             label = label.rstrip("0")
900             label = label.rstrip(".")
901             return label
902 
903         formatter.scaled[1/(24*60)] = my_format_function
904     """
905 
906     # This can be improved by providing some user-level direction on
907     # how to choose the best format (precedence, etc.).
908 
909     # Perhaps a 'struct' that has a field for each time-type where a
910     # zero would indicate "don't show" and a number would indicate
911     # "show" with some sort of priority.  Same priorities could mean
912     # show all with the same priority.
913 
914     # Or more simply, perhaps just a format string for each
915     # possibility...
916 
917     def __init__(self, locator, tz=None, defaultfmt='%Y-%m-%d', *,
918                  usetex=None):
919         """
920         Autoformat the date labels.
921 
922         Parameters
923         ----------
924         locator : `.ticker.Locator`
925             Locator that this axis is using.
926 
927         tz : str or `~datetime.tzinfo`, optional
928             Passed to `.dates.num2date`.
929 
930         defaultfmt : str
931             The default format to use if none of the values in ``self.scaled``
932             are greater than the unit returned by ``locator._get_unit()``.
933 
934         usetex : bool, default: :rc:`text.usetex`
935             To enable/disable the use of TeX's math mode for rendering the
936             results of the formatter. If any entries in ``self.scaled`` are set
937             as functions, then it is up to the customized function to enable or
938             disable TeX's math mode itself.
939         """
940         self._locator = locator
941         self._tz = tz
942         self.defaultfmt = defaultfmt
943         self._formatter = DateFormatter(self.defaultfmt, tz)
944         rcParams = mpl.rcParams
945         self._usetex = (usetex if usetex is not None else
946                         mpl.rcParams['text.usetex'])
947         self.scaled = {
948             DAYS_PER_YEAR: rcParams['date.autoformatter.year'],
949             DAYS_PER_MONTH: rcParams['date.autoformatter.month'],
950             1: rcParams['date.autoformatter.day'],
951             1 / HOURS_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformatter.hour'],
952             1 / MINUTES_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformatter.minute'],
953             1 / SEC_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformatter.second'],
954             1 / MUSECONDS_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformatter.microsecond']
955         }
956 
957     def _set_locator(self, locator):
958         self._locator = locator
959 
960     def __call__(self, x, pos=None):
961         try:
962             locator_unit_scale = float(self._locator._get_unit())
963         except AttributeError:
964             locator_unit_scale = 1
965         # Pick the first scale which is greater than the locator unit.
966         fmt = next((fmt for scale, fmt in sorted(self.scaled.items())
967                     if scale >= locator_unit_scale),
968                    self.defaultfmt)
969 
970         if isinstance(fmt, str):
971             self._formatter = DateFormatter(fmt, self._tz, usetex=self._usetex)
972             result = self._formatter(x, pos)
973         elif callable(fmt):
974             result = fmt(x, pos)
975         else:
976             raise TypeError('Unexpected type passed to {0!r}.'.format(self))
977 
978         return result
