2980     def _update_title_position(self, renderer):
2981         """
2982         Update the title position based on the bounding box enclosing
2983         all the ticklabels and x-axis spine and xlabel...
2984         """
2985         if self._autotitlepos is not None and not self._autotitlepos:
2986             _log.debug('title position was updated manually, not adjusting')
2987             return
2988 
2989         titles = (self.title, self._left_title, self._right_title)
2990 
2991         # Need to check all our twins too, and all the children as well.
2992         axs = self._twinned_axes.get_siblings(self) + self.child_axes
2993         for ax in self.child_axes:  # Child positions must be updated first.
2994             locator = ax.get_axes_locator()
2995             ax.apply_aspect(locator(self, renderer) if locator else None)
2996 
2997         for title in titles:
2998             x, _ = title.get_position()
2999             # need to start again in case of window resizing
3000             title.set_position((x, 1.0))
3001             top = -np.inf
3002             for ax in axs:
3003                 bb = None
3004                 if (ax.xaxis.get_ticks_position() in ['top', 'unknown']
3005                         or ax.xaxis.get_label_position() == 'top'):
3006                     bb = ax.xaxis.get_tightbbox(renderer)
3007                 if bb is None:
3008                     if 'outline' in ax.spines:
3009                         # Special case for colorbars:
3010                         bb = ax.spines['outline'].get_window_extent()
3011                     else:
3012                         bb = ax.get_window_extent(renderer)
3013                 top = max(top, bb.ymax)
3014                 if title.get_text():
3015                     ax.yaxis.get_tightbbox(renderer)  # update offsetText
3016                     if ax.yaxis.offsetText.get_text():
3017                         bb = ax.yaxis.offsetText.get_tightbbox(renderer)
3018                         if bb.intersection(title.get_tightbbox(renderer), bb):
3019                             top = bb.ymax
3020             if top < 0:
3021                 # the top of Axes is not even on the figure, so don't try and
3022                 # automatically place it.
3023                 _log.debug('top of Axes not in the figure, so title not moved')
3024                 return
3025             if title.get_window_extent(renderer).ymin < top:
3026                 _, y = self.transAxes.inverted().transform((0, top))
3027                 title.set_position((x, y))
3028                 # empirically, this doesn't always get the min to top,
3029                 # so we need to adjust again.
3030                 if title.get_window_extent(renderer).ymin < top:
3031                     _, y = self.transAxes.inverted().transform(
3032                         (0., 2 * top - title.get_window_extent(renderer).ymin))
3033                     title.set_position((x, y))
3034 
3035         ymax = max(title.get_position()[1] for title in titles)
3036         for title in titles:
3037             # now line up all the titles at the highest baseline.
3038             x, _ = title.get_position()
3039             title.set_position((x, ymax))

3041     # Drawing
3042     @martist.allow_rasterization
3043     def draw(self, renderer):
3044         # docstring inherited
3045         if renderer is None:
3046             raise RuntimeError('No renderer defined')
3047         if not self.get_visible():
3048             return
3049         self._unstale_viewLim()
3050 
3051         renderer.open_group('axes', gid=self.get_gid())
3052 
3053         # prevent triggering call backs during the draw process
3054         self._stale = True
3055 
3056         # loop over self and child Axes...
3057         locator = self.get_axes_locator()
3058         self.apply_aspect(locator(self, renderer) if locator else None)
3059 
3060         artists = self.get_children()
3061         artists.remove(self.patch)
3062 
3063         # the frame draws the edges around the Axes patch -- we
3064         # decouple these so the patch can be in the background and the
3065         # frame in the foreground. Do this before drawing the axis
3066         # objects so that the spine has the opportunity to update them.
3067         if not (self.axison and self._frameon):
3068             for spine in self.spines.values():
3069                 artists.remove(spine)
3070 
3071         self._update_title_position(renderer)
3072 
3073         if not self.axison:
3074             for _axis in self._axis_map.values():
3075                 artists.remove(_axis)
3076 
3077         if not self.figure.canvas.is_saving():
3078             artists = [
3079                 a for a in artists
3080                 if not a.get_animated() or isinstance(a, mimage.AxesImage)]
3081         artists = sorted(artists, key=attrgetter('zorder'))
3082 
3083         # rasterize artists with negative zorder
3084         # if the minimum zorder is negative, start rasterization
3085         rasterization_zorder = self._rasterization_zorder
3086 
3087         if (rasterization_zorder is not None and
3088                 artists and artists[0].zorder < rasterization_zorder):
3089             renderer.start_rasterizing()
3090             artists_rasterized = [a for a in artists
3091                                   if a.zorder < rasterization_zorder]
3092             artists = [a for a in artists
3093                        if a.zorder >= rasterization_zorder]
3094         else:
3095             artists_rasterized = []
3096 
3097         # the patch draws the background rectangle -- the frame below
3098         # will draw the edges
3099         if self.axison and self._frameon:
3100             self.patch.draw(renderer)
3101 
3102         if artists_rasterized:
3103             for a in artists_rasterized:
3104                 a.draw(renderer)
3105             renderer.stop_rasterizing()
3106 
3107         mimage._draw_list_compositing_images(
3108             renderer, self, artists, self.figure.suppressComposite)
3109 
3110         renderer.close_group('axes')
3111         self.stale = False

4072     def _prepare_view_from_bbox(self, bbox, direction='in',
4073                                 mode=None, twinx=False, twiny=False):
4074         """
4075         Helper function to prepare the new bounds from a bbox.
4076 
4077         This helper function returns the new x and y bounds from the zoom
4078         bbox. This a convenience method to abstract the bbox logic
4079         out of the base setter.
4080         """
4081         if len(bbox) == 3:
4082             xp, yp, scl = bbox  # Zooming code
4083             if scl == 0:  # Should not happen
4084                 scl = 1.
4085             if scl > 1:
4086                 direction = 'in'
4087             else:
4088                 direction = 'out'
4089                 scl = 1/scl
4090             # get the limits of the axes
4091             (xmin, ymin), (xmax, ymax) = self.transData.transform(
4092                 np.transpose([self.get_xlim(), self.get_ylim()]))
4093             # set the range
4094             xwidth = xmax - xmin
4095             ywidth = ymax - ymin
4096             xcen = (xmax + xmin)*.5
4097             ycen = (ymax + ymin)*.5
4098             xzc = (xp*(scl - 1) + xcen)/scl
4099             yzc = (yp*(scl - 1) + ycen)/scl
4100             bbox = [xzc - xwidth/2./scl, yzc - ywidth/2./scl,
4101                     xzc + xwidth/2./scl, yzc + ywidth/2./scl]
4102         elif len(bbox) != 4:
4103             # should be len 3 or 4 but nothing else
4104             _api.warn_external(
4105                 "Warning in _set_view_from_bbox: bounding box is not a tuple "
4106                 "of length 3 or 4. Ignoring the view change.")
4107             return
4108 
4109         # Original limits.
4110         xmin0, xmax0 = self.get_xbound()
4111         ymin0, ymax0 = self.get_ybound()
4112         # The zoom box in screen coords.
4113         startx, starty, stopx, stopy = bbox
4114         # Convert to data coords.
4115         (startx, starty), (stopx, stopy) = self.transData.inverted().transform(
4116             [(startx, starty), (stopx, stopy)])
4117         # Clip to axes limits.
4118         xmin, xmax = np.clip(sorted([startx, stopx]), xmin0, xmax0)
4119         ymin, ymax = np.clip(sorted([starty, stopy]), ymin0, ymax0)
4120         # Don't double-zoom twinned axes or if zooming only the other axis.
4121         if twinx or mode == "y":
4122             xmin, xmax = xmin0, xmax0
4123         if twiny or mode == "x":
4124             ymin, ymax = ymin0, ymax0
4125 
4126         if direction == "in":
4127             new_xbound = xmin, xmax
4128             new_ybound = ymin, ymax

49 def _get_packed_offsets(widths, total, sep, mode="fixed"):
50     r"""
51     Pack boxes specified by their *widths*.
52 
53     For simplicity of the description, the terminology used here assumes a
54     horizontal layout, but the function works equally for a vertical layout.
55 
56     There are three packing *mode*\s:
57 
58     - 'fixed': The elements are packed tight to the left with a spacing of
59       *sep* in between. If *total* is *None* the returned total will be the
60       right edge of the last box. A non-*None* total will be passed unchecked
61       to the output. In particular this means that right edge of the last
62       box may be further to the right than the returned total.
63 
64     - 'expand': Distribute the boxes with equal spacing so that the left edge
65       of the first box is at 0, and the right edge of the last box is at
66       *total*. The parameter *sep* is ignored in this mode. A total of *None*
67       is accepted and considered equal to 1. The total is returned unchanged
68       (except for the conversion *None* to 1). If the total is smaller than
69       the sum of the widths, the laid out boxes will overlap.
70 
71     - 'equal': If *total* is given, the total space is divided in N equal
72       ranges and each box is left-aligned within its subspace.
73       Otherwise (*total* is *None*), *sep* must be provided and each box is
74       left-aligned in its subspace of width ``(max(widths) + sep)``. The
75       total width is then calculated to be ``N * (max(widths) + sep)``.
76 
77     Parameters
78     ----------
79     widths : list of float
80         Widths of boxes to be packed.
81     total : float or None
82         Intended total length. *None* if not used.
83     sep : float
84         Spacing between boxes.
85     mode : {'fixed', 'expand', 'equal'}
86         The packing mode.
87 
88     Returns
89     -------
90     total : float
91         The total width needed to accommodate the laid out boxes.
92     offsets : array of float
93         The left offsets of the boxes.
94     """
95     _api.check_in_list(["fixed", "expand", "equal"], mode=mode)
96 
97     if mode == "fixed":
98         offsets_ = np.cumsum([0] + [w + sep for w in widths])
99         offsets = offsets_[:-1]
100         if total is None:
101             total = offsets_[-1] - sep
102         return total, offsets
103 
104     elif mode == "expand":
105         # This is a bit of a hack to avoid a TypeError when *total*
106         # is None and used in conjugation with tight layout.
107         if total is None:
108             total = 1
109         if len(widths) > 1:
110             sep = (total - sum(widths)) / (len(widths) - 1)
111         else:
112             sep = 0
113         offsets_ = np.cumsum([0] + [w + sep for w in widths])
114         offsets = offsets_[:-1]
115         return total, offsets
116 
117     elif mode == "equal":
118         maxh = max(widths)
119         if total is None:
120             if sep is None:
121                 raise ValueError("total and sep cannot both be None when "
122                                  "using layout mode 'equal'")
123             total = (maxh + sep) * len(widths)
124         else:
125             sep = total / len(widths) - maxh
126         offsets = (maxh + sep) * np.arange(len(widths))
127         return total, offsets
128

130 def _get_aligned_offsets(hd_list, height, align="baseline"):
131     """
132     Align boxes each specified by their ``(height, descent)`` pair.
133 
134     For simplicity of the description, the terminology used here assumes a
135     horizontal layout (i.e., vertical alignment), but the function works
136     equally for a vertical layout.
137 
138     Parameters
139     ----------
140     hd_list
141         List of (height, xdescent) of boxes to be aligned.
142     height : float or None
143         Intended total height. If None, the maximum of the heights in *hd_list*
144         is used.
145     align : {'baseline', 'left', 'top', 'right', 'bottom', 'center'}
146         The alignment anchor of the boxes.
147 
148     Returns
149     -------
150     height
151         The total height of the packing (if a value was originally passed in,
152         it is returned without checking that it is actually large enough).
153     descent
154         The descent of the packing.
155     offsets
156         The bottom offsets of the boxes.
157     """
158 
159     if height is None:
160         height = max(h for h, d in hd_list)
161     _api.check_in_list(
162         ["baseline", "left", "top", "right", "bottom", "center"], align=align)
163 
164     if align == "baseline":
165         height_descent = max(h - d for h, d in hd_list)
166         descent = max(d for h, d in hd_list)
167         height = height_descent + descent
168         offsets = [0. for h, d in hd_list]
169     elif align in ["left", "top"]:
170         descent = 0.
171         offsets = [d for h, d in hd_list]
172     elif align in ["right", "bottom"]:
173         descent = 0.
174         offsets = [height - h + d for h, d in hd_list]
175     elif align == "center":
176         descent = 0.
177         offsets = [(height - h) * .5 + d for h, d in hd_list]
178 
179     return height, descent, offsets

182 class OffsetBox(martist.Artist):
183     """
184     The OffsetBox is a simple container artist.
185 
186     The child artists are meant to be drawn at a relative position to its
187     parent.
188 
189     Being an artist itself, all parameters are passed on to `.Artist`.
190     """
191     def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
192         super().__init__(*args)
193         self._internal_update(kwargs)
194         # Clipping has not been implemented in the OffsetBox family, so
195         # disable the clip flag for consistency. It can always be turned back
196         # on to zero effect.
197         self.set_clip_on(False)
198         self._children = []
199         self._offset = (0, 0)
200 
201     def set_figure(self, fig):
202         """
203         Set the `.Figure` for the `.OffsetBox` and all its children.
204 
205         Parameters
206         ----------
207         fig : `~matplotlib.figure.Figure`
208         """
209         super().set_figure(fig)
210         for c in self.get_children():
211             c.set_figure(fig)
212 
213     @martist.Artist.axes.setter
214     def axes(self, ax):
215         # TODO deal with this better
216         martist.Artist.axes.fset(self, ax)
217         for c in self.get_children():
218             if c is not None:
219                 c.axes = ax
220 
221     def contains(self, mouseevent):
222         """
223         Delegate the mouse event contains-check to the children.
224 
225         As a container, the `.OffsetBox` does not respond itself to
226         mouseevents.
227 
228         Parameters
229         ----------
230         mouseevent : `matplotlib.backend_bases.MouseEvent`
231 
232         Returns
233         -------
234         contains : bool
235             Whether any values are within the radius.
236         details : dict
237             An artist-specific dictionary of details of the event context,
238             such as which points are contained in the pick radius. See the
239             individual Artist subclasses for details.
240 
241         See Also
242         --------
243         .Artist.contains
244         """
245         inside, info = self._default_contains(mouseevent)
246         if inside is not None:
247             return inside, info
248         for c in self.get_children():
249             a, b = c.contains(mouseevent)
250             if a:
251                 return a, b
252         return False, {}
253 
254     def set_offset(self, xy):
255         """
256         Set the offset.
257 
258         Parameters
259         ----------
260         xy : (float, float) or callable
261             The (x, y) coordinates of the offset in display units. These can
262             either be given explicitly as a tuple (x, y), or by providing a
263             function that converts the extent into the offset. This function
264             must have the signature::
265 
266                 def offset(width, height, xdescent, ydescent, renderer) \
267 -> (float, float)
268         """
269         self._offset = xy
270         self.stale = True
271 
272     def get_offset(self, width, height, xdescent, ydescent, renderer):
273         """
274         Return the offset as a tuple (x, y).
275 
276         The extent parameters have to be provided to handle the case where the
277         offset is dynamically determined by a callable (see
278         `~.OffsetBox.set_offset`).
279 
280         Parameters
281         ----------
282         width, height, xdescent, ydescent
283             Extent parameters.
284         renderer : `.RendererBase` subclass
285 
286         """
287         return (self._offset(width, height, xdescent, ydescent, renderer)
288                 if callable(self._offset)
289                 else self._offset)
290 
291     def set_width(self, width):
292         """
293         Set the width of the box.
294 
295         Parameters
296         ----------
297         width : float
298         """
299         self.width = width
300         self.stale = True
301 
302     def set_height(self, height):
303         """
304         Set the height of the box.
305 
306         Parameters
307         ----------
308         height : float
309         """
310         self.height = height
311         self.stale = True
312 
313     def get_visible_children(self):
314         r"""Return a list of the visible child `.Artist`\s."""
315         return [c for c in self._children if c.get_visible()]
316 
317     def get_children(self):
318         r"""Return a list of the child `.Artist`\s."""
319         return self._children
320 
321     def get_extent_offsets(self, renderer):
322         """
323         Update offset of the children and return the extent of the box.
324 
325         Parameters
326         ----------
327         renderer : `.RendererBase` subclass
328 
329         Returns
330         -------
331         width
332         height
333         xdescent
334         ydescent
335         list of (xoffset, yoffset) pairs
336         """
337         raise NotImplementedError(
338             "get_extent_offsets must be overridden in derived classes.")
339 
340     def get_extent(self, renderer):
341         """Return a tuple ``width, height, xdescent, ydescent`` of the box."""
342         w, h, xd, yd, offsets = self.get_extent_offsets(renderer)
343         return w, h, xd, yd
344 
345     def get_window_extent(self, renderer=None):
346         # docstring inherited
347         if renderer is None:
348             renderer = self.figure._get_renderer()
349         w, h, xd, yd = self.get_extent(renderer)
350         # Some subclasses redefine get_offset to take no args.
351         try:
352             px, py = self.get_offset(w, h, xd, yd, renderer)
353         except TypeError:
354             px, py = self.get_offset()
355         return mtransforms.Bbox.from_bounds(px - xd, py - yd, w, h)
356 
357     def draw(self, renderer):
358         """
359         Update the location of children if necessary and draw them
360         to the given *renderer*.
361         """
362         w, h, xdescent, ydescent, offsets = self.get_extent_offsets(renderer)
363         px, py = self.get_offset(w, h, xdescent, ydescent, renderer)
364         for c, (ox, oy) in zip(self.get_visible_children(), offsets):
365             c.set_offset((px + ox, py + oy))
366             c.draw(renderer)
367         bbox_artist(self, renderer, fill=False, props=dict(pad=0.))
368         self.stale = False

371 class PackerBase(OffsetBox):
372     def __init__(self, pad=None, sep=None, width=None, height=None,
373                  align="baseline", mode="fixed", children=None):
374         """
375         Parameters
376         ----------
377         pad : float, optional
378             The boundary padding in points.
379 
380         sep : float, optional
381             The spacing between items in points.
382 
383         width, height : float, optional
384             Width and height of the container box in pixels, calculated if
385             *None*.
386 
387         align : {'top', 'bottom', 'left', 'right', 'center', 'baseline'}, \
388 default: 'baseline'
389             Alignment of boxes.
390 
391         mode : {'fixed', 'expand', 'equal'}, default: 'fixed'
392             The packing mode.
393 
394             - 'fixed' packs the given `.Artist`\\s tight with *sep* spacing.
395             - 'expand' uses the maximal available space to distribute the
396               artists with equal spacing in between.
397             - 'equal': Each artist an equal fraction of the available space
398               and is left-aligned (or top-aligned) therein.
399 
400         children : list of `.Artist`
401             The artists to pack.
402 
403         Notes
404         -----
405         *pad* and *sep* are in points and will be scaled with the renderer
406         dpi, while *width* and *height* are in pixels.
407         """
408         super().__init__()
409         self.height = height
410         self.width = width
411         self.sep = sep
412         self.pad = pad
413         self.mode = mode
414         self.align = align
415         self._children = children

418 class VPacker(PackerBase):
419     """
420     VPacker packs its children vertically, automatically adjusting their
421     relative positions at draw time.
422     """
423 
424     def get_extent_offsets(self, renderer):
425         # docstring inherited
426         dpicor = renderer.points_to_pixels(1.)
427         pad = self.pad * dpicor
428         sep = self.sep * dpicor
429 
430         if self.width is not None:
431             for c in self.get_visible_children():
432                 if isinstance(c, PackerBase) and c.mode == "expand":
433                     c.set_width(self.width)
434 
435         whd_list = [c.get_extent(renderer)
436                     for c in self.get_visible_children()]
437         whd_list = [(w, h, xd, (h - yd)) for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
438 
439         wd_list = [(w, xd) for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
440         width, xdescent, xoffsets = _get_aligned_offsets(wd_list,
441                                                          self.width,
442                                                          self.align)
443 
444         pack_list = [h for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
445         height, yoffsets_ = _get_packed_offsets(pack_list, self.height,
446                                                 sep, self.mode)
447 
448         yoffsets = yoffsets_ + [yd for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
449         ydescent = height - yoffsets[0]
450         yoffsets = height - yoffsets
451 
452         yoffsets = yoffsets - ydescent
453 
454         return (width + 2 * pad, height + 2 * pad,
455                 xdescent + pad, ydescent + pad,
456                 list(zip(xoffsets, yoffsets)))
457

459 class HPacker(PackerBase):
460     """
461     HPacker packs its children horizontally, automatically adjusting their
462     relative positions at draw time.
463     """
464 
465     def get_extent_offsets(self, renderer):
466         # docstring inherited
467         dpicor = renderer.points_to_pixels(1.)
468         pad = self.pad * dpicor
469         sep = self.sep * dpicor
470 
471         whd_list = [c.get_extent(renderer)
472                     for c in self.get_visible_children()]
473 
474         if not whd_list:
475             return 2 * pad, 2 * pad, pad, pad, []
476 
477         hd_list = [(h, yd) for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
478         height, ydescent, yoffsets = _get_aligned_offsets(hd_list,
479                                                           self.height,
480                                                           self.align)
481 
482         pack_list = [w for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
483         width, xoffsets_ = _get_packed_offsets(pack_list, self.width,
484                                                sep, self.mode)
485 
486         xoffsets = xoffsets_ + [xd for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
487 
488         xdescent = whd_list[0][2]
489         xoffsets = xoffsets - xdescent
490 
491         return (width + 2 * pad, height + 2 * pad,
492                 xdescent + pad, ydescent + pad,
493                 list(zip(xoffsets, yoffsets)))

496 class PaddedBox(OffsetBox):
497     """
498     A container to add a padding around an `.Artist`.
499 
500     The `.PaddedBox` contains a `.FancyBboxPatch` that is used to visualize
501     it when rendering.
502     """
503 
504     @_api.make_keyword_only("3.6", name="draw_frame")
505     def __init__(self, child, pad=None, draw_frame=False, patch_attrs=None):
506         """
507         Parameters
508         ----------
509         child : `~matplotlib.artist.Artist`
510             The contained `.Artist`.
511         pad : float
512             The padding in points. This will be scaled with the renderer dpi.
513             In contrast, *width* and *height* are in *pixels* and thus not
514             scaled.
515         draw_frame : bool
516             Whether to draw the contained `.FancyBboxPatch`.
517         patch_attrs : dict or None
518             Additional parameters passed to the contained `.FancyBboxPatch`.
519         """
520         super().__init__()
521         self.pad = pad
522         self._children = [child]
523         self.patch = FancyBboxPatch(
524             xy=(0.0, 0.0), width=1., height=1.,
525             facecolor='w', edgecolor='k',
526             mutation_scale=1,  # self.prop.get_size_in_points(),
527             snap=True,
528             visible=draw_frame,
529             boxstyle="square,pad=0",
530         )
531         if patch_attrs is not None:
532             self.patch.update(patch_attrs)
533 
534     def get_extent_offsets(self, renderer):
535         # docstring inherited.
536         dpicor = renderer.points_to_pixels(1.)
537         pad = self.pad * dpicor
538         w, h, xd, yd = self._children[0].get_extent(renderer)
539         return (w + 2 * pad, h + 2 * pad, xd + pad, yd + pad,
540                 [(0, 0)])
541 
542     def draw(self, renderer):
543         # docstring inherited
544         w, h, xdescent, ydescent, offsets = self.get_extent_offsets(renderer)
545         px, py = self.get_offset(w, h, xdescent, ydescent, renderer)
546         for c, (ox, oy) in zip(self.get_visible_children(), offsets):
547             c.set_offset((px + ox, py + oy))
548 
549         self.draw_frame(renderer)
550 
551         for c in self.get_visible_children():
552             c.draw(renderer)
553 
554         self.stale = False
555 
556     def update_frame(self, bbox, fontsize=None):
557         self.patch.set_bounds(bbox.bounds)
558         if fontsize:
559             self.patch.set_mutation_scale(fontsize)
560         self.stale = True
561 
562     def draw_frame(self, renderer):
563         # update the location and size of the legend
564         self.update_frame(self.get_window_extent(renderer))
565         self.patch.draw(renderer)

568 class DrawingArea(OffsetBox):
569     """
570     The DrawingArea can contain any Artist as a child. The DrawingArea
571     has a fixed width and height. The position of children relative to
572     the parent is fixed. The children can be clipped at the
573     boundaries of the parent.
574     """
575 
576     def __init__(self, width, height, xdescent=0., ydescent=0., clip=False):
577         """
578         Parameters
579         ----------
580         width, height : float
581             Width and height of the container box.
582         xdescent, ydescent : float
583             Descent of the box in x- and y-direction.
584         clip : bool
585             Whether to clip the children to the box.
586         """
587         super().__init__()
588         self.width = width
589         self.height = height
590         self.xdescent = xdescent
591         self.ydescent = ydescent
592         self._clip_children = clip
593         self.offset_transform = mtransforms.Affine2D()
594         self.dpi_transform = mtransforms.Affine2D()
595 
596     @property
597     def clip_children(self):
598         """
599         If the children of this DrawingArea should be clipped
600         by DrawingArea bounding box.
601         """
602         return self._clip_children
603 
604     @clip_children.setter
605     def clip_children(self, val):
606         self._clip_children = bool(val)
607         self.stale = True
608 
609     def get_transform(self):
610         """
611         Return the `~matplotlib.transforms.Transform` applied to the children.
612         """
613         return self.dpi_transform + self.offset_transform
614 
615     def set_transform(self, t):
616         """
617         set_transform is ignored.
618         """
619 
620     def set_offset(self, xy):
621         """
622         Set the offset of the container.
623 
624         Parameters
625         ----------
626         xy : (float, float)
627             The (x, y) coordinates of the offset in display units.
628         """
629         self._offset = xy
630         self.offset_transform.clear()
631         self.offset_transform.translate(xy[0], xy[1])
632         self.stale = True
633 
634     def get_offset(self):
635         """Return offset of the container."""
636         return self._offset
637 
638     def get_extent(self, renderer):
639         """Return width, height, xdescent, ydescent of box."""
640         dpi_cor = renderer.points_to_pixels(1.)
641         return (self.width * dpi_cor, self.height * dpi_cor,
642                 self.xdescent * dpi_cor, self.ydescent * dpi_cor)
643 
644     def add_artist(self, a):
645         """Add an `.Artist` to the container box."""
646         self._children.append(a)
647         if not a.is_transform_set():
648             a.set_transform(self.get_transform())
649         if self.axes is not None:
650             a.axes = self.axes
651         fig = self.figure
652         if fig is not None:
653             a.set_figure(fig)
654 
655     def draw(self, renderer):
656         # docstring inherited
657 
658         dpi_cor = renderer.points_to_pixels(1.)
659         self.dpi_transform.clear()
660         self.dpi_transform.scale(dpi_cor)
661 
662         # At this point the DrawingArea has a transform
663         # to the display space so the path created is
664         # good for clipping children
665         tpath = mtransforms.TransformedPath(
666             mpath.Path([[0, 0], [0, self.height],
667                         [self.width, self.height],
668                         [self.width, 0]]),
669             self.get_transform())
670         for c in self._children:
671             if self._clip_children and not (c.clipbox or c._clippath):
672                 c.set_clip_path(tpath)
673             c.draw(renderer)
674 
675         bbox_artist(self, renderer, fill=False, props=dict(pad=0.))
676         self.stale = False

695         ----------

820         # lower-left corner of the bbox of its children.

861     def get_extent(self, renderer):

863         _off = self.offset_transform.get_matrix()  # to be restored later

865         self.offset_transform.clear()

949         self.set_bbox_to_anchor(bbox_to_anchor, bbox_transform)

964                 self.prop.set_size(mpl.rcParams["legend.fontsize"])

966         self.patch = FancyBboxPatch(
967             xy=(0.0, 0.0), width=1., height=1.,
968             facecolor='w', edgecolor='k',
969             mutation_scale=self.prop.get_size_in_points(),
970             snap=True,
971             visible=frameon,

1017         *bbox* can be a Bbox instance, a list of [left, bottom, width,
1018         height], or a list of [left, bottom] where the width and
1019         height will be assumed to be zero. The bbox will be
1020         transformed to display coordinate by the given transform.
1021         """
1022         if bbox is None or isinstance(bbox, BboxBase):

1026                 l = len(bbox)
1027             except TypeError as err:

1030             if l == 2:

1038     def get_offset(self, width, height, xdescent, ydescent, renderer):
1039         # docstring inherited

1042                * renderer.points_to_pixels(self.prop.get_size_in_points()))
1043         bbox_to_anchor = self.get_bbox_to_anchor()

1050             self.patch.set_mutation_scale(fontsize)

1053         # docstring inherited

1055             return
1056 
1057         # update the location and size of the legend
1058         bbox = self.get_window_extent(renderer)
1059         fontsize = renderer.points_to_pixels(self.prop.get_size_in_points())
1060         self.update_frame(bbox, fontsize)
1061         self.patch.draw(renderer)
1062 
1063         width, height, xdescent, ydescent = self.get_extent(renderer)
1064 
1065         px, py = self.get_offset(width, height, xdescent, ydescent, renderer)
1066 
1067         self.get_child().set_offset((px, py))
1068         self.get_child().draw(renderer)
1069         self.stale = False

1072 def _get_anchored_bbox(loc, bbox, parentbbox, borderpad):
1073     """
1074     Return the (x, y) position of the *bbox* anchored at the *parentbbox* with
1075     the *loc* code with the *borderpad*.

1077     # This is only called internally and *loc* should already have been
1078     # validated.  If 0 (None), we just let ``bbox.anchored`` raise.
1079     c = [None, "NE", "NW", "SW", "SE", "E", "W", "E", "S", "N", "C"][loc]
1080     container = parentbbox.padded(-borderpad)
1081     return bbox.anchored(c, container=container).p0

55 def _get_packed_offsets(widths, total, sep, mode="fixed"):
56     r"""
57     Pack boxes specified by their *widths*.
58 
59     For simplicity of the description, the terminology used here assumes a
60     horizontal layout, but the function works equally for a vertical layout.
61 
62     There are three packing *mode*\s:
63 
64     - 'fixed': The elements are packed tight to the left with a spacing of
65       *sep* in between. If *total* is *None* the returned total will be the
66       right edge of the last box. A non-*None* total will be passed unchecked
67       to the output. In particular this means that right edge of the last
68       box may be further to the right than the returned total.
69 
70     - 'expand': Distribute the boxes with equal spacing so that the left edge
71       of the first box is at 0, and the right edge of the last box is at
72       *total*. The parameter *sep* is ignored in this mode. A total of *None*
73       is accepted and considered equal to 1. The total is returned unchanged
74       (except for the conversion *None* to 1). If the total is smaller than
75       the sum of the widths, the laid out boxes will overlap.
76 
77     - 'equal': If *total* is given, the total space is divided in N equal
78       ranges and each box is left-aligned within its subspace.
79       Otherwise (*total* is *None*), *sep* must be provided and each box is
80       left-aligned in its subspace of width ``(max(widths) + sep)``. The
81       total width is then calculated to be ``N * (max(widths) + sep)``.
82 
83     Parameters
84     ----------
85     widths : list of float
86         Widths of boxes to be packed.
87     total : float or None
88         Intended total length. *None* if not used.
89     sep : float
90         Spacing between boxes.
91     mode : {'fixed', 'expand', 'equal'}
92         The packing mode.
93 
94     Returns
95     -------
96     total : float
97         The total width needed to accommodate the laid out boxes.
98     offsets : array of float
99         The left offsets of the boxes.
100     """
101     _api.check_in_list(["fixed", "expand", "equal"], mode=mode)
102 
103     if mode == "fixed":
104         offsets_ = np.cumsum([0] + [w + sep for w in widths])
105         offsets = offsets_[:-1]
106         if total is None:
107             total = offsets_[-1] - sep
108         return total, offsets
109 
110     elif mode == "expand":
111         # This is a bit of a hack to avoid a TypeError when *total*
112         # is None and used in conjugation with tight layout.
113         if total is None:
114             total = 1
115         if len(widths) > 1:
116             sep = (total - sum(widths)) / (len(widths) - 1)
117         else:
118             sep = 0
119         offsets_ = np.cumsum([0] + [w + sep for w in widths])
120         offsets = offsets_[:-1]
121         return total, offsets
122 
123     elif mode == "equal":
124         maxh = max(widths)
125         if total is None:
126             if sep is None:
127                 raise ValueError("total and sep cannot both be None when "
128                                  "using layout mode 'equal'")
129             total = (maxh + sep) * len(widths)
130         else:
131             sep = total / len(widths) - maxh
132         offsets = (maxh + sep) * np.arange(len(widths))
133         return total, offsets

193     parent.

196     """
197     def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
198         super().__init__(*args)
199         self._internal_update(kwargs)

201         # disable the clip flag for consistency. It can always be turned back
202         # on to zero effect.

210

212         ----------

217             c.set_figure(fig)
218 
219     @martist.Artist.axes.setter
220     def axes(self, ax):

222         martist.Artist.axes.fset(self, ax)
223         for c in self.get_children():
224             if c is not None:
225                 c.axes = ax

227     def contains(self, mouseevent):
228         """
229         Delegate the mouse event contains-check to the children.
230 
231         As a container, the `.OffsetBox` does not respond itself to
232         mouseevents.
233 
234         Parameters
235         ----------
236         mouseevent : `matplotlib.backend_bases.MouseEvent`
237 
238         Returns
239         -------
240         contains : bool
241             Whether any values are within the radius.
242         details : dict
243             An artist-specific dictionary of details of the event context,
244             such as which points are contained in the pick radius. See the
245             individual Artist subclasses for details.
246 
247         See Also
248         --------
249         .Artist.contains
250         """
251         inside, info = self._default_contains(mouseevent)
252         if inside is not None:
253             return inside, info

260     def set_offset(self, xy):
261         """
262         Set the offset.
263 
264         Parameters
265         ----------
266         xy : (float, float) or callable
267             The (x, y) coordinates of the offset in display units. These can
268             either be given explicitly as a tuple (x, y), or by providing a
269             function that converts the extent into the offset. This function
270             must have the signature::
271 
272                 def offset(width, height, xdescent, ydescent, renderer) \
273 -> (float, float)

278     def get_offset(self, width, height, xdescent, ydescent, renderer):

283         offset is dynamically determined by a callable (see
284         `~.OffsetBox.set_offset`).

287         ----------
288         width, height, xdescent, ydescent

290         renderer : `.RendererBase` subclass
291 
292         """
293         return (self._offset(width, height, xdescent, ydescent, renderer)
294                 if callable(self._offset)
295                 else self._offset)
296 
297     def set_width(self, width):
298         """
299         Set the width of the box.
300 
301         Parameters
302         ----------
303         width : float
304         """
305         self.width = width
306         self.stale = True
307 
308     def set_height(self, height):

310         Set the height of the box.
311 
312         Parameters
313         ----------
314         height : float
315         """
316         self.height = height
317         self.stale = True
318 
319     def get_visible_children(self):
320         r"""Return a list of the visible child `.Artist`\s."""
321         return [c for c in self._children if c.get_visible()]
322 
323     def get_children(self):
324         r"""Return a list of the child `.Artist`\s."""
325         return self._children
326 
327     def get_extent_offsets(self, renderer):
328         """
329         Update offset of the children and return the extent of the box.
330 
331         Parameters
332         ----------
333         renderer : `.RendererBase` subclass
334 
335         Returns
336         -------
337         width
338         height
339         xdescent
340         ydescent
341         list of (xoffset, yoffset) pairs
342         """
343         raise NotImplementedError(
344             "get_extent_offsets must be overridden in derived classes.")
345 
346     def get_extent(self, renderer):
347         """Return a tuple ``width, height, xdescent, ydescent`` of the box."""
348         w, h, xd, yd, offsets = self.get_extent_offsets(renderer)
349         return w, h, xd, yd
350 
351     def get_window_extent(self, renderer=None):
352         # docstring inherited
353         if renderer is None:
354             renderer = self.figure._get_renderer()
355         w, h, xd, yd = self.get_extent(renderer)
356         # Some subclasses redefine get_offset to take no args.
357         try:
358             px, py = self.get_offset(w, h, xd, yd, renderer)
359         except TypeError:
360             px, py = self.get_offset()
361         return mtransforms.Bbox.from_bounds(px - xd, py - yd, w, h)
362 
363     def draw(self, renderer):
364         """

366         to the given *renderer*.
367         """
368         w, h, xdescent, ydescent, offsets = self.get_extent_offsets(renderer)
369         px, py = self.get_offset(w, h, xdescent, ydescent, renderer)
370         for c, (ox, oy) in zip(self.get_visible_children(), offsets):
371             c.set_offset((px + ox, py + oy))
372             c.draw(renderer)
373         _bbox_artist(self, renderer, fill=False, props=dict(pad=0.))
374         self.stale = False

379                  align="baseline", mode="fixed", children=None):
380         """
381         Parameters
382         ----------
383         pad : float, default: 0.0
384             The boundary padding in points.
385

412         dpi, while *width* and *height* are in pixels.
413         """

424 class VPacker(PackerBase):
425     """
426     VPacker packs its children vertically, automatically adjusting their
427     relative positions at draw time.
428     """
429 
430     def get_extent_offsets(self, renderer):
431         # docstring inherited
432         dpicor = renderer.points_to_pixels(1.)
433         pad = self.pad * dpicor
434         sep = self.sep * dpicor
435 
436         if self.width is not None:
437             for c in self.get_visible_children():
438                 if isinstance(c, PackerBase) and c.mode == "expand":
439                     c.set_width(self.width)
440 
441         whd_list = [c.get_extent(renderer)
442                     for c in self.get_visible_children()]
443         whd_list = [(w, h, xd, (h - yd)) for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
444 
445         wd_list = [(w, xd) for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
446         width, xdescent, xoffsets = _get_aligned_offsets(wd_list,
447                                                          self.width,
448                                                          self.align)
449 
450         pack_list = [h for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
451         height, yoffsets_ = _get_packed_offsets(pack_list, self.height,
452                                                 sep, self.mode)
453 
454         yoffsets = yoffsets_ + [yd for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
455         ydescent = height - yoffsets[0]
456         yoffsets = height - yoffsets
457 
458         yoffsets = yoffsets - ydescent
459 
460         return (width + 2 * pad, height + 2 * pad,
461                 xdescent + pad, ydescent + pad,
462                 list(zip(xoffsets, yoffsets)))
463 
464 
465 class HPacker(PackerBase):
466     """
467     HPacker packs its children horizontally, automatically adjusting their
468     relative positions at draw time.
469     """
470 
471     def get_extent_offsets(self, renderer):
472         # docstring inherited
473         dpicor = renderer.points_to_pixels(1.)
474         pad = self.pad * dpicor
475         sep = self.sep * dpicor
476 
477         whd_list = [c.get_extent(renderer)
478                     for c in self.get_visible_children()]
479 
480         if not whd_list:
481             return 2 * pad, 2 * pad, pad, pad, []
482 
483         hd_list = [(h, yd) for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
484         height, ydescent, yoffsets = _get_aligned_offsets(hd_list,
485                                                           self.height,
486                                                           self.align)
487 
488         pack_list = [w for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
489         width, xoffsets_ = _get_packed_offsets(pack_list, self.width,
490                                                sep, self.mode)
491 
492         xoffsets = xoffsets_ + [xd for w, h, xd, yd in whd_list]
493 
494         xdescent = whd_list[0][2]
495         xoffsets = xoffsets - xdescent
496 
497         return (width + 2 * pad, height + 2 * pad,
498                 xdescent + pad, ydescent + pad,
499                 list(zip(xoffsets, yoffsets)))

808     """
809     Offset Box with the aux_transform. Its children will be
810     transformed with the aux_transform first then will be
811     offsetted. The absolute coordinate of the aux_transform is meaning
812     as it will be automatically adjust so that the left-lower corner
813     of the bounding box of children will be set to (0, 0) before the
814     offset transform.
815 
816     It is similar to drawing area, except that the extent of the box
817     is not predetermined but calculated from the window extent of its
818     children. Furthermore, the extent of the children will be
819     calculated in the transformed coordinate.
820     """
821     def __init__(self, aux_transform):
822         self.aux_transform = aux_transform
823         super().__init__()
824         self.offset_transform = mtransforms.Affine2D()
825         # ref_offset_transform makes offset_transform always relative to the
826         # lower-left corner of the bbox of its children.
827         self.ref_offset_transform = mtransforms.Affine2D()
828 
829     def add_artist(self, a):
830         """Add an `.Artist` to the container box."""
831         self._children.append(a)
832         a.set_transform(self.get_transform())
833         self.stale = True
834 
835     def get_transform(self):
836         """
837         Return the :class:`~matplotlib.transforms.Transform` applied
838         to the children
839         """
840         return (self.aux_transform
841                 + self.ref_offset_transform
842                 + self.offset_transform)
843 
844     def set_transform(self, t):
845         """
846         set_transform is ignored.
847         """
848 
849     def set_offset(self, xy):
850         """
851         Set the offset of the container.
852 
853         Parameters
854         ----------
855         xy : (float, float)
856             The (x, y) coordinates of the offset in display units.
857         """
858         self._offset = xy
859         self.offset_transform.clear()
860         self.offset_transform.translate(xy[0], xy[1])
861         self.stale = True
862 
863     def get_offset(self):
864         """Return offset of the container."""
865         return self._offset
866 
867     def get_extent(self, renderer):
868         # clear the offset transforms
869         _off = self.offset_transform.get_matrix()  # to be restored later
870         self.ref_offset_transform.clear()
871         self.offset_transform.clear()
872         # calculate the extent
873         bboxes = [c.get_window_extent(renderer) for c in self._children]
874         ub = mtransforms.Bbox.union(bboxes)
875         # adjust ref_offset_transform
876         self.ref_offset_transform.translate(-ub.x0, -ub.y0)
877         # restore offset transform
878         self.offset_transform.set_matrix(_off)
879 
880         return ub.width, ub.height, 0., 0.
881 
882     def draw(self, renderer):
883         # docstring inherited
884         for c in self._children:
885             c.draw(renderer)
886         _bbox_artist(self, renderer, fill=False, props=dict(pad=0.))
887         self.stale = False

1078 def _get_anchored_bbox(loc, bbox, parentbbox, borderpad):
1079     """
1080     Return the (x, y) position of the *bbox* anchored at the *parentbbox* with
1081     the *loc* code with the *borderpad*.

1083     # This is only called internally and *loc* should already have been
1084     # validated.  If 0 (None), we just let ``bbox.anchored`` raise.
1085     c = [None, "NE", "NW", "SW", "SE", "E", "W", "E", "S", "N", "C"][loc]
1086     container = parentbbox.padded(-borderpad)
1087     return bbox.anchored(c, container=container).p0

1465 class DraggableBase:
1466     """
1467     Helper base class for a draggable artist (legend, offsetbox).
1468 
1469     Derived classes must override the following methods::
1470 
1471         def save_offset(self):
1472             '''
1473             Called when the object is picked for dragging; should save the
1474             reference position of the artist.
1475             '''
1476 
1477         def update_offset(self, dx, dy):
1478             '''
1479             Called during the dragging; (*dx*, *dy*) is the pixel offset from
1480             the point where the mouse drag started.
1481             '''
1482 
1483     Optionally, you may override the following method::
1484 
1485         def finalize_offset(self):
1486             '''Called when the mouse is released.'''
1487 
1488     In the current implementation of `.DraggableLegend` and
1489     `DraggableAnnotation`, `update_offset` places the artists in display
1490     coordinates, and `finalize_offset` recalculates their position in axes
1491     coordinate and set a relevant attribute.
1492     """
1493 
1494     def __init__(self, ref_artist, use_blit=False):
1495         self.ref_artist = ref_artist
1496         if not ref_artist.pickable():
1497             ref_artist.set_picker(True)
1498         self.got_artist = False
1499         self.canvas = self.ref_artist.figure.canvas
1500         self._use_blit = use_blit and self.canvas.supports_blit
1501         self.cids = [
1502             self.canvas.callbacks._connect_picklable(
1503                 'pick_event', self.on_pick),
1504             self.canvas.callbacks._connect_picklable(
1505                 'button_release_event', self.on_release),
1506         ]
1507 
1508     def on_motion(self, evt):
1509         if self._check_still_parented() and self.got_artist:
1510             dx = evt.x - self.mouse_x
1511             dy = evt.y - self.mouse_y
1512             self.update_offset(dx, dy)
1513             if self._use_blit:
1514                 self.canvas.restore_region(self.background)
1515                 self.ref_artist.draw(
1516                     self.ref_artist.figure._get_renderer())
1517                 self.canvas.blit()
1518             else:
1519                 self.canvas.draw()
1520 
1521     def on_pick(self, evt):
1522         if self._check_still_parented() and evt.artist == self.ref_artist:
1523             self.mouse_x = evt.mouseevent.x
1524             self.mouse_y = evt.mouseevent.y
1525             self.got_artist = True

38 def _append_path(ctx, path, transform, clip=None):
39     for points, code in path.iter_segments(
40             transform, remove_nans=True, clip=clip):
41         if code == Path.MOVETO:
42             ctx.move_to(*points)
43         elif code == Path.CLOSEPOLY:
44             ctx.close_path()
45         elif code == Path.LINETO:
46             ctx.line_to(*points)
47         elif code == Path.CURVE3:
48             cur = np.asarray(ctx.get_current_point())
49             a = points[:2]
50             b = points[-2:]
51             ctx.curve_to(*(cur / 3 + a * 2 / 3), *(a * 2 / 3 + b / 3), *b)
52         elif code == Path.CURVE4:
53             ctx.curve_to(*points)

149                      + Affine2D().scale(1, -1).translate(0, self.height))

153                 path.iter_segments(transform, simplify=False)):

26 def _get_textbox(text, renderer):
27     """
28     Calculate the bounding box of the text.
29 
30     The bbox position takes text rotation into account, but the width and
31     height are those of the unrotated box (unlike `.Text.get_window_extent`).
32     """
33     # TODO : This function may move into the Text class as a method. As a
34     # matter of fact, the information from the _get_textbox function
35     # should be available during the Text._get_layout() call, which is
36     # called within the _get_textbox. So, it would better to move this
37     # function as a method with some refactoring of _get_layout method.
38 
39     projected_xs = []
40     projected_ys = []
41 
42     theta = np.deg2rad(text.get_rotation())
43     tr = Affine2D().rotate(-theta)
44 
45     _, parts, d = text._get_layout(renderer)
46 
47     for t, wh, x, y in parts:
48         w, h = wh
49 
50         xt1, yt1 = tr.transform((x, y))
51         yt1 -= d
52         xt2, yt2 = xt1 + w, yt1 + h
53 
54         projected_xs.extend([xt1, xt2])
55         projected_ys.extend([yt1, yt2])
56 
57     xt_box, yt_box = min(projected_xs), min(projected_ys)
58     w_box, h_box = max(projected_xs) - xt_box, max(projected_ys) - yt_box
59 
60     x_box, y_box = Affine2D().rotate(theta).transform((xt_box, yt_box))
61 
62     return x_box, y_box, w_box, h_box

327     def _get_layout(self, renderer):
328         """
329         Return the extent (bbox) of the text together with
330         multiple-alignment information. Note that it returns an extent
331         of a rotated text when necessary.
332         """
333         thisx, thisy = 0.0, 0.0
334         lines = self._get_wrapped_text().split("\n")  # Ensures lines is not empty.
335 
336         ws = []
337         hs = []
338         xs = []
339         ys = []
340 
341         # Full vertical extent of font, including ascenders and descenders:
342         _, lp_h, lp_d = _get_text_metrics_with_cache(
343             renderer, "lp", self._fontproperties,
344             ismath="TeX" if self.get_usetex() else False, dpi=self.figure.dpi)
345         min_dy = (lp_h - lp_d) * self._linespacing
346 
347         for i, line in enumerate(lines):
348             clean_line, ismath = self._preprocess_math(line)
349             if clean_line:
350                 w, h, d = _get_text_metrics_with_cache(
351                     renderer, clean_line, self._fontproperties,
352                     ismath=ismath, dpi=self.figure.dpi)
353             else:
354                 w = h = d = 0
355 
356             # For multiline text, increase the line spacing when the text
357             # net-height (excluding baseline) is larger than that of a "l"
358             # (e.g., use of superscripts), which seems what TeX does.
359             h = max(h, lp_h)
360             d = max(d, lp_d)
361 
362             ws.append(w)
363             hs.append(h)
364 
365             # Metrics of the last line that are needed later:
366             baseline = (h - d) - thisy
367 
368             if i == 0:
369                 # position at baseline
370                 thisy = -(h - d)
371             else:
372                 # put baseline a good distance from bottom of previous line
373                 thisy -= max(min_dy, (h - d) * self._linespacing)
374 
375             xs.append(thisx)  # == 0.
376             ys.append(thisy)
377 
378             thisy -= d
379 
380         # Metrics of the last line that are needed later:
381         descent = d
382 
383         # Bounding box definition:
384         width = max(ws)
385         xmin = 0
386         xmax = width
387         ymax = 0
388         ymin = ys[-1] - descent  # baseline of last line minus its descent
389 
390         # get the rotation matrix
391         M = Affine2D().rotate_deg(self.get_rotation())
392 
393         # now offset the individual text lines within the box
394         malign = self._get_multialignment()
395         if malign == 'left':
396             offset_layout = [(x, y) for x, y in zip(xs, ys)]
397         elif malign == 'center':
398             offset_layout = [(x + width / 2 - w / 2, y)
399                              for x, y, w in zip(xs, ys, ws)]
400         elif malign == 'right':
401             offset_layout = [(x + width - w, y)
402                              for x, y, w in zip(xs, ys, ws)]
403 
404         # the corners of the unrotated bounding box
405         corners_horiz = np.array(
406             [(xmin, ymin), (xmin, ymax), (xmax, ymax), (xmax, ymin)])
407 
408         # now rotate the bbox
409         corners_rotated = M.transform(corners_horiz)
410         # compute the bounds of the rotated box
411         xmin = corners_rotated[:, 0].min()
412         xmax = corners_rotated[:, 0].max()
413         ymin = corners_rotated[:, 1].min()
414         ymax = corners_rotated[:, 1].max()
415         width = xmax - xmin
416         height = ymax - ymin
417 
418         # Now move the box to the target position offset the display
419         # bbox by alignment
420         halign = self._horizontalalignment
421         valign = self._verticalalignment
422 
423         rotation_mode = self.get_rotation_mode()
424         if rotation_mode != "anchor":
425             # compute the text location in display coords and the offsets
426             # necessary to align the bbox with that location
427             if halign == 'center':
428                 offsetx = (xmin + xmax) / 2
429             elif halign == 'right':
430                 offsetx = xmax
431             else:
432                 offsetx = xmin
433 
434             if valign == 'center':
435                 offsety = (ymin + ymax) / 2
436             elif valign == 'top':
437                 offsety = ymax
438             elif valign == 'baseline':
439                 offsety = ymin + descent
440             elif valign == 'center_baseline':
441                 offsety = ymin + height - baseline / 2.0
442             else:
443                 offsety = ymin
444         else:
445             xmin1, ymin1 = corners_horiz[0]
446             xmax1, ymax1 = corners_horiz[2]
447 
448             if halign == 'center':
449                 offsetx = (xmin1 + xmax1) / 2.0
450             elif halign == 'right':
451                 offsetx = xmax1
452             else:
453                 offsetx = xmin1
454 
455             if valign == 'center':
456                 offsety = (ymin1 + ymax1) / 2.0
457             elif valign == 'top':
458                 offsety = ymax1
459             elif valign == 'baseline':
460                 offsety = ymax1 - baseline
461             elif valign == 'center_baseline':
462                 offsety = ymax1 - baseline / 2.0
463             else:
464                 offsety = ymin1
465 
466             offsetx, offsety = M.transform((offsetx, offsety))
467 
468         xmin -= offsetx
469         ymin -= offsety
470 
471         bbox = Bbox.from_bounds(xmin, ymin, width, height)
472 
473         # now rotate the positions around the first (x, y) position
474         xys = M.transform(offset_layout) - (offsetx, offsety)
475 
476         return bbox, list(zip(lines, zip(ws, hs), *xys.T)), descent

605         left = self._get_dist_to_box(rotation, x0, y0, figure_box)
606         right = self._get_dist_to_box(
607             (180 + rotation) % 360, x0, y0, figure_box)
608 
609         if alignment == 'left':
610             line_width = left
611         elif alignment == 'right':
612             line_width = right
613         else:
614             line_width = 2 * min(left, right)
615 
616         return line_width
617 
618     def _get_dist_to_box(self, rotation, x0, y0, figure_box):
619         """
620         Return the distance from the given points to the boundaries of a
621         rotated box, in pixels.
622         """
623         if rotation > 270:
624             quad = rotation - 270
625             h1 = y0 / math.cos(math.radians(quad))
626             h2 = (figure_box.x1 - x0) / math.cos(math.radians(90 - quad))
627         elif rotation > 180:
628             quad = rotation - 180
629             h1 = x0 / math.cos(math.radians(quad))
630             h2 = y0 / math.cos(math.radians(90 - quad))
631         elif rotation > 90:
632             quad = rotation - 90
633             h1 = (figure_box.y1 - y0) / math.cos(math.radians(quad))
634             h2 = x0 / math.cos(math.radians(90 - quad))
635         else:
636             h1 = (figure_box.x1 - x0) / math.cos(math.radians(rotation))
637             h2 = (figure_box.y1 - y0) / math.cos(math.radians(90 - rotation))
638 
639         return min(h1, h2)
640

652     def _get_wrapped_text(self):
653         """
654         Return a copy of the text string with new lines added so that the text
655         is wrapped relative to the parent figure (if `get_wrap` is True).
656         """
657         if not self.get_wrap():
658             return self.get_text()
659 
660         # Not fit to handle breaking up latex syntax correctly, so
661         # ignore latex for now.
662         if self.get_usetex():
663             return self.get_text()
664 
665         # Build the line incrementally, for a more accurate measure of length
666         line_width = self._get_wrap_line_width()
667         wrapped_lines = []
668 
669         # New lines in the user's text force a split
670         unwrapped_lines = self.get_text().split('\n')
671 
672         # Now wrap each individual unwrapped line
673         for unwrapped_line in unwrapped_lines:
674 
675             sub_words = unwrapped_line.split(' ')
676             # Remove items from sub_words as we go, so stop when empty
677             while len(sub_words) > 0:
678                 if len(sub_words) == 1:
679                     # Only one word, so just add it to the end
680                     wrapped_lines.append(sub_words.pop(0))
681                     continue
682 
683                 for i in range(2, len(sub_words) + 1):
684                     # Get width of all words up to and including here
685                     line = ' '.join(sub_words[:i])
686                     current_width = self._get_rendered_text_width(line)
687 
688                     # If all these words are too wide, append all not including
689                     # last word
690                     if current_width > line_width:
691                         wrapped_lines.append(' '.join(sub_words[:i - 1]))
692                         sub_words = sub_words[i - 1:]
693                         break
694 
695                     # Otherwise if all words fit in the width, append them all
696                     elif i == len(sub_words):
697                         wrapped_lines.append(' '.join(sub_words[:i]))
698                         sub_words = []
699                         break
700 
701         return '\n'.join(wrapped_lines)
702 
703     @artist.allow_rasterization
704     def draw(self, renderer):
705         # docstring inherited
706 
707         if renderer is not None:
708             self._renderer = renderer
709         if not self.get_visible():
710             return
711         if self.get_text() == '':
712             return
713 
714         renderer.open_group('text', self.get_gid())
715 
716         with self._cm_set(text=self._get_wrapped_text()):
717             bbox, info, descent = self._get_layout(renderer)
718             trans = self.get_transform()
719 
720             # don't use self.get_position here, which refers to text
721             # position in Text:
722             posx = float(self.convert_xunits(self._x))
723             posy = float(self.convert_yunits(self._y))
724             posx, posy = trans.transform((posx, posy))
725             if not np.isfinite(posx) or not np.isfinite(posy):
726                 _log.warning("posx and posy should be finite values")
727                 return
728             canvasw, canvash = renderer.get_canvas_width_height()
729 
730             # Update the location and size of the bbox
731             # (`.patches.FancyBboxPatch`), and draw it.
732             if self._bbox_patch:
733                 self.update_bbox_position_size(renderer)
734                 self._bbox_patch.draw(renderer)
735 
736             gc = renderer.new_gc()
737             gc.set_foreground(self.get_color())
738             gc.set_alpha(self.get_alpha())
739             gc.set_url(self._url)
740             self._set_gc_clip(gc)
741 
742             angle = self.get_rotation()
743 
744             for line, wh, x, y in info:
745 
746                 mtext = self if len(info) == 1 else None
747                 x = x + posx
748                 y = y + posy
749                 if renderer.flipy():
750                     y = canvash - y
751                 clean_line, ismath = self._preprocess_math(line)
752 
753                 if self.get_path_effects():
754                     from matplotlib.patheffects import PathEffectRenderer
755                     textrenderer = PathEffectRenderer(
756                         self.get_path_effects(), renderer)
757                 else:
758                     textrenderer = renderer
759 
760                 if self.get_usetex():
761                     textrenderer.draw_tex(gc, x, y, clean_line,
762                                           self._fontproperties, angle,
763                                           mtext=mtext)
764                 else:
765                     textrenderer.draw_text(gc, x, y, clean_line,
766                                            self._fontproperties, angle,
767                                            ismath=ismath, mtext=mtext)
768 
769         gc.restore()
770         renderer.close_group('text')
771         self.stale = False
772

883     def get_window_extent(self, renderer=None, dpi=None):
884         """
885         Return the `.Bbox` bounding the text, in display units.
886 
887         In addition to being used internally, this is useful for specifying
888         clickable regions in a png file on a web page.
889 
890         Parameters
891         ----------
892         renderer : Renderer, optional
893             A renderer is needed to compute the bounding box.  If the artist
894             has already been drawn, the renderer is cached; thus, it is only
895             necessary to pass this argument when calling `get_window_extent`
896             before the first draw.  In practice, it is usually easier to
897             trigger a draw first, e.g. by calling
898             `~.Figure.draw_without_rendering` or ``plt.show()``.
899 
900         dpi : float, optional
901             The dpi value for computing the bbox, defaults to
902             ``self.figure.dpi`` (*not* the renderer dpi); should be set e.g. if
903             to match regions with a figure saved with a custom dpi value.
904         """
905         if not self.get_visible():
906             return Bbox.unit()
907         if dpi is None:
908             dpi = self.figure.dpi
909         if self.get_text() == '':
910             with cbook._setattr_cm(self.figure, dpi=dpi):
911                 tx, ty = self._get_xy_display()
912                 return Bbox.from_bounds(tx, ty, 0, 0)
913 
914         if renderer is not None:
915             self._renderer = renderer
916         if self._renderer is None:
917             self._renderer = self.figure._get_renderer()
918         if self._renderer is None:
919             raise RuntimeError(
920                 "Cannot get window extent of text w/o renderer. You likely "
921                 "want to call 'figure.draw_without_rendering()' first.")
922 
923         with cbook._setattr_cm(self.figure, dpi=dpi):
924             bbox, info, descent = self._get_layout(self._renderer)
925             x, y = self.get_unitless_position()
926             x, y = self.get_transform().transform((x, y))
927             bbox = bbox.translated(x, y)
928             return bbox

1248     def _preprocess_math(self, s):
1249         """
1250         Return the string *s* after mathtext preprocessing, and the kind of
1251         mathtext support needed.
1252 
1253         - If *self* is configured to use TeX, return *s* unchanged except that
1254           a single space gets escaped, and the flag "TeX".
1255         - Otherwise, if *s* is mathtext (has an even number of unescaped dollar
1256           signs) and ``parse_math`` is not set to False, return *s* and the
1257           flag True.
1258         - Otherwise, return *s* with dollar signs unescaped, and the flag
1259           False.
1260         """
1261         if self.get_usetex():
1262             if s == " ":
1263                 s = r"\ "
1264             return s, "TeX"
1265         elif not self.get_parse_math():
1266             return s, False
1267         elif cbook.is_math_text(s):
1268             return s, True
1269         else:
1270             return s.replace(r"\$", "$"), False

1339 class OffsetFrom:
1340     """Callable helper class for working with `Annotation`."""
1341 
1342     def __init__(self, artist, ref_coord, unit="points"):
1343         """
1344         Parameters
1345         ----------
1346         artist : `.Artist` or `.BboxBase` or `.Transform`
1347             The object to compute the offset from.
1348 
1349         ref_coord : (float, float)
1350             If *artist* is an `.Artist` or `.BboxBase`, this values is
1351             the location to of the offset origin in fractions of the
1352             *artist* bounding box.
1353 
1354             If *artist* is a transform, the offset origin is the
1355             transform applied to this value.
1356 
1357         unit : {'points, 'pixels'}, default: 'points'
1358             The screen units to use (pixels or points) for the offset input.
1359         """
1360         self._artist = artist
1361         self._ref_coord = ref_coord
1362         self.set_unit(unit)
1363 
1364     def set_unit(self, unit):
1365         """
1366         Set the unit for input to the transform used by ``__call__``.
1367 
1368         Parameters
1369         ----------
1370         unit : {'points', 'pixels'}
1371         """
1372         _api.check_in_list(["points", "pixels"], unit=unit)
1373         self._unit = unit
1374 
1375     def get_unit(self):
1376         """Return the unit for input to the transform used by ``__call__``."""
1377         return self._unit
1378 
1379     def _get_scale(self, renderer):
1380         unit = self.get_unit()
1381         if unit == "pixels":
1382             return 1.
1383         else:
1384             return renderer.points_to_pixels(1.)
1385 
1386     def __call__(self, renderer):
1387         """
1388         Return the offset transform.
1389 
1390         Parameters
1391         ----------
1392         renderer : `RendererBase`
1393             The renderer to use to compute the offset
1394 
1395         Returns
1396         -------
1397         `Transform`
1398             Maps (x, y) in pixel or point units to screen units
1399             relative to the given artist.
1400         """
1401         if isinstance(self._artist, Artist):
1402             bbox = self._artist.get_window_extent(renderer)
1403             xf, yf = self._ref_coord
1404             x = bbox.x0 + bbox.width * xf
1405             y = bbox.y0 + bbox.height * yf
1406         elif isinstance(self._artist, BboxBase):
1407             bbox = self._artist
1408             xf, yf = self._ref_coord
1409             x = bbox.x0 + bbox.width * xf
1410             y = bbox.y0 + bbox.height * yf
1411         elif isinstance(self._artist, Transform):
1412             x, y = self._artist.transform(self._ref_coord)
1413         else:
1414             _api.check_isinstance((Artist, BboxBase, Transform), artist=self._artist)
1415 
1416         sc = self._get_scale(renderer)
1417         tr = Affine2D().scale(sc).translate(x, y)
1418 
1419         return tr
1420
