822 def apply_ufunc(
823     func: Callable,
824     *args: Any,
825     input_core_dims: Sequence[Sequence] = None,
826     output_core_dims: Sequence[Sequence] | None = ((),),
827     exclude_dims: AbstractSet = frozenset(),
828     vectorize: bool = False,
829     join: str = "exact",
830     dataset_join: str = "exact",
831     dataset_fill_value: object = _NO_FILL_VALUE,
832     keep_attrs: bool | str | None = None,
833     kwargs: Mapping | None = None,
834     dask: str = "forbidden",
835     output_dtypes: Sequence | None = None,
836     output_sizes: Mapping[Any, int] | None = None,
837     meta: Any = None,
838     dask_gufunc_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
839 ) -> Any:
840     """Apply a vectorized function for unlabeled arrays on xarray objects.
841 
842     The function will be mapped over the data variable(s) of the input
843     arguments using xarray's standard rules for labeled computation, including
844     alignment, broadcasting, looping over GroupBy/Dataset variables, and
845     merging of coordinates.
846 
847     Parameters
848     ----------
849     func : callable
850         Function to call like ``func(*args, **kwargs)`` on unlabeled arrays
851         (``.data``) that returns an array or tuple of arrays. If multiple
852         arguments with non-matching dimensions are supplied, this function is
853         expected to vectorize (broadcast) over axes of positional arguments in
854         the style of NumPy universal functions [1]_ (if this is not the case,
855         set ``vectorize=True``). If this function returns multiple outputs, you
856         must set ``output_core_dims`` as well.
857     *args : Dataset, DataArray, DataArrayGroupBy, DatasetGroupBy, Variable, numpy.ndarray, dask.array.Array or scalar
858         Mix of labeled and/or unlabeled arrays to which to apply the function.
859     input_core_dims : sequence of sequence, optional
860         List of the same length as ``args`` giving the list of core dimensions
861         on each input argument that should not be broadcast. By default, we
862         assume there are no core dimensions on any input arguments.
863 
864         For example, ``input_core_dims=[[], ['time']]`` indicates that all
865         dimensions on the first argument and all dimensions other than 'time'
866         on the second argument should be broadcast.
867 
868         Core dimensions are automatically moved to the last axes of input
869         variables before applying ``func``, which facilitates using NumPy style
870         generalized ufuncs [2]_.
871     output_core_dims : list of tuple, optional
872         List of the same length as the number of output arguments from
873         ``func``, giving the list of core dimensions on each output that were
874         not broadcast on the inputs. By default, we assume that ``func``
875         outputs exactly one array, with axes corresponding to each broadcast
876         dimension.
877 
878         Core dimensions are assumed to appear as the last dimensions of each
879         output in the provided order.
880     exclude_dims : set, optional
881         Core dimensions on the inputs to exclude from alignment and
882         broadcasting entirely. Any input coordinates along these dimensions
883         will be dropped. Each excluded dimension must also appear in
884         ``input_core_dims`` for at least one argument. Only dimensions listed
885         here are allowed to change size between input and output objects.
886     vectorize : bool, optional
887         If True, then assume ``func`` only takes arrays defined over core
888         dimensions as input and vectorize it automatically with
889         :py:func:`numpy.vectorize`. This option exists for convenience, but is
890         almost always slower than supplying a pre-vectorized function.
891         Using this option requires NumPy version 1.12 or newer.
892     join : {"outer", "inner", "left", "right", "exact"}, default: "exact"
893         Method for joining the indexes of the passed objects along each
894         dimension, and the variables of Dataset objects with mismatched
895         data variables:
896 
897         - 'outer': use the union of object indexes
898         - 'inner': use the intersection of object indexes
899         - 'left': use indexes from the first object with each dimension
900         - 'right': use indexes from the last object with each dimension
901         - 'exact': raise `ValueError` instead of aligning when indexes to be
902           aligned are not equal
903     dataset_join : {"outer", "inner", "left", "right", "exact"}, default: "exact"
904         Method for joining variables of Dataset objects with mismatched
905         data variables.
906 
907         - 'outer': take variables from both Dataset objects
908         - 'inner': take only overlapped variables
909         - 'left': take only variables from the first object
910         - 'right': take only variables from the last object
911         - 'exact': data variables on all Dataset objects must match exactly
912     dataset_fill_value : optional
913         Value used in place of missing variables on Dataset inputs when the
914         datasets do not share the exact same ``data_vars``. Required if
915         ``dataset_join not in {'inner', 'exact'}``, otherwise ignored.
916     keep_attrs : bool, optional
917         Whether to copy attributes from the first argument to the output.
918     kwargs : dict, optional
919         Optional keyword arguments passed directly on to call ``func``.
920     dask : {"forbidden", "allowed", "parallelized"}, default: "forbidden"
921         How to handle applying to objects containing lazy data in the form of
922         dask arrays:
923 
924         - 'forbidden' (default): raise an error if a dask array is encountered.
925         - 'allowed': pass dask arrays directly on to ``func``. Prefer this option if
926           ``func`` natively supports dask arrays.
927         - 'parallelized': automatically parallelize ``func`` if any of the
928           inputs are a dask array by using :py:func:`dask.array.apply_gufunc`. Multiple output
929           arguments are supported. Only use this option if ``func`` does not natively
930           support dask arrays (e.g. converts them to numpy arrays).
931     dask_gufunc_kwargs : dict, optional
932         Optional keyword arguments passed to :py:func:`dask.array.apply_gufunc` if
933         dask='parallelized'. Possible keywords are ``output_sizes``, ``allow_rechunk``
934         and ``meta``.
935     output_dtypes : list of dtype, optional
936         Optional list of output dtypes. Only used if ``dask='parallelized'`` or
937         ``vectorize=True``.
938     output_sizes : dict, optional
939         Optional mapping from dimension names to sizes for outputs. Only used
940         if dask='parallelized' and new dimensions (not found on inputs) appear
941         on outputs. ``output_sizes`` should be given in the ``dask_gufunc_kwargs``
942         parameter. It will be removed as direct parameter in a future version.
943     meta : optional
944         Size-0 object representing the type of array wrapped by dask array. Passed on to
945         :py:func:`dask.array.apply_gufunc`. ``meta`` should be given in the
946         ``dask_gufunc_kwargs`` parameter . It will be removed as direct parameter
947         a future version.
948 
949     Returns
950     -------
951     Single value or tuple of Dataset, DataArray, Variable, dask.array.Array or
952     numpy.ndarray, the first type on that list to appear on an input.
953 
954     Notes
955     -----
956     This function is designed for the more common case where ``func`` can work on numpy
957     arrays. If ``func`` needs to manipulate a whole xarray object subset to each block
958     it is possible to use :py:func:`xarray.map_blocks`.
959 
960     Note that due to the overhead :py:func:`xarray.map_blocks` is considerably slower than ``apply_ufunc``.
961 
962     Examples
963     --------
964     Calculate the vector magnitude of two arguments:
965 
966     >>> def magnitude(a, b):
967     ...     func = lambda x, y: np.sqrt(x**2 + y**2)
968     ...     return xr.apply_ufunc(func, a, b)
969     ...
970 
971     You can now apply ``magnitude()`` to :py:class:`DataArray` and :py:class:`Dataset`
972     objects, with automatically preserved dimensions and coordinates, e.g.,
973 
974     >>> array = xr.DataArray([1, 2, 3], coords=[("x", [0.1, 0.2, 0.3])])
975     >>> magnitude(array, -array)
976     <xarray.DataArray (x: 3)>
977     array([1.41421356, 2.82842712, 4.24264069])
978     Coordinates:
979       * x        (x) float64 0.1 0.2 0.3
980 
981     Plain scalars, numpy arrays and a mix of these with xarray objects is also
982     supported:
983 
984     >>> magnitude(3, 4)
985     5.0
986     >>> magnitude(3, np.array([0, 4]))
987     array([3., 5.])
988     >>> magnitude(array, 0)
989     <xarray.DataArray (x: 3)>
990     array([1., 2., 3.])
991     Coordinates:
992       * x        (x) float64 0.1 0.2 0.3
993 
994     Other examples of how you could use ``apply_ufunc`` to write functions to
995     (very nearly) replicate existing xarray functionality:
996 
997     Compute the mean (``.mean``) over one dimension:
998 
999     >>> def mean(obj, dim):
1000     ...     # note: apply always moves core dimensions to the end
1001     ...     return apply_ufunc(
1002     ...         np.mean, obj, input_core_dims=[[dim]], kwargs={"axis": -1}
1003     ...     )
1004     ...
1005 
1006     Inner product over a specific dimension (like :py:func:`dot`):
1007 
1008     >>> def _inner(x, y):
1009     ...     result = np.matmul(x[..., np.newaxis, :], y[..., :, np.newaxis])
1010     ...     return result[..., 0, 0]
1011     ...
1012     >>> def inner_product(a, b, dim):
1013     ...     return apply_ufunc(_inner, a, b, input_core_dims=[[dim], [dim]])
1014     ...
1015 
1016     Stack objects along a new dimension (like :py:func:`concat`):
1017 
1018     >>> def stack(objects, dim, new_coord):
1019     ...     # note: this version does not stack coordinates
1020     ...     func = lambda *x: np.stack(x, axis=-1)
1021     ...     result = apply_ufunc(
1022     ...         func,
1023     ...         *objects,
1024     ...         output_core_dims=[[dim]],
1025     ...         join="outer",
1026     ...         dataset_fill_value=np.nan
1027     ...     )
1028     ...     result[dim] = new_coord
1029     ...     return result
1030     ...
1031 
1032     If your function is not vectorized but can be applied only to core
1033     dimensions, you can use ``vectorize=True`` to turn into a vectorized
1034     function. This wraps :py:func:`numpy.vectorize`, so the operation isn't
1035     terribly fast. Here we'll use it to calculate the distance between
1036     empirical samples from two probability distributions, using a scipy
1037     function that needs to be applied to vectors:
1038 
1039     >>> import scipy.stats
1040     >>> def earth_mover_distance(first_samples, second_samples, dim="ensemble"):
1041     ...     return apply_ufunc(
1042     ...         scipy.stats.wasserstein_distance,
1043     ...         first_samples,
1044     ...         second_samples,
1045     ...         input_core_dims=[[dim], [dim]],
1046     ...         vectorize=True,
1047     ...     )
1048     ...
1049 
1050     Most of NumPy's builtin functions already broadcast their inputs
1051     appropriately for use in ``apply_ufunc``. You may find helper functions such as
1052     :py:func:`numpy.broadcast_arrays` helpful in writing your function. ``apply_ufunc`` also
1053     works well with :py:func:`numba.vectorize` and :py:func:`numba.guvectorize`.
1054 
1055     See Also
1056     --------
1057     numpy.broadcast_arrays
1058     numba.vectorize
1059     numba.guvectorize
1060     dask.array.apply_gufunc
1061     xarray.map_blocks
1062     :ref:`dask.automatic-parallelization`
1063         User guide describing :py:func:`apply_ufunc` and :py:func:`map_blocks`.
1064 
1065     References
1066     ----------
1067     .. [1] https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/ufuncs.html
1068     .. [2] https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/c-api/generalized-ufuncs.html
1069     """
1070     from .dataarray import DataArray
1071     from .groupby import GroupBy
1072     from .variable import Variable
1073 
1074     if input_core_dims is None:
1075         input_core_dims = ((),) * (len(args))
1076     elif len(input_core_dims) != len(args):
1077         raise ValueError(
1078             f"input_core_dims must be None or a tuple with the length same to "
1079             f"the number of arguments. "
1080             f"Given {len(input_core_dims)} input_core_dims: {input_core_dims}, "
1081             f" but number of args is {len(args)}."
1082         )
1083 
1084     if kwargs is None:

1353 def _cov_corr(da_a, da_b, dim=None, ddof=0, method=None):
1354     """
1355     Internal method for xr.cov() and xr.corr() so only have to
1356     sanitize the input arrays once and we don't repeat code.
1357     """
1358     # 1. Broadcast the two arrays
1359     da_a, da_b = align(da_a, da_b, join="inner", copy=False)
1360 
1361     # 2. Ignore the nans
1362     valid_values = da_a.notnull() & da_b.notnull()
1363     da_a = da_a.where(valid_values)
1364     da_b = da_b.where(valid_values)
1365     valid_count = valid_values.sum(dim) - ddof
1366 
1367     # 3. Detrend along the given dim
1368     demeaned_da_a = da_a - da_a.mean(dim=dim)
1369     demeaned_da_b = da_b - da_b.mean(dim=dim)
1370 
1371     # 4. Compute covariance along the given dim
1372     # N.B. `skipna=False` is required or there is a bug when computing
1373     # auto-covariance. E.g. Try xr.cov(da,da) for
1374     # da = xr.DataArray([[1, 2], [1, np.nan]], dims=["x", "time"])
1375     cov = (demeaned_da_a * demeaned_da_b).sum(dim=dim, skipna=True, min_count=1) / (
1376         valid_count
1377     )
1378 
1379     if method == "cov":
1380         return cov
1381 
1382     else:
1383         # compute std + corr
1384         da_a_std = da_a.std(dim=dim)
1385         da_b_std = da_b.std(dim=dim)
1386         corr = cov / (da_a_std * da_b_std)
1387         return corr

1390 def cross(
1391     a: DataArray | Variable, b: DataArray | Variable, *, dim: Hashable
1392 ) -> DataArray | Variable:
1393     """
1394     Compute the cross product of two (arrays of) vectors.
1395 
1396     The cross product of `a` and `b` in :math:`R^3` is a vector
1397     perpendicular to both `a` and `b`. The vectors in `a` and `b` are
1398     defined by the values along the dimension `dim` and can have sizes
1399     1, 2 or 3. Where the size of either `a` or `b` is
1400     1 or 2, the remaining components of the input vector is assumed to
1401     be zero and the cross product calculated accordingly. In cases where
1402     both input vectors have dimension 2, the z-component of the cross
1403     product is returned.
1404 
1405     Parameters
1406     ----------
1407     a, b : DataArray or Variable
1408         Components of the first and second vector(s).
1409     dim : hashable
1410         The dimension along which the cross product will be computed.
1411         Must be available in both vectors.
1412 
1413     Examples
1414     --------
1415     Vector cross-product with 3 dimensions:
1416 
1417     >>> a = xr.DataArray([1, 2, 3])
1418     >>> b = xr.DataArray([4, 5, 6])
1419     >>> xr.cross(a, b, dim="dim_0")
1420     <xarray.DataArray (dim_0: 3)>
1421     array([-3,  6, -3])
1422     Dimensions without coordinates: dim_0
1423 
1424     Vector cross-product with 2 dimensions, returns in the perpendicular
1425     direction:
1426 
1427     >>> a = xr.DataArray([1, 2])
1428     >>> b = xr.DataArray([4, 5])
1429     >>> xr.cross(a, b, dim="dim_0")
1430     <xarray.DataArray ()>
1431     array(-3)
1432 
1433     Vector cross-product with 3 dimensions but zeros at the last axis
1434     yields the same results as with 2 dimensions:
1435 
1436     >>> a = xr.DataArray([1, 2, 0])
1437     >>> b = xr.DataArray([4, 5, 0])
1438     >>> xr.cross(a, b, dim="dim_0")
1439     <xarray.DataArray (dim_0: 3)>
1440     array([ 0,  0, -3])
1441     Dimensions without coordinates: dim_0
1442 
1443     One vector with dimension 2:
1444 
1445     >>> a = xr.DataArray(
1446     ...     [1, 2],
1447     ...     dims=["cartesian"],
1448     ...     coords=dict(cartesian=(["cartesian"], ["x", "y"])),
1449     ... )
1450     >>> b = xr.DataArray(
1451     ...     [4, 5, 6],
1452     ...     dims=["cartesian"],
1453     ...     coords=dict(cartesian=(["cartesian"], ["x", "y", "z"])),
1454     ... )
1455     >>> xr.cross(a, b, dim="cartesian")
1456     <xarray.DataArray (cartesian: 3)>
1457     array([12, -6, -3])
1458     Coordinates:
1459       * cartesian  (cartesian) <U1 'x' 'y' 'z'
1460 
1461     One vector with dimension 2 but coords in other positions:
1462 
1463     >>> a = xr.DataArray(
1464     ...     [1, 2],
1465     ...     dims=["cartesian"],
1466     ...     coords=dict(cartesian=(["cartesian"], ["x", "z"])),
1467     ... )
1468     >>> b = xr.DataArray(
1469     ...     [4, 5, 6],
1470     ...     dims=["cartesian"],
1471     ...     coords=dict(cartesian=(["cartesian"], ["x", "y", "z"])),
1472     ... )
1473     >>> xr.cross(a, b, dim="cartesian")
1474     <xarray.DataArray (cartesian: 3)>
1475     array([-10,   2,   5])
1476     Coordinates:
1477       * cartesian  (cartesian) <U1 'x' 'y' 'z'
1478 
1479     Multiple vector cross-products. Note that the direction of the
1480     cross product vector is defined by the right-hand rule:
1481 
1482     >>> a = xr.DataArray(
1483     ...     [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]],
1484     ...     dims=("time", "cartesian"),
1485     ...     coords=dict(
1486     ...         time=(["time"], [0, 1]),
1487     ...         cartesian=(["cartesian"], ["x", "y", "z"]),
1488     ...     ),
1489     ... )
1490     >>> b = xr.DataArray(
1491     ...     [[4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3]],
1492     ...     dims=("time", "cartesian"),
1493     ...     coords=dict(
1494     ...         time=(["time"], [0, 1]),
1495     ...         cartesian=(["cartesian"], ["x", "y", "z"]),
1496     ...     ),
1497     ... )
1498     >>> xr.cross(a, b, dim="cartesian")
1499     <xarray.DataArray (time: 2, cartesian: 3)>
1500     array([[-3,  6, -3],
1501            [ 3, -6,  3]])
1502     Coordinates:
1503       * time       (time) int64 0 1
1504       * cartesian  (cartesian) <U1 'x' 'y' 'z'
1505 
1506     Cross can be called on Datasets by converting to DataArrays and later
1507     back to a Dataset:
1508 
1509     >>> ds_a = xr.Dataset(dict(x=("dim_0", [1]), y=("dim_0", [2]), z=("dim_0", [3])))
1510     >>> ds_b = xr.Dataset(dict(x=("dim_0", [4]), y=("dim_0", [5]), z=("dim_0", [6])))
1511     >>> c = xr.cross(
1512     ...     ds_a.to_array("cartesian"), ds_b.to_array("cartesian"), dim="cartesian"
1513     ... )
1514     >>> c.to_dataset(dim="cartesian")
1515     <xarray.Dataset>
1516     Dimensions:  (dim_0: 1)
1517     Dimensions without coordinates: dim_0
1518     Data variables:
1519         x        (dim_0) int64 -3
1520         y        (dim_0) int64 6
1521         z        (dim_0) int64 -3
1522 
1523     See Also
1524     --------
1525     numpy.cross : Corresponding numpy function
1526     """
1527 
1528     if dim not in a.dims:
1529         raise ValueError(f"Dimension {dim!r} not on a")
1530     elif dim not in b.dims:
1531         raise ValueError(f"Dimension {dim!r} not on b")
1532 
1533     if not 1 <= a.sizes[dim] <= 3:
1534         raise ValueError(
1535             f"The size of {dim!r} on a must be 1, 2, or 3 to be "
1536             f"compatible with a cross product but is {a.sizes[dim]}"
1537         )
1538     elif not 1 <= b.sizes[dim] <= 3:
1539         raise ValueError(
1540             f"The size of {dim!r} on b must be 1, 2, or 3 to be "
1541             f"compatible with a cross product but is {b.sizes[dim]}"
1542         )
1543 
1544     all_dims = list(dict.fromkeys(a.dims + b.dims))
1545 
1546     if a.sizes[dim] != b.sizes[dim]:
1547         # Arrays have different sizes. Append zeros where the smaller
1548         # array is missing a value, zeros will not affect np.cross:
1549 
1550         if (
1551             not isinstance(a, Variable)  # Only used to make mypy happy.
1552             and dim in getattr(a, "coords", {})
1553             and not isinstance(b, Variable)  # Only used to make mypy happy.
1554             and dim in getattr(b, "coords", {})
1555         ):
1556             # If the arrays have coords we know which indexes to fill
1557             # with zeros:
1558             a, b = align(
1559                 a,
1560                 b,
1561                 fill_value=0,
1562                 join="outer",
1563                 exclude=set(all_dims) - {dim},
1564             )
1565         elif min(a.sizes[dim], b.sizes[dim]) == 2:
1566             # If the array doesn't have coords we can only infer
1567             # that it has composite values if the size is at least 2.
1568             # Once padded, rechunk the padded array because apply_ufunc
1569             # requires core dimensions not to be chunked:
1570             if a.sizes[dim] < b.sizes[dim]:
1571                 a = a.pad({dim: (0, 1)}, constant_values=0)
1572                 # TODO: Should pad or apply_ufunc handle correct chunking?
1573                 a = a.chunk({dim: -1}) if is_duck_dask_array(a.data) else a
1574             else:
1575                 b = b.pad({dim: (0, 1)}, constant_values=0)
1576                 # TODO: Should pad or apply_ufunc handle correct chunking?
1577                 b = b.chunk({dim: -1}) if is_duck_dask_array(b.data) else b
1578         else:
1579             raise ValueError(
1580                 f"{dim!r} on {'a' if a.sizes[dim] == 1 else 'b'} is incompatible:"
1581                 " dimensions without coordinates must have have a length of 2 or 3"
1582             )
1583 
1584     c = apply_ufunc(
1585         np.cross,
1586         a,
1587         b,
1588         input_core_dims=[[dim], [dim]],
1589         output_core_dims=[[dim] if a.sizes[dim] == 3 else []],
1590         dask="parallelized",
1591         output_dtypes=[np.result_type(a, b)],
1592     )
1593     c = c.transpose(*all_dims, missing_dims="ignore")
1594 
1595     return c
1596

1598 def dot(*arrays, dims=None, **kwargs):
1599     """Generalized dot product for xarray objects. Like np.einsum, but
1600     provides a simpler interface based on array dimensions.
1601 
1602     Parameters
1603     ----------
1604     *arrays : DataArray or Variable
1605         Arrays to compute.
1606     dims : ..., str or tuple of str, optional
1607         Which dimensions to sum over. Ellipsis ('...') sums over all dimensions.
1608         If not specified, then all the common dimensions are summed over.
1609     **kwargs : dict
1610         Additional keyword arguments passed to numpy.einsum or
1611         dask.array.einsum
1612 
1613     Returns
1614     -------
1615     DataArray
1616 
1617     Examples
1618     --------
1619     >>> da_a = xr.DataArray(np.arange(3 * 2).reshape(3, 2), dims=["a", "b"])
1620     >>> da_b = xr.DataArray(np.arange(3 * 2 * 2).reshape(3, 2, 2), dims=["a", "b", "c"])
1621     >>> da_c = xr.DataArray(np.arange(2 * 3).reshape(2, 3), dims=["c", "d"])
1622 
1623     >>> da_a
1624     <xarray.DataArray (a: 3, b: 2)>
1625     array([[0, 1],
1626            [2, 3],
1627            [4, 5]])
1628     Dimensions without coordinates: a, b
1629 
1630     >>> da_b
1631     <xarray.DataArray (a: 3, b: 2, c: 2)>
1632     array([[[ 0,  1],
1633             [ 2,  3]],
1634     <BLANKLINE>
1635            [[ 4,  5],
1636             [ 6,  7]],
1637     <BLANKLINE>
1638            [[ 8,  9],
1639             [10, 11]]])
1640     Dimensions without coordinates: a, b, c
1641 
1642     >>> da_c
1643     <xarray.DataArray (c: 2, d: 3)>
1644     array([[0, 1, 2],
1645            [3, 4, 5]])
1646     Dimensions without coordinates: c, d
1647 
1648     >>> xr.dot(da_a, da_b, dims=["a", "b"])
1649     <xarray.DataArray (c: 2)>
1650     array([110, 125])
1651     Dimensions without coordinates: c
1652 
1653     >>> xr.dot(da_a, da_b, dims=["a"])
1654     <xarray.DataArray (b: 2, c: 2)>
1655     array([[40, 46],
1656            [70, 79]])

142     def _add_arguments_to_parser(
143         self, section: str, section_desc: str | None, argument: _Argument
144     ) -> None:
145         """Add an argument to the correct argument section/group."""
146         try:
147             section_group = self._argument_groups_dict[section]

151                     section, section_desc

158     @staticmethod
159     def _add_parser_option(
160         section_group: argparse._ArgumentGroup, argument: _Argument
161     ) -> None:
162         """Add an argument."""
163         if isinstance(argument, _StoreArgument):
164             section_group.add_argument(
165                 *argument.flags,
166                 action=argument.action,
167                 default=argument.default,
168                 type=argument.type,  # type: ignore[arg-type] # incorrect typing in typeshed
169                 help=argument.help,
170                 metavar=argument.metavar,
171                 choices=argument.choices,
172             )
173         elif isinstance(argument, _StoreOldNamesArgument):
174             section_group.add_argument(
175                 *argument.flags,
176                 **argument.kwargs,
177                 action=argument.action,
178                 default=argument.default,
179                 type=argument.type,  # type: ignore[arg-type] # incorrect typing in typeshed
180                 help=argument.help,
181                 metavar=argument.metavar,
182                 choices=argument.choices,
183             )
184             # We add the old name as hidden option to make it's default value gets loaded when
185             # argparse initializes all options from the checker
186             assert argument.kwargs["old_names"]
187             for old_name in argument.kwargs["old_names"]:
188                 section_group.add_argument(
189                     f"--{old_name}",
190                     action="store",
191                     default=argument.default,
192                     type=argument.type,  # type: ignore[arg-type] # incorrect typing in typeshed
193                     help=argparse.SUPPRESS,
194                     metavar=argument.metavar,
195                     choices=argument.choices,
196                 )
197         elif isinstance(argument, _StoreNewNamesArgument):
198             section_group.add_argument(
199                 *argument.flags,
200                 **argument.kwargs,
201                 action=argument.action,
202                 default=argument.default,
203                 type=argument.type,  # type: ignore[arg-type] # incorrect typing in typeshed
204                 help=argument.help,
205                 metavar=argument.metavar,
206                 choices=argument.choices,
207             )
208         elif isinstance(argument, _StoreTrueArgument):
209             section_group.add_argument(
210                 *argument.flags,
211                 action=argument.action,
212                 default=argument.default,
213                 help=argument.help,
214             )
215         elif isinstance(argument, _CallableArgument):
216             section_group.add_argument(
217                 *argument.flags,
218                 **argument.kwargs,
219                 action=argument.action,
220                 help=argument.help,
221             )
222         elif isinstance(argument, _ExtendArgument):
223             section_group.add_argument(
224                 *argument.flags,
225                 action=argument.action,
226                 default=argument.default,
227                 type=argument.type,  # type: ignore[arg-type] # incorrect typing in typeshed
228                 help=argument.help,
229                 metavar=argument.metavar,
230                 choices=argument.choices,
231                 dest=argument.dest,
232             )
233         else:
234             raise UnrecognizedArgumentAction

657     def _generate_config_file(self) -> None:
658         """Write a configuration file according to the current configuration into stdout."""
659         toml_doc = tomlkit.document()
660         pylint_tool_table = tomlkit.table(is_super_table=True)
661         toml_doc.add(tomlkit.key(["tool", "pylint"]), pylint_tool_table)
662 
663         for group in sorted(
664             self._arg_parser._action_groups,
665             key=lambda x: (x.title != "Master", x.title),
666         ):
667             # Skip the options section with the --help option
668             if group.title == "options":
669                 continue
670 
671             # Skip sections without options such as "positional arguments"
672             if not group._group_actions:
673                 continue
674 
675             group_table = tomlkit.table()
676             for action in sorted(
677                 group._group_actions, key=lambda x: x.option_strings[0][2:]
678             ):
679                 optname = action.option_strings[0][2:]
680 
681                 # We skip old name options that don't have their own optdict
682                 try:
683                     optdict = self._option_dicts[optname]
684                 except KeyError:
685                     continue
686 
687                 if optdict.get("hide_from_config_file"):
688                     continue
689 
690                 # Add help comment
691                 help_msg = optdict.get("help", "")
692                 assert isinstance(help_msg, str)
693                 help_text = textwrap.wrap(help_msg, width=79)
694                 for line in help_text:
695                     group_table.add(tomlkit.comment(line))
696 
697                 # Get current value of option
698                 value = getattr(self.config, optname.replace("-", "_"))
699 
700                 # Create a comment if the option has no value
701                 if not value:
702                     group_table.add(tomlkit.comment(f"{optname} ="))
703                     group_table.add(tomlkit.nl())
704                     continue
705 
706                 # Tomlkit doesn't support regular expressions
707                 if isinstance(value, re.Pattern):
708                     value = value.pattern
709                 elif isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) and isinstance(
710                     value[0], re.Pattern
711                 ):
712                     value = [i.pattern for i in value]
713 
714                 # Add to table
715                 group_table.add(optname, value)
716                 group_table.add(tomlkit.nl())
717 
718             assert group.title
719             pylint_tool_table.add(group.title.lower(), group_table)
720 
721         toml_string = tomlkit.dumps(toml_doc)
722 
723         # Make sure the string we produce is valid toml and can be parsed
724         tomllib.loads(toml_string)
725 
726         print(toml_string)

31 def _convert_option_to_argument(
32     opt: str, optdict: dict[str, Any]
33 ) -> (
34     _StoreArgument
35     | _StoreTrueArgument
36     | _CallableArgument
37     | _StoreOldNamesArgument
38     | _StoreNewNamesArgument
39     | _ExtendArgument
40 ):
41     """Convert an optdict to an Argument class instance."""
42     if "level" in optdict and "hide" not in optdict:
43         warnings.warn(
44             "The 'level' key in optdicts has been deprecated. "
45             "Use 'hide' with a boolean to hide an option from the help message.",
46             DeprecationWarning,
47         )
48 
49     # Get the long and short flags
50     flags = [f"--{opt}"]
51     if "short" in optdict:
52         flags += [f"-{optdict['short']}"]
53 
54     # Get the action type
55     action = optdict.get("action", "store")
56 
57     if action == "store_true":
58         return _StoreTrueArgument(
59             flags=flags,
60             action=action,
61             default=optdict.get("default", True),
62             arg_help=optdict.get("help", ""),
63             hide_help=optdict.get("hide", False),
64             section=optdict.get("group", None),
65         )
66     if not isinstance(action, str) and issubclass(action, _CallbackAction):
67         return _CallableArgument(
68             flags=flags,
69             action=action,
70             arg_help=optdict.get("help", ""),
71             kwargs=optdict.get("kwargs", {}),
72             hide_help=optdict.get("hide", False),
73             section=optdict.get("group", None),
74         )
75     try:
76         default = optdict["default"]
77     except KeyError:
78         warnings.warn(
79             "An option dictionary should have a 'default' key to specify "
80             "the option's default value. This key will be required in pylint "
81             "3.0. It is not required for 'store_true' and callable actions.",
82             DeprecationWarning,
83         )
84         default = None
85     if action == "extend":
86         return _ExtendArgument(
87             flags=flags,
88             action=action,
89             default=default,
90             arg_type=optdict["type"],
91             choices=optdict.get("choices", None),
92             arg_help=optdict.get("help", ""),
93             metavar=optdict.get("metavar", ""),
94             hide_help=optdict.get("hide", False),
95             section=optdict.get("group", None),
96             dest=optdict.get("dest", None),
97         )
98     if "kwargs" in optdict:
99         if "old_names" in optdict["kwargs"]:
100             return _StoreOldNamesArgument(
101                 flags=flags,
102                 default=default,
103                 arg_type=optdict["type"],
104                 choices=optdict.get("choices", None),
105                 arg_help=optdict.get("help", ""),
106                 metavar=optdict.get("metavar", ""),
107                 hide_help=optdict.get("hide", False),
108                 kwargs=optdict.get("kwargs", {}),
109                 section=optdict.get("group", None),
110             )
111         if "new_names" in optdict["kwargs"]:
112             return _StoreNewNamesArgument(
113                 flags=flags,
114                 default=default,
115                 arg_type=optdict["type"],
116                 choices=optdict.get("choices", None),
117                 arg_help=optdict.get("help", ""),
118                 metavar=optdict.get("metavar", ""),
119                 hide_help=optdict.get("hide", False),
120                 kwargs=optdict.get("kwargs", {}),
121                 section=optdict.get("group", None),
122             )
123     if "dest" in optdict:
124         return _StoreOldNamesArgument(
125             flags=flags,
126             default=default,
127             arg_type=optdict["type"],
128             choices=optdict.get("choices", None),
129             arg_help=optdict.get("help", ""),
130             metavar=optdict.get("metavar", ""),
131             hide_help=optdict.get("hide", False),
132             kwargs={"old_names": [optdict["dest"]]},
133             section=optdict.get("group", None),
134         )
135     return _StoreArgument(
136         flags=flags,
137         action=action,
138         default=default,
139         arg_type=optdict["type"],
140         choices=optdict.get("choices", None),
141         arg_help=optdict.get("help", ""),
142         metavar=optdict.get("metavar", ""),
143         hide_help=optdict.get("hide", False),
144         section=optdict.get("group", None),
145     )

214 def _preprocess_options(run: Run, args: Sequence[str]) -> list[str]:
215     """Preprocess options before full config parsing has started."""
216     processed_args: list[str] = []
217 
218     i = 0
219     while i < len(args):
220         argument = args[i]
221         if not argument.startswith("--"):
222             processed_args.append(argument)
223             i += 1
224             continue
225 
226         try:
227             option, value = argument.split("=", 1)
228         except ValueError:
229             option, value = argument, None
230 
231         if option not in PREPROCESSABLE_OPTIONS:
232             processed_args.append(argument)
233             i += 1
234             continue
235 
236         takearg, cb = PREPROCESSABLE_OPTIONS[option]
237 
238         if takearg and value is None:
239             i += 1
240             if i >= len(args) or args[i].startswith("-"):
241                 raise ArgumentPreprocessingError(f"Option {option} expects a value")
242             value = args[i]
243         elif not takearg and value is not None:
244             raise ArgumentPreprocessingError(f"Option {option} doesn't expects a value")
245 
246         cb(run, value)
247         i += 1
248 
249     return processed_args

Pylint does not respect the `--ignore`, `--ignore-paths`, or `--ignore-patterns` setting when running in recursive mode. This contradicts the documentation and seriously compromises the usefulness of recursive mode.

_No response_

```shell
### .a/foo.py

# import re

pylint --recursive=y --ignore-patterns="^\.a" .

All of these commands give the same output:

```
************* Module bar
bar.py:1:0: C0104: Disallowed name "bar" (disallowed-name)
bar.py:1:0: C0114: Missing module docstring (missing-module-docstring)

60     path = sys.path.copy()

66             or _is_in_ignore_list_re(os.path.basename(something), ignore_list_re)
67             or _is_in_ignore_list_re(something, ignore_list_paths_re)
68         ):

70         module_path = get_python_path(something)
71         additional_search_path = [".", module_path] + path
72         if os.path.exists(something):
73             # this is a file or a directory
74             try:
75                 modname = ".".join(
76                     modutils.modpath_from_file(something, path=additional_search_path)
77                 )
78             except ImportError:
79                 modname = os.path.splitext(basename)[0]
80             if os.path.isdir(something):
81                 filepath = os.path.join(something, "__init__.py")
82             else:
83                 filepath = something
84         else:
85             # suppose it's a module or package
86             modname = something
87             try:
88                 filepath = modutils.file_from_modpath(
89                     modname.split("."), path=additional_search_path

99         modparts = (modname or something).split(".")
100         try:

102                 modparts, path=additional_search_path
103             )
104         except ImportError:
105             # Might not be acceptable, don't crash.
106             is_namespace = False
107             is_directory = os.path.isdir(something)
108         else:
109             is_namespace = modutils.is_namespace(spec)
110             is_directory = modutils.is_directory(spec)
111         if not is_namespace:
112             result.append(
113                 {
114                     "path": filepath,
115                     "name": modname,
116                     "isarg": True,
117                     "basepath": filepath,
118                     "basename": modname,
119                 }
120             )
121         has_init = (
122             not (modname.endswith(".__init__") or modname == "__init__")
123             and os.path.basename(filepath) == "__init__.py"
124         )
125         if has_init or is_namespace or is_directory:
126             for subfilepath in modutils.get_module_files(
127                 os.path.dirname(filepath), ignore_list, list_all=is_namespace
128             ):
129                 if filepath == subfilepath:

132                     os.path.basename(subfilepath), ignore_list_re
133                 ) or _is_in_ignore_list_re(subfilepath, ignore_list_paths_re):
134                     continue
135 
136                 modpath = _modpath_from_file(
137                     subfilepath, is_namespace, path=additional_search_path
138                 )
139                 submodname = ".".join(modpath)
140                 result.append(
141                     {
142                         "path": subfilepath,
143                         "name": submodname,
144                         "isarg": False,
145                         "basepath": filepath,
146                         "basename": modname,

45 class ColoredLevelFormatter(logging.Formatter):
46     """
47     Colorize the %(levelname)..s part of the log format passed to __init__.
48     """
49 
50     LOGLEVEL_COLOROPTS = {
51         logging.CRITICAL: {"red"},
52         logging.ERROR: {"red", "bold"},
53         logging.WARNING: {"yellow"},
54         logging.WARN: {"yellow"},
55         logging.INFO: {"green"},
56         logging.DEBUG: {"purple"},
57         logging.NOTSET: set(),
58     }  # type: Mapping[int, AbstractSet[str]]
59     LEVELNAME_FMT_REGEX = re.compile(r"%\(levelname\)([+-.]?\d*s)")
60 
61     def __init__(self, terminalwriter: TerminalWriter, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
62         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
63         self._original_fmt = self._style._fmt
64         self._level_to_fmt_mapping = {}  # type: Dict[int, str]
65 
66         assert self._fmt is not None
67         levelname_fmt_match = self.LEVELNAME_FMT_REGEX.search(self._fmt)
68         if not levelname_fmt_match:
69             return
70         levelname_fmt = levelname_fmt_match.group()
71 
72         for level, color_opts in self.LOGLEVEL_COLOROPTS.items():
73             formatted_levelname = levelname_fmt % {
74                 "levelname": logging.getLevelName(level)
75             }
76 
77             # add ANSI escape sequences around the formatted levelname
78             color_kwargs = {name: True for name in color_opts}
79             colorized_formatted_levelname = terminalwriter.markup(
80                 formatted_levelname, **color_kwargs
81             )
82             self._level_to_fmt_mapping[level] = self.LEVELNAME_FMT_REGEX.sub(
83                 colorized_formatted_levelname, self._fmt
84             )
85 
86     def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
87         fmt = self._level_to_fmt_mapping.get(record.levelno, self._original_fmt)
88         self._style._fmt = fmt
89         return super().format(record)

100         super().__init__(fmt)
101         self._auto_indent = self._get_auto_indent(auto_indent)
102 
103     @staticmethod
104     def _update_message(
105         record_dict: Dict[str, object], message: str
106     ) -> Dict[str, object]:
107         tmp = record_dict.copy()
108         tmp["message"] = message
109         return tmp

111     @staticmethod
112     def _get_auto_indent(auto_indent_option: Union[int, str, bool, None]) -> int:
113         """Determines the current auto indentation setting
114 
115         Specify auto indent behavior (on/off/fixed) by passing in
116         extra={"auto_indent": [value]} to the call to logging.log() or
117         using a --log-auto-indent [value] command line or the
118         log_auto_indent [value] config option.
119 
120         Default behavior is auto-indent off.
121 
122         Using the string "True" or "on" or the boolean True as the value
123         turns auto indent on, using the string "False" or "off" or the
124         boolean False or the int 0 turns it off, and specifying a
125         positive integer fixes the indentation position to the value
126         specified.
127 
128         Any other values for the option are invalid, and will silently be
129         converted to the default.
130 
131         :param any auto_indent_option: User specified option for indentation
132             from command line, config or extra kwarg. Accepts int, bool or str.
133             str option accepts the same range of values as boolean config options,
134             as well as positive integers represented in str form.
135 
136         :returns: indentation value, which can be
137             -1 (automatically determine indentation) or
138             0 (auto-indent turned off) or
139             >0 (explicitly set indentation position).
140         """
141 
142         if auto_indent_option is None:
143             return 0
144         elif isinstance(auto_indent_option, bool):
145             if auto_indent_option:
146                 return -1
147             else:
148                 return 0
149         elif isinstance(auto_indent_option, int):
150             return int(auto_indent_option)
151         elif isinstance(auto_indent_option, str):
152             try:
153                 return int(auto_indent_option)
154             except ValueError:
155                 pass
156             try:
157                 if _strtobool(auto_indent_option):
158                     return -1
159             except ValueError:
160                 return 0
161 
162         return 0
163 
164     def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
165         if "\n" in record.message:
166             if hasattr(record, "auto_indent"):
167                 # passed in from the "extra={}" kwarg on the call to logging.log()
168                 auto_indent = self._get_auto_indent(record.auto_indent)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
169             else:
170                 auto_indent = self._auto_indent
171 
172             if auto_indent:
173                 lines = record.message.splitlines()
174                 formatted = self._fmt % self._update_message(record.__dict__, lines[0])
175 
176                 if auto_indent < 0:

178                         lines[0]
179                     )

181                     # optimizes logging by allowing a fixed indentation
182                     indentation = auto_indent
183                 lines[0] = formatted
184                 return ("\n" + " " * indentation).join(lines)

34 def check_clusterings(labels_true, labels_pred):
35     """Check that the two clusterings matching 1D integer arrays."""

53 def contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred, eps=None, sparse=False):
54     """Build a contingency matrix describing the relationship between labels.
55 
56     Parameters
57     ----------
58     labels_true : int array, shape = [n_samples]
59         Ground truth class labels to be used as a reference
60 
61     labels_pred : array, shape = [n_samples]
62         Cluster labels to evaluate
63 
64     eps : None or float, optional.
65         If a float, that value is added to all values in the contingency
66         matrix. This helps to stop NaN propagation.
67         If ``None``, nothing is adjusted.
68 
69     sparse : boolean, optional.
70         If True, return a sparse CSR continency matrix. If ``eps is not None``,
71         and ``sparse is True``, will throw ValueError.
72 
73         .. versionadded:: 0.18
74 
75     Returns
76     -------
77     contingency : {array-like, sparse}, shape=[n_classes_true, n_classes_pred]
78         Matrix :math:`C` such that :math:`C_{i, j}` is the number of samples in
79         true class :math:`i` and in predicted class :math:`j`. If
80         ``eps is None``, the dtype of this array will be integer. If ``eps`` is
81         given, the dtype will be float.
82         Will be a ``scipy.sparse.csr_matrix`` if ``sparse=True``.
83     """
84 
85     if eps is not None and sparse:
86         raise ValueError("Cannot set 'eps' when sparse=True")
87 
88     classes, class_idx = np.unique(labels_true, return_inverse=True)
89     clusters, cluster_idx = np.unique(labels_pred, return_inverse=True)
90     n_classes = classes.shape[0]
91     n_clusters = clusters.shape[0]
92     # Using coo_matrix to accelerate simple histogram calculation,
93     # i.e. bins are consecutive integers
94     # Currently, coo_matrix is faster than histogram2d for simple cases
95     contingency = sp.coo_matrix((np.ones(class_idx.shape[0]),
96                                  (class_idx, cluster_idx)),
97                                 shape=(n_classes, n_clusters),
98                                 dtype=np.int)
99     if sparse:
100         contingency = contingency.tocsr()
101         contingency.sum_duplicates()
102     else:
103         contingency = contingency.toarray()
104         if eps is not None:
105             # don't use += as contingency is integer
106             contingency = contingency + eps
107     return contingency

112 def adjusted_rand_score(labels_true, labels_pred):
113     """Rand index adjusted for chance.
114 
115     The Rand Index computes a similarity measure between two clusterings
116     by considering all pairs of samples and counting pairs that are
117     assigned in the same or different clusters in the predicted and
118     true clusterings.
119 
120     The raw RI score is then "adjusted for chance" into the ARI score
121     using the following scheme::
122 
123         ARI = (RI - Expected_RI) / (max(RI) - Expected_RI)
124 
125     The adjusted Rand index is thus ensured to have a value close to
126     0.0 for random labeling independently of the number of clusters and
127     samples and exactly 1.0 when the clusterings are identical (up to
128     a permutation).
129 
130     ARI is a symmetric measure::
131 
132         adjusted_rand_score(a, b) == adjusted_rand_score(b, a)
133 
134     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <adjusted_rand_score>`.
135 
136     Parameters
137     ----------
138     labels_true : int array, shape = [n_samples]
139         Ground truth class labels to be used as a reference
140 
141     labels_pred : array, shape = [n_samples]
142         Cluster labels to evaluate
143 
144     Returns
145     -------
146     ari : float
147        Similarity score between -1.0 and 1.0. Random labelings have an ARI
148        close to 0.0. 1.0 stands for perfect match.
149 
150     Examples
151     --------
152 
153     Perfectly matching labelings have a score of 1 even
154 
155       >>> from sklearn.metrics.cluster import adjusted_rand_score
156       >>> adjusted_rand_score([0, 0, 1, 1], [0, 0, 1, 1])
157       1.0
158       >>> adjusted_rand_score([0, 0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 0, 0])
159       1.0
160 
161     Labelings that assign all classes members to the same clusters
162     are complete be not always pure, hence penalized::
163 
164       >>> adjusted_rand_score([0, 0, 1, 2], [0, 0, 1, 1])  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
165       0.57...
166 
167     ARI is symmetric, so labelings that have pure clusters with members
168     coming from the same classes but unnecessary splits are penalized::
169 
170       >>> adjusted_rand_score([0, 0, 1, 1], [0, 0, 1, 2])  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
171       0.57...
172 
173     If classes members are completely split across different clusters, the
174     assignment is totally incomplete, hence the ARI is very low::
175 
176       >>> adjusted_rand_score([0, 0, 0, 0], [0, 1, 2, 3])
177       0.0
178 
179     References
180     ----------
181 
182     .. [Hubert1985] `L. Hubert and P. Arabie, Comparing Partitions,
183       Journal of Classification 1985`
184       http://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF01908075
185 
186     .. [wk] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rand_index#Adjusted_Rand_index
187 
188     See also
189     --------
190     adjusted_mutual_info_score: Adjusted Mutual Information
191 
192     """
193     labels_true, labels_pred = check_clusterings(labels_true, labels_pred)
194     n_samples = labels_true.shape[0]
195     n_classes = np.unique(labels_true).shape[0]
196     n_clusters = np.unique(labels_pred).shape[0]
197 
198     # Special limit cases: no clustering since the data is not split;
199     # or trivial clustering where each document is assigned a unique cluster.
200     # These are perfect matches hence return 1.0.
201     if (n_classes == n_clusters == 1 or
202             n_classes == n_clusters == 0 or
203             n_classes == n_clusters == n_samples):
204         return 1.0
205 
206     # Compute the ARI using the contingency data
207     contingency = contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred, sparse=True)
208     sum_comb_c = sum(comb2(n_c) for n_c in np.ravel(contingency.sum(axis=1)))
209     sum_comb_k = sum(comb2(n_k) for n_k in np.ravel(contingency.sum(axis=0)))
210     sum_comb = sum(comb2(n_ij) for n_ij in contingency.data)
211 
212     prod_comb = (sum_comb_c * sum_comb_k) / comb2(n_samples)
213     mean_comb = (sum_comb_k + sum_comb_c) / 2.
214     return (sum_comb - prod_comb) / (mean_comb - prod_comb)
215

217 def homogeneity_completeness_v_measure(labels_true, labels_pred):
218     """Compute the homogeneity and completeness and V-Measure scores at once.
219 
220     Those metrics are based on normalized conditional entropy measures of
221     the clustering labeling to evaluate given the knowledge of a Ground
222     Truth class labels of the same samples.
223 
224     A clustering result satisfies homogeneity if all of its clusters
225     contain only data points which are members of a single class.
226 
227     A clustering result satisfies completeness if all the data points
228     that are members of a given class are elements of the same cluster.
229 
230     Both scores have positive values between 0.0 and 1.0, larger values
231     being desirable.
232 
233     Those 3 metrics are independent of the absolute values of the labels:
234     a permutation of the class or cluster label values won't change the
235     score values in any way.
236 
237     V-Measure is furthermore symmetric: swapping ``labels_true`` and
238     ``label_pred`` will give the same score. This does not hold for
239     homogeneity and completeness.
240 
241     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <homogeneity_completeness>`.
242 
243     Parameters
244     ----------
245     labels_true : int array, shape = [n_samples]
246         ground truth class labels to be used as a reference
247 
248     labels_pred : array, shape = [n_samples]
249         cluster labels to evaluate
250 
251     Returns
252     -------
253     homogeneity : float
254        score between 0.0 and 1.0. 1.0 stands for perfectly homogeneous labeling
255 
256     completeness : float
257        score between 0.0 and 1.0. 1.0 stands for perfectly complete labeling
258 
259     v_measure : float
260         harmonic mean of the first two
261 
262     See also
263     --------
264     homogeneity_score
265     completeness_score
266     v_measure_score
267     """
268     labels_true, labels_pred = check_clusterings(labels_true, labels_pred)
269 
270     if len(labels_true) == 0:
271         return 1.0, 1.0, 1.0
272 
273     entropy_C = entropy(labels_true)
274     entropy_K = entropy(labels_pred)
275 
276     contingency = contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred, sparse=True)
277     MI = mutual_info_score(None, None, contingency=contingency)
278 
279     homogeneity = MI / (entropy_C) if entropy_C else 1.0
280     completeness = MI / (entropy_K) if entropy_K else 1.0
281 
282     if homogeneity + completeness == 0.0:
283         v_measure_score = 0.0
284     else:
285         v_measure_score = (2.0 * homogeneity * completeness /
286                            (homogeneity + completeness))
287 
288     return homogeneity, completeness, v_measure_score

530 def mutual_info_score(labels_true, labels_pred, contingency=None):
531     r"""Mutual Information between two clusterings.
532 
533     The Mutual Information is a measure of the similarity between two labels of
534     the same data. Where :math:`|U_i|` is the number of the samples
535     in cluster :math:`U_i` and :math:`|V_j|` is the number of the
536     samples in cluster :math:`V_j`, the Mutual Information
537     between clusterings :math:`U` and :math:`V` is given as:
538 
539     .. math::
540 
541         MI(U,V)=\sum_{i=1}^{|U|} \sum_{j=1}^{|V|} \\frac{|U_i\cap V_j|}{N}
542         \log\\frac{N|U_i \cap V_j|}{|U_i||V_j|}
543 
544     This metric is independent of the absolute values of the labels:
545     a permutation of the class or cluster label values won't change the
546     score value in any way.
547 
548     This metric is furthermore symmetric: switching ``label_true`` with
549     ``label_pred`` will return the same score value. This can be useful to
550     measure the agreement of two independent label assignments strategies
551     on the same dataset when the real ground truth is not known.
552 
553     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <mutual_info_score>`.
554 
555     Parameters
556     ----------
557     labels_true : int array, shape = [n_samples]
558         A clustering of the data into disjoint subsets.
559 
560     labels_pred : array, shape = [n_samples]
561         A clustering of the data into disjoint subsets.
562 
563     contingency : {None, array, sparse matrix},
564                   shape = [n_classes_true, n_classes_pred]
565         A contingency matrix given by the :func:`contingency_matrix` function.
566         If value is ``None``, it will be computed, otherwise the given value is
567         used, with ``labels_true`` and ``labels_pred`` ignored.
568 
569     Returns
570     -------
571     mi : float
572        Mutual information, a non-negative value
573 
574     See also
575     --------
576     adjusted_mutual_info_score: Adjusted against chance Mutual Information
577     normalized_mutual_info_score: Normalized Mutual Information
578     """
579     if contingency is None:
580         labels_true, labels_pred = check_clusterings(labels_true, labels_pred)
581         contingency = contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred, sparse=True)
582     else:
583         contingency = check_array(contingency,
584                                   accept_sparse=['csr', 'csc', 'coo'],
585                                   dtype=[int, np.int32, np.int64])
586 
587     if isinstance(contingency, np.ndarray):
588         # For an array
589         nzx, nzy = np.nonzero(contingency)
590         nz_val = contingency[nzx, nzy]
591     elif sp.issparse(contingency):
592         # For a sparse matrix
593         nzx, nzy, nz_val = sp.find(contingency)
594     else:
595         raise ValueError("Unsupported type for 'contingency': %s" %
596                          type(contingency))
597 
598     contingency_sum = contingency.sum()
599     pi = np.ravel(contingency.sum(axis=1))
600     pj = np.ravel(contingency.sum(axis=0))
601     log_contingency_nm = np.log(nz_val)
602     contingency_nm = nz_val / contingency_sum
603     # Don't need to calculate the full outer product, just for non-zeroes
604     outer = pi.take(nzx).astype(np.int64) * pj.take(nzy).astype(np.int64)
605     log_outer = -np.log(outer) + log(pi.sum()) + log(pj.sum())
606     mi = (contingency_nm * (log_contingency_nm - log(contingency_sum)) +
607           contingency_nm * log_outer)
608     return mi.sum()
609

611 def adjusted_mutual_info_score(labels_true, labels_pred):
612     """Adjusted Mutual Information between two clusterings.
613 
614     Adjusted Mutual Information (AMI) is an adjustment of the Mutual
615     Information (MI) score to account for chance. It accounts for the fact that
616     the MI is generally higher for two clusterings with a larger number of
617     clusters, regardless of whether there is actually more information shared.
618     For two clusterings :math:`U` and :math:`V`, the AMI is given as::
619 
620         AMI(U, V) = [MI(U, V) - E(MI(U, V))] / [max(H(U), H(V)) - E(MI(U, V))]
621 
622     This metric is independent of the absolute values of the labels:
623     a permutation of the class or cluster label values won't change the
624     score value in any way.
625 
626     This metric is furthermore symmetric: switching ``label_true`` with
627     ``label_pred`` will return the same score value. This can be useful to
628     measure the agreement of two independent label assignments strategies
629     on the same dataset when the real ground truth is not known.
630 
631     Be mindful that this function is an order of magnitude slower than other
632     metrics, such as the Adjusted Rand Index.
633 
634     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <mutual_info_score>`.
635 
636     Parameters
637     ----------
638     labels_true : int array, shape = [n_samples]
639         A clustering of the data into disjoint subsets.
640 
641     labels_pred : array, shape = [n_samples]
642         A clustering of the data into disjoint subsets.
643 
644     Returns
645     -------
646     ami: float(upperlimited by 1.0)
647        The AMI returns a value of 1 when the two partitions are identical
648        (ie perfectly matched). Random partitions (independent labellings) have
649        an expected AMI around 0 on average hence can be negative.
650 
651     See also
652     --------
653     adjusted_rand_score: Adjusted Rand Index
654     mutual_info_score: Mutual Information (not adjusted for chance)
655 
656     Examples
657     --------
658 
659     Perfect labelings are both homogeneous and complete, hence have
660     score 1.0::
661 
662       >>> from sklearn.metrics.cluster import adjusted_mutual_info_score
663       >>> adjusted_mutual_info_score([0, 0, 1, 1], [0, 0, 1, 1])
664       1.0
665       >>> adjusted_mutual_info_score([0, 0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 0, 0])
666       1.0
667 
668     If classes members are completely split across different clusters,
669     the assignment is totally in-complete, hence the AMI is null::
670 
671       >>> adjusted_mutual_info_score([0, 0, 0, 0], [0, 1, 2, 3])
672       0.0
673 
674     References
675     ----------
676     .. [1] `Vinh, Epps, and Bailey, (2010). Information Theoretic Measures for
677        Clusterings Comparison: Variants, Properties, Normalization and
678        Correction for Chance, JMLR
679        <http://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/papers/volume11/vinh10a/vinh10a.pdf>`_
680 
681     .. [2] `Wikipedia entry for the Adjusted Mutual Information
682        <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adjusted_Mutual_Information>`_
683 
684     """
685     labels_true, labels_pred = check_clusterings(labels_true, labels_pred)
686     n_samples = labels_true.shape[0]
687     classes = np.unique(labels_true)
688     clusters = np.unique(labels_pred)
689     # Special limit cases: no clustering since the data is not split.
690     # This is a perfect match hence return 1.0.
691     if (classes.shape[0] == clusters.shape[0] == 1 or
692             classes.shape[0] == clusters.shape[0] == 0):
693         return 1.0
694     contingency = contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred, sparse=True)
695     contingency = contingency.astype(np.float64)
696     # Calculate the MI for the two clusterings
697     mi = mutual_info_score(labels_true, labels_pred,
698                            contingency=contingency)
699     # Calculate the expected value for the mutual information
700     emi = expected_mutual_information(contingency, n_samples)
701     # Calculate entropy for each labeling
702     h_true, h_pred = entropy(labels_true), entropy(labels_pred)
703     ami = (mi - emi) / (max(h_true, h_pred) - emi)
704     return ami

CountVectorizer's get_feature_names raise not NotFittedError when the vocabulary parameter is provided
If you initialize a `CounterVectorizer` and try to perform a transformation without training you will get a `NotFittedError` exception.

```python
In [1]: from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer
In [2]: vectorizer = CountVectorizer()
In [3]: corpus = [
    ...:     'This is the first document.',
    ...:     'This is the second second document.',
    ...:     'And the third one.',
    ...:     'Is this the first document?',
    ...: ]

In [4]: vectorizer.transform(corpus)
NotFittedError: CountVectorizer - Vocabulary wasn't fitted.
```
On the other hand if you provide the `vocabulary` at the initialization of the vectorizer you could transform a corpus without a prior training, right?

```python
In [1]: from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer

In [2]: vectorizer = CountVectorizer()

In [3]: corpus = [
    ...:     'This is the first document.',
    ...:     'This is the second second document.',
    ...:     'And the third one.',
    ...:     'Is this the first document?',
    ...: ]

In [4]: vocabulary = ['and', 'document', 'first', 'is', 'one', 'second', 'the', 'third', 'this']

In [5]: vectorizer = CountVectorizer(vocabulary=vocabulary)

In [6]: hasattr(vectorizer, "vocabulary_")
Out[6]: False

In [7]: vectorizer.get_feature_names()
NotFittedError: CountVectorizer - Vocabulary wasn't fitted.

In [8]: vectorizer.transform(corpus)
Out[8]:
<4x9 sparse matrix of type '<class 'numpy.int64'>'
        with 19 stored elements in Compressed Sparse Row format>

In [9]: hasattr(vectorizer, "vocabulary_")
Out[9]: True
```

The `CountVectorizer`'s `transform` calls `_validate_vocabulary` method which sets the `vocabulary_` instance variable.

In the same manner I believe that the `get_feature_names` method should not raise `NotFittedError` if the vocabulary parameter is provided but the vectorizer has not been trained.

44 def strip_accents_unicode(s):
45     """Transform accentuated unicode symbols into their simple counterpart
46 
47     Warning: the python-level loop and join operations make this
48     implementation 20 times slower than the strip_accents_ascii basic
49     normalization.
50 
51     See also
52     --------
53     strip_accents_ascii
54         Remove accentuated char for any unicode symbol that has a direct
55         ASCII equivalent.
56     """
57     normalized = unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', s)
58     if normalized == s:
59         return s
60     else:
61         return ''.join([c for c in normalized if not unicodedata.combining(c)])
62 
63 
64 def strip_accents_ascii(s):
65     """Transform accentuated unicode symbols into ascii or nothing
66 
67     Warning: this solution is only suited for languages that have a direct
68     transliteration to ASCII symbols.
69 
70     See also
71     --------
72     strip_accents_unicode
73         Remove accentuated char for any unicode symbol.
74     """
75     nkfd_form = unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', s)
76     return nkfd_form.encode('ASCII', 'ignore').decode('ASCII')

99 class VectorizerMixin(object):
100     """Provides common code for text vectorizers (tokenization logic)."""
101 
102     _white_spaces = re.compile(r"\s\s+")
103 
104     def decode(self, doc):
105         """Decode the input into a string of unicode symbols
106 
107         The decoding strategy depends on the vectorizer parameters.
108         """
109         if self.input == 'filename':
110             with open(doc, 'rb') as fh:
111                 doc = fh.read()
112 
113         elif self.input == 'file':
114             doc = doc.read()
115 
116         if isinstance(doc, bytes):
117             doc = doc.decode(self.encoding, self.decode_error)
118 
119         if doc is np.nan:
120             raise ValueError("np.nan is an invalid document, expected byte or "
121                              "unicode string.")
122 
123         return doc
124 
125     def _word_ngrams(self, tokens, stop_words=None):
126         """Turn tokens into a sequence of n-grams after stop words filtering"""
127         # handle stop words
128         if stop_words is not None:
129             tokens = [w for w in tokens if w not in stop_words]
130 
131         # handle token n-grams
132         min_n, max_n = self.ngram_range
133         if max_n != 1:
134             original_tokens = tokens
135             if min_n == 1:
136                 # no need to do any slicing for unigrams
137                 # just iterate through the original tokens
138                 tokens = list(original_tokens)
139                 min_n += 1
140             else:
141                 tokens = []
142 
143             n_original_tokens = len(original_tokens)
144 
145             # bind method outside of loop to reduce overhead
146             tokens_append = tokens.append
147             space_join = " ".join
148 
149             for n in xrange(min_n,
150                             min(max_n + 1, n_original_tokens + 1)):
151                 for i in xrange(n_original_tokens - n + 1):
152                     tokens_append(space_join(original_tokens[i: i + n]))
153 
154         return tokens
155 
156     def _char_ngrams(self, text_document):
157         """Tokenize text_document into a sequence of character n-grams"""
158         # normalize white spaces
159         text_document = self._white_spaces.sub(" ", text_document)
160 
161         text_len = len(text_document)
162         min_n, max_n = self.ngram_range
163         if min_n == 1:
164             # no need to do any slicing for unigrams
165             # iterate through the string
166             ngrams = list(text_document)
167             min_n += 1
168         else:
169             ngrams = []
170 
171         # bind method outside of loop to reduce overhead
172         ngrams_append = ngrams.append
173 
174         for n in xrange(min_n, min(max_n + 1, text_len + 1)):
175             for i in xrange(text_len - n + 1):
176                 ngrams_append(text_document[i: i + n])
177         return ngrams
178 
179     def _char_wb_ngrams(self, text_document):
180         """Whitespace sensitive char-n-gram tokenization.
181 
182         Tokenize text_document into a sequence of character n-grams
183         operating only inside word boundaries. n-grams at the edges
184         of words are padded with space."""
185         # normalize white spaces
186         text_document = self._white_spaces.sub(" ", text_document)
187 
188         min_n, max_n = self.ngram_range
189         ngrams = []
190 
191         # bind method outside of loop to reduce overhead
192         ngrams_append = ngrams.append
193 
194         for w in text_document.split():
195             w = ' ' + w + ' '
196             w_len = len(w)
197             for n in xrange(min_n, max_n + 1):
198                 offset = 0
199                 ngrams_append(w[offset:offset + n])
200                 while offset + n < w_len:
201                     offset += 1
202                     ngrams_append(w[offset:offset + n])
203                 if offset == 0:   # count a short word (w_len < n) only once
204                     break
205         return ngrams
206 
207     def build_preprocessor(self):
208         """Return a function to preprocess the text before tokenization"""
209         if self.preprocessor is not None:
210             return self.preprocessor
211 
212         # unfortunately python functools package does not have an efficient
213         # `compose` function that would have allowed us to chain a dynamic
214         # number of functions. However the cost of a lambda call is a few
215         # hundreds of nanoseconds which is negligible when compared to the
216         # cost of tokenizing a string of 1000 chars for instance.
217         noop = lambda x: x
218 
219         # accent stripping
220         if not self.strip_accents:
221             strip_accents = noop
222         elif callable(self.strip_accents):
223             strip_accents = self.strip_accents
224         elif self.strip_accents == 'ascii':
225             strip_accents = strip_accents_ascii
226         elif self.strip_accents == 'unicode':
227             strip_accents = strip_accents_unicode
228         else:
229             raise ValueError('Invalid value for "strip_accents": %s' %
230                              self.strip_accents)
231 
232         if self.lowercase:
233             return lambda x: strip_accents(x.lower())
234         else:
235             return strip_accents
236 
237     def build_tokenizer(self):
238         """Return a function that splits a string into a sequence of tokens"""
239         if self.tokenizer is not None:
240             return self.tokenizer
241         token_pattern = re.compile(self.token_pattern)
242         return lambda doc: token_pattern.findall(doc)
243 
244     def get_stop_words(self):
245         """Build or fetch the effective stop words list"""
246         return _check_stop_list(self.stop_words)
247 
248     def build_analyzer(self):
249         """Return a callable that handles preprocessing and tokenization"""
250         if callable(self.analyzer):
251             return self.analyzer
252 
253         preprocess = self.build_preprocessor()
254 
255         if self.analyzer == 'char':
256             return lambda doc: self._char_ngrams(preprocess(self.decode(doc)))
257 
258         elif self.analyzer == 'char_wb':
259             return lambda doc: self._char_wb_ngrams(
260                 preprocess(self.decode(doc)))
261 
262         elif self.analyzer == 'word':
263             stop_words = self.get_stop_words()
264             tokenize = self.build_tokenizer()
265 
266             return lambda doc: self._word_ngrams(
267                 tokenize(preprocess(self.decode(doc))), stop_words)
268 
269         else:
270             raise ValueError('%s is not a valid tokenization scheme/analyzer' %
271                              self.analyzer)
272 
273     def _validate_vocabulary(self):
274         vocabulary = self.vocabulary
275         if vocabulary is not None:
276             if isinstance(vocabulary, set):
277                 vocabulary = sorted(vocabulary)
278             if not isinstance(vocabulary, Mapping):
279                 vocab = {}
280                 for i, t in enumerate(vocabulary):
281                     if vocab.setdefault(t, i) != i:
282                         msg = "Duplicate term in vocabulary: %r" % t
283                         raise ValueError(msg)
284                 vocabulary = vocab
285             else:
286                 indices = set(six.itervalues(vocabulary))
287                 if len(indices) != len(vocabulary):
288                     raise ValueError("Vocabulary contains repeated indices.")
289                 for i in xrange(len(vocabulary)):
290                     if i not in indices:
291                         msg = ("Vocabulary of size %d doesn't contain index "
292                                "%d." % (len(vocabulary), i))
293                         raise ValueError(msg)
294             if not vocabulary:
295                 raise ValueError("empty vocabulary passed to fit")
296             self.fixed_vocabulary_ = True
297             self.vocabulary_ = dict(vocabulary)
298         else:
299             self.fixed_vocabulary_ = False
300 
301     def _check_vocabulary(self):
302         """Check if vocabulary is empty or missing (not fit-ed)"""
303         msg = "%(name)s - Vocabulary wasn't fitted."
304         check_is_fitted(self, 'vocabulary_', msg=msg),
305 
306         if len(self.vocabulary_) == 0:
307             raise ValueError("Vocabulary is empty")
308 
309     def _validate_params(self):
310         """Check validity of ngram_range parameter"""
311         min_n, max_m = self.ngram_range
312         if min_n > max_m:
313             raise ValueError(
314                 "Invalid value for ngram_range=%s "
315                 "lower boundary larger than the upper boundary."
316                 % str(self.ngram_range))
