319 class HashingVectorizer(BaseEstimator, VectorizerMixin, TransformerMixin):
320     """Convert a collection of text documents to a matrix of token occurrences
321 
322     It turns a collection of text documents into a scipy.sparse matrix holding
323     token occurrence counts (or binary occurrence information), possibly
324     normalized as token frequencies if norm='l1' or projected on the euclidean
325     unit sphere if norm='l2'.
326 
327     This text vectorizer implementation uses the hashing trick to find the
328     token string name to feature integer index mapping.
329 
330     This strategy has several advantages:
331 
332     - it is very low memory scalable to large datasets as there is no need to
333       store a vocabulary dictionary in memory
334 
335     - it is fast to pickle and un-pickle as it holds no state besides the
336       constructor parameters
337 
338     - it can be used in a streaming (partial fit) or parallel pipeline as there
339       is no state computed during fit.
340 
341     There are also a couple of cons (vs using a CountVectorizer with an
342     in-memory vocabulary):
343 
344     - there is no way to compute the inverse transform (from feature indices to
345       string feature names) which can be a problem when trying to introspect
346       which features are most important to a model.
347 
348     - there can be collisions: distinct tokens can be mapped to the same
349       feature index. However in practice this is rarely an issue if n_features
350       is large enough (e.g. 2 ** 18 for text classification problems).
351 
352     - no IDF weighting as this would render the transformer stateful.
353 
354     The hash function employed is the signed 32-bit version of Murmurhash3.
355 
356     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <text_feature_extraction>`.
357 
358     Parameters
359     ----------
360 
361     input : string {'filename', 'file', 'content'}
362         If 'filename', the sequence passed as an argument to fit is
363         expected to be a list of filenames that need reading to fetch
364         the raw content to analyze.
365 
366         If 'file', the sequence items must have a 'read' method (file-like
367         object) that is called to fetch the bytes in memory.
368 
369         Otherwise the input is expected to be the sequence strings or
370         bytes items are expected to be analyzed directly.
371 
372     encoding : string, default='utf-8'
373         If bytes or files are given to analyze, this encoding is used to
374         decode.
375 
376     decode_error : {'strict', 'ignore', 'replace'}
377         Instruction on what to do if a byte sequence is given to analyze that
378         contains characters not of the given `encoding`. By default, it is
379         'strict', meaning that a UnicodeDecodeError will be raised. Other
380         values are 'ignore' and 'replace'.
381 
382     strip_accents : {'ascii', 'unicode', None}
383         Remove accents and perform other character normalization
384         during the preprocessing step.
385         'ascii' is a fast method that only works on characters that have
386         an direct ASCII mapping.
387         'unicode' is a slightly slower method that works on any characters.
388         None (default) does nothing.
389 
390         Both 'ascii' and 'unicode' use NFKD normalization from
391         :func:`unicodedata.normalize`.
392 
393     analyzer : string, {'word', 'char', 'char_wb'} or callable
394         Whether the feature should be made of word or character n-grams.
395         Option 'char_wb' creates character n-grams only from text inside
396         word boundaries; n-grams at the edges of words are padded with space.
397 
398         If a callable is passed it is used to extract the sequence of features
399         out of the raw, unprocessed input.
400 
401     preprocessor : callable or None (default)
402         Override the preprocessing (string transformation) stage while
403         preserving the tokenizing and n-grams generation steps.
404 
405     tokenizer : callable or None (default)
406         Override the string tokenization step while preserving the
407         preprocessing and n-grams generation steps.
408         Only applies if ``analyzer == 'word'``.
409 
410     ngram_range : tuple (min_n, max_n), default=(1, 1)
411         The lower and upper boundary of the range of n-values for different
412         n-grams to be extracted. All values of n such that min_n <= n <= max_n
413         will be used.
414 
415     stop_words : string {'english'}, list, or None (default)
416         If 'english', a built-in stop word list for English is used.
417 
418         If a list, that list is assumed to contain stop words, all of which
419         will be removed from the resulting tokens.
420         Only applies if ``analyzer == 'word'``.
421 
422     lowercase : boolean, default=True
423         Convert all characters to lowercase before tokenizing.
424 
425     token_pattern : string
426         Regular expression denoting what constitutes a "token", only used
427         if ``analyzer == 'word'``. The default regexp selects tokens of 2
428         or more alphanumeric characters (punctuation is completely ignored
429         and always treated as a token separator).
430 
431     n_features : integer, default=(2 ** 20)
432         The number of features (columns) in the output matrices. Small numbers
433         of features are likely to cause hash collisions, but large numbers
434         will cause larger coefficient dimensions in linear learners.
435 
436     norm : 'l1', 'l2' or None, optional
437         Norm used to normalize term vectors. None for no normalization.
438 
439     binary : boolean, default=False.
440         If True, all non zero counts are set to 1. This is useful for discrete
441         probabilistic models that model binary events rather than integer
442         counts.
443 
444     dtype : type, optional
445         Type of the matrix returned by fit_transform() or transform().
446 
447     alternate_sign : boolean, optional, default True
448         When True, an alternating sign is added to the features as to
449         approximately conserve the inner product in the hashed space even for
450         small n_features. This approach is similar to sparse random projection.
451 
452         .. versionadded:: 0.19
453 
454     non_negative : boolean, optional, default False
455         When True, an absolute value is applied to the features matrix prior to
456         returning it. When used in conjunction with alternate_sign=True, this
457         significantly reduces the inner product preservation property.
458 
459         .. deprecated:: 0.19
460             This option will be removed in 0.21.
461 
462     See also
463     --------
464     CountVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer
465 
466     """
467     def __init__(self, input='content', encoding='utf-8',
468                  decode_error='strict', strip_accents=None,
469                  lowercase=True, preprocessor=None, tokenizer=None,
470                  stop_words=None, token_pattern=r"(?u)\b\w\w+\b",
471                  ngram_range=(1, 1), analyzer='word', n_features=(2 ** 20),
472                  binary=False, norm='l2', alternate_sign=True,
473                  non_negative=False, dtype=np.float64):
474         self.input = input
475         self.encoding = encoding
476         self.decode_error = decode_error
477         self.strip_accents = strip_accents
478         self.preprocessor = preprocessor
479         self.tokenizer = tokenizer
480         self.analyzer = analyzer
481         self.lowercase = lowercase
482         self.token_pattern = token_pattern
483         self.stop_words = stop_words
484         self.n_features = n_features
485         self.ngram_range = ngram_range
486         self.binary = binary
487         self.norm = norm
488         self.alternate_sign = alternate_sign
489         self.non_negative = non_negative
490         self.dtype = dtype
491 
492     def partial_fit(self, X, y=None):
493         """Does nothing: this transformer is stateless.
494 
495         This method is just there to mark the fact that this transformer
496         can work in a streaming setup.
497 
498         """
499         return self
500 
501     def fit(self, X, y=None):
502         """Does nothing: this transformer is stateless."""
503         # triggers a parameter validation
504         if isinstance(X, six.string_types):
505             raise ValueError(
506                 "Iterable over raw text documents expected, "
507                 "string object received.")
508 
509         self._validate_params()
510 
511         self._get_hasher().fit(X, y=y)
512         return self
513 
514     def transform(self, X):
515         """Transform a sequence of documents to a document-term matrix.
516 
517         Parameters
518         ----------
519         X : iterable over raw text documents, length = n_samples
520             Samples. Each sample must be a text document (either bytes or
521             unicode strings, file name or file object depending on the
522             constructor argument) which will be tokenized and hashed.
523 
524         Returns
525         -------
526         X : scipy.sparse matrix, shape = (n_samples, self.n_features)
527             Document-term matrix.
528         """
529         if isinstance(X, six.string_types):
530             raise ValueError(
531                 "Iterable over raw text documents expected, "
532                 "string object received.")
533 
534         self._validate_params()
535 
536         analyzer = self.build_analyzer()
537         X = self._get_hasher().transform(analyzer(doc) for doc in X)
538         if self.binary:
539             X.data.fill(1)
540         if self.norm is not None:
541             X = normalize(X, norm=self.norm, copy=False)
542         return X
543 
544     def _get_hasher(self):
545         return FeatureHasher(n_features=self.n_features,
546                              input_type='string', dtype=self.dtype,
547                              alternate_sign=self.alternate_sign,
548                              non_negative=self.non_negative)
549 
550 
551 def _document_frequency(X):
552     """Count the number of non-zero values for each feature in sparse X."""
553     if sp.isspmatrix_csr(X):
554         return np.bincount(X.indices, minlength=X.shape[1])
555     else:
556         return np.diff(sp.csc_matrix(X, copy=False).indptr)

559 class CountVectorizer(BaseEstimator, VectorizerMixin):

562     This implementation produces a sparse representation of the counts using
563     scipy.sparse.csr_matrix.
564 
565     If you do not provide an a-priori dictionary and you do not use an analyzer
566     that does some kind of feature selection then the number of features will
567     be equal to the vocabulary size found by analyzing the data.
568 
569     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <text_feature_extraction>`.
570 
571     Parameters
572     ----------
573     input : string {'filename', 'file', 'content'}
574         If 'filename', the sequence passed as an argument to fit is
575         expected to be a list of filenames that need reading to fetch
576         the raw content to analyze.
577 
578         If 'file', the sequence items must have a 'read' method (file-like
579         object) that is called to fetch the bytes in memory.
580 
581         Otherwise the input is expected to be the sequence strings or
582         bytes items are expected to be analyzed directly.
583 
584     encoding : string, 'utf-8' by default.
585         If bytes or files are given to analyze, this encoding is used to
586         decode.
587 
588     decode_error : {'strict', 'ignore', 'replace'}
589         Instruction on what to do if a byte sequence is given to analyze that
590         contains characters not of the given `encoding`. By default, it is
591         'strict', meaning that a UnicodeDecodeError will be raised. Other
592         values are 'ignore' and 'replace'.
593 
594     strip_accents : {'ascii', 'unicode', None}
595         Remove accents and perform other character normalization
596         during the preprocessing step.
597         'ascii' is a fast method that only works on characters that have
598         an direct ASCII mapping.
599         'unicode' is a slightly slower method that works on any characters.
600         None (default) does nothing.
601 
602         Both 'ascii' and 'unicode' use NFKD normalization from
603         :func:`unicodedata.normalize`.
604 
605     analyzer : string, {'word', 'char', 'char_wb'} or callable
606         Whether the feature should be made of word or character n-grams.
607         Option 'char_wb' creates character n-grams only from text inside
608         word boundaries; n-grams at the edges of words are padded with space.
609 
610         If a callable is passed it is used to extract the sequence of features
611         out of the raw, unprocessed input.
612 
613     preprocessor : callable or None (default)
614         Override the preprocessing (string transformation) stage while
615         preserving the tokenizing and n-grams generation steps.
616 
617     tokenizer : callable or None (default)
618         Override the string tokenization step while preserving the
619         preprocessing and n-grams generation steps.
620         Only applies if ``analyzer == 'word'``.
621 
622     ngram_range : tuple (min_n, max_n)
623         The lower and upper boundary of the range of n-values for different
624         n-grams to be extracted. All values of n such that min_n <= n <= max_n
625         will be used.
626 
627     stop_words : string {'english'}, list, or None (default)
628         If 'english', a built-in stop word list for English is used.
629 
630         If a list, that list is assumed to contain stop words, all of which
631         will be removed from the resulting tokens.
632         Only applies if ``analyzer == 'word'``.
633 
634         If None, no stop words will be used. max_df can be set to a value
635         in the range [0.7, 1.0) to automatically detect and filter stop
636         words based on intra corpus document frequency of terms.
637 
638     lowercase : boolean, True by default
639         Convert all characters to lowercase before tokenizing.
640 
641     token_pattern : string
642         Regular expression denoting what constitutes a "token", only used
643         if ``analyzer == 'word'``. The default regexp select tokens of 2
644         or more alphanumeric characters (punctuation is completely ignored
645         and always treated as a token separator).

647     max_df : float in range [0.0, 1.0] or int, default=1.0
648         When building the vocabulary ignore terms that have a document
649         frequency strictly higher than the given threshold (corpus-specific
650         stop words).
651         If float, the parameter represents a proportion of documents, integer
652         absolute counts.
653         This parameter is ignored if vocabulary is not None.
654 
655     min_df : float in range [0.0, 1.0] or int, default=1
656         When building the vocabulary ignore terms that have a document
657         frequency strictly lower than the given threshold. This value is also
658         called cut-off in the literature.
659         If float, the parameter represents a proportion of documents, integer
660         absolute counts.
661         This parameter is ignored if vocabulary is not None.
662 
663     max_features : int or None, default=None
664         If not None, build a vocabulary that only consider the top
665         max_features ordered by term frequency across the corpus.
666 
667         This parameter is ignored if vocabulary is not None.
668 
669     vocabulary : Mapping or iterable, optional
670         Either a Mapping (e.g., a dict) where keys are terms and values are
671         indices in the feature matrix, or an iterable over terms. If not
672         given, a vocabulary is determined from the input documents. Indices
673         in the mapping should not be repeated and should not have any gap
674         between 0 and the largest index.
675 
676     binary : boolean, default=False
677         If True, all non zero counts are set to 1. This is useful for discrete
678         probabilistic models that model binary events rather than integer
679         counts.
680 
681     dtype : type, optional
682         Type of the matrix returned by fit_transform() or transform().
683 
684     Attributes
685     ----------
686     vocabulary_ : dict
687         A mapping of terms to feature indices.
688 
689     stop_words_ : set
690         Terms that were ignored because they either:
691 
692           - occurred in too many documents (`max_df`)
693           - occurred in too few documents (`min_df`)
694           - were cut off by feature selection (`max_features`).
695 
696         This is only available if no vocabulary was given.
697 
698     See also
699     --------
700     HashingVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer
701 
702     Notes
703     -----
704     The ``stop_words_`` attribute can get large and increase the model size
705     when pickling. This attribute is provided only for introspection and can
706     be safely removed using delattr or set to None before pickling.
707     """
708 
709     def __init__(self, input='content', encoding='utf-8',
710                  decode_error='strict', strip_accents=None,
711                  lowercase=True, preprocessor=None, tokenizer=None,
712                  stop_words=None, token_pattern=r"(?u)\b\w\w+\b",
713                  ngram_range=(1, 1), analyzer='word',
714                  max_df=1.0, min_df=1, max_features=None,
715                  vocabulary=None, binary=False, dtype=np.int64):
716         self.input = input
717         self.encoding = encoding
718         self.decode_error = decode_error
719         self.strip_accents = strip_accents
720         self.preprocessor = preprocessor
721         self.tokenizer = tokenizer
722         self.analyzer = analyzer
723         self.lowercase = lowercase
724         self.token_pattern = token_pattern
725         self.stop_words = stop_words
726         self.max_df = max_df
727         self.min_df = min_df
728         if max_df < 0 or min_df < 0:
729             raise ValueError("negative value for max_df or min_df")
730         self.max_features = max_features
731         if max_features is not None:
732             if (not isinstance(max_features, numbers.Integral) or
733                     max_features <= 0):
734                 raise ValueError(
735                     "max_features=%r, neither a positive integer nor None"
736                     % max_features)
737         self.ngram_range = ngram_range
738         self.vocabulary = vocabulary
739         self.binary = binary
740         self.dtype = dtype
741 
742     def _sort_features(self, X, vocabulary):
743         """Sort features by name
744 
745         Returns a reordered matrix and modifies the vocabulary in place
746         """
747         sorted_features = sorted(six.iteritems(vocabulary))
748         map_index = np.empty(len(sorted_features), dtype=np.int32)
749         for new_val, (term, old_val) in enumerate(sorted_features):
750             vocabulary[term] = new_val
751             map_index[old_val] = new_val
752 
753         X.indices = map_index.take(X.indices, mode='clip')
754         return X
755 
756     def _limit_features(self, X, vocabulary, high=None, low=None,
757                         limit=None):
758         """Remove too rare or too common features.
759 
760         Prune features that are non zero in more samples than high or less
761         documents than low, modifying the vocabulary, and restricting it to
762         at most the limit most frequent.
763 
764         This does not prune samples with zero features.
765         """
766         if high is None and low is None and limit is None:
767             return X, set()
768 
769         # Calculate a mask based on document frequencies
770         dfs = _document_frequency(X)
771         tfs = np.asarray(X.sum(axis=0)).ravel()
772         mask = np.ones(len(dfs), dtype=bool)
773         if high is not None:
774             mask &= dfs <= high
775         if low is not None:
776             mask &= dfs >= low
777         if limit is not None and mask.sum() > limit:
778             mask_inds = (-tfs[mask]).argsort()[:limit]
779             new_mask = np.zeros(len(dfs), dtype=bool)
780             new_mask[np.where(mask)[0][mask_inds]] = True
781             mask = new_mask
782 
783         new_indices = np.cumsum(mask) - 1  # maps old indices to new
784         removed_terms = set()
785         for term, old_index in list(six.iteritems(vocabulary)):
786             if mask[old_index]:
787                 vocabulary[term] = new_indices[old_index]
788             else:
789                 del vocabulary[term]
790                 removed_terms.add(term)
791         kept_indices = np.where(mask)[0]
792         if len(kept_indices) == 0:
793             raise ValueError("After pruning, no terms remain. Try a lower"
794                              " min_df or a higher max_df.")
795         return X[:, kept_indices], removed_terms
796 
797     def _count_vocab(self, raw_documents, fixed_vocab):
798         """Create sparse feature matrix, and vocabulary where fixed_vocab=False
799         """
800         if fixed_vocab:
801             vocabulary = self.vocabulary_
802         else:
803             # Add a new value when a new vocabulary item is seen
804             vocabulary = defaultdict()
805             vocabulary.default_factory = vocabulary.__len__
806 
807         analyze = self.build_analyzer()
808         j_indices = []
809         indptr = []
810 
811         values = _make_int_array()
812         indptr.append(0)
813         for doc in raw_documents:
814             feature_counter = {}
815             for feature in analyze(doc):
816                 try:
817                     feature_idx = vocabulary[feature]
818                     if feature_idx not in feature_counter:
819                         feature_counter[feature_idx] = 1
820                     else:
821                         feature_counter[feature_idx] += 1
822                 except KeyError:
823                     # Ignore out-of-vocabulary items for fixed_vocab=True
824                     continue
825 
826             j_indices.extend(feature_counter.keys())
827             values.extend(feature_counter.values())
828             indptr.append(len(j_indices))
829 
830         if not fixed_vocab:
831             # disable defaultdict behaviour
832             vocabulary = dict(vocabulary)
833             if not vocabulary:
834                 raise ValueError("empty vocabulary; perhaps the documents only"
835                                  " contain stop words")
836 
837         if indptr[-1] > 2147483648:  # = 2**31 - 1
838             if sp_version >= (0, 14):
839                 indices_dtype = np.int64
840             else:
841                 raise ValueError(('sparse CSR array has {} non-zero '
842                                   'elements and requires 64 bit indexing, '
843                                   ' which is unsupported with scipy {}. '
844                                   'Please upgrade to scipy >=0.14')
845                                  .format(indptr[-1], '.'.join(sp_version)))
846 
847         else:
848             indices_dtype = np.int32
849         j_indices = np.asarray(j_indices, dtype=indices_dtype)
850         indptr = np.asarray(indptr, dtype=indices_dtype)
851         values = np.frombuffer(values, dtype=np.intc)
852 
853         X = sp.csr_matrix((values, j_indices, indptr),
854                           shape=(len(indptr) - 1, len(vocabulary)),
855                           dtype=self.dtype)
856         X.sort_indices()
857         return vocabulary, X
858 
859     def fit(self, raw_documents, y=None):
860         """Learn a vocabulary dictionary of all tokens in the raw documents.
861 
862         Parameters
863         ----------
864         raw_documents : iterable
865             An iterable which yields either str, unicode or file objects.
866 
867         Returns
868         -------
869         self
870         """
871         self.fit_transform(raw_documents)
872         return self
873 
874     def fit_transform(self, raw_documents, y=None):
875         """Learn the vocabulary dictionary and return term-document matrix.
876 
877         This is equivalent to fit followed by transform, but more efficiently
878         implemented.
879 
880         Parameters
881         ----------
882         raw_documents : iterable
883             An iterable which yields either str, unicode or file objects.
884 
885         Returns
886         -------
887         X : array, [n_samples, n_features]
888             Document-term matrix.
889         """
890         # We intentionally don't call the transform method to make
891         # fit_transform overridable without unwanted side effects in
892         # TfidfVectorizer.
893         if isinstance(raw_documents, six.string_types):
894             raise ValueError(
895                 "Iterable over raw text documents expected, "
896                 "string object received.")
897 
898         self._validate_params()
899         self._validate_vocabulary()
900         max_df = self.max_df
901         min_df = self.min_df
902         max_features = self.max_features
903 
904         vocabulary, X = self._count_vocab(raw_documents,
905                                           self.fixed_vocabulary_)
906 
907         if self.binary:
908             X.data.fill(1)
909 
910         if not self.fixed_vocabulary_:
911             X = self._sort_features(X, vocabulary)
912 
913             n_doc = X.shape[0]
914             max_doc_count = (max_df
915                              if isinstance(max_df, numbers.Integral)
916                              else max_df * n_doc)
917             min_doc_count = (min_df
918                              if isinstance(min_df, numbers.Integral)
919                              else min_df * n_doc)
920             if max_doc_count < min_doc_count:
921                 raise ValueError(
922                     "max_df corresponds to < documents than min_df")
923             X, self.stop_words_ = self._limit_features(X, vocabulary,
924                                                        max_doc_count,
925                                                        min_doc_count,
926                                                        max_features)
927 
928             self.vocabulary_ = vocabulary
929 
930         return X
931 
932     def transform(self, raw_documents):
933         """Transform documents to document-term matrix.
934 
935         Extract token counts out of raw text documents using the vocabulary
936         fitted with fit or the one provided to the constructor.
937 
938         Parameters
939         ----------
940         raw_documents : iterable
941             An iterable which yields either str, unicode or file objects.
942 
943         Returns
944         -------
945         X : sparse matrix, [n_samples, n_features]
946             Document-term matrix.
947         """
948         if isinstance(raw_documents, six.string_types):
949             raise ValueError(
950                 "Iterable over raw text documents expected, "
951                 "string object received.")
952 
953         if not hasattr(self, 'vocabulary_'):
954             self._validate_vocabulary()
955 
956         self._check_vocabulary()
957 
958         # use the same matrix-building strategy as fit_transform
959         _, X = self._count_vocab(raw_documents, fixed_vocab=True)
960         if self.binary:
961             X.data.fill(1)
962         return X
963 
964     def inverse_transform(self, X):
965         """Return terms per document with nonzero entries in X.
966 
967         Parameters
968         ----------
969         X : {array, sparse matrix}, shape = [n_samples, n_features]
970 
971         Returns
972         -------
973         X_inv : list of arrays, len = n_samples
974             List of arrays of terms.
975         """
976         self._check_vocabulary()
977 
978         if sp.issparse(X):
979             # We need CSR format for fast row manipulations.
980             X = X.tocsr()
981         else:
982             # We need to convert X to a matrix, so that the indexing
983             # returns 2D objects
984             X = np.asmatrix(X)
985         n_samples = X.shape[0]
986 
987         terms = np.array(list(self.vocabulary_.keys()))
988         indices = np.array(list(self.vocabulary_.values()))
989         inverse_vocabulary = terms[np.argsort(indices)]
990 
991         return [inverse_vocabulary[X[i, :].nonzero()[1]].ravel()
992                 for i in range(n_samples)]
993 
994     def get_feature_names(self):
995         """Array mapping from feature integer indices to feature name"""
996         self._check_vocabulary()
997 
998         return [t for t, i in sorted(six.iteritems(self.vocabulary_),
999                                      key=itemgetter(1))]
1000 
1001 
1002 def _make_int_array():
1003     """Construct an array.array of a type suitable for scipy.sparse indices."""
1004     return array.array(str("i"))
1005

1007 class TfidfTransformer(BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin):
1008     """Transform a count matrix to a normalized tf or tf-idf representation
1009 
1010     Tf means term-frequency while tf-idf means term-frequency times inverse
1011     document-frequency. This is a common term weighting scheme in information
1012     retrieval, that has also found good use in document classification.
1013 
1014     The goal of using tf-idf instead of the raw frequencies of occurrence of a
1015     token in a given document is to scale down the impact of tokens that occur
1016     very frequently in a given corpus and that are hence empirically less
1017     informative than features that occur in a small fraction of the training
1018     corpus.
1019 
1020     The formula that is used to compute the tf-idf of term t is
1021     tf-idf(d, t) = tf(t) * idf(d, t), and the idf is computed as
1022     idf(d, t) = log [ n / df(d, t) ] + 1 (if ``smooth_idf=False``),
1023     where n is the total number of documents and df(d, t) is the
1024     document frequency; the document frequency is the number of documents d
1025     that contain term t. The effect of adding "1" to the idf in the equation
1026     above is that terms with zero idf, i.e., terms  that occur in all documents
1027     in a training set, will not be entirely ignored.
1028     (Note that the idf formula above differs from the standard
1029     textbook notation that defines the idf as
1030     idf(d, t) = log [ n / (df(d, t) + 1) ]).
1031 
1032     If ``smooth_idf=True`` (the default), the constant "1" is added to the
1033     numerator and denominator of the idf as if an extra document was seen
1034     containing every term in the collection exactly once, which prevents
1035     zero divisions: idf(d, t) = log [ (1 + n) / (1 + df(d, t)) ] + 1.
1036 
1037     Furthermore, the formulas used to compute tf and idf depend
1038     on parameter settings that correspond to the SMART notation used in IR
1039     as follows:
1040 
1041     Tf is "n" (natural) by default, "l" (logarithmic) when
1042     ``sublinear_tf=True``.
1043     Idf is "t" when use_idf is given, "n" (none) otherwise.
1044     Normalization is "c" (cosine) when ``norm='l2'``, "n" (none)
1045     when ``norm=None``.
1046 
1047     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <text_feature_extraction>`.
1048 
1049     Parameters
1050     ----------
1051     norm : 'l1', 'l2' or None, optional
1052         Norm used to normalize term vectors. None for no normalization.
1053 
1054     use_idf : boolean, default=True
1055         Enable inverse-document-frequency reweighting.
1056 
1057     smooth_idf : boolean, default=True
1058         Smooth idf weights by adding one to document frequencies, as if an
1059         extra document was seen containing every term in the collection
1060         exactly once. Prevents zero divisions.
1061 
1062     sublinear_tf : boolean, default=False
1063         Apply sublinear tf scaling, i.e. replace tf with 1 + log(tf).
1064 
1065     References
1066     ----------
1067 
1068     .. [Yates2011] `R. Baeza-Yates and B. Ribeiro-Neto (2011). Modern
1069                    Information Retrieval. Addison Wesley, pp. 68-74.`
1070 
1071     .. [MRS2008] `C.D. Manning, P. Raghavan and H. Schütze  (2008).
1072                    Introduction to Information Retrieval. Cambridge University
1073                    Press, pp. 118-120.`
1074     """
1075 
1076     def __init__(self, norm='l2', use_idf=True, smooth_idf=True,
1077                  sublinear_tf=False):
1078         self.norm = norm
1079         self.use_idf = use_idf
1080         self.smooth_idf = smooth_idf
1081         self.sublinear_tf = sublinear_tf
1082 
1083     def fit(self, X, y=None):
1084         """Learn the idf vector (global term weights)
1085 
1086         Parameters
1087         ----------
1088         X : sparse matrix, [n_samples, n_features]
1089             a matrix of term/token counts
1090         """
1091         if not sp.issparse(X):
1092             X = sp.csc_matrix(X)
1093         if self.use_idf:
1094             n_samples, n_features = X.shape
1095             df = _document_frequency(X)
1096 
1097             # perform idf smoothing if required
1098             df += int(self.smooth_idf)
1099             n_samples += int(self.smooth_idf)
1100 
1101             # log+1 instead of log makes sure terms with zero idf don't get
1102             # suppressed entirely.
1103             idf = np.log(float(n_samples) / df) + 1.0
1104             self._idf_diag = sp.spdiags(idf, diags=0, m=n_features,
1105                                         n=n_features, format='csr')
1106 
1107         return self
1108 
1109     def transform(self, X, copy=True):
1110         """Transform a count matrix to a tf or tf-idf representation
1111 
1112         Parameters
1113         ----------
1114         X : sparse matrix, [n_samples, n_features]
1115             a matrix of term/token counts
1116 
1117         copy : boolean, default True
1118             Whether to copy X and operate on the copy or perform in-place
1119             operations.
1120 
1121         Returns
1122         -------
1123         vectors : sparse matrix, [n_samples, n_features]
1124         """
1125         if hasattr(X, 'dtype') and np.issubdtype(X.dtype, np.floating):
1126             # preserve float family dtype
1127             X = sp.csr_matrix(X, copy=copy)
1128         else:
1129             # convert counts or binary occurrences to floats
1130             X = sp.csr_matrix(X, dtype=np.float64, copy=copy)
1131 
1132         n_samples, n_features = X.shape
1133 
1134         if self.sublinear_tf:
1135             np.log(X.data, X.data)
1136             X.data += 1
1137 
1138         if self.use_idf:
1139             check_is_fitted(self, '_idf_diag', 'idf vector is not fitted')
1140 
1141             expected_n_features = self._idf_diag.shape[0]
1142             if n_features != expected_n_features:
1143                 raise ValueError("Input has n_features=%d while the model"
1144                                  " has been trained with n_features=%d" % (
1145                                      n_features, expected_n_features))
1146             # *= doesn't work
1147             X = X * self._idf_diag
1148 
1149         if self.norm:
1150             X = normalize(X, norm=self.norm, copy=False)
1151 
1152         return X
1153 
1154     @property
1155     def idf_(self):
1156         # if _idf_diag is not set, this will raise an attribute error,
1157         # which means hasattr(self, "idf_") is False
1158         return np.ravel(self._idf_diag.sum(axis=0))
1159

202     def __getitem__(self, ind):
203         """Returns a sub-pipeline or a single esimtator in the pipeline
204 
205         Indexing with an integer will return an estimator; using a slice
206         returns another Pipeline instance which copies a slice of this
207         Pipeline. This copy is shallow: modifying (or fitting) estimators in
208         the sub-pipeline will affect the larger pipeline and vice-versa.
209         However, replacing a value in `step` will not affect a copy.
210         """
211         if isinstance(ind, slice):
212             if ind.step not in (1, None):
213                 raise ValueError('Pipeline slicing only supports a step of 1')
214             return self.__class__(self.steps[ind])
215         try:
216             name, est = self.steps[ind]
217         except TypeError:
218             # Not an int, try get step by name
219             return self.named_steps[ind]
220         return est
221

223     def _estimator_type(self):
224         return self.steps[-1][1]._estimator_type

227     def named_steps(self):
228         # Use Bunch object to improve autocomplete
229         return Bunch(**dict(self.steps))
230

232     def _final_estimator(self):
233         estimator = self.steps[-1][1]
234         return 'passthrough' if estimator is None else estimator

238     def _fit(self, X, y=None, **fit_params):
239         # shallow copy of steps - this should really be steps_
240         self.steps = list(self.steps)
241         self._validate_steps()
242         # Setup the memory
243         memory = check_memory(self.memory)
244 
245         fit_transform_one_cached = memory.cache(_fit_transform_one)
246 
247         fit_params_steps = {name: {} for name, step in self.steps
248                             if step is not None}
249         for pname, pval in fit_params.items():
250             step, param = pname.split('__', 1)
251             fit_params_steps[step][param] = pval
252         Xt = X
253         for step_idx, name, transformer in self._iter(with_final=False):
254             if hasattr(memory, 'location'):
255                 # joblib >= 0.12
256                 if memory.location is None:
257                     # we do not clone when caching is disabled to
258                     # preserve backward compatibility
259                     cloned_transformer = transformer
260                 else:
261                     cloned_transformer = clone(transformer)
262             elif hasattr(memory, 'cachedir'):
263                 # joblib < 0.11
264                 if memory.cachedir is None:
265                     # we do not clone when caching is disabled to
266                     # preserve backward compatibility
267                     cloned_transformer = transformer
268                 else:
269                     cloned_transformer = clone(transformer)
270             else:
271                 cloned_transformer = clone(transformer)
272             # Fit or load from cache the current transfomer
273             Xt, fitted_transformer = fit_transform_one_cached(
274                 cloned_transformer, Xt, y, None,
275                 **fit_params_steps[name])
276             # Replace the transformer of the step with the fitted
277             # transformer. This is necessary when loading the transformer
278             # from the cache.
279             self.steps[step_idx] = (name, fitted_transformer)
280         if self._final_estimator == 'passthrough':
281             return Xt, {}
282         return Xt, fit_params_steps[self.steps[-1][0]]
283 
284     def fit(self, X, y=None, **fit_params):
285         """Fit the model
286 
287         Fit all the transforms one after the other and transform the
288         data, then fit the transformed data using the final estimator.
289 
290         Parameters
291         ----------
292         X : iterable
293             Training data. Must fulfill input requirements of first step of the
294             pipeline.
295 
296         y : iterable, default=None
297             Training targets. Must fulfill label requirements for all steps of
298             the pipeline.
299 
300         **fit_params : dict of string -> object
301             Parameters passed to the ``fit`` method of each step, where
302             each parameter name is prefixed such that parameter ``p`` for step
303             ``s`` has key ``s__p``.
304 
305         Returns
306         -------
307         self : Pipeline
308             This estimator
309         """
310         Xt, fit_params = self._fit(X, y, **fit_params)
311         if self._final_estimator != 'passthrough':
312             self._final_estimator.fit(Xt, y, **fit_params)
313         return self
314 
315     def fit_transform(self, X, y=None, **fit_params):
316         """Fit the model and transform with the final estimator
317 
318         Fits all the transforms one after the other and transforms the
319         data, then uses fit_transform on transformed data with the final
320         estimator.
321 
322         Parameters
323         ----------
324         X : iterable
325             Training data. Must fulfill input requirements of first step of the
326             pipeline.
327 
328         y : iterable, default=None
329             Training targets. Must fulfill label requirements for all steps of
330             the pipeline.
331 
332         **fit_params : dict of string -> object
333             Parameters passed to the ``fit`` method of each step, where
334             each parameter name is prefixed such that parameter ``p`` for step
335             ``s`` has key ``s__p``.
336 
337         Returns
338         -------
339         Xt : array-like, shape = [n_samples, n_transformed_features]
340             Transformed samples
341         """
342         last_step = self._final_estimator
343         Xt, fit_params = self._fit(X, y, **fit_params)
344         if hasattr(last_step, 'fit_transform'):
345             return last_step.fit_transform(Xt, y, **fit_params)
346         elif last_step == 'passthrough':
347             return Xt
348         else:
349             return last_step.fit(Xt, y, **fit_params).transform(Xt)

565 def _name_estimators(estimators):
566     """Generate names for estimators."""
567 
568     names = [
569         estimator
570         if isinstance(estimator, str) else type(estimator).__name__.lower()
571         for estimator in estimators
572     ]
573     namecount = defaultdict(int)
574     for est, name in zip(estimators, names):
575         namecount[name] += 1
576 
577     for k, v in list(namecount.items()):
578         if v == 1:
579             del namecount[k]
580 
581     for i in reversed(range(len(estimators))):
582         name = names[i]
583         if name in namecount:
584             names[i] += "-%d" % namecount[name]
585             namecount[name] -= 1
586 
587     return list(zip(names, estimators))
588

590 def make_pipeline(*steps, **kwargs):
591     """Construct a Pipeline from the given estimators.
592 
593     This is a shorthand for the Pipeline constructor; it does not require, and
594     does not permit, naming the estimators. Instead, their names will be set
595     to the lowercase of their types automatically.
596 
597     Parameters
598     ----------
599     *steps : list of estimators.
600 
601     memory : None, str or object with the joblib.Memory interface, optional
602         Used to cache the fitted transformers of the pipeline. By default,
603         no caching is performed. If a string is given, it is the path to
604         the caching directory. Enabling caching triggers a clone of
605         the transformers before fitting. Therefore, the transformer
606         instance given to the pipeline cannot be inspected
607         directly. Use the attribute ``named_steps`` or ``steps`` to
608         inspect estimators within the pipeline. Caching the
609         transformers is advantageous when fitting is time consuming.
610 
611     See also
612     --------
613     sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline : Class for creating a pipeline of
614         transforms with a final estimator.
615 
616     Examples
617     --------
618     >>> from sklearn.naive_bayes import GaussianNB
619     >>> from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
620     >>> make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), GaussianNB(priors=None))
621     ...     # doctest: +NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE
622     Pipeline(memory=None,
623              steps=[('standardscaler',
624                      StandardScaler(copy=True, with_mean=True, with_std=True)),
625                     ('gaussiannb',
626                      GaussianNB(priors=None, var_smoothing=1e-09))])
627 
628     Returns
629     -------
630     p : Pipeline
631     """
632     memory = kwargs.pop('memory', None)
633     if kwargs:
634         raise TypeError('Unknown keyword arguments: "{}"'
635                         .format(list(kwargs.keys())[0]))
636     return Pipeline(_name_estimators(steps), memory=memory)
637

639 # weight and fit_params are not used but it allows _fit_one_transformer,
640 # _transform_one and _fit_transform_one to have the same signature to
641 #  factorize the code in ColumnTransformer
642 def _fit_one_transformer(transformer, X, y, weight=None, **fit_params):
643     return transformer.fit(X, y)
644 
645 
646 def _transform_one(transformer, X, y, weight, **fit_params):
647     res = transformer.transform(X)
648     # if we have a weight for this transformer, multiply output
649     if weight is None:
650         return res
651     return res * weight
652 
653 
654 def _fit_transform_one(transformer, X, y, weight, **fit_params):
655     if hasattr(transformer, 'fit_transform'):
656         res = transformer.fit_transform(X, y, **fit_params)
657     else:
658         res = transformer.fit(X, y, **fit_params).transform(X)
659     # if we have a weight for this transformer, multiply output
660     if weight is None:
661         return res, transformer
662     return res * weight, transformer

665 class FeatureUnion(_BaseComposition, TransformerMixin):
666     """Concatenates results of multiple transformer objects.
667 
668     This estimator applies a list of transformer objects in parallel to the
669     input data, then concatenates the results. This is useful to combine
670     several feature extraction mechanisms into a single transformer.
671 
672     Parameters of the transformers may be set using its name and the parameter
673     name separated by a '__'. A transformer may be replaced entirely by
674     setting the parameter with its name to another transformer,
675     or removed by setting to 'drop' or ``None``.
676 
677     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <feature_union>`.
678 
679     Parameters
680     ----------
681     transformer_list : list of (string, transformer) tuples
682         List of transformer objects to be applied to the data. The first
683         half of each tuple is the name of the transformer.
684 
685     n_jobs : int or None, optional (default=None)
686         Number of jobs to run in parallel.
687         ``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
688         ``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
689         for more details.
690 
691     transformer_weights : dict, optional
692         Multiplicative weights for features per transformer.
693         Keys are transformer names, values the weights.
694 
695     See also
696     --------
697     sklearn.pipeline.make_union : convenience function for simplified
698         feature union construction.
699 
700     Examples
701     --------
702     >>> from sklearn.pipeline import FeatureUnion
703     >>> from sklearn.decomposition import PCA, TruncatedSVD
704     >>> union = FeatureUnion([("pca", PCA(n_components=1)),
705     ...                       ("svd", TruncatedSVD(n_components=2))])
706     >>> X = [[0., 1., 3], [2., 2., 5]]
707     >>> union.fit_transform(X)    # doctest: +NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE +ELLIPSIS
708     array([[ 1.5       ,  3.0...,  0.8...],
709            [-1.5       ,  5.7..., -0.4...]])
710     """
711     _required_parameters = ["transformer_list"]
712 
713     def __init__(self, transformer_list, n_jobs=None,
714                  transformer_weights=None):
715         self.transformer_list = transformer_list
716         self.n_jobs = n_jobs
717         self.transformer_weights = transformer_weights
718         self._validate_transformers()
719 
720     def get_params(self, deep=True):
721         """Get parameters for this estimator.
722 
723         Parameters
724         ----------
725         deep : boolean, optional
726             If True, will return the parameters for this estimator and
727             contained subobjects that are estimators.
728 
729         Returns
730         -------
731         params : mapping of string to any
732             Parameter names mapped to their values.
733         """
734         return self._get_params('transformer_list', deep=deep)
735 
736     def set_params(self, **kwargs):
737         """Set the parameters of this estimator.
738 
739         Valid parameter keys can be listed with ``get_params()``.
740 
741         Returns
742         -------
743         self
744         """
745         self._set_params('transformer_list', **kwargs)
746         return self
747 
748     def _validate_transformers(self):
749         names, transformers = zip(*self.transformer_list)
750 
751         # validate names
752         self._validate_names(names)
753 
754         # validate estimators
755         for t in transformers:
756             if t is None or t == 'drop':
757                 continue
758             if (not (hasattr(t, "fit") or hasattr(t, "fit_transform")) or not
759                     hasattr(t, "transform")):
760                 raise TypeError("All estimators should implement fit and "
761                                 "transform. '%s' (type %s) doesn't" %
762                                 (t, type(t)))
763 
764     def _iter(self):
765         """
766         Generate (name, trans, weight) tuples excluding None and
767         'drop' transformers.
768         """
769         get_weight = (self.transformer_weights or {}).get
770         return ((name, trans, get_weight(name))
771                 for name, trans in self.transformer_list
772                 if trans is not None and trans != 'drop')
773 
774     def get_feature_names(self):
775         """Get feature names from all transformers.
776 
777         Returns
778         -------
779         feature_names : list of strings
780             Names of the features produced by transform.
781         """
782         feature_names = []
783         for name, trans, weight in self._iter():
784             if not hasattr(trans, 'get_feature_names'):
785                 raise AttributeError("Transformer %s (type %s) does not "
786                                      "provide get_feature_names."
787                                      % (str(name), type(trans).__name__))
788             feature_names.extend([name + "__" + f for f in
789                                   trans.get_feature_names()])
790         return feature_names
791 
792     def fit(self, X, y=None):
793         """Fit all transformers using X.
794 
795         Parameters
796         ----------
797         X : iterable or array-like, depending on transformers
798             Input data, used to fit transformers.
799 
800         y : array-like, shape (n_samples, ...), optional
801             Targets for supervised learning.
802 
803         Returns
804         -------
805         self : FeatureUnion
806             This estimator
807         """
808         self.transformer_list = list(self.transformer_list)
809         self._validate_transformers()
810         transformers = Parallel(n_jobs=self.n_jobs)(
811             delayed(_fit_one_transformer)(trans, X, y)
812             for _, trans, _ in self._iter())
813         self._update_transformer_list(transformers)
814         return self
815 
816     def fit_transform(self, X, y=None, **fit_params):
817         """Fit all transformers, transform the data and concatenate results.
818 
819         Parameters
820         ----------
821         X : iterable or array-like, depending on transformers
822             Input data to be transformed.
823 
824         y : array-like, shape (n_samples, ...), optional
825             Targets for supervised learning.
826 
827         Returns
828         -------
829         X_t : array-like or sparse matrix, shape (n_samples, sum_n_components)
830             hstack of results of transformers. sum_n_components is the
831             sum of n_components (output dimension) over transformers.
832         """
833         self._validate_transformers()
834         result = Parallel(n_jobs=self.n_jobs)(
835             delayed(_fit_transform_one)(trans, X, y, weight,
836                                         **fit_params)
837             for name, trans, weight in self._iter())
838 
839         if not result:
840             # All transformers are None
841             return np.zeros((X.shape[0], 0))
842         Xs, transformers = zip(*result)
843         self._update_transformer_list(transformers)
844         if any(sparse.issparse(f) for f in Xs):
845             Xs = sparse.hstack(Xs).tocsr()
846         else:
847             Xs = np.hstack(Xs)
848         return Xs
849 
850     def transform(self, X):
851         """Transform X separately by each transformer, concatenate results.
852 
853         Parameters
854         ----------
855         X : iterable or array-like, depending on transformers
856             Input data to be transformed.
857 
858         Returns
859         -------
860         X_t : array-like or sparse matrix, shape (n_samples, sum_n_components)
861             hstack of results of transformers. sum_n_components is the
862             sum of n_components (output dimension) over transformers.
863         """
864         Xs = Parallel(n_jobs=self.n_jobs)(
865             delayed(_transform_one)(trans, X, None, weight)
866             for name, trans, weight in self._iter())
867         if not Xs:
868             # All transformers are None
869             return np.zeros((X.shape[0], 0))
870         if any(sparse.issparse(f) for f in Xs):
871             Xs = sparse.hstack(Xs).tocsr()
872         else:
873             Xs = np.hstack(Xs)
874         return Xs
875 
876     def _update_transformer_list(self, transformers):
877         transformers = iter(transformers)
878         self.transformer_list[:] = [(name, old if old is None or old == 'drop'
879                                      else next(transformers))
880                                     for name, old in self.transformer_list]
881

Expose warm_start in Isolation forest
It seems to me that `sklearn.ensemble.IsolationForest` supports incremental addition of new trees with the `warm_start` parameter of its parent class, `sklearn.ensemble.BaseBagging`.

Even though this parameter is not exposed in `__init__()` , it gets inherited from `BaseBagging` and one can use it by changing it to `True` after initialization. To make it work, you have to also increment `n_estimators` on every iteration. 

It took me a while to notice that it actually works, and I had to inspect the source code of both `IsolationForest` and `BaseBagging`. Also, it looks to me that the behavior is in-line with `sklearn.ensemble.BaseForest` that is behind e.g. `sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier`.

To make it more easier to use, I'd suggest to:
* expose `warm_start` in `IsolationForest.__init__()`, default `False`;
* document it in the same way as it is documented for `RandomForestClassifier`, i.e. say:
```py
    warm_start : bool, optional (default=False)
        When set to ``True``, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit
        and add more estimators to the ensemble, otherwise, just fit a whole
        new forest. See :term:`the Glossary <warm_start>`.
```
* add a test to make sure it works properly;
* possibly also mention in the "IsolationForest example" documentation entry;

31 
32     Return the anomaly score of each sample using the IsolationForest algorithm
33 
34     The IsolationForest 'isolates' observations by randomly selecting a feature
35     and then randomly selecting a split value between the maximum and minimum
36     values of the selected feature.
37 
38     Since recursive partitioning can be represented by a tree structure, the
39     number of splittings required to isolate a sample is equivalent to the path
40     length from the root node to the terminating node.
41 
42     This path length, averaged over a forest of such random trees, is a
43     measure of normality and our decision function.
44 
45     Random partitioning produces noticeably shorter paths for anomalies.
46     Hence, when a forest of random trees collectively produce shorter path
47     lengths for particular samples, they are highly likely to be anomalies.
48 
49     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <isolation_forest>`.
50

52

60             - If int, then draw `max_samples` samples.
61             - If float, then draw `max_samples * X.shape[0]` samples.
62             - If "auto", then `max_samples=min(256, n_samples)`.
63

65         all samples will be used for all trees (no sampling).
66

69         of outliers in the data set. Used when fitting to define the threshold
70         on the decision function. If 'auto', the decision function threshold is
71         determined as in the original paper.

101         its natural threshold to detect outliers.

457             X_subset = X[:, features] if subsample_features else X

478     """The average path length in a n_samples iTree, which is equal to
479     the average path length of an unsuccessful BST search since the
480     latter has the same structure as an isolation tree.
481     Parameters

494

496     n_samples_leaf = n_samples_leaf.reshape((1, -1))
497     average_path_length = np.zeros(n_samples_leaf.shape)
498 
499     mask_1 = n_samples_leaf <= 1
500     mask_2 = n_samples_leaf == 2
501     not_mask = ~np.logical_or(mask_1, mask_2)
502 
503     average_path_length[mask_1] = 0.
504     average_path_length[mask_2] = 1.
505     average_path_length[not_mask] = (
506         2.0 * (np.log(n_samples_leaf[not_mask] - 1.0) + np.euler_gamma)
507         - 2.0 * (n_samples_leaf[not_mask] - 1.0) / n_samples_leaf[not_mask]
508     )
509 
510     return average_path_length.reshape(n_samples_leaf_shape)

256 
257     Y : ndarray, shape (n_samples, n_classes)
258         Transformed labels according to the output of LabelBinarizer.
259 
260     alpha : float
261         Regularization parameter. alpha is equal to 1 / C.
262 
263     sample_weight : array-like, shape (n_samples,)
264         Array of weights that are assigned to individual samples.
265 
266     Returns
267     -------
268     loss : float
269         Multinomial loss.
270 
271     p : ndarray, shape (n_samples, n_classes)
272         Estimated class probabilities.
273 
274     w : ndarray, shape (n_classes, n_features)
275         Reshaped param vector excluding intercept terms.
276 
277     Reference
278     ---------
279     Bishop, C. M. (2006). Pattern recognition and machine learning.
280     Springer. (Chapter 4.3.4)
281     """
282     n_classes = Y.shape[1]
283     n_features = X.shape[1]
284     fit_intercept = w.size == (n_classes * (n_features + 1))
285     w = w.reshape(n_classes, -1)
286     sample_weight = sample_weight[:, np.newaxis]
287     if fit_intercept:
288         intercept = w[:, -1]
289         w = w[:, :-1]
290     else:
291         intercept = 0
292     p = safe_sparse_dot(X, w.T)
293     p += intercept
294     p -= logsumexp(p, axis=1)[:, np.newaxis]
295     loss = -(sample_weight * Y * p).sum()
296     loss += 0.5 * alpha * squared_norm(w)
297     p = np.exp(p, p)
298     return loss, p, w
299 
300 
301 def _multinomial_loss_grad(w, X, Y, alpha, sample_weight):
302     """Computes the multinomial loss, gradient and class probabilities.
303 
304     Parameters
305     ----------
306     w : ndarray, shape (n_classes * n_features,) or
307         (n_classes * (n_features + 1),)
308         Coefficient vector.
309 
310     X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_samples, n_features)
311         Training data.
312 
313     Y : ndarray, shape (n_samples, n_classes)
314         Transformed labels according to the output of LabelBinarizer.
315 
316     alpha : float
317         Regularization parameter. alpha is equal to 1 / C.
318 
319     sample_weight : array-like, shape (n_samples,)
320         Array of weights that are assigned to individual samples.
321 
322     Returns
323     -------
324     loss : float
325         Multinomial loss.
326 
327     grad : ndarray, shape (n_classes * n_features,) or
328         (n_classes * (n_features + 1),)
329         Ravelled gradient of the multinomial loss.
330 
331     p : ndarray, shape (n_samples, n_classes)
332         Estimated class probabilities
333 
334     Reference
335     ---------
336     Bishop, C. M. (2006). Pattern recognition and machine learning.
337     Springer. (Chapter 4.3.4)
338     """
339     n_classes = Y.shape[1]
340     n_features = X.shape[1]
341     fit_intercept = (w.size == n_classes * (n_features + 1))
342     grad = np.zeros((n_classes, n_features + bool(fit_intercept)),
343                     dtype=X.dtype)
344     loss, p, w = _multinomial_loss(w, X, Y, alpha, sample_weight)
345     sample_weight = sample_weight[:, np.newaxis]
346     diff = sample_weight * (p - Y)
347     grad[:, :n_features] = safe_sparse_dot(diff.T, X)
348     grad[:, :n_features] += alpha * w
349     if fit_intercept:
350         grad[:, -1] = diff.sum(axis=0)
351     return loss, grad.ravel(), p
352

354 def _multinomial_grad_hess(w, X, Y, alpha, sample_weight):
355     """
356     Computes the gradient and the Hessian, in the case of a multinomial loss.
357 
358     Parameters
359     ----------
360     w : ndarray, shape (n_classes * n_features,) or
361         (n_classes * (n_features + 1),)
362         Coefficient vector.
363 
364     X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_samples, n_features)
365         Training data.
366 
367     Y : ndarray, shape (n_samples, n_classes)
368         Transformed labels according to the output of LabelBinarizer.
369 
370     alpha : float
371         Regularization parameter. alpha is equal to 1 / C.
372 
373     sample_weight : array-like, shape (n_samples,)
374         Array of weights that are assigned to individual samples.
375 
376     Returns
377     -------
378     grad : array, shape (n_classes * n_features,) or
379         (n_classes * (n_features + 1),)
380         Ravelled gradient of the multinomial loss.
381 
382     hessp : callable
383         Function that takes in a vector input of shape (n_classes * n_features)
384         or (n_classes * (n_features + 1)) and returns matrix-vector product
385         with hessian.
386 
387     References
388     ----------
389     Barak A. Pearlmutter (1993). Fast Exact Multiplication by the Hessian.
390         http://www.bcl.hamilton.ie/~barak/papers/nc-hessian.pdf
391     """
392     n_features = X.shape[1]
393     n_classes = Y.shape[1]
394     fit_intercept = w.size == (n_classes * (n_features + 1))
395 
396     # `loss` is unused. Refactoring to avoid computing it does not
397     # significantly speed up the computation and decreases readability
398     loss, grad, p = _multinomial_loss_grad(w, X, Y, alpha, sample_weight)
399     sample_weight = sample_weight[:, np.newaxis]
400 
401     # Hessian-vector product derived by applying the R-operator on the gradient
402     # of the multinomial loss function.
403     def hessp(v):
404         v = v.reshape(n_classes, -1)
405         if fit_intercept:
406             inter_terms = v[:, -1]
407             v = v[:, :-1]
408         else:
409             inter_terms = 0
410         # r_yhat holds the result of applying the R-operator on the multinomial
411         # estimator.
412         r_yhat = safe_sparse_dot(X, v.T)
413         r_yhat += inter_terms
414         r_yhat += (-p * r_yhat).sum(axis=1)[:, np.newaxis]
415         r_yhat *= p
416         r_yhat *= sample_weight
417         hessProd = np.zeros((n_classes, n_features + bool(fit_intercept)))
418         hessProd[:, :n_features] = safe_sparse_dot(r_yhat.T, X)
419         hessProd[:, :n_features] += v * alpha
420         if fit_intercept:
421             hessProd[:, -1] = r_yhat.sum(axis=0)
422         return hessProd.ravel()
423 
424     return grad, hessp
425

427 def _check_solver(solver, penalty, dual):
428     all_solvers = ['liblinear', 'newton-cg', 'lbfgs', 'sag', 'saga']
429     if solver not in all_solvers:
430         raise ValueError("Logistic Regression supports only solvers in %s, got"
431                          " %s." % (all_solvers, solver))
432 
433     all_penalties = ['l1', 'l2', 'elasticnet', 'none']
434     if penalty not in all_penalties:
435         raise ValueError("Logistic Regression supports only penalties in %s,"
436                          " got %s." % (all_penalties, penalty))
437 
438     if solver not in ['liblinear', 'saga'] and penalty not in ('l2', 'none'):
439         raise ValueError("Solver %s supports only 'l2' or 'none' penalties, "
440                          "got %s penalty." % (solver, penalty))
441     if solver != 'liblinear' and dual:
442         raise ValueError("Solver %s supports only "
443                          "dual=False, got dual=%s" % (solver, dual))
444 
445     if penalty == 'elasticnet' and solver != 'saga':
446         raise ValueError("Only 'saga' solver supports elasticnet penalty,"
447                          " got solver={}.".format(solver))
448 
449     if solver == 'liblinear' and penalty == 'none':
450         raise ValueError(
451             "penalty='none' is not supported for the liblinear solver"
452         )
453 
454     return solver
455 
456 
457 def _check_multi_class(multi_class, solver, n_classes):
458     if multi_class == 'auto':
459         if solver == 'liblinear':
460             multi_class = 'ovr'
461         elif n_classes > 2:
462             multi_class = 'multinomial'
463         else:
464             multi_class = 'ovr'
465     if multi_class not in ('multinomial', 'ovr'):
466         raise ValueError("multi_class should be 'multinomial', 'ovr' or "
467                          "'auto'. Got %s." % multi_class)
468     if multi_class == 'multinomial' and solver == 'liblinear':
469         raise ValueError("Solver %s does not support "
470                          "a multinomial backend." % solver)
471     return multi_class
472

849         y_bin = np.ones(y.shape, dtype=X.dtype)
850         y_bin[~mask] = -1.
851         # for compute_class_weight
852 
853         if class_weight == "balanced":
854             class_weight_ = compute_class_weight(class_weight, mask_classes,
855                                                  y_bin)
856             sample_weight *= class_weight_[le.fit_transform(y_bin)]
857 
858     else:
859         if solver not in ['sag', 'saga']:
860             lbin = LabelBinarizer()
861             Y_multi = lbin.fit_transform(y)
862             if Y_multi.shape[1] == 1:
863                 Y_multi = np.hstack([1 - Y_multi, Y_multi])
864         else:
865             # SAG multinomial solver needs LabelEncoder, not LabelBinarizer
866             le = LabelEncoder()
867             Y_multi = le.fit_transform(y).astype(X.dtype, copy=False)
868 
869         w0 = np.zeros((classes.size, n_features + int(fit_intercept)),
870                       order='F', dtype=X.dtype)
871 
872     if coef is not None:
873         # it must work both giving the bias term and not
874         if multi_class == 'ovr':
875             if coef.size not in (n_features, w0.size):
876                 raise ValueError(
877                     'Initialization coef is of shape %d, expected shape '
878                     '%d or %d' % (coef.size, n_features, w0.size))
879             w0[:coef.size] = coef
880         else:
881             # For binary problems coef.shape[0] should be 1, otherwise it
882             # should be classes.size.
883             n_classes = classes.size
884             if n_classes == 2:
885                 n_classes = 1
886 
887             if (coef.shape[0] != n_classes or
888                     coef.shape[1] not in (n_features, n_features + 1)):
889                 raise ValueError(
890                     'Initialization coef is of shape (%d, %d), expected '
891                     'shape (%d, %d) or (%d, %d)' % (
892                         coef.shape[0], coef.shape[1], classes.size,
893                         n_features, classes.size, n_features + 1))
894 
895             if n_classes == 1:
896                 w0[0, :coef.shape[1]] = -coef
897                 w0[1, :coef.shape[1]] = coef
898             else:
899                 w0[:, :coef.shape[1]] = coef
900 
901     if multi_class == 'multinomial':
902         # fmin_l_bfgs_b and newton-cg accepts only ravelled parameters.
903         if solver in ['lbfgs', 'newton-cg']:
904             w0 = w0.ravel()
905         target = Y_multi
906         if solver == 'lbfgs':
907             func = lambda x, *args: _multinomial_loss_grad(x, *args)[0:2]
908         elif solver == 'newton-cg':
909             func = lambda x, *args: _multinomial_loss(x, *args)[0]
910             grad = lambda x, *args: _multinomial_loss_grad(x, *args)[1]
911             hess = _multinomial_grad_hess
912         warm_start_sag = {'coef': w0.T}
913     else:
914         target = y_bin
915         if solver == 'lbfgs':
916             func = _logistic_loss_and_grad
917         elif solver == 'newton-cg':
918             func = _logistic_loss
919             grad = lambda x, *args: _logistic_loss_and_grad(x, *args)[1]
920             hess = _logistic_grad_hess
921         warm_start_sag = {'coef': np.expand_dims(w0, axis=1)}
922 
923     coefs = list()
924     n_iter = np.zeros(len(Cs), dtype=np.int32)
925     for i, C in enumerate(Cs):
926         if solver == 'lbfgs':
927             iprint = [-1, 50, 1, 100, 101][
928                 np.searchsorted(np.array([0, 1, 2, 3]), verbose)]
929             w0, loss, info = optimize.fmin_l_bfgs_b(
930                 func, w0, fprime=None,
931                 args=(X, target, 1. / C, sample_weight),
932                 iprint=iprint, pgtol=tol, maxiter=max_iter)
933             if info["warnflag"] == 1:
934                 warnings.warn("lbfgs failed to converge. Increase the number "
935                               "of iterations.", ConvergenceWarning)
936             # In scipy <= 1.0.0, nit may exceed maxiter.
937             # See https://github.com/scipy/scipy/issues/7854.
938             n_iter_i = min(info['nit'], max_iter)
939         elif solver == 'newton-cg':
940             args = (X, target, 1. / C, sample_weight)
941             w0, n_iter_i = newton_cg(hess, func, grad, w0, args=args,
942                                      maxiter=max_iter, tol=tol)
943         elif solver == 'liblinear':
944             coef_, intercept_, n_iter_i, = _fit_liblinear(
945                 X, target, C, fit_intercept, intercept_scaling, None,
946                 penalty, dual, verbose, max_iter, tol, random_state,
947                 sample_weight=sample_weight)
948             if fit_intercept:
949                 w0 = np.concatenate([coef_.ravel(), intercept_])
950             else:
951                 w0 = coef_.ravel()
952 
953         elif solver in ['sag', 'saga']:
954             if multi_class == 'multinomial':
955                 target = target.astype(X.dtype, copy=False)
956                 loss = 'multinomial'
957             else:
958                 loss = 'log'
959             # alpha is for L2-norm, beta is for L1-norm
960             if penalty == 'l1':
961                 alpha = 0.
962                 beta = 1. / C
963             elif penalty == 'l2':
964                 alpha = 1. / C
965                 beta = 0.
966             else:  # Elastic-Net penalty
967                 alpha = (1. / C) * (1 - l1_ratio)
968                 beta = (1. / C) * l1_ratio
969 
970             w0, n_iter_i, warm_start_sag = sag_solver(
971                 X, target, sample_weight, loss, alpha,
972                 beta, max_iter, tol,
973                 verbose, random_state, False, max_squared_sum, warm_start_sag,
974                 is_saga=(solver == 'saga'))
975 
976         else:
977             raise ValueError("solver must be one of {'liblinear', 'lbfgs', "
978                              "'newton-cg', 'sag'}, got '%s' instead" % solver)
979 
980         if multi_class == 'multinomial':
981             n_classes = max(2, classes.size)
982             multi_w0 = np.reshape(w0, (n_classes, -1))
983             if n_classes == 2:
984                 multi_w0 = multi_w0[1][np.newaxis, :]
985             coefs.append(multi_w0.copy())
986         else:
987             coefs.append(w0.copy())
988 
989         n_iter[i] = n_iter_i
990 
991     return np.array(coefs), np.array(Cs), n_iter
992
