168 def between(marker: str, what: Sequence[str] = None, keepempty: bool = False,
169             exclude: bool = False) -> Callable:
170     """Return a listener that either keeps, or if *exclude* is True excludes,
171     lines between lines that match the *marker* regular expression.  If no line
172     matches, the resulting docstring would be empty, so no change will be made
173     unless *keepempty* is true.
174 
175     If *what* is a sequence of strings, only docstrings of a type in *what* will
176     be processed.
177     """
178     marker_re = re.compile(marker)
179 
180     def process(app: Sphinx, what_: str, name: str, obj: Any, options: Any, lines: List[str]
181                 ) -> None:
182         if what and what_ not in what:
183             return
184         deleted = 0
185         delete = not exclude
186         orig_lines = lines[:]
187         for i, line in enumerate(orig_lines):
188             if delete:
189                 lines.pop(i - deleted)
190                 deleted += 1
191             if marker_re.match(line):
192                 delete = not delete
193                 if delete:
194                     lines.pop(i - deleted)
195                     deleted += 1
196         if not lines and not keepempty:
197             lines[:] = orig_lines
198         # make sure there is a blank line at the end
199         if lines and lines[-1]:
200             lines.append('')
201     return process

356     def get_real_modname(self) -> str:
357         """Get the real module name of an object to document.
358 
359         It can differ from the name of the module through which the object was
360         imported.
361         """
362         return self.get_attr(self.object, '__module__', None) or self.modname
363 
364     def check_module(self) -> bool:
365         """Check if *self.object* is really defined in the module given by
366         *self.modname*.
367         """
368         if self.options.imported_members:
369             return True
370 
371         subject = inspect.unpartial(self.object)
372         modname = self.get_attr(subject, '__module__', None)
373         if modname and modname != self.modname:
374             return False
375         return True
376 
377     def format_args(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
378         """Format the argument signature of *self.object*.
379 
380         Should return None if the object does not have a signature.
381         """
382         return None
383 
384     def format_name(self) -> str:
385         """Format the name of *self.object*.
386 
387         This normally should be something that can be parsed by the generated
388         directive, but doesn't need to be (Sphinx will display it unparsed
389         then).
390         """
391         # normally the name doesn't contain the module (except for module
392         # directives of course)
393         return '.'.join(self.objpath) or self.modname
394 
395     def _call_format_args(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
396         if kwargs:
397             try:
398                 return self.format_args(**kwargs)
399             except TypeError:
400                 # avoid chaining exceptions, by putting nothing here
401                 pass
402 
403         # retry without arguments for old documenters
404         return self.format_args()
405 
406     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
407         """Format the signature (arguments and return annotation) of the object.
408 
409         Let the user process it via the ``autodoc-process-signature`` event.
410         """
411         if self.args is not None:
412             # signature given explicitly
413             args = "(%s)" % self.args
414             retann = self.retann
415         else:
416             # try to introspect the signature
417             try:
418                 retann = None
419                 args = self._call_format_args(**kwargs)
420                 if args:
421                     matched = re.match(r'^(\(.*\))\s+->\s+(.*)$', args)
422                     if matched:
423                         args = matched.group(1)
424                         retann = matched.group(2)
425             except Exception:
426                 logger.warning(__('error while formatting arguments for %s:') %
427                                self.fullname, type='autodoc', exc_info=True)
428                 args = None
429 
430         result = self.env.events.emit_firstresult('autodoc-process-signature',
431                                                   self.objtype, self.fullname,
432                                                   self.object, self.options, args, retann)
433         if result:
434             args, retann = result
435 
436         if args is not None:
437             return args + ((' -> %s' % retann) if retann else '')
438         else:
439             return ''
440 
441     def add_directive_header(self, sig: str) -> None:
442         """Add the directive header and options to the generated content."""
443         domain = getattr(self, 'domain', 'py')
444         directive = getattr(self, 'directivetype', self.objtype)
445         name = self.format_name()
446         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
447 
448         # one signature per line, indented by column
449         prefix = '.. %s:%s:: ' % (domain, directive)
450         for i, sig_line in enumerate(sig.split("\n")):
451             self.add_line('%s%s%s' % (prefix, name, sig_line),
452                           sourcename)
453             if i == 0:
454                 prefix = " " * len(prefix)
455 
456         if self.options.noindex:
457             self.add_line('   :noindex:', sourcename)
458         if self.objpath:
459             # Be explicit about the module, this is necessary since .. class::
460             # etc. don't support a prepended module name
461             self.add_line('   :module: %s' % self.modname, sourcename)
462 
463     def get_doc(self, encoding: str = None, ignore: int = None) -> List[List[str]]:
464         """Decode and return lines of the docstring(s) for the object."""
465         if encoding is not None:
466             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
467                           % self.__class__.__name__,
468                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
469         if ignore is not None:
470             warnings.warn("The 'ignore' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
471                           % self.__class__.__name__,
472                           RemovedInSphinx50Warning, stacklevel=2)
473         docstring = getdoc(self.object, self.get_attr,
474                            self.env.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
475                            self.parent, self.object_name)
476         if docstring:
477             tab_width = self.directive.state.document.settings.tab_width
478             return [prepare_docstring(docstring, ignore, tab_width)]
479         return []

481     def process_doc(self, docstrings: List[List[str]]) -> Iterator[str]:
482         """Let the user process the docstrings before adding them."""
483         for docstringlines in docstrings:
484             if self.env.app:
485                 # let extensions preprocess docstrings
486                 self.env.app.emit('autodoc-process-docstring',
487                                   self.objtype, self.fullname, self.object,
488                                   self.options, docstringlines)
489             yield from docstringlines
490 
491     def get_sourcename(self) -> str:
492         if self.analyzer:
493             return '%s:docstring of %s' % (self.analyzer.srcname, self.fullname)
494         return 'docstring of %s' % self.fullname
495 
496     def add_content(self, more_content: Any, no_docstring: bool = False) -> None:
497         """Add content from docstrings, attribute documentation and user."""
498         # set sourcename and add content from attribute documentation
499         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
500         if self.analyzer:
501             attr_docs = self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
502             if self.objpath:
503                 key = ('.'.join(self.objpath[:-1]), self.objpath[-1])
504                 if key in attr_docs:
505                     no_docstring = True
506                     # make a copy of docstring for attributes to avoid cache
507                     # the change of autodoc-process-docstring event.
508                     docstrings = [list(attr_docs[key])]
509 
510                     for i, line in enumerate(self.process_doc(docstrings)):
511                         self.add_line(line, sourcename, i)
512 
513         # add content from docstrings
514         if not no_docstring:
515             docstrings = self.get_doc()
516             if not docstrings:
517                 # append at least a dummy docstring, so that the event
518                 # autodoc-process-docstring is fired and can add some
519                 # content if desired
520                 docstrings.append([])
521             for i, line in enumerate(self.process_doc(docstrings)):
522                 self.add_line(line, sourcename, i)
523 
524         # add additional content (e.g. from document), if present
525         if more_content:
526             for line, src in zip(more_content.data, more_content.items):
527                 self.add_line(line, src[0], src[1])

529     def get_object_members(self, want_all: bool) -> Tuple[bool, List[Tuple[str, Any]]]:
530         """Return `(members_check_module, members)` where `members` is a
531         list of `(membername, member)` pairs of the members of *self.object*.
532 
533         If *want_all* is True, return all members.  Else, only return those
534         members given by *self.options.members* (which may also be none).
535         """
536         members = get_object_members(self.object, self.objpath, self.get_attr, self.analyzer)
537         if not want_all:
538             if not self.options.members:
539                 return False, []
540             # specific members given
541             selected = []
542             for name in self.options.members:
543                 if name in members:
544                     selected.append((name, members[name].value))
545                 else:
546                     logger.warning(__('missing attribute %s in object %s') %
547                                    (name, self.fullname), type='autodoc')
548             return False, selected
549         elif self.options.inherited_members:
550             return False, [(m.name, m.value) for m in members.values()]
551         else:
552             return False, [(m.name, m.value) for m in members.values()
553                            if m.directly_defined]
554 
555     def filter_members(self, members: List[Tuple[str, Any]], want_all: bool
556                        ) -> List[Tuple[str, Any, bool]]:
557         """Filter the given member list.
558 
559         Members are skipped if
560 
561         - they are private (except if given explicitly or the private-members
562           option is set)
563         - they are special methods (except if given explicitly or the
564           special-members option is set)
565         - they are undocumented (except if the undoc-members option is set)
566 
567         The user can override the skipping decision by connecting to the
568         ``autodoc-skip-member`` event.
569         """
570         def is_filtered_inherited_member(name: str) -> bool:
571             if inspect.isclass(self.object):
572                 for cls in self.object.__mro__:
573                     if cls.__name__ == self.options.inherited_members and cls != self.object:
574                         # given member is a member of specified *super class*
575                         return True
576                     elif name in cls.__dict__:
577                         return False
578 
579             return False
580 
581         ret = []
582 
583         # search for members in source code too
584         namespace = '.'.join(self.objpath)  # will be empty for modules
585 
586         if self.analyzer:
587             attr_docs = self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
588         else:
589             attr_docs = {}
590 
591         # process members and determine which to skip
592         for (membername, member) in members:
593             # if isattr is True, the member is documented as an attribute
594             if member is INSTANCEATTR:
595                 isattr = True
596             else:
597                 isattr = False
598 
599             doc = getdoc(member, self.get_attr, self.env.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
600                          self.parent, self.object_name)
601             if not isinstance(doc, str):
602                 # Ignore non-string __doc__
603                 doc = None
604 
605             # if the member __doc__ is the same as self's __doc__, it's just
606             # inherited and therefore not the member's doc
607             cls = self.get_attr(member, '__class__', None)
608             if cls:
609                 cls_doc = self.get_attr(cls, '__doc__', None)
610                 if cls_doc == doc:
611                     doc = None
612             has_doc = bool(doc)
613 
614             metadata = extract_metadata(doc)
615             if 'private' in metadata:
616                 # consider a member private if docstring has "private" metadata
617                 isprivate = True
618             elif 'public' in metadata:
619                 # consider a member public if docstring has "public" metadata
620                 isprivate = False
621             else:
622                 isprivate = membername.startswith('_')
623 
624             keep = False
625             if safe_getattr(member, '__sphinx_mock__', False):
626                 # mocked module or object
627                 pass
628             elif want_all and membername.startswith('__') and \
629                     membername.endswith('__') and len(membername) > 4:
630                 # special __methods__
631                 if self.options.special_members is ALL:
632                     if membername == '__doc__':
633                         keep = False
634                     elif is_filtered_inherited_member(membername):
635                         keep = False
636                     else:
637                         keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
638                 elif self.options.special_members:
639                     if membername in self.options.special_members:
640                         keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
641             elif (namespace, membername) in attr_docs:
642                 if want_all and isprivate:
643                     # ignore members whose name starts with _ by default
644                     keep = self.options.private_members
645                 else:
646                     # keep documented attributes
647                     keep = True
648                 isattr = True
649             elif want_all and isprivate:
650                 # ignore members whose name starts with _ by default
651                 keep = self.options.private_members and \
652                     (has_doc or self.options.undoc_members)
653             else:
654                 if self.options.members is ALL and is_filtered_inherited_member(membername):
655                     keep = False
656                 else:
657                     # ignore undocumented members if :undoc-members: is not given
658                     keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
659 
660             # give the user a chance to decide whether this member
661             # should be skipped
662             if self.env.app:
663                 # let extensions preprocess docstrings
664                 try:
665                     skip_user = self.env.app.emit_firstresult(
666                         'autodoc-skip-member', self.objtype, membername, member,
667                         not keep, self.options)
668                     if skip_user is not None:
669                         keep = not skip_user
670                 except Exception as exc:
671                     logger.warning(__('autodoc: failed to determine %r to be documented, '
672                                       'the following exception was raised:\n%s'),
673                                    member, exc, type='autodoc')
674                     keep = False
675 
676             if keep:
677                 ret.append((membername, member, isattr))
678 
679         return ret
680 
681     def document_members(self, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
682         """Generate reST for member documentation.
683 
684         If *all_members* is True, do all members, else those given by
685         *self.options.members*.
686         """
687         # set current namespace for finding members
688         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = self.modname
689         if self.objpath:
690             self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = self.objpath[0]
691 
692         want_all = all_members or self.options.inherited_members or \
693             self.options.members is ALL
694         # find out which members are documentable
695         members_check_module, members = self.get_object_members(want_all)
696 
697         # remove members given by exclude-members
698         if self.options.exclude_members:
699             members = [
700                 (membername, member) for (membername, member) in members
701                 if (
702                     self.options.exclude_members is ALL or
703                     membername not in self.options.exclude_members
704                 )
705             ]
706 
707         # document non-skipped members
708         memberdocumenters = []  # type: List[Tuple[Documenter, bool]]
709         for (mname, member, isattr) in self.filter_members(members, want_all):
710             classes = [cls for cls in self.documenters.values()
711                        if cls.can_document_member(member, mname, isattr, self)]
712             if not classes:
713                 # don't know how to document this member
714                 continue
715             # prefer the documenter with the highest priority
716             classes.sort(key=lambda cls: cls.priority)
717             # give explicitly separated module name, so that members
718             # of inner classes can be documented
719             full_mname = self.modname + '::' + \
720                 '.'.join(self.objpath + [mname])
721             documenter = classes[-1](self.directive, full_mname, self.indent)
722             memberdocumenters.append((documenter, isattr))
723 
724         member_order = self.options.member_order or self.env.config.autodoc_member_order
725         memberdocumenters = self.sort_members(memberdocumenters, member_order)
726 
727         for documenter, isattr in memberdocumenters:
728             documenter.generate(
729                 all_members=True, real_modname=self.real_modname,
730                 check_module=members_check_module and not isattr)
731 
732         # reset current objects
733         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = None
734         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = None
735 
736     def sort_members(self, documenters: List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]],
737                      order: str) -> List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]]:
738         """Sort the given member list."""
739         if order == 'groupwise':
740             # sort by group; alphabetically within groups
741             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0].member_order, e[0].name))
742         elif order == 'bysource':
743             if self.analyzer:
744                 # sort by source order, by virtue of the module analyzer
745                 tagorder = self.analyzer.tagorder
746 
747                 def keyfunc(entry: Tuple[Documenter, bool]) -> int:
748                     fullname = entry[0].name.split('::')[1]
749                     return tagorder.get(fullname, len(tagorder))
750                 documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
751             else:
752                 # Assume that member discovery order matches source order.
753                 # This is a reasonable assumption in Python 3.6 and up, where
754                 # module.__dict__ is insertion-ordered.
755                 pass
756         else:  # alphabetical
757             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].name)
758 
759         return documenters
760 
761     def generate(self, more_content: Any = None, real_modname: str = None,
762                  check_module: bool = False, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
763         """Generate reST for the object given by *self.name*, and possibly for
764         its members.
765 
766         If *more_content* is given, include that content. If *real_modname* is
767         given, use that module name to find attribute docs. If *check_module* is
768         True, only generate if the object is defined in the module name it is
769         imported from. If *all_members* is True, document all members.
770         """
771         if not self.parse_name():
772             # need a module to import
773             logger.warning(
774                 __('don\'t know which module to import for autodocumenting '
775                    '%r (try placing a "module" or "currentmodule" directive '
776                    'in the document, or giving an explicit module name)') %
777                 self.name, type='autodoc')
778             return
779 
780         # now, import the module and get object to document
781         if not self.import_object():
782             return
783 
784         # If there is no real module defined, figure out which to use.
785         # The real module is used in the module analyzer to look up the module
786         # where the attribute documentation would actually be found in.
787         # This is used for situations where you have a module that collects the
788         # functions and classes of internal submodules.
789         guess_modname = self.get_real_modname()
790         self.real_modname = real_modname or guess_modname
791 
792         # try to also get a source code analyzer for attribute docs
793         try:
794             self.analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(self.real_modname)
795             # parse right now, to get PycodeErrors on parsing (results will
796             # be cached anyway)
797             self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
798         except PycodeError:
799             logger.debug('[autodoc] module analyzer failed:', exc_info=True)
800             # no source file -- e.g. for builtin and C modules
801             self.analyzer = None
802             # at least add the module.__file__ as a dependency
803             if hasattr(self.module, '__file__') and self.module.__file__:
804                 self.directive.filename_set.add(self.module.__file__)
805         else:
806             self.directive.filename_set.add(self.analyzer.srcname)
807 
808         if self.real_modname != guess_modname:
809             # Add module to dependency list if target object is defined in other module.
810             try:
811                 analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(guess_modname)
812                 self.directive.filename_set.add(analyzer.srcname)
813             except PycodeError:
814                 pass
815 
816         # check __module__ of object (for members not given explicitly)
817         if check_module:
818             if not self.check_module():
819                 return
820 
821         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
822 
823         # make sure that the result starts with an empty line.  This is
824         # necessary for some situations where another directive preprocesses
825         # reST and no starting newline is present
826         self.add_line('', sourcename)
827 
828         # format the object's signature, if any
829         sig = self.format_signature()
830 
831         # generate the directive header and options, if applicable
832         self.add_directive_header(sig)
833         self.add_line('', sourcename)
834 
835         # e.g. the module directive doesn't have content
836         self.indent += self.content_indent
837 
838         # add all content (from docstrings, attribute docs etc.)
839         self.add_content(more_content)
840 
841         # document members, if possible
842         self.document_members(all_members)
843 
844 
845 class ModuleDocumenter(Documenter):
846     """
847     Specialized Documenter subclass for modules.
848     """

851     titles_allowed = True
852 
853     option_spec = {
854         'members': members_option, 'undoc-members': bool_option,
855         'noindex': bool_option, 'inherited-members': inherited_members_option,
856         'show-inheritance': bool_option, 'synopsis': identity,
857         'platform': identity, 'deprecated': bool_option,
858         'member-order': member_order_option, 'exclude-members': members_set_option,
859         'private-members': bool_option, 'special-members': members_option,
860         'imported-members': bool_option, 'ignore-module-all': bool_option
861     }  # type: Dict[str, Callable]

863     def __init__(self, *args: Any) -> None:
864         super().__init__(*args)

870                             ) -> bool:

872         return False

874     def resolve_name(self, modname: str, parents: Any, path: str, base: Any
875                      ) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:

877             logger.warning(__('"::" in automodule name doesn\'t make sense'),
878                            type='autodoc')

881     def parse_name(self) -> bool:
882         ret = super().parse_name()
883         if self.args or self.retann:
884             logger.warning(__('signature arguments or return annotation '
885                               'given for automodule %s') % self.fullname,
886                            type='autodoc')

889     def import_object(self) -> Any:
890         def is_valid_module_all(__all__: Any) -> bool:
891             """Check the given *__all__* is valid for a module."""
892             if (isinstance(__all__, (list, tuple)) and
893                     all(isinstance(e, str) for e in __all__)):
894                 return True
895             else:
896                 return False
897 
898         ret = super().import_object()
899 
900         if not self.options.ignore_module_all:
901             __all__ = getattr(self.object, '__all__', None)
902             if is_valid_module_all(__all__):
903                 # valid __all__ found. copy it to self.__all__
904                 self.__all__ = __all__
905             elif __all__:
906                 # invalid __all__ found.
907                 logger.warning(__('__all__ should be a list of strings, not %r '
908                                   '(in module %s) -- ignoring __all__') %
909                                (__all__, self.fullname), type='autodoc')
910 
911         return ret

913     def add_directive_header(self, sig: str) -> None:
914         Documenter.add_directive_header(self, sig)

916         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
917 
918         # add some module-specific options
919         if self.options.synopsis:
920             self.add_line('   :synopsis: ' + self.options.synopsis, sourcename)
921         if self.options.platform:
922             self.add_line('   :platform: ' + self.options.platform, sourcename)

924             self.add_line('   :deprecated:', sourcename)

926     def get_object_members(self, want_all: bool) -> Tuple[bool, List[Tuple[str, Any]]]:
927         if want_all:
928             if self.__all__:
929                 memberlist = self.__all__
930             else:
931                 # for implicit module members, check __module__ to avoid
932                 # documenting imported objects
933                 return True, get_module_members(self.object)
934         else:
935             memberlist = self.options.members or []
936         ret = []
937         for mname in memberlist:
938             try:
939                 ret.append((mname, safe_getattr(self.object, mname)))
940             except AttributeError:
941                 logger.warning(
942                     __('missing attribute mentioned in :members: or __all__: '
943                        'module %s, attribute %s') %
944                     (safe_getattr(self.object, '__name__', '???'), mname),
945                     type='autodoc'
946                 )
947         return False, ret

949     def sort_members(self, documenters: List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]],
950                      order: str) -> List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]]:
951         if order == 'bysource' and self.__all__:
952             # Sort alphabetically first (for members not listed on the __all__)
953             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].name)
954 
955             # Sort by __all__
956             def keyfunc(entry: Tuple[Documenter, bool]) -> int:
957                 name = entry[0].name.split('::')[1]
958                 if name in self.__all__:
959                     return self.__all__.index(name)
960                 else:
961                     return len(self.__all__)
962             documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
963 
964             return documenters
965         else:
966             return super().sort_members(documenters, order)

969 class ModuleLevelDocumenter(Documenter):
970     """
971     Specialized Documenter subclass for objects on module level (functions,
972     classes, data/constants).
973     """
974     def resolve_name(self, modname: str, parents: Any, path: str, base: Any
975                      ) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
976         if modname is None:
977             if path:
978                 stripped = path.rstrip('.')

996 class ClassLevelDocumenter(Documenter):
997     """
998     Specialized Documenter subclass for objects on class level (methods,
999     attributes).
1000     """
1001     def resolve_name(self, modname: str, parents: Any, path: str, base: Any
1002                      ) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
1003         if modname is None:
1004             if path:
1005                 mod_cls = path.rstrip('.')
1006             else:
1007                 mod_cls = None
1008                 # if documenting a class-level object without path,
1009                 # there must be a current class, either from a parent
1010                 # auto directive ...
1011                 mod_cls = self.env.temp_data.get('autodoc:class')
1012                 # ... or from a class directive
1013                 if mod_cls is None:
1014                     mod_cls = self.env.ref_context.get('py:class')
1015                 # ... if still None, there's no way to know
1016                 if mod_cls is None:
1017                     return None, []
1018 
1019             try:
1020                 modname, qualname = split_full_qualified_name(mod_cls)
1021                 parents = qualname.split(".") if qualname else []
1022             except ImportError:
1023                 parents = mod_cls.split(".")
1024 
1025             # if the module name is still missing, get it like above
1026             if not modname:
1027                 modname = self.env.temp_data.get('autodoc:module')
1028             if not modname:
1029                 modname = self.env.ref_context.get('py:module')

1034 class DocstringSignatureMixin:
1035     """
1036     Mixin for FunctionDocumenter and MethodDocumenter to provide the
1037     feature of reading the signature from the docstring.
1038     """
1039 
1040     def _find_signature(self, encoding: str = None) -> Tuple[str, str]:
1041         if encoding is not None:
1042             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s._find_signature() is "
1043                           "deprecated." % self.__class__.__name__,
1044                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
1045         docstrings = self.get_doc()
1046         self._new_docstrings = docstrings[:]
1047         result = None
1048         for i, doclines in enumerate(docstrings):
1049             # no lines in docstring, no match
1050             if not doclines:
1051                 continue
1052             # match first line of docstring against signature RE
1053             match = py_ext_sig_re.match(doclines[0])
1054             if not match:
1055                 continue
1056             exmod, path, base, args, retann = match.groups()
1057             # the base name must match ours
1058             valid_names = [self.objpath[-1]]  # type: ignore
1059             if isinstance(self, ClassDocumenter):
1060                 valid_names.append('__init__')
1061                 if hasattr(self.object, '__mro__'):
1062                     valid_names.extend(cls.__name__ for cls in self.object.__mro__)
1063             if base not in valid_names:
1064                 continue
1065             # re-prepare docstring to ignore more leading indentation
1066             tab_width = self.directive.state.document.settings.tab_width  # type: ignore
1067             self._new_docstrings[i] = prepare_docstring('\n'.join(doclines[1:]),
1068                                                         tabsize=tab_width)
1069             result = args, retann
1070             # don't look any further
1071             break
1072         return result
1073 
1074     def get_doc(self, encoding: str = None, ignore: int = None) -> List[List[str]]:
1075         if encoding is not None:
1076             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
1077                           % self.__class__.__name__,
1078                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
1079         lines = getattr(self, '_new_docstrings', None)
1080         if lines is not None:
1081             return lines
1082         return super().get_doc(None, ignore)  # type: ignore
1083 
1084     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1085         if self.args is None and self.env.config.autodoc_docstring_signature:  # type: ignore
1086             # only act if a signature is not explicitly given already, and if
1087             # the feature is enabled
1088             result = self._find_signature()
1089             if result is not None:
1090                 self.args, self.retann = result
1091         return super().format_signature(**kwargs)  # type: ignore

1222 class ClassDocumenter(DocstringSignatureMixin, ModuleLevelDocumenter):  # type: ignore
1223     """
1224     Specialized Documenter subclass for classes.
1225     """
1226     objtype = 'class'
1227     member_order = 20
1228     option_spec = {
1229         'members': members_option, 'undoc-members': bool_option,
1230         'noindex': bool_option, 'inherited-members': inherited_members_option,
1231         'show-inheritance': bool_option, 'member-order': member_order_option,
1232         'exclude-members': members_set_option,
1233         'private-members': bool_option, 'special-members': members_option,
1234     }  # type: Dict[str, Callable]
1235 
1236     def __init__(self, *args: Any) -> None:
1237         super().__init__(*args)
1238         merge_special_members_option(self.options)

1240     @classmethod
1241     def can_document_member(cls, member: Any, membername: str, isattr: bool, parent: Any
1242                             ) -> bool:
1243         return isinstance(member, type)
1244 
1245     def import_object(self) -> Any:
1246         ret = super().import_object()
1247         # if the class is documented under another name, document it
1248         # as data/attribute
1249         if ret:
1250             if hasattr(self.object, '__name__'):
1251                 self.doc_as_attr = (self.objpath[-1] != self.object.__name__)
1252             else:
1253                 self.doc_as_attr = True
1254         return ret
1255 
1256     def _get_signature(self) -> Optional[Signature]:
1257         def get_user_defined_function_or_method(obj: Any, attr: str) -> Any:
1258             """ Get the `attr` function or method from `obj`, if it is user-defined. """
1259             if inspect.is_builtin_class_method(obj, attr):
1260                 return None
1261             attr = self.get_attr(obj, attr, None)
1262             if not (inspect.ismethod(attr) or inspect.isfunction(attr)):
1263                 return None
1264             return attr
1265 
1266         # This sequence is copied from inspect._signature_from_callable.
1267         # ValueError means that no signature could be found, so we keep going.
1268 
1269         # First, let's see if it has an overloaded __call__ defined
1270         # in its metaclass
1271         call = get_user_defined_function_or_method(type(self.object), '__call__')
1272 
1273         if call is not None:
1274             if "{0.__module__}.{0.__qualname__}".format(call) in _METACLASS_CALL_BLACKLIST:
1275                 call = None
1276 
1277         if call is not None:
1278             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', call, True)
1279             try:
1280                 return inspect.signature(call, bound_method=True)
1281             except ValueError:
1282                 pass
1283 
1284         # Now we check if the 'obj' class has a '__new__' method
1285         new = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__new__')
1286         if new is not None:
1287             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', new, True)
1288             try:
1289                 return inspect.signature(new, bound_method=True)
1290             except ValueError:
1291                 pass
1292 
1293         # Finally, we should have at least __init__ implemented
1294         init = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__init__')
1295         if init is not None:
1296             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', init, True)
1297             try:
1298                 return inspect.signature(init, bound_method=True)
1299             except ValueError:
1300                 pass
1301 
1302         # None of the attributes are user-defined, so fall back to let inspect
1303         # handle it.
1304         # We don't know the exact method that inspect.signature will read
1305         # the signature from, so just pass the object itself to our hook.
1306         self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', self.object, False)
1307         try:
1308             return inspect.signature(self.object, bound_method=False)
1309         except ValueError:
1310             pass
1311 
1312         # Still no signature: happens e.g. for old-style classes
1313         # with __init__ in C and no `__text_signature__`.
1314         return None

1316     def format_args(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1317         if self.env.config.autodoc_typehints in ('none', 'description'):
1318             kwargs.setdefault('show_annotation', False)
1319 
1320         try:
1321             sig = self._get_signature()
1322         except TypeError as exc:
1323             # __signature__ attribute contained junk
1324             logger.warning(__("Failed to get a constructor signature for %s: %s"),
1325                            self.fullname, exc)
1326             return None
1327 
1328         if sig is None:
1329             return None
1330 
1331         return stringify_signature(sig, show_return_annotation=False, **kwargs)

1362         if encoding is not None:
1363             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
1364                           % self.__class__.__name__,
1365                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
1366         lines = getattr(self, '_new_docstrings', None)
1367         if lines is not None:
1368             return lines
1369 
1370         content = self.env.config.autoclass_content
1371 
1372         docstrings = []
1373         attrdocstring = self.get_attr(self.object, '__doc__', None)
1374         if attrdocstring:
1375             docstrings.append(attrdocstring)
1376 
1377         # for classes, what the "docstring" is can be controlled via a

1382                                    self.env.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,

1392                 initdocstring = getdoc(__new__, self.get_attr,
1393                                        self.env.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
1394                                        self.parent, self.object_name)
1395                 # for new-style classes, no __new__ means default __new__
1396                 if (initdocstring is not None and
1397                     (initdocstring == object.__new__.__doc__ or  # for pypy
1398                      initdocstring.strip() == object.__new__.__doc__)):  # for !pypy
1399                     initdocstring = None
1400             if initdocstring:
1401                 if content == 'init':

1404                     docstrings.append(initdocstring)

141 def cut_lines(pre: int, post: int = 0, what: str = None) -> Callable:
142     """Return a listener that removes the first *pre* and last *post*
143     lines of every docstring.  If *what* is a sequence of strings,
144     only docstrings of a type in *what* will be processed.
145 
146     Use like this (e.g. in the ``setup()`` function of :file:`conf.py`)::
147 
148        from sphinx.ext.autodoc import cut_lines
149        app.connect('autodoc-process-docstring', cut_lines(4, what=['module']))
150 
151     This can (and should) be used in place of :confval:`automodule_skip_lines`.
152     """
153     def process(app: Sphinx, what_: str, name: str, obj: Any, options: Any, lines: List[str]
154                 ) -> None:
155         if what and what_ not in what:
156             return
157         del lines[:pre]
158         if post:
159             # remove one trailing blank line.
160             if lines and not lines[-1]:
161                 lines.pop(-1)
162             del lines[-post:]
163         # make sure there is a blank line at the end
164         if lines and lines[-1]:
165             lines.append('')
166     return process

169 def between(marker: str, what: Sequence[str] = None, keepempty: bool = False,
170             exclude: bool = False) -> Callable:
171     """Return a listener that either keeps, or if *exclude* is True excludes,
172     lines between lines that match the *marker* regular expression.  If no line
173     matches, the resulting docstring would be empty, so no change will be made
174     unless *keepempty* is true.
175 
176     If *what* is a sequence of strings, only docstrings of a type in *what* will
177     be processed.
178     """
179     marker_re = re.compile(marker)
180 
181     def process(app: Sphinx, what_: str, name: str, obj: Any, options: Any, lines: List[str]
182                 ) -> None:
183         if what and what_ not in what:
184             return
185         deleted = 0
186         delete = not exclude
187         orig_lines = lines[:]
188         for i, line in enumerate(orig_lines):
189             if delete:
190                 lines.pop(i - deleted)
191                 deleted += 1
192             if marker_re.match(line):
193                 delete = not delete
194                 if delete:
195                     lines.pop(i - deleted)
196                     deleted += 1
197         if not lines and not keepempty:
198             lines[:] = orig_lines
199         # make sure there is a blank line at the end
200         if lines and lines[-1]:
201             lines.append('')
202     return process

216 class Documenter:

218     A Documenter knows how to autodocument a single object type.  When
219     registered with the AutoDirective, it will be used to document objects
220     of that type when needed by autodoc.
221 
222     Its *objtype* attribute selects what auto directive it is assigned to
223     (the directive name is 'auto' + objtype), and what directive it generates
224     by default, though that can be overridden by an attribute called
225     *directivetype*.

227     A Documenter has an *option_spec* that works like a docutils directive's;
228     in fact, it will be used to parse an auto directive's options that matches
229     the documenter.

232     #: generated directive name
233     objtype = 'object'

238     #: order if autodoc_member_order is set to 'groupwise'
239     member_order = 0
240     #: true if the generated content may contain titles
241     titles_allowed = False

243     option_spec = {'noindex': bool_option}  # type: Dict[str, Callable]

291     def resolve_name(self, modname: str, parents: Any, path: str, base: Any
292                      ) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
293         """Resolve the module and name of the object to document given by the
294         arguments and the current module/class.
295 
296         Must return a pair of the module name and a chain of attributes; for
297         example, it would return ``('zipfile', ['ZipFile', 'open'])`` for the
298         ``zipfile.ZipFile.open`` method.
299         """
300         raise NotImplementedError('must be implemented in subclasses')

302     def parse_name(self) -> bool:
303         """Determine what module to import and what attribute to document.
304 
305         Returns True and sets *self.modname*, *self.objpath*, *self.fullname*,
306         *self.args* and *self.retann* if parsing and resolving was successful.
307         """
308         # first, parse the definition -- auto directives for classes and
309         # functions can contain a signature which is then used instead of
310         # an autogenerated one
311         try:
312             explicit_modname, path, base, args, retann = \
313                 py_ext_sig_re.match(self.name).groups()
314         except AttributeError:
315             logger.warning(__('invalid signature for auto%s (%r)') % (self.objtype, self.name),
316                            type='autodoc')
317             return False
318 
319         # support explicit module and class name separation via ::
320         if explicit_modname is not None:
321             modname = explicit_modname[:-2]
322             parents = path.rstrip('.').split('.') if path else []
323         else:
324             modname = None
325             parents = []
326 
327         with mock(self.env.config.autodoc_mock_imports):
328             self.modname, self.objpath = self.resolve_name(modname, parents, path, base)
329 
330         if not self.modname:
331             return False
332 
333         self.args = args
334         self.retann = retann
335         self.fullname = (self.modname or '') + \
336                         ('.' + '.'.join(self.objpath) if self.objpath else '')
337         return True

339     def import_object(self, raiseerror: bool = False) -> bool:
340         """Import the object given by *self.modname* and *self.objpath* and set

344         """
345         with mock(self.env.config.autodoc_mock_imports):
346             try:
347                 ret = import_object(self.modname, self.objpath, self.objtype,
348                                     attrgetter=self.get_attr,
349                                     warningiserror=self.env.config.autodoc_warningiserror)
350                 self.module, self.parent, self.object_name, self.object = ret

353                 if raiseerror:
354                     raise

356                     logger.warning(exc.args[0], type='autodoc', subtype='import_object')

399     def _call_format_args(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
400         if kwargs:
401             try:
402                 return self.format_args(**kwargs)
403             except TypeError:
404                 # avoid chaining exceptions, by putting nothing here
405                 pass

407         # retry without arguments for old documenters

410     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
411         """Format the signature (arguments and return annotation) of the object.
412 
413         Let the user process it via the ``autodoc-process-signature`` event.
414         """
415         if self.args is not None:
416             # signature given explicitly
417             args = "(%s)" % self.args
418             retann = self.retann
419         else:
420             # try to introspect the signature
421             try:
422                 retann = None
423                 args = self._call_format_args(**kwargs)
424                 if args:
425                     matched = re.match(r'^(\(.*\))\s+->\s+(.*)$', args)
426                     if matched:
427                         args = matched.group(1)
428                         retann = matched.group(2)
429             except Exception as exc:
430                 logger.warning(__('error while formatting arguments for %s: %s'),
431                                self.fullname, exc, type='autodoc')
432                 args = None
433 
434         result = self.env.events.emit_firstresult('autodoc-process-signature',
435                                                   self.objtype, self.fullname,
436                                                   self.object, self.options, args, retann)
437         if result:
438             args, retann = result
439 
440         if args is not None:
441             return args + ((' -> %s' % retann) if retann else '')
442         else:
443             return ''

445     def add_directive_header(self, sig: str) -> None:
446         """Add the directive header and options to the generated content."""
447         domain = getattr(self, 'domain', 'py')
448         directive = getattr(self, 'directivetype', self.objtype)
449         name = self.format_name()
450         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
451 
452         # one signature per line, indented by column
453         prefix = '.. %s:%s:: ' % (domain, directive)
454         for i, sig_line in enumerate(sig.split("\n")):
455             self.add_line('%s%s%s' % (prefix, name, sig_line),
456                           sourcename)
457             if i == 0:
458                 prefix = " " * len(prefix)
459 
460         if self.options.noindex:
461             self.add_line('   :noindex:', sourcename)
462         if self.objpath:
463             # Be explicit about the module, this is necessary since .. class::
464             # etc. don't support a prepended module name
465             self.add_line('   :module: %s' % self.modname, sourcename)

533     def get_object_members(self, want_all: bool) -> Tuple[bool, List[Tuple[str, Any]]]:

535         list of `(membername, member)` pairs of the members of *self.object*.
536 
537         If *want_all* is True, return all members.  Else, only return those
538         members given by *self.options.members* (which may also be none).
539         """
540         members = get_object_members(self.object, self.objpath, self.get_attr, self.analyzer)
541         if not want_all:
542             if not self.options.members:
543                 return False, []
544             # specific members given
545             selected = []
546             for name in self.options.members:
547                 if name in members:
548                     selected.append((name, members[name].value))
549                 else:
550                     logger.warning(__('missing attribute %s in object %s') %

553         elif self.options.inherited_members:

559     def filter_members(self, members: List[Tuple[str, Any]], want_all: bool
560                        ) -> List[Tuple[str, Any, bool]]:
561         """Filter the given member list.
562 
563         Members are skipped if
564 
565         - they are private (except if given explicitly or the private-members
566           option is set)
567         - they are special methods (except if given explicitly or the
568           special-members option is set)
569         - they are undocumented (except if the undoc-members option is set)
570 
571         The user can override the skipping decision by connecting to the
572         ``autodoc-skip-member`` event.
573         """
574         def is_filtered_inherited_member(name: str) -> bool:
575             if inspect.isclass(self.object):
576                 for cls in self.object.__mro__:
577                     if cls.__name__ == self.options.inherited_members and cls != self.object:
578                         # given member is a member of specified *super class*
579                         return True
580                     elif name in cls.__dict__:
581                         return False
582 
583             return False
584 
585         ret = []
586 
587         # search for members in source code too
588         namespace = '.'.join(self.objpath)  # will be empty for modules
589 
590         if self.analyzer:
591             attr_docs = self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
592         else:
593             attr_docs = {}
594 
595         # process members and determine which to skip
596         for (membername, member) in members:
597             # if isattr is True, the member is documented as an attribute
598             if member is INSTANCEATTR:
599                 isattr = True
600             else:
601                 isattr = False
602 
603             doc = getdoc(member, self.get_attr, self.env.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
604                          self.parent, self.object_name)
605             if not isinstance(doc, str):
606                 # Ignore non-string __doc__
607                 doc = None
608 
609             # if the member __doc__ is the same as self's __doc__, it's just
610             # inherited and therefore not the member's doc
611             cls = self.get_attr(member, '__class__', None)
612             if cls:
613                 cls_doc = self.get_attr(cls, '__doc__', None)
614                 if cls_doc == doc:
615                     doc = None
616             has_doc = bool(doc)
617 
618             metadata = extract_metadata(doc)
619             if 'private' in metadata:
620                 # consider a member private if docstring has "private" metadata
621                 isprivate = True
622             elif 'public' in metadata:
623                 # consider a member public if docstring has "public" metadata
624                 isprivate = False
625             else:
626                 isprivate = membername.startswith('_')
627 
628             keep = False
629             if safe_getattr(member, '__sphinx_mock__', False):
630                 # mocked module or object
631                 pass
632             elif (self.options.exclude_members not in (None, ALL) and
633                   membername in self.options.exclude_members):
634                 # remove members given by exclude-members
635                 keep = False
636             elif want_all and membername.startswith('__') and \
637                     membername.endswith('__') and len(membername) > 4:
638                 # special __methods__
639                 if self.options.special_members is ALL:
640                     if membername == '__doc__':
641                         keep = False
642                     elif is_filtered_inherited_member(membername):
643                         keep = False
644                     else:
645                         keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
646                 elif self.options.special_members:
647                     if membername in self.options.special_members:
648                         keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
649             elif (namespace, membername) in attr_docs:
650                 if want_all and isprivate:
651                     # ignore members whose name starts with _ by default
652                     keep = self.options.private_members
653                 else:
654                     # keep documented attributes
655                     keep = True
656                 isattr = True
657             elif want_all and isprivate:
658                 # ignore members whose name starts with _ by default
659                 keep = self.options.private_members and \
660                     (has_doc or self.options.undoc_members)
661             else:
662                 if self.options.members is ALL and is_filtered_inherited_member(membername):
663                     keep = False
664                 else:
665                     # ignore undocumented members if :undoc-members: is not given
666                     keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
667 
668             # give the user a chance to decide whether this member
669             # should be skipped
670             if self.env.app:
671                 # let extensions preprocess docstrings
672                 try:
673                     skip_user = self.env.app.emit_firstresult(
674                         'autodoc-skip-member', self.objtype, membername, member,
675                         not keep, self.options)
676                     if skip_user is not None:
677                         keep = not skip_user
678                 except Exception as exc:
679                     logger.warning(__('autodoc: failed to determine %r to be documented, '
680                                       'the following exception was raised:\n%s'),
681                                    member, exc, type='autodoc')
682                     keep = False
683 
684             if keep:
685                 ret.append((membername, member, isattr))
686 
687         return ret
688 
689     def document_members(self, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
690         """Generate reST for member documentation.
691 
692         If *all_members* is True, do all members, else those given by
693         *self.options.members*.
694         """
695         # set current namespace for finding members
696         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = self.modname
697         if self.objpath:
698             self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = self.objpath[0]
699 
700         want_all = all_members or self.options.inherited_members or \
701             self.options.members is ALL
702         # find out which members are documentable
703         members_check_module, members = self.get_object_members(want_all)
704 
705         # document non-skipped members
706         memberdocumenters = []  # type: List[Tuple[Documenter, bool]]
707         for (mname, member, isattr) in self.filter_members(members, want_all):
708             classes = [cls for cls in self.documenters.values()
709                        if cls.can_document_member(member, mname, isattr, self)]
710             if not classes:
711                 # don't know how to document this member
712                 continue
713             # prefer the documenter with the highest priority
714             classes.sort(key=lambda cls: cls.priority)
715             # give explicitly separated module name, so that members
716             # of inner classes can be documented
717             full_mname = self.modname + '::' + \
718                 '.'.join(self.objpath + [mname])
719             documenter = classes[-1](self.directive, full_mname, self.indent)
720             memberdocumenters.append((documenter, isattr))
721 
722         member_order = self.options.member_order or self.env.config.autodoc_member_order
723         memberdocumenters = self.sort_members(memberdocumenters, member_order)
724 
725         for documenter, isattr in memberdocumenters:
726             documenter.generate(
727                 all_members=True, real_modname=self.real_modname,
728                 check_module=members_check_module and not isattr)
729 
730         # reset current objects
731         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = None
732         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = None
733 
734     def sort_members(self, documenters: List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]],
735                      order: str) -> List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]]:
736         """Sort the given member list."""
737         if order == 'groupwise':
738             # sort by group; alphabetically within groups
739             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0].member_order, e[0].name))
740         elif order == 'bysource':
741             if self.analyzer:
742                 # sort by source order, by virtue of the module analyzer
743                 tagorder = self.analyzer.tagorder
744 
745                 def keyfunc(entry: Tuple[Documenter, bool]) -> int:
746                     fullname = entry[0].name.split('::')[1]
747                     return tagorder.get(fullname, len(tagorder))
748                 documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
749             else:
750                 # Assume that member discovery order matches source order.
751                 # This is a reasonable assumption in Python 3.6 and up, where
752                 # module.__dict__ is insertion-ordered.
753                 pass
754         else:  # alphabetical
755             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].name)
756 
757         return documenters
758 
759     def generate(self, more_content: Any = None, real_modname: str = None,
760                  check_module: bool = False, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
761         """Generate reST for the object given by *self.name*, and possibly for
762         its members.
763 
764         If *more_content* is given, include that content. If *real_modname* is
765         given, use that module name to find attribute docs. If *check_module* is
766         True, only generate if the object is defined in the module name it is
767         imported from. If *all_members* is True, document all members.
768         """
769         if not self.parse_name():
770             # need a module to import
771             logger.warning(
772                 __('don\'t know which module to import for autodocumenting '
773                    '%r (try placing a "module" or "currentmodule" directive '
774                    'in the document, or giving an explicit module name)') %
775                 self.name, type='autodoc')
776             return
777 
778         # now, import the module and get object to document
779         if not self.import_object():
780             return
781 
782         # If there is no real module defined, figure out which to use.
783         # The real module is used in the module analyzer to look up the module
784         # where the attribute documentation would actually be found in.
785         # This is used for situations where you have a module that collects the
786         # functions and classes of internal submodules.
787         guess_modname = self.get_real_modname()
788         self.real_modname = real_modname or guess_modname
789 
790         # try to also get a source code analyzer for attribute docs
791         try:
792             self.analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(self.real_modname)
793             # parse right now, to get PycodeErrors on parsing (results will
794             # be cached anyway)
795             self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
796         except PycodeError as exc:
797             logger.debug('[autodoc] module analyzer failed: %s', exc)
798             # no source file -- e.g. for builtin and C modules
799             self.analyzer = None
800             # at least add the module.__file__ as a dependency
801             if hasattr(self.module, '__file__') and self.module.__file__:
802                 self.directive.filename_set.add(self.module.__file__)
803         else:
804             self.directive.filename_set.add(self.analyzer.srcname)
805 
806         if self.real_modname != guess_modname:
807             # Add module to dependency list if target object is defined in other module.
808             try:
809                 analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(guess_modname)
810                 self.directive.filename_set.add(analyzer.srcname)
811             except PycodeError:
812                 pass
813 
814         # check __module__ of object (for members not given explicitly)
815         if check_module:
816             if not self.check_module():
817                 return
818 
819         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
820 
821         # make sure that the result starts with an empty line.  This is
822         # necessary for some situations where another directive preprocesses
823         # reST and no starting newline is present
824         self.add_line('', sourcename)
825 
826         # format the object's signature, if any
827         try:
828             sig = self.format_signature()
829         except Exception as exc:
830             logger.warning(__('error while formatting signature for %s: %s'),
831                            self.fullname, exc, type='autodoc')
832             return
833 
834         # generate the directive header and options, if applicable
835         self.add_directive_header(sig)
836         self.add_line('', sourcename)
837 
838         # e.g. the module directive doesn't have content
839         self.indent += self.content_indent
840 
841         # add all content (from docstrings, attribute docs etc.)
842         self.add_content(more_content)
843 
844         # document members, if possible
845         self.document_members(all_members)
846

859         'show-inheritance': bool_option, 'synopsis': identity,

862         'private-members': bool_option, 'special-members': members_option,
863         'imported-members': bool_option, 'ignore-module-all': bool_option

866     def __init__(self, *args: Any) -> None:
867         super().__init__(*args)

873                             ) -> bool:

877     def resolve_name(self, modname: str, parents: Any, path: str, base: Any

888                               'given for automodule %s') % self.fullname,

892     def import_object(self, raiseerror: bool = False) -> bool:
893         def is_valid_module_all(__all__: Any) -> bool:
894             """Check the given *__all__* is valid for a module."""
895             if (isinstance(__all__, (list, tuple)) and
896                     all(isinstance(e, str) for e in __all__)):
897                 return True
898             else:
899                 return False

901         ret = super().import_object(raiseerror)
902 
903         if not self.options.ignore_module_all:
904             __all__ = getattr(self.object, '__all__', None)
905             if is_valid_module_all(__all__):
906                 # valid __all__ found. copy it to self.__all__
907                 self.__all__ = __all__
908             elif __all__:
909                 # invalid __all__ found.
910                 logger.warning(__('__all__ should be a list of strings, not %r '
911                                   '(in module %s) -- ignoring __all__') %
912                                (__all__, self.fullname), type='autodoc')
913 
914         return ret

916     def add_directive_header(self, sig: str) -> None:
917         Documenter.add_directive_header(self, sig)
918 
919         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
920 
921         # add some module-specific options
922         if self.options.synopsis:
923             self.add_line('   :synopsis: ' + self.options.synopsis, sourcename)
924         if self.options.platform:
925             self.add_line('   :platform: ' + self.options.platform, sourcename)
926         if self.options.deprecated:
927             self.add_line('   :deprecated:', sourcename)

929     def get_object_members(self, want_all: bool) -> Tuple[bool, List[Tuple[str, Any]]]:
930         if want_all:
931             if self.__all__:
932                 memberlist = self.__all__
933             else:
934                 # for implicit module members, check __module__ to avoid
935                 # documenting imported objects
936                 return True, get_module_members(self.object)
937         else:
938             memberlist = self.options.members or []
939         ret = []
940         for mname in memberlist:
941             try:
942                 ret.append((mname, safe_getattr(self.object, mname)))
943             except AttributeError:
944                 logger.warning(
945                     __('missing attribute mentioned in :members: or __all__: '
946                        'module %s, attribute %s') %
947                     (safe_getattr(self.object, '__name__', '???'), mname),
948                     type='autodoc'
949                 )
950         return False, ret
951 
952     def sort_members(self, documenters: List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]],
953                      order: str) -> List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]]:
954         if order == 'bysource' and self.__all__:
955             # Sort alphabetically first (for members not listed on the __all__)
956             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].name)
957 
958             # Sort by __all__
959             def keyfunc(entry: Tuple[Documenter, bool]) -> int:
960                 name = entry[0].name.split('::')[1]
961                 if name in self.__all__:
962                     return self.__all__.index(name)
963                 else:
964                     return len(self.__all__)
965             documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
966 
967             return documenters
968         else:
969             return super().sort_members(documenters, order)

972 class ModuleLevelDocumenter(Documenter):
973     """
974     Specialized Documenter subclass for objects on module level (functions,
975     classes, data/constants).

978                      ) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
979         if modname is None:
980             if path:
981                 modname = path.rstrip('.')
982             else:
983                 # if documenting a toplevel object without explicit module,
984                 # it can be contained in another auto directive ...
985                 modname = self.env.temp_data.get('autodoc:module')
986                 # ... or in the scope of a module directive
987                 if not modname:
988                     modname = self.env.ref_context.get('py:module')
989                 # ... else, it stays None, which means invalid
990         return modname, parents + [base]

993 class ClassLevelDocumenter(Documenter):
994     """
995     Specialized Documenter subclass for objects on class level (methods,
996     attributes).
997     """
998     def resolve_name(self, modname: str, parents: Any, path: str, base: Any
999                      ) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
1000         if modname is None:
1001             if path:
1002                 mod_cls = path.rstrip('.')
1003             else:
1004                 mod_cls = None
1005                 # if documenting a class-level object without path,
1006                 # there must be a current class, either from a parent
1007                 # auto directive ...
1008                 mod_cls = self.env.temp_data.get('autodoc:class')
1009                 # ... or from a class directive
1010                 if mod_cls is None:
1011                     mod_cls = self.env.ref_context.get('py:class')
1012                 # ... if still None, there's no way to know
1013                 if mod_cls is None:
1014                     return None, []
1015             modname, sep, cls = mod_cls.rpartition('.')
1016             parents = [cls]
1017             # if the module name is still missing, get it like above
1018             if not modname:
1019                 modname = self.env.temp_data.get('autodoc:module')
1020             if not modname:
1021                 modname = self.env.ref_context.get('py:module')
1022             # ... else, it stays None, which means invalid
1023         return modname, parents + [base]

1026 class DocstringSignatureMixin:
1027     """
1028     Mixin for FunctionDocumenter and MethodDocumenter to provide the
1029     feature of reading the signature from the docstring.
1030     """
1031     _new_docstrings = None  # type: List[List[str]]
1032     _signatures = None      # type: List[str]
1033 
1034     def _find_signature(self, encoding: str = None) -> Tuple[str, str]:
1035         if encoding is not None:
1036             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s._find_signature() is "
1037                           "deprecated." % self.__class__.__name__,
1038                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
1039 
1040         # candidates of the object name
1041         valid_names = [self.objpath[-1]]  # type: ignore
1042         if isinstance(self, ClassDocumenter):
1043             valid_names.append('__init__')
1044             if hasattr(self.object, '__mro__'):
1045                 valid_names.extend(cls.__name__ for cls in self.object.__mro__)
1046 
1047         docstrings = self.get_doc()
1048         self._new_docstrings = docstrings[:]
1049         self._signatures = []
1050         result = None
1051         for i, doclines in enumerate(docstrings):
1052             for j, line in enumerate(doclines):
1053                 if not line:
1054                     # no lines in docstring, no match
1055                     break
1056 
1057                 if line.endswith('\\'):
1058                     multiline = True
1059                     line = line.rstrip('\\').rstrip()
1060                 else:
1061                     multiline = False
1062 
1063                 # match first line of docstring against signature RE
1064                 match = py_ext_sig_re.match(line)
1065                 if not match:
1066                     continue
1067                 exmod, path, base, args, retann = match.groups()
1068 
1069                 # the base name must match ours
1070                 if base not in valid_names:
1071                     continue
1072 
1073                 # re-prepare docstring to ignore more leading indentation
1074                 tab_width = self.directive.state.document.settings.tab_width  # type: ignore
1075                 self._new_docstrings[i] = prepare_docstring('\n'.join(doclines[j + 1:]),
1076                                                             tabsize=tab_width)
1077 
1078                 if result is None:
1079                     # first signature
1080                     result = args, retann
1081                 else:
1082                     # subsequent signatures
1083                     self._signatures.append("(%s) -> %s" % (args, retann))
1084 
1085                 if multiline:
1086                     # the signature have multiple signatures on docstring
1087                     continue
1088                 else:
1089                     # don't look any further
1090                     break
1091 
1092             if result:
1093                 # finish the loop when signature found
1094                 break
1095 
1096         return result
1097 
1098     def get_doc(self, encoding: str = None, ignore: int = None) -> List[List[str]]:
1099         if encoding is not None:
1100             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
1101                           % self.__class__.__name__,
1102                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
1103         if self._new_docstrings is not None:
1104             return self._new_docstrings
1105         return super().get_doc(None, ignore)  # type: ignore
1106 
1107     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1108         if self.args is None and self.env.config.autodoc_docstring_signature:  # type: ignore
1109             # only act if a signature is not explicitly given already, and if
1110             # the feature is enabled
1111             result = self._find_signature()
1112             if result is not None:
1113                 self.args, self.retann = result
1114         sig = super().format_signature(**kwargs)  # type: ignore
1115         if self._signatures:
1116             return "\n".join([sig] + self._signatures)
1117         else:
1118             return sig
1119

1140     """

1143     objtype = 'function'

1147     def can_document_member(cls, member: Any, membername: str, isattr: bool, parent: Any
1148                             ) -> bool:
1149         # supports functions, builtins and bound methods exported at the module level
1150         return (inspect.isfunction(member) or inspect.isbuiltin(member) or
1151                 (inspect.isroutine(member) and isinstance(parent, ModuleDocumenter)))

1153     def format_args(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1154         if self.env.config.autodoc_typehints in ('none', 'description'):
1155             kwargs.setdefault('show_annotation', False)
1156 
1157         try:
1158             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', self.object, False)
1159             sig = inspect.signature(self.object, follow_wrapped=True)
1160             args = stringify_signature(sig, **kwargs)
1161         except TypeError as exc:
1162             logger.warning(__("Failed to get a function signature for %s: %s"),
1163                            self.fullname, exc)
1164             return None
1165         except ValueError:
1166             args = ''
1167 
1168         if self.env.config.strip_signature_backslash:
1169             # escape backslashes for reST
1170             args = args.replace('\\', '\\\\')
1171         return args

1174         pass
