1176     def add_directive_header(self, sig: str) -> None:
1177         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
1178         super().add_directive_header(sig)
1179 
1180         if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(self.object):
1181             self.add_line('   :async:', sourcename)
1182 
1183     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1184         sigs = []
1185         if self.analyzer and '.'.join(self.objpath) in self.analyzer.overloads:
1186             # Use signatures for overloaded functions instead of the implementation function.
1187             overloaded = True
1188         else:
1189             overloaded = False
1190             sig = super().format_signature(**kwargs)
1191             sigs.append(sig)
1192 
1193         if inspect.is_singledispatch_function(self.object):
1194             # append signature of singledispatch'ed functions
1195             for typ, func in self.object.registry.items():
1196                 if typ is object:
1197                     pass  # default implementation. skipped.
1198                 else:
1199                     self.annotate_to_first_argument(func, typ)
1200 
1201                     documenter = FunctionDocumenter(self.directive, '')
1202                     documenter.object = func
1203                     documenter.objpath = [None]
1204                     sigs.append(documenter.format_signature())
1205         if overloaded:
1206             __globals__ = safe_getattr(self.object, '__globals__', {})
1207             for overload in self.analyzer.overloads.get('.'.join(self.objpath)):
1208                 overload = evaluate_signature(overload, __globals__)
1209                 sig = stringify_signature(overload, **kwargs)
1210                 sigs.append(sig)
1211 
1212         return "\n".join(sigs)
1213 
1214     def annotate_to_first_argument(self, func: Callable, typ: Type) -> None:
1215         """Annotate type hint to the first argument of function if needed."""
1216         try:
1217             sig = inspect.signature(func)
1218         except TypeError as exc:
1219             logger.warning(__("Failed to get a function signature for %s: %s"),
1220                            self.fullname, exc)
1221             return
1222         except ValueError:
1223             return
1224 
1225         if len(sig.parameters) == 0:
1226             return
1227 
1228         params = list(sig.parameters.values())
1229         if params[0].annotation is Parameter.empty:
1230             params[0] = params[0].replace(annotation=typ)
1231             try:
1232                 func.__signature__ = sig.replace(parameters=params)  # type: ignore
1233             except TypeError:
1234                 # failed to update signature (ex. built-in or extension types)
1235                 return

1303                 self.doc_as_attr = (self.objpath[-1] != self.object.__name__)
1304             else:
1305                 self.doc_as_attr = True
1306         return ret
1307 
1308     def _get_signature(self) -> Tuple[Optional[Any], Optional[str], Optional[Signature]]:
1309         def get_user_defined_function_or_method(obj: Any, attr: str) -> Any:
1310             """ Get the `attr` function or method from `obj`, if it is user-defined. """
1311             if inspect.is_builtin_class_method(obj, attr):
1312                 return None
1313             attr = self.get_attr(obj, attr, None)
1314             if not (inspect.ismethod(attr) or inspect.isfunction(attr)):
1315                 return None
1316             return attr
1317 
1318         # This sequence is copied from inspect._signature_from_callable.
1319         # ValueError means that no signature could be found, so we keep going.
1320 
1321         # First, let's see if it has an overloaded __call__ defined
1322         # in its metaclass
1323         call = get_user_defined_function_or_method(type(self.object), '__call__')
1324 
1325         if call is not None:
1326             if "{0.__module__}.{0.__qualname__}".format(call) in _METACLASS_CALL_BLACKLIST:
1327                 call = None
1328 
1329         if call is not None:
1330             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', call, True)
1331             try:
1332                 sig = inspect.signature(call, bound_method=True)
1333                 return type(self.object), '__call__', sig
1334             except ValueError:
1335                 pass
1336 
1337         # Now we check if the 'obj' class has a '__new__' method
1338         new = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__new__')
1339         if new is not None:
1340             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', new, True)
1341             try:
1342                 sig = inspect.signature(new, bound_method=True)
1343                 return self.object, '__new__', sig
1344             except ValueError:
1345                 pass
1346 
1347         # Finally, we should have at least __init__ implemented
1348         init = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__init__')
1349         if init is not None:
1350             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', init, True)
1351             try:
1352                 sig = inspect.signature(init, bound_method=True)
1353                 return self.object, '__init__', sig
1354             except ValueError:
1355                 pass
1356 
1357         # None of the attributes are user-defined, so fall back to let inspect
1358         # handle it.
1359         # We don't know the exact method that inspect.signature will read
1360         # the signature from, so just pass the object itself to our hook.
1361         self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', self.object, False)
1362         try:
1363             sig = inspect.signature(self.object, bound_method=False)
1364             return None, None, sig
1365         except ValueError:
1366             pass
1367 
1368         # Still no signature: happens e.g. for old-style classes
1369         # with __init__ in C and no `__text_signature__`.
1370         return None, None, None
1371 
1372     def format_args(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1373         if self.env.config.autodoc_typehints in ('none', 'description'):
1374             kwargs.setdefault('show_annotation', False)
1375 
1376         try:
1377             self._signature_class, self._signature_method_name, sig = self._get_signature()
1378         except TypeError as exc:
1379             # __signature__ attribute contained junk
1380             logger.warning(__("Failed to get a constructor signature for %s: %s"),
1381                            self.fullname, exc)
1382             return None
1383 
1384         if sig is None:
1385             return None
1386 
1387         return stringify_signature(sig, show_return_annotation=False, **kwargs)
1388 
1389     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1390         if self.doc_as_attr:
1391             return ''
1392 
1393         sig = super().format_signature()
1394 
1395         overloaded = False
1396         qualname = None
1397         # TODO: recreate analyzer for the module of class (To be clear, owner of the method)
1398         if self._signature_class and self._signature_method_name and self.analyzer:
1399             qualname = '.'.join([self._signature_class.__qualname__,
1400                                  self._signature_method_name])
1401             if qualname in self.analyzer.overloads:
1402                 overloaded = True
1403 
1404         sigs = []
1405         if overloaded:
1406             # Use signatures for overloaded methods instead of the implementation method.
1407             method = safe_getattr(self._signature_class, self._signature_method_name, None)
1408             __globals__ = safe_getattr(method, '__globals__', {})
1409             for overload in self.analyzer.overloads.get(qualname):
1410                 overload = evaluate_signature(overload, __globals__)
1411 
1412                 parameters = list(overload.parameters.values())
1413                 overload = overload.replace(parameters=parameters[1:],
1414                                             return_annotation=Parameter.empty)
1415                 sig = stringify_signature(overload, **kwargs)
1416                 sigs.append(sig)
1417         else:
1418             sigs.append(sig)
1419 
1420         return "\n".join(sigs)

1422     def add_directive_header(self, sig: str) -> None:
1423         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
1424 
1425         if self.doc_as_attr:

1427         super().add_directive_header(sig)
1428 
1429         if self.analyzer and '.'.join(self.objpath) in self.analyzer.finals:
1430             self.add_line('   :final:', sourcename)
1431 
1432         # add inheritance info, if wanted
1433         if not self.doc_as_attr and self.options.show_inheritance:
1434             sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
1435             self.add_line('', sourcename)
1436             if hasattr(self.object, '__bases__') and len(self.object.__bases__):
1437                 bases = [':class:`%s`' % b.__name__
1438                          if b.__module__ in ('__builtin__', 'builtins')
1439                          else ':class:`%s.%s`' % (b.__module__, b.__qualname__)
1440                          for b in self.object.__bases__]

1444     def get_doc(self, encoding: str = None, ignore: int = None) -> List[List[str]]:
1445         if encoding is not None:
1446             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
1447                           % self.__class__.__name__,
1448                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
1449         lines = getattr(self, '_new_docstrings', None)
1450         if lines is not None:
1451             return lines
1452 
1453         content = self.env.config.autoclass_content
1454 
1455         docstrings = []
1456         attrdocstring = self.get_attr(self.object, '__doc__', None)
1457         if attrdocstring:
1458             docstrings.append(attrdocstring)
1459 
1460         # for classes, what the "docstring" is can be controlled via a
1461         # config value; the default is only the class docstring
1462         if content in ('both', 'init'):
1463             __init__ = self.get_attr(self.object, '__init__', None)
1464             initdocstring = getdoc(__init__, self.get_attr,
1465                                    self.env.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
1466                                    self.parent, self.object_name)
1467             # for new-style classes, no __init__ means default __init__
1468             if (initdocstring is not None and
1469                 (initdocstring == object.__init__.__doc__ or  # for pypy
1470                  initdocstring.strip() == object.__init__.__doc__)):  # for !pypy
1471                 initdocstring = None
1472             if not initdocstring:
1473                 # try __new__
1474                 __new__ = self.get_attr(self.object, '__new__', None)
1475                 initdocstring = getdoc(__new__, self.get_attr,
1476                                        self.env.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
1477                                        self.parent, self.object_name)
1478                 # for new-style classes, no __new__ means default __new__
1479                 if (initdocstring is not None and
1480                     (initdocstring == object.__new__.__doc__ or  # for pypy
1481                      initdocstring.strip() == object.__new__.__doc__)):  # for !pypy
1482                     initdocstring = None
1483             if initdocstring:
1484                 if content == 'init':
1485                     docstrings = [initdocstring]
1486                 else:
1487                     docstrings.append(initdocstring)
1488 
1489         tab_width = self.directive.state.document.settings.tab_width
1490         return [prepare_docstring(docstring, ignore, tab_width) for docstring in docstrings]

1492     def add_content(self, more_content: Any, no_docstring: bool = False) -> None:

1728     def format_args(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1729         if self.env.config.autodoc_typehints in ('none', 'description'):

1733             if self.object == object.__init__ and self.parent != object:
1734                 # Classes not having own __init__() method are shown as no arguments.
1735                 #
1736                 # Note: The signature of object.__init__() is (self, /, *args, **kwargs).
1737                 #       But it makes users confused.

1741                     self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', self.object, False)

1743                 else:
1744                     self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', self.object, True)
1745                     sig = inspect.signature(self.object, bound_method=True,
1746                                             follow_wrapped=True)
1747                 args = stringify_signature(sig, **kwargs)
1748         except TypeError as exc:
1749             logger.warning(__("Failed to get a method signature for %s: %s"),
1750                            self.fullname, exc)
1751             return None
1752         except ValueError:
1753             args = ''
1754 
1755         if self.env.config.strip_signature_backslash:

1762 
1763         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
1764         obj = self.parent.__dict__.get(self.object_name, self.object)
1765         if inspect.isabstractmethod(obj):
1766             self.add_line('   :abstractmethod:', sourcename)
1767         if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(obj):
1768             self.add_line('   :async:', sourcename)
1769         if inspect.isclassmethod(obj):
1770             self.add_line('   :classmethod:', sourcename)
1771         if inspect.isstaticmethod(obj, cls=self.parent, name=self.object_name):
1772             self.add_line('   :staticmethod:', sourcename)
1773         if self.analyzer and '.'.join(self.objpath) in self.analyzer.finals:
1774             self.add_line('   :final:', sourcename)

1777         pass

1779     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1780         sigs = []
1781         if self.analyzer and '.'.join(self.objpath) in self.analyzer.overloads:
1782             # Use signatures for overloaded methods instead of the implementation method.
1783             overloaded = True
1784         else:
1785             overloaded = False
1786             sig = super().format_signature(**kwargs)
1787             sigs.append(sig)
1788 
1789         meth = self.parent.__dict__.get(self.objpath[-1])
1790         if inspect.is_singledispatch_method(meth):
1791             # append signature of singledispatch'ed functions
1792             for typ, func in meth.dispatcher.registry.items():
1793                 if typ is object:
1794                     pass  # default implementation. skipped.
1795                 else:
1796                     self.annotate_to_first_argument(func, typ)
1797 
1798                     documenter = MethodDocumenter(self.directive, '')
1799                     documenter.parent = self.parent
1800                     documenter.object = func
1801                     documenter.objpath = [None]
1802                     sigs.append(documenter.format_signature())
1803         if overloaded:
1804             __globals__ = safe_getattr(self.object, '__globals__', {})
1805             for overload in self.analyzer.overloads.get('.'.join(self.objpath)):
1806                 overload = evaluate_signature(overload, __globals__)
1807                 if not inspect.isstaticmethod(self.object, cls=self.parent,
1808                                               name=self.object_name):
1809                     parameters = list(overload.parameters.values())
1810                     overload = overload.replace(parameters=parameters[1:])
1811                 sig = stringify_signature(overload, **kwargs)
1812                 sigs.append(sig)
1813 
1814         return "\n".join(sigs)

1816     def annotate_to_first_argument(self, func: Callable, typ: Type) -> None:
1817         """Annotate type hint to the first argument of function if needed."""
1818         try:
1819             sig = inspect.signature(func)
1820         except TypeError as exc:
1821             logger.warning(__("Failed to get a method signature for %s: %s"),
1822                            self.fullname, exc)
1823             return
1824         except ValueError:
1825             return
1826         if len(sig.parameters) == 1:
1827             return
1828 
1829         params = list(sig.parameters.values())
1830         if params[1].annotation is Parameter.empty:
1831             params[1] = params[1].replace(annotation=typ)
1832             try:
1833                 func.__signature__ = sig.replace(parameters=params)  # type: ignore
1834             except TypeError:
1835                 # failed to update signature (ex. built-in or extension types)
1836                 return

128 class Sphinx:
129     """The main application class and extensibility interface.
130 
131     :ivar srcdir: Directory containing source.
132     :ivar confdir: Directory containing ``conf.py``.
133     :ivar doctreedir: Directory for storing pickled doctrees.
134     :ivar outdir: Directory for storing build documents.
135     """
136 
137     def __init__(self, srcdir: str, confdir: str, outdir: str, doctreedir: str,
138                  buildername: str, confoverrides: Dict = None,
139                  status: IO = sys.stdout, warning: IO = sys.stderr,
140                  freshenv: bool = False, warningiserror: bool = False, tags: List[str] = None,
141                  verbosity: int = 0, parallel: int = 0, keep_going: bool = False) -> None:
142         self.phase = BuildPhase.INITIALIZATION
143         self.verbosity = verbosity
144         self.extensions = {}                    # type: Dict[str, Extension]
145         self.builder = None                     # type: Builder
146         self.env = None                         # type: BuildEnvironment
147         self.project = None                     # type: Project
148         self.registry = SphinxComponentRegistry()
149         self.html_themes = {}                   # type: Dict[str, str]
150 
151         # validate provided directories
152         self.srcdir = abspath(srcdir)
153         self.outdir = abspath(outdir)
154         self.doctreedir = abspath(doctreedir)
155         self.confdir = confdir
156         if self.confdir:  # confdir is optional
157             self.confdir = abspath(self.confdir)
158             if not path.isfile(path.join(self.confdir, 'conf.py')):
159                 raise ApplicationError(__("config directory doesn't contain a "
160                                           "conf.py file (%s)") % confdir)
161 
162         if not path.isdir(self.srcdir):
163             raise ApplicationError(__('Cannot find source directory (%s)') %
164                                    self.srcdir)
165 
166         if path.exists(self.outdir) and not path.isdir(self.outdir):
167             raise ApplicationError(__('Output directory (%s) is not a directory') %
168                                    self.outdir)
169 
170         if self.srcdir == self.outdir:
171             raise ApplicationError(__('Source directory and destination '
172                                       'directory cannot be identical'))
173 
174         self.parallel = parallel
175 
176         if status is None:
177             self._status = StringIO()      # type: IO
178             self.quiet = True
179         else:
180             self._status = status
181             self.quiet = False
182 
183         if warning is None:
184             self._warning = StringIO()     # type: IO
185         else:
186             self._warning = warning
187         self._warncount = 0
188         self.keep_going = warningiserror and keep_going
189         if self.keep_going:
190             self.warningiserror = False
191         else:
192             self.warningiserror = warningiserror
193         logging.setup(self, self._status, self._warning)
194 
195         self.events = EventManager(self)
196 
197         # keep last few messages for traceback
198         # This will be filled by sphinx.util.logging.LastMessagesWriter
199         self.messagelog = deque(maxlen=10)  # type: deque
200 
201         # say hello to the world
202         logger.info(bold(__('Running Sphinx v%s') % sphinx.__display_version__))
203 
204         # notice for parallel build on macOS and py38+
205         if sys.version_info > (3, 8) and platform.system() == 'Darwin' and parallel > 1:
206             logger.info(bold(__("For security reason, parallel mode is disabled on macOS and "
207                                 "python3.8 and above. For more details, please read "
208                                 "https://github.com/sphinx-doc/sphinx/issues/6803")))
209 
210         # status code for command-line application
211         self.statuscode = 0
212 
213         # read config
214         self.tags = Tags(tags)
215         if self.confdir is None:
216             self.config = Config({}, confoverrides or {})
217         else:
218             self.config = Config.read(self.confdir, confoverrides or {}, self.tags)
219 
220         # initialize some limited config variables before initialize i18n and loading
221         # extensions
222         self.config.pre_init_values()
223 
224         # set up translation infrastructure
225         self._init_i18n()
226 
227         # check the Sphinx version if requested
228         if self.config.needs_sphinx and self.config.needs_sphinx > sphinx.__display_version__:
229             raise VersionRequirementError(
230                 __('This project needs at least Sphinx v%s and therefore cannot '
231                    'be built with this version.') % self.config.needs_sphinx)
232 
233         # set confdir to srcdir if -C given (!= no confdir); a few pieces
234         # of code expect a confdir to be set
235         if self.confdir is None:
236             self.confdir = self.srcdir
237 
238         # load all built-in extension modules
239         for extension in builtin_extensions:
240             self.setup_extension(extension)
241 
242         # load all user-given extension modules
243         for extension in self.config.extensions:
244             self.setup_extension(extension)
245 
246         # preload builder module (before init config values)
247         self.preload_builder(buildername)
248 
249         if not path.isdir(outdir):
250             with progress_message(__('making output directory')):
251                 ensuredir(outdir)
252 
253         # the config file itself can be an extension
254         if self.config.setup:
255             prefix = __('while setting up extension %s:') % "conf.py"
256             with prefixed_warnings(prefix):
257                 if callable(self.config.setup):
258                     self.config.setup(self)
259                 else:
260                     raise ConfigError(
261                         __("'setup' as currently defined in conf.py isn't a Python callable. "
262                            "Please modify its definition to make it a callable function. "
263                            "This is needed for conf.py to behave as a Sphinx extension.")
264                     )
265 
266         # now that we know all config values, collect them from conf.py
267         self.config.init_values()
268         self.events.emit('config-inited', self.config)
269 
270         # create the project
271         self.project = Project(self.srcdir, self.config.source_suffix)
272         # create the builder
273         self.builder = self.create_builder(buildername)
274         # set up the build environment
275         self._init_env(freshenv)
276         # set up the builder
277         self._init_builder()
278 
279     def _init_i18n(self) -> None:
280         """Load translated strings from the configured localedirs if enabled in
281         the configuration.
282         """
283         if self.config.language is None:
284             self.translator, has_translation = locale.init([], None)
285         else:
286             logger.info(bold(__('loading translations [%s]... ') % self.config.language),
287                         nonl=True)
288 
289             # compile mo files if sphinx.po file in user locale directories are updated
290             repo = CatalogRepository(self.srcdir, self.config.locale_dirs,
291                                      self.config.language, self.config.source_encoding)
292             for catalog in repo.catalogs:
293                 if catalog.domain == 'sphinx' and catalog.is_outdated():
294                     catalog.write_mo(self.config.language)
295 
296             locale_dirs = [None, path.join(package_dir, 'locale')] + list(repo.locale_dirs)
297             self.translator, has_translation = locale.init(locale_dirs, self.config.language)
298             if has_translation or self.config.language == 'en':
299                 # "en" never needs to be translated
300                 logger.info(__('done'))
301             else:
302                 logger.info(__('not available for built-in messages'))
303 
304     def _init_env(self, freshenv: bool) -> None:
305         filename = path.join(self.doctreedir, ENV_PICKLE_FILENAME)
306         if freshenv or not os.path.exists(filename):
307             self.env = BuildEnvironment()
308             self.env.setup(self)
309             self.env.find_files(self.config, self.builder)
310         else:
311             try:
312                 with progress_message(__('loading pickled environment')):
313                     with open(filename, 'rb') as f:
314                         self.env = pickle.load(f)
315                         self.env.setup(self)
316             except Exception as err:
317                 logger.info(__('failed: %s'), err)
318                 self._init_env(freshenv=True)
319 
320     def preload_builder(self, name: str) -> None:
321         self.registry.preload_builder(self, name)
322 
323     def create_builder(self, name: str) -> "Builder":
324         if name is None:
325             logger.info(__('No builder selected, using default: html'))
326             name = 'html'
327 
328         return self.registry.create_builder(self, name)
329 
330     def _init_builder(self) -> None:
331         self.builder.set_environment(self.env)
332         self.builder.init()
333         self.events.emit('builder-inited')

335     # ---- main "build" method -------------------------------------------------
336 
337     def build(self, force_all: bool = False, filenames: List[str] = None) -> None:
338         self.phase = BuildPhase.READING
339         try:
340             if force_all:
341                 self.builder.compile_all_catalogs()
342                 self.builder.build_all()
343             elif filenames:
344                 self.builder.compile_specific_catalogs(filenames)
345                 self.builder.build_specific(filenames)
346             else:
347                 self.builder.compile_update_catalogs()
348                 self.builder.build_update()
349 
350             if self._warncount and self.keep_going:
351                 self.statuscode = 1
352 
353             status = (__('succeeded') if self.statuscode == 0
354                       else __('finished with problems'))
355             if self._warncount:
356                 if self.warningiserror:
357                     if self._warncount == 1:
358                         msg = __('build %s, %s warning (with warnings treated as errors).')
359                     else:
360                         msg = __('build %s, %s warnings (with warnings treated as errors).')
361                 else:
362                     if self._warncount == 1:
363                         msg = __('build %s, %s warning.')
364                     else:
365                         msg = __('build %s, %s warnings.')
366 
367                 logger.info(bold(msg % (status, self._warncount)))
368             else:
369                 logger.info(bold(__('build %s.') % status))
370 
371             if self.statuscode == 0 and self.builder.epilog:
372                 logger.info('')
373                 logger.info(self.builder.epilog % {
374                     'outdir': relpath(self.outdir),
375                     'project': self.config.project
376                 })
377         except Exception as err:
378             # delete the saved env to force a fresh build next time
379             envfile = path.join(self.doctreedir, ENV_PICKLE_FILENAME)
380             if path.isfile(envfile):
381                 os.unlink(envfile)
382             self.events.emit('build-finished', err)
383             raise
384         else:
385             self.events.emit('build-finished', None)
386         self.builder.cleanup()

412     # event interface
413     def connect(self, event: str, callback: Callable, priority: int = 500) -> int:
414         """Register *callback* to be called when *event* is emitted.
415 
416         For details on available core events and the arguments of callback
417         functions, please see :ref:`events`.
418 
419         Registered callbacks will be invoked on event in the order of *priority* and
420         registration.  The priority is ascending order.
421 
422         The method returns a "listener ID" that can be used as an argument to
423         :meth:`disconnect`.
424 
425         .. versionchanged:: 3.0
426 
427            Support *priority*
428         """
429         listener_id = self.events.connect(event, callback, priority)
430         logger.debug('[app] connecting event %r (%d): %r [id=%s]',
431                      event, priority, callback, listener_id)
432         return listener_id
433 
434     def disconnect(self, listener_id: int) -> None:
435         """Unregister callback by *listener_id*."""
436         logger.debug('[app] disconnecting event: [id=%s]', listener_id)
437         self.events.disconnect(listener_id)
438 
439     def emit(self, event: str, *args: Any,
440              allowed_exceptions: Tuple["Type[Exception]", ...] = ()) -> List:
441         """Emit *event* and pass *arguments* to the callback functions.
442 
443         Return the return values of all callbacks as a list.  Do not emit core
444         Sphinx events in extensions!
445 
446         .. versionchanged:: 3.1
447 
448            Added *allowed_exceptions* to specify path-through exceptions
449         """
450         return self.events.emit(event, *args, allowed_exceptions=allowed_exceptions)
451 
452     def emit_firstresult(self, event: str, *args: Any,
453                          allowed_exceptions: Tuple["Type[Exception]", ...] = ()) -> Any:
454         """Emit *event* and pass *arguments* to the callback functions.
455 
456         Return the result of the first callback that doesn't return ``None``.
457 
458         .. versionadded:: 0.5
459         .. versionchanged:: 3.1
460 
461            Added *allowed_exceptions* to specify path-through exceptions
462         """
463         return self.events.emit_firstresult(event, *args,
464                                             allowed_exceptions=allowed_exceptions)

479     # TODO(stephenfin): Describe 'types' parameter
480     def add_config_value(self, name: str, default: Any, rebuild: Union[bool, str],
481                          types: Any = ()) -> None:
482         """Register a configuration value.
483 
484         This is necessary for Sphinx to recognize new values and set default
485         values accordingly.  The *name* should be prefixed with the extension
486         name, to avoid clashes.  The *default* value can be any Python object.
487         The string value *rebuild* must be one of those values:
488 
489         * ``'env'`` if a change in the setting only takes effect when a
490           document is parsed -- this means that the whole environment must be
491           rebuilt.
492         * ``'html'`` if a change in the setting needs a full rebuild of HTML
493           documents.
494         * ``''`` if a change in the setting will not need any special rebuild.
495 
496         .. versionchanged:: 0.6
497            Changed *rebuild* from a simple boolean (equivalent to ``''`` or
498            ``'env'``) to a string.  However, booleans are still accepted and
499            converted internally.
500 
501         .. versionchanged:: 0.4
502            If the *default* value is a callable, it will be called with the
503            config object as its argument in order to get the default value.
504            This can be used to implement config values whose default depends on
505            other values.
506         """
507         logger.debug('[app] adding config value: %r',
508                      (name, default, rebuild) + ((types,) if types else ()))
509         if rebuild in (False, True):
510             rebuild = 'env' if rebuild else ''
511         self.config.add(name, default, rebuild, types)

535     def add_node(self, node: "Type[Element]", override: bool = False,
536                  **kwargs: Tuple[Callable, Callable]) -> None:
537         """Register a Docutils node class.
538 
539         This is necessary for Docutils internals.  It may also be used in the
540         future to validate nodes in the parsed documents.
541 
542         Node visitor functions for the Sphinx HTML, LaTeX, text and manpage
543         writers can be given as keyword arguments: the keyword should be one or
544         more of ``'html'``, ``'latex'``, ``'text'``, ``'man'``, ``'texinfo'``
545         or any other supported translators, the value a 2-tuple of ``(visit,
546         depart)`` methods.  ``depart`` can be ``None`` if the ``visit``
547         function raises :exc:`docutils.nodes.SkipNode`.  Example:
548 
549         .. code-block:: python
550 
551            class math(docutils.nodes.Element): pass
552 
553            def visit_math_html(self, node):
554                self.body.append(self.starttag(node, 'math'))
555            def depart_math_html(self, node):
556                self.body.append('</math>')
557 
558            app.add_node(math, html=(visit_math_html, depart_math_html))
559 
560         Obviously, translators for which you don't specify visitor methods will
561         choke on the node when encountered in a document to translate.
562 
563         .. versionchanged:: 0.5
564            Added the support for keyword arguments giving visit functions.
565         """
566         logger.debug('[app] adding node: %r', (node, kwargs))
567         if not override and docutils.is_node_registered(node):
568             logger.warning(__('node class %r is already registered, '
569                               'its visitors will be overridden'),
570                            node.__name__, type='app', subtype='add_node')
571         docutils.register_node(node)
572         self.registry.add_translation_handlers(node, **kwargs)
573 
574     def add_enumerable_node(self, node: "Type[Element]", figtype: str,
575                             title_getter: TitleGetter = None, override: bool = False,
576                             **kwargs: Tuple[Callable, Callable]) -> None:
577         """Register a Docutils node class as a numfig target.
578 
579         Sphinx numbers the node automatically. And then the users can refer it
580         using :rst:role:`numref`.
581 
582         *figtype* is a type of enumerable nodes.  Each figtypes have individual
583         numbering sequences.  As a system figtypes, ``figure``, ``table`` and
584         ``code-block`` are defined.  It is able to add custom nodes to these
585         default figtypes.  It is also able to define new custom figtype if new
586         figtype is given.
587 
588         *title_getter* is a getter function to obtain the title of node.  It
589         takes an instance of the enumerable node, and it must return its title
590         as string.  The title is used to the default title of references for
591         :rst:role:`ref`.  By default, Sphinx searches
592         ``docutils.nodes.caption`` or ``docutils.nodes.title`` from the node as
593         a title.
594 
595         Other keyword arguments are used for node visitor functions. See the
596         :meth:`.Sphinx.add_node` for details.
597 
598         .. versionadded:: 1.4
599         """
600         self.registry.add_enumerable_node(node, figtype, title_getter, override=override)
601         self.add_node(node, override=override, **kwargs)

603     def add_directive(self, name: str, cls: "Type[Directive]", override: bool = False) -> None:
604         """Register a Docutils directive.
605 
606         *name* must be the prospective directive name.  *cls* is a directive
607         class which inherits ``docutils.parsers.rst.Directive``.  For more
608         details, see `the Docutils docs
609         <http://docutils.sourceforge.net/docs/howto/rst-directives.html>`_ .
610 
611         For example, the (already existing) :rst:dir:`literalinclude` directive
612         would be added like this:
613 
614         .. code-block:: python
615 
616            from docutils.parsers.rst import Directive, directives
617 
618            class LiteralIncludeDirective(Directive):
619                has_content = True
620                required_arguments = 1
621                optional_arguments = 0
622                final_argument_whitespace = True
623                option_spec = {
624                    'class': directives.class_option,
625                    'name': directives.unchanged,
626                }
627 
628                def run(self):
629                    ...
630 
631            add_directive('literalinclude', LiteralIncludeDirective)
632 
633         .. versionchanged:: 0.6
634            Docutils 0.5-style directive classes are now supported.
635         .. deprecated:: 1.8
636            Docutils 0.4-style (function based) directives support is deprecated.
637         .. versionchanged:: 1.8
638            Add *override* keyword.
639         """
640         logger.debug('[app] adding directive: %r', (name, cls))
641         if not override and docutils.is_directive_registered(name):
642             logger.warning(__('directive %r is already registered, it will be overridden'),
643                            name, type='app', subtype='add_directive')
644 
645         docutils.register_directive(name, cls)

1137         """Check parallel processing is allowed or not.
1138 
1139         ``typ`` is a type of processing; ``'read'`` or ``'write'``.
1140         """
1141         if typ == 'read':
1142             attrname = 'parallel_read_safe'
1143             message_not_declared = __("the %s extension does not declare if it "
1144                                       "is safe for parallel reading, assuming "
1145                                       "it isn't - please ask the extension author "
1146                                       "to check and make it explicit")
1147             message_not_safe = __("the %s extension is not safe for parallel reading")
1148         elif typ == 'write':
1149             attrname = 'parallel_write_safe'
1150             message_not_declared = __("the %s extension does not declare if it "
1151                                       "is safe for parallel writing, assuming "
1152                                       "it isn't - please ask the extension author "
1153                                       "to check and make it explicit")
1154             message_not_safe = __("the %s extension is not safe for parallel writing")
1155         else:
1156             raise ValueError('parallel type %s is not supported' % typ)
1157 
1158         for ext in self.extensions.values():
1159             allowed = getattr(ext, attrname, None)
1160             if allowed is None:
1161                 logger.warning(message_not_declared, ext.name)
1162                 logger.warning(__('doing serial %s'), typ)
1163                 return False
1164             elif not allowed:
1165                 logger.warning(message_not_safe, ext.name)
1166                 logger.warning(__('doing serial %s'), typ)
1167                 return False
1168 
1169         return True

109 def init(locale_dirs: List[str], language: str,
110          catalog: str = 'sphinx', namespace: str = 'general') -> Tuple[NullTranslations, bool]:
111     """Look for message catalogs in `locale_dirs` and *ensure* that there is at
112     least a NullTranslations catalog set in `translators`. If called multiple
113     times or if several ``.mo`` files are found, their contents are merged
114     together (thus making ``init`` reentrant).
115     """
116     global translators
117     translator = translators.get((namespace, catalog))
118     # ignore previously failed attempts to find message catalogs
119     if translator.__class__ is NullTranslations:
120         translator = None
121     # the None entry is the system's default locale path
122     has_translation = True
123 
124     if language and '_' in language:
125         # for language having country code (like "de_AT")
126         languages = [language, language.split('_')[0]]
127     else:
128         languages = [language]
129 
130     # loading
131     for dir_ in locale_dirs:
132         try:
133             trans = gettext.translation(catalog, localedir=dir_, languages=languages)
134             if translator is None:
135                 translator = trans
136             else:
137                 translator.add_fallback(trans)
138         except Exception:
139             # Language couldn't be found in the specified path
140             pass
141     # guarantee translators[(namespace, catalog)] exists
142     if translator is None:
143         translator = NullTranslations()
144         has_translation = False
145     translators[(namespace, catalog)] = translator
146     return translator, has_translation

185 def cut_lines(pre: int, post: int = 0, what: str = None) -> Callable:
186     """Return a listener that removes the first *pre* and last *post*
187     lines of every docstring.  If *what* is a sequence of strings,
188     only docstrings of a type in *what* will be processed.
189 
190     Use like this (e.g. in the ``setup()`` function of :file:`conf.py`)::
191 
192        from sphinx.ext.autodoc import cut_lines
193        app.connect('autodoc-process-docstring', cut_lines(4, what=['module']))
194 
195     This can (and should) be used in place of :confval:`automodule_skip_lines`.
196     """
197     def process(app: Sphinx, what_: str, name: str, obj: Any, options: Any, lines: List[str]
198                 ) -> None:
199         if what and what_ not in what:
200             return
201         del lines[:pre]
202         if post:
203             # remove one trailing blank line.
204             if lines and not lines[-1]:
205                 lines.pop(-1)
206             del lines[-post:]
207         # make sure there is a blank line at the end
208         if lines and lines[-1]:
209             lines.append('')
210     return process
211

213 def between(marker: str, what: Sequence[str] = None, keepempty: bool = False,
214             exclude: bool = False) -> Callable:
215     """Return a listener that either keeps, or if *exclude* is True excludes,
216     lines between lines that match the *marker* regular expression.  If no line
217     matches, the resulting docstring would be empty, so no change will be made
218     unless *keepempty* is true.
219 
220     If *what* is a sequence of strings, only docstrings of a type in *what* will
221     be processed.
222     """
223     marker_re = re.compile(marker)
224 
225     def process(app: Sphinx, what_: str, name: str, obj: Any, options: Any, lines: List[str]
226                 ) -> None:
227         if what and what_ not in what:
228             return
229         deleted = 0
230         delete = not exclude
231         orig_lines = lines[:]
232         for i, line in enumerate(orig_lines):
233             if delete:
234                 lines.pop(i - deleted)
235                 deleted += 1
236             if marker_re.match(line):
237                 delete = not delete
238                 if delete:
239                     lines.pop(i - deleted)
240                     deleted += 1
241         if not lines and not keepempty:
242             lines[:] = orig_lines
243         # make sure there is a blank line at the end
244         if lines and lines[-1]:
245             lines.append('')
246     return process

365     def resolve_name(self, modname: str, parents: Any, path: str, base: Any
366                      ) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
367         """Resolve the module and name of the object to document given by the
368         arguments and the current module/class.

370         Must return a pair of the module name and a chain of attributes; for
371         example, it would return ``('zipfile', ['ZipFile', 'open'])`` for the

376     def parse_name(self) -> bool:
377         """Determine what module to import and what attribute to document.
378 
379         Returns True and sets *self.modname*, *self.objpath*, *self.fullname*,
380         *self.args* and *self.retann* if parsing and resolving was successful.
381         """
382         # first, parse the definition -- auto directives for classes and
383         # functions can contain a signature which is then used instead of
384         # an autogenerated one
385         try:
386             explicit_modname, path, base, args, retann = \
387                 py_ext_sig_re.match(self.name).groups()
388         except AttributeError:
389             logger.warning(__('invalid signature for auto%s (%r)') % (self.objtype, self.name),
390                            type='autodoc')
391             return False
392 
393         # support explicit module and class name separation via ::
394         if explicit_modname is not None:
395             modname = explicit_modname[:-2]
396             parents = path.rstrip('.').split('.') if path else []
397         else:
398             modname = None
399             parents = []
400 
401         with mock(self.config.autodoc_mock_imports):
402             self.modname, self.objpath = self.resolve_name(modname, parents, path, base)
403 
404         if not self.modname:
405             return False
406 
407         self.args = args
408         self.retann = retann
409         self.fullname = (self.modname or '') + \
410                         ('.' + '.'.join(self.objpath) if self.objpath else '')
411         return True

484     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
485         """Format the signature (arguments and return annotation) of the object.
486 
487         Let the user process it via the ``autodoc-process-signature`` event.
488         """
489         if self.args is not None:
490             # signature given explicitly
491             args = "(%s)" % self.args
492             retann = self.retann
493         else:
494             # try to introspect the signature
495             try:
496                 retann = None
497                 args = self._call_format_args(**kwargs)
498                 if args:
499                     matched = re.match(r'^(\(.*\))\s+->\s+(.*)$', args)
500                     if matched:
501                         args = matched.group(1)
502                         retann = matched.group(2)
503             except Exception as exc:
504                 logger.warning(__('error while formatting arguments for %s: %s'),
505                                self.fullname, exc, type='autodoc')

508         result = self.env.events.emit_firstresult('autodoc-process-signature',
509                                                   self.objtype, self.fullname,
510                                                   self.object, self.options, args, retann)
511         if result:
512             args, retann = result
513 
514         if args is not None:
515             return args + ((' -> %s' % retann) if retann else '')

517             return ''

519     def add_directive_header(self, sig: str) -> None:

530                           sourcename)

662     def filter_members(self, members: ObjectMembers, want_all: bool
663                        ) -> List[Tuple[str, Any, bool]]:
664         """Filter the given member list.
665 
666         Members are skipped if
667 
668         - they are private (except if given explicitly or the private-members
669           option is set)
670         - they are special methods (except if given explicitly or the
671           special-members option is set)
672         - they are undocumented (except if the undoc-members option is set)
673 
674         The user can override the skipping decision by connecting to the
675         ``autodoc-skip-member`` event.
676         """
677         def is_filtered_inherited_member(name: str, obj: Any) -> bool:
678             if inspect.isclass(self.object):
679                 for cls in self.object.__mro__:
680                     if cls.__name__ == self.options.inherited_members and cls != self.object:
681                         # given member is a member of specified *super class*
682                         return True
683                     elif name in cls.__dict__:
684                         return False
685                     elif name in self.get_attr(cls, '__annotations__', {}):
686                         return False
687                     elif isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.class_ is cls:
688                         return False
689 
690             return False
691 
692         ret = []
693 
694         # search for members in source code too
695         namespace = '.'.join(self.objpath)  # will be empty for modules
696 
697         if self.analyzer:
698             attr_docs = self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
699         else:
700             attr_docs = {}
701 
702         # process members and determine which to skip
703         for obj in members:
704             membername, member = obj
705             # if isattr is True, the member is documented as an attribute
706             if member is INSTANCEATTR:
707                 isattr = True
708             else:
709                 isattr = False
710 
711             doc = getdoc(member, self.get_attr, self.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
712                          self.parent, self.object_name)
713             if not isinstance(doc, str):
714                 # Ignore non-string __doc__
715                 doc = None
716 
717             # if the member __doc__ is the same as self's __doc__, it's just
718             # inherited and therefore not the member's doc
719             cls = self.get_attr(member, '__class__', None)
720             if cls:
721                 cls_doc = self.get_attr(cls, '__doc__', None)
722                 if cls_doc == doc:
723                     doc = None
724 
725             if isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.docstring:
726                 # hack for ClassDocumenter to inject docstring via ObjectMember
727                 doc = obj.docstring
728 
729             has_doc = bool(doc)
730 
731             metadata = extract_metadata(doc)
732             if 'private' in metadata:
733                 # consider a member private if docstring has "private" metadata
734                 isprivate = True
735             elif 'public' in metadata:
736                 # consider a member public if docstring has "public" metadata
737                 isprivate = False
738             else:
739                 isprivate = membername.startswith('_')
740 
741             keep = False
742             if safe_getattr(member, '__sphinx_mock__', None) is not None:
743                 # mocked module or object
744                 pass
745             elif self.options.exclude_members and membername in self.options.exclude_members:
746                 # remove members given by exclude-members
747                 keep = False
748             elif want_all and special_member_re.match(membername):
749                 # special __methods__
750                 if self.options.special_members and membername in self.options.special_members:
751                     if membername == '__doc__':
752                         keep = False
753                     elif is_filtered_inherited_member(membername, obj):
754                         keep = False
755                     else:
756                         keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
757                 else:
758                     keep = False
759             elif (namespace, membername) in attr_docs:
760                 if want_all and isprivate:
761                     if self.options.private_members is None:
762                         keep = False
763                     else:
764                         keep = membername in self.options.private_members
765                 else:
766                     # keep documented attributes
767                     keep = True
768                 isattr = True
769             elif want_all and isprivate:
770                 if has_doc or self.options.undoc_members:
771                     if self.options.private_members is None:
772                         keep = False
773                     elif is_filtered_inherited_member(membername, obj):
774                         keep = False
775                     else:
776                         keep = membername in self.options.private_members
777                 else:
778                     keep = False
779             else:
780                 if (self.options.members is ALL and
781                         is_filtered_inherited_member(membername, obj)):
782                     keep = False
783                 else:
784                     # ignore undocumented members if :undoc-members: is not given
785                     keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
786 
787             if isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.skipped:
788                 # forcedly skipped member (ex. a module attribute not defined in __all__)
789                 keep = False
790 
791             # give the user a chance to decide whether this member
792             # should be skipped
793             if self.env.app:
794                 # let extensions preprocess docstrings
795                 try:
796                     skip_user = self.env.app.emit_firstresult(
797                         'autodoc-skip-member', self.objtype, membername, member,
798                         not keep, self.options)
799                     if skip_user is not None:
800                         keep = not skip_user
801                 except Exception as exc:
802                     logger.warning(__('autodoc: failed to determine %r to be documented, '
803                                       'the following exception was raised:\n%s'),
804                                    member, exc, type='autodoc')
805                     keep = False
806 
807             if keep:
808                 ret.append((membername, member, isattr))
809 
810         return ret
811 
812     def document_members(self, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
813         """Generate reST for member documentation.
814 
815         If *all_members* is True, do all members, else those given by
816         *self.options.members*.
817         """
818         # set current namespace for finding members
819         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = self.modname
820         if self.objpath:
821             self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = self.objpath[0]
822 
823         want_all = all_members or self.options.inherited_members or \
824             self.options.members is ALL
825         # find out which members are documentable
826         members_check_module, members = self.get_object_members(want_all)
827 
828         # document non-skipped members
829         memberdocumenters = []  # type: List[Tuple[Documenter, bool]]
830         for (mname, member, isattr) in self.filter_members(members, want_all):
831             classes = [cls for cls in self.documenters.values()
832                        if cls.can_document_member(member, mname, isattr, self)]
833             if not classes:
834                 # don't know how to document this member
835                 continue
836             # prefer the documenter with the highest priority
837             classes.sort(key=lambda cls: cls.priority)
838             # give explicitly separated module name, so that members
839             # of inner classes can be documented
840             full_mname = self.modname + '::' + \
841                 '.'.join(self.objpath + [mname])
842             documenter = classes[-1](self.directive, full_mname, self.indent)
843             memberdocumenters.append((documenter, isattr))
844 
845         member_order = self.options.member_order or self.config.autodoc_member_order
846         memberdocumenters = self.sort_members(memberdocumenters, member_order)
847 
848         for documenter, isattr in memberdocumenters:
849             documenter.generate(
850                 all_members=True, real_modname=self.real_modname,
851                 check_module=members_check_module and not isattr)
852 
853         # reset current objects
854         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = None
855         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = None
856 
857     def sort_members(self, documenters: List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]],
858                      order: str) -> List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]]:
859         """Sort the given member list."""
860         if order == 'groupwise':
861             # sort by group; alphabetically within groups
862             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0].member_order, e[0].name))
863         elif order == 'bysource':
864             if self.analyzer:
865                 # sort by source order, by virtue of the module analyzer
866                 tagorder = self.analyzer.tagorder
867 
868                 def keyfunc(entry: Tuple[Documenter, bool]) -> int:
869                     fullname = entry[0].name.split('::')[1]
870                     return tagorder.get(fullname, len(tagorder))
871                 documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
872             else:
873                 # Assume that member discovery order matches source order.
874                 # This is a reasonable assumption in Python 3.6 and up, where
875                 # module.__dict__ is insertion-ordered.
876                 pass
877         else:  # alphabetical
878             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].name)
879 
880         return documenters
881 
882     def generate(self, more_content: Optional[StringList] = None, real_modname: str = None,
883                  check_module: bool = False, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
884         """Generate reST for the object given by *self.name*, and possibly for
885         its members.
886 
887         If *more_content* is given, include that content. If *real_modname* is
888         given, use that module name to find attribute docs. If *check_module* is
889         True, only generate if the object is defined in the module name it is
890         imported from. If *all_members* is True, document all members.
891         """
892         if not self.parse_name():
893             # need a module to import
894             logger.warning(
895                 __('don\'t know which module to import for autodocumenting '
896                    '%r (try placing a "module" or "currentmodule" directive '
897                    'in the document, or giving an explicit module name)') %
898                 self.name, type='autodoc')
899             return
900 
901         # now, import the module and get object to document
902         if not self.import_object():
903             return
904 
905         # If there is no real module defined, figure out which to use.
906         # The real module is used in the module analyzer to look up the module
907         # where the attribute documentation would actually be found in.
908         # This is used for situations where you have a module that collects the
909         # functions and classes of internal submodules.
910         guess_modname = self.get_real_modname()
911         self.real_modname = real_modname or guess_modname
912 
913         # try to also get a source code analyzer for attribute docs
914         try:
915             self.analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(self.real_modname)
916             # parse right now, to get PycodeErrors on parsing (results will
917             # be cached anyway)
918             self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
919         except PycodeError as exc:
920             logger.debug('[autodoc] module analyzer failed: %s', exc)
921             # no source file -- e.g. for builtin and C modules
922             self.analyzer = None
923             # at least add the module.__file__ as a dependency
924             if hasattr(self.module, '__file__') and self.module.__file__:
925                 self.directive.filename_set.add(self.module.__file__)
926         else:
927             self.directive.filename_set.add(self.analyzer.srcname)
928 
929         if self.real_modname != guess_modname:
930             # Add module to dependency list if target object is defined in other module.
931             try:
932                 analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(guess_modname)
933                 self.directive.filename_set.add(analyzer.srcname)
934             except PycodeError:
935                 pass
936 
937         # check __module__ of object (for members not given explicitly)
938         if check_module:
939             if not self.check_module():
940                 return
941 
942         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
943 
944         # make sure that the result starts with an empty line.  This is
945         # necessary for some situations where another directive preprocesses
946         # reST and no starting newline is present
947         self.add_line('', sourcename)
948 
949         # format the object's signature, if any
950         try:
951             sig = self.format_signature()
952         except Exception as exc:
953             logger.warning(__('error while formatting signature for %s: %s'),
954                            self.fullname, exc, type='autodoc')
955             return
956 
957         # generate the directive header and options, if applicable
958         self.add_directive_header(sig)
959         self.add_line('', sourcename)
960 
961         # e.g. the module directive doesn't have content
962         self.indent += self.content_indent
963 
964         # add all content (from docstrings, attribute docs etc.)
965         self.add_content(more_content)
966 
967         # document members, if possible
968         self.document_members(all_members)
969

1046     def get_module_members(self) -> Dict[str, ObjectMember]:
1047         """Get members of target module."""
1048         if self.analyzer:
1049             attr_docs = self.analyzer.attr_docs
1050         else:
1051             attr_docs = {}
1052 
1053         members = {}  # type: Dict[str, ObjectMember]
1054         for name in dir(self.object):
1055             try:
1056                 value = safe_getattr(self.object, name, None)
1057                 docstring = attr_docs.get(('', name), [])
1058                 members[name] = ObjectMember(name, value, docstring="\n".join(docstring))
1059             except AttributeError:
1060                 continue
1061 
1062         # annotation only member (ex. attr: int)
1063         try:
1064             for name in inspect.getannotations(self.object):
1065                 if name not in members:
1066                     docstring = attr_docs.get(('', name), [])
1067                     members[name] = ObjectMember(name, INSTANCEATTR,
1068                                                  docstring="\n".join(docstring))
1069         except AttributeError:
1070             pass
1071 
1072         return members

1074     def get_object_members(self, want_all: bool) -> Tuple[bool, ObjectMembers]:
1075         members = self.get_module_members()
1076         if want_all:
1077             if not self.__all__:
1078                 # for implicit module members, check __module__ to avoid
1079                 # documenting imported objects
1080                 return True, list(members.values())
1081             else:
1082                 for member in members.values():
1083                     if member.__name__ not in self.__all__:
1084                         member.skipped = True
1085 
1086                 return False, list(members.values())
1087         else:
1088             memberlist = self.options.members or []
1089             ret = []
1090             for name in memberlist:
1091                 if name in members:
1092                     ret.append(members[name])
1093                 else:
1094                     logger.warning(__('missing attribute mentioned in :members: option: '
1095                                       'module %s, attribute %s') %
1096                                    (safe_getattr(self.object, '__name__', '???'), name),
1097                                    type='autodoc')
1098             return False, ret

1100     def sort_members(self, documenters: List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]],
1101                      order: str) -> List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]]:
1102         if order == 'bysource' and self.__all__:
1103             # Sort alphabetically first (for members not listed on the __all__)
1104             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].name)
1105 
1106             # Sort by __all__
1107             def keyfunc(entry: Tuple[Documenter, bool]) -> int:
1108                 name = entry[0].name.split('::')[1]
1109                 if name in self.__all__:
1110                     return self.__all__.index(name)
1111                 else:
1112                     return len(self.__all__)
1113             documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
1114 
1115             return documenters
1116         else:
1117             return super().sort_members(documenters, order)

1141 class ClassLevelDocumenter(Documenter):
1142     """
1143     Specialized Documenter subclass for objects on class level (methods,
1144     attributes).
1145     """
1146     def resolve_name(self, modname: str, parents: Any, path: str, base: Any
1147                      ) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
1148         if modname is None:
1149             if path:
1150                 mod_cls = path.rstrip('.')
1151             else:
1152                 mod_cls = None
1153                 # if documenting a class-level object without path,
1154                 # there must be a current class, either from a parent
1155                 # auto directive ...
1156                 mod_cls = self.env.temp_data.get('autodoc:class')
1157                 # ... or from a class directive

1163             modname, sep, cls = mod_cls.rpartition('.')
1164             parents = [cls]

1166             if not modname:
1167                 modname = self.env.temp_data.get('autodoc:module')
1168             if not modname:
1169                 modname = self.env.ref_context.get('py:module')
1170             # ... else, it stays None, which means invalid

1174 class DocstringSignatureMixin:
1175     """
1176     Mixin for FunctionDocumenter and MethodDocumenter to provide the
1177     feature of reading the signature from the docstring.
1178     """
1179     _new_docstrings = None  # type: List[List[str]]
1180     _signatures = None      # type: List[str]
1181 
1182     def _find_signature(self, encoding: str = None) -> Tuple[str, str]:
1183         if encoding is not None:
1184             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s._find_signature() is "
1185                           "deprecated." % self.__class__.__name__,
1186                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
1187 
1188         # candidates of the object name
1189         valid_names = [self.objpath[-1]]  # type: ignore
1190         if isinstance(self, ClassDocumenter):
1191             valid_names.append('__init__')
1192             if hasattr(self.object, '__mro__'):
1193                 valid_names.extend(cls.__name__ for cls in self.object.__mro__)
1194 
1195         docstrings = self.get_doc()
1196         self._new_docstrings = docstrings[:]
1197         self._signatures = []
1198         result = None
1199         for i, doclines in enumerate(docstrings):
1200             for j, line in enumerate(doclines):
1201                 if not line:
1202                     # no lines in docstring, no match
1203                     break
1204 
1205                 if line.endswith('\\'):
1206                     multiline = True
1207                     line = line.rstrip('\\').rstrip()
1208                 else:
1209                     multiline = False
1210 
1211                 # match first line of docstring against signature RE
1212                 match = py_ext_sig_re.match(line)
1213                 if not match:
1214                     continue
1215                 exmod, path, base, args, retann = match.groups()
1216 
1217                 # the base name must match ours
1218                 if base not in valid_names:
1219                     continue
1220 
1221                 # re-prepare docstring to ignore more leading indentation
1222                 tab_width = self.directive.state.document.settings.tab_width  # type: ignore
1223                 self._new_docstrings[i] = prepare_docstring('\n'.join(doclines[j + 1:]),
1224                                                             tabsize=tab_width)
1225 
1226                 if result is None:
1227                     # first signature
1228                     result = args, retann
1229                 else:
1230                     # subsequent signatures
1231                     self._signatures.append("(%s) -> %s" % (args, retann))
1232 
1233                 if multiline:
1234                     # the signature have multiple signatures on docstring
1235                     continue
1236                 else:
1237                     # don't look any further
1238                     break
1239 
1240             if result:
1241                 # finish the loop when signature found
1242                 break
1243 
1244         return result
1245 
1246     def get_doc(self, encoding: str = None, ignore: int = None) -> Optional[List[List[str]]]:
1247         if encoding is not None:
1248             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
1249                           % self.__class__.__name__,
1250                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
1251         if self._new_docstrings is not None:
1252             return self._new_docstrings
1253         return super().get_doc(None, ignore)  # type: ignore
1254 
1255     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1256         if self.args is None and self.config.autodoc_docstring_signature:  # type: ignore
1257             # only act if a signature is not explicitly given already, and if
1258             # the feature is enabled
1259             result = self._find_signature()
1260             if result is not None:
1261                 self.args, self.retann = result
1262         sig = super().format_signature(**kwargs)  # type: ignore
1263         if self._signatures:
1264             return "\n".join([sig] + self._signatures)
1265         else:
1266             return sig

1377         if len(sig.parameters) == 0:

1380         params = list(sig.parameters.values())
1381         if params[0].annotation is Parameter.empty:
1382             params[0] = params[0].replace(annotation=typ)

1384                 func.__signature__ = sig.replace(parameters=params)  # type: ignore
1385             except TypeError:

1458     def _get_signature(self) -> Tuple[Optional[Any], Optional[str], Optional[Signature]]:
1459         def get_user_defined_function_or_method(obj: Any, attr: str) -> Any:
1460             """ Get the `attr` function or method from `obj`, if it is user-defined. """
1461             if inspect.is_builtin_class_method(obj, attr):
1462                 return None
1463             attr = self.get_attr(obj, attr, None)
1464             if not (inspect.ismethod(attr) or inspect.isfunction(attr)):
1465                 return None
1466             return attr
1467 
1468         # This sequence is copied from inspect._signature_from_callable.
1469         # ValueError means that no signature could be found, so we keep going.
1470 
1471         # First, we check the obj has a __signature__ attribute
1472         if (hasattr(self.object, '__signature__') and
1473                 isinstance(self.object.__signature__, Signature)):
1474             return None, None, self.object.__signature__
1475 
1476         # Next, let's see if it has an overloaded __call__ defined
1477         # in its metaclass
1478         call = get_user_defined_function_or_method(type(self.object), '__call__')
1479 
1480         if call is not None:
1481             if "{0.__module__}.{0.__qualname__}".format(call) in _METACLASS_CALL_BLACKLIST:
1482                 call = None
1483 
1484         if call is not None:
1485             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', call, True)
1486             try:
1487                 sig = inspect.signature(call, bound_method=True,
1488                                         type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1489                 return type(self.object), '__call__', sig
1490             except ValueError:
1491                 pass
1492 
1493         # Now we check if the 'obj' class has a '__new__' method
1494         new = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__new__')
1495 
1496         if new is not None:
1497             if "{0.__module__}.{0.__qualname__}".format(new) in _CLASS_NEW_BLACKLIST:
1498                 new = None
1499 
1500         if new is not None:
1501             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', new, True)
1502             try:
1503                 sig = inspect.signature(new, bound_method=True,
1504                                         type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1505                 return self.object, '__new__', sig
1506             except ValueError:
1507                 pass
1508 
1509         # Finally, we should have at least __init__ implemented
1510         init = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__init__')
1511         if init is not None:
1512             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', init, True)
1513             try:
1514                 sig = inspect.signature(init, bound_method=True,
1515                                         type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1516                 return self.object, '__init__', sig
1517             except ValueError:
1518                 pass
1519 
1520         # None of the attributes are user-defined, so fall back to let inspect
1521         # handle it.
1522         # We don't know the exact method that inspect.signature will read
1523         # the signature from, so just pass the object itself to our hook.
1524         self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', self.object, False)
1525         try:
1526             sig = inspect.signature(self.object, bound_method=False,
1527                                     type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1528             return None, None, sig
1529         except ValueError:
1530             pass
1531 
1532         # Still no signature: happens e.g. for old-style classes
1533         # with __init__ in C and no `__text_signature__`.
1534         return None, None, None
1535

1559

2092     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
2093         sigs = []

2095                 '.'.join(self.objpath) in self.analyzer.overloads and
2096                 self.config.autodoc_typehints == 'signature'):
2097             # Use signatures for overloaded methods instead of the implementation method.
2098             overloaded = True
2099         else:
2100             overloaded = False
2101             sig = super().format_signature(**kwargs)
2102             sigs.append(sig)
2103 
2104         meth = self.parent.__dict__.get(self.objpath[-1])
2105         if inspect.is_singledispatch_method(meth):
2106             # append signature of singledispatch'ed functions
2107             for typ, func in meth.dispatcher.registry.items():
2108                 if typ is object:
2109                     pass  # default implementation. skipped.
2110                 else:
2111                     self.annotate_to_first_argument(func, typ)
2112 
2113                     documenter = MethodDocumenter(self.directive, '')
2114                     documenter.parent = self.parent
2115                     documenter.object = func
2116                     documenter.objpath = [None]
2117                     sigs.append(documenter.format_signature())
2118         if overloaded:
2119             __globals__ = safe_getattr(self.object, '__globals__', {})
2120             for overload in self.analyzer.overloads.get('.'.join(self.objpath)):
2121                 overload = evaluate_signature(overload, __globals__,
2122                                               self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
2123 
2124                 if not inspect.isstaticmethod(self.object, cls=self.parent,
2125                                               name=self.object_name):
2126                     parameters = list(overload.parameters.values())
2127                     overload = overload.replace(parameters=parameters[1:])
2128                 sig = stringify_signature(overload, **kwargs)
2129                 sigs.append(sig)
2130 
2131         return "\n".join(sigs)

2133     def annotate_to_first_argument(self, func: Callable, typ: Type) -> None:
2134         """Annotate type hint to the first argument of function if needed."""
2135         try:
2136             sig = inspect.signature(func, type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
2137         except TypeError as exc:
2138             logger.warning(__("Failed to get a method signature for %s: %s"),
2139                            self.fullname, exc)
2140             return
2141         except ValueError:
2142             return
2143         if len(sig.parameters) == 1:
2144             return
2145 
2146         params = list(sig.parameters.values())
2147         if params[1].annotation is Parameter.empty:
2148             params[1] = params[1].replace(annotation=typ)
2149             try:
2150                 func.__signature__ = sig.replace(parameters=params)  # type: ignore
2151             except TypeError:
2152                 # failed to update signature (ex. built-in or extension types)
2153                 return

273     .. Note::

275        An instance of this class behaves as a tuple of (name, object)
276        for compatibility to old Sphinx.  The behavior will be dropped
277        in the future.  Therefore extensions should not use the tuple
278        interface.
279     """
