189 def _parse_arglist(arglist: str, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> addnodes.desc_parameterlist:
190     """Parse a list of arguments using AST parser"""
191     params = addnodes.desc_parameterlist(arglist)
192     sig = signature_from_str('(%s)' % arglist)
193     last_kind = None
194     for param in sig.parameters.values():
195         if param.kind != param.POSITIONAL_ONLY and last_kind == param.POSITIONAL_ONLY:
196             # PEP-570: Separator for Positional Only Parameter: /
197             params += addnodes.desc_parameter('', '', addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '/'))
198         if param.kind == param.KEYWORD_ONLY and last_kind in (param.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
199                                                               param.POSITIONAL_ONLY,
200                                                               None):
201             # PEP-3102: Separator for Keyword Only Parameter: *
202             params += addnodes.desc_parameter('', '', addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '*'))
203 
204         node = addnodes.desc_parameter()
205         if param.kind == param.VAR_POSITIONAL:
206             node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '*')
207             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', param.name)
208         elif param.kind == param.VAR_KEYWORD:
209             node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '**')
210             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', param.name)
211         else:
212             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', param.name)
213 
214         if param.annotation is not param.empty:
215             children = _parse_annotation(param.annotation, env)
216             node += addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ':')
217             node += nodes.Text(' ')
218             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', '', *children)  # type: ignore
219         if param.default is not param.empty:
220             if param.annotation is not param.empty:
221                 node += nodes.Text(' ')
222                 node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '=')
223                 node += nodes.Text(' ')
224             else:
225                 node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '=')
226             node += nodes.inline('', param.default, classes=['default_value'],
227                                  support_smartquotes=False)
228 
229         params += node
230         last_kind = param.kind
231 
232     if last_kind == Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY:
233         # PEP-570: Separator for Positional Only Parameter: /
234         params += addnodes.desc_parameter('', '', addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '/'))
235 
236     return params

239 def _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode: desc_signature, arglist: str) -> None:
240     """"Parse" a list of arguments separated by commas.
241 
242     Arguments can have "optional" annotations given by enclosing them in
243     brackets.  Currently, this will split at any comma, even if it's inside a
244     string literal (e.g. default argument value).
245     """
246     paramlist = addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
247     stack: List[Element] = [paramlist]
248     try:
249         for argument in arglist.split(','):
250             argument = argument.strip()
251             ends_open = ends_close = 0
252             while argument.startswith('['):
253                 stack.append(addnodes.desc_optional())
254                 stack[-2] += stack[-1]
255                 argument = argument[1:].strip()
256             while argument.startswith(']'):
257                 stack.pop()
258                 argument = argument[1:].strip()
259             while argument.endswith(']') and not argument.endswith('[]'):
260                 ends_close += 1
261                 argument = argument[:-1].strip()
262             while argument.endswith('['):
263                 ends_open += 1
264                 argument = argument[:-1].strip()
265             if argument:
266                 stack[-1] += addnodes.desc_parameter(argument, argument)
267             while ends_open:
268                 stack.append(addnodes.desc_optional())
269                 stack[-2] += stack[-1]
270                 ends_open -= 1
271             while ends_close:
272                 stack.pop()
273                 ends_close -= 1
274         if len(stack) != 1:
275             raise IndexError
276     except IndexError:
277         # if there are too few or too many elements on the stack, just give up
278         # and treat the whole argument list as one argument, discarding the
279         # already partially populated paramlist node
280         paramlist = addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
281         paramlist += addnodes.desc_parameter(arglist, arglist)
282         signode += paramlist
283     else:
284         signode += paramlist

287 # This override allows our inline type specifiers to behave like :class: link
288 # when it comes to handling "." and "~" prefixes.
289 class PyXrefMixin:
290     def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
291                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
292                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None,
293                   inliner: Inliner = None, location: Node = None) -> Node:
294         # we use inliner=None to make sure we get the old behaviour with a single
295         # pending_xref node
296         result = super().make_xref(rolename, domain, target,  # type: ignore
297                                    innernode, contnode,
298                                    env, inliner=None, location=None)
299         result['refspecific'] = True
300         result['py:module'] = env.ref_context.get('py:module')
301         result['py:class'] = env.ref_context.get('py:class')
302         if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
303             prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
304             if prefix == '.':
305                 text = target[1:]
306             elif prefix == '~':
307                 text = target.split('.')[-1]
308             for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
309                 node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
310                 break
311         elif isinstance(result, pending_xref) and env.config.python_use_unqualified_type_names:
312             children = result.children
313             result.clear()
314 
315             shortname = target.split('.')[-1]
316             textnode = innernode('', shortname)
317             contnodes = [pending_xref_condition('', '', textnode, condition='resolved'),
318                          pending_xref_condition('', '', *children, condition='*')]
319             result.extend(contnodes)
320 
321         return result
322 
323     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
324                    innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
325                    contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None,
326                    inliner: Inliner = None, location: Node = None) -> List[Node]:
327         delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\s*\|\s*|\.\.\.)'
328         delims_re = re.compile(delims)
329         sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)
330 
331         split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)
332 
333         results = []
334         for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
335             if split_contnode:
336                 contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)
337 
338             if delims_re.match(sub_target):
339                 results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
340             else:
341                 results.append(self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
342                                               innernode, contnode, env, inliner, location))
343 
344         return results
345

425     def handle_signature(self, sig: str, signode: desc_signature) -> Tuple[str, str]:
426         """Transform a Python signature into RST nodes.
427 
428         Return (fully qualified name of the thing, classname if any).
429 
430         If inside a class, the current class name is handled intelligently:
431         * it is stripped from the displayed name if present
432         * it is added to the full name (return value) if not present
433         """
434         m = py_sig_re.match(sig)
435         if m is None:
436             raise ValueError
437         prefix, name, arglist, retann = m.groups()
438 
439         # determine module and class name (if applicable), as well as full name
440         modname = self.options.get('module', self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
441         classname = self.env.ref_context.get('py:class')
442         if classname:
443             add_module = False
444             if prefix and (prefix == classname or
445                            prefix.startswith(classname + ".")):
446                 fullname = prefix + name
447                 # class name is given again in the signature
448                 prefix = prefix[len(classname):].lstrip('.')
449             elif prefix:
450                 # class name is given in the signature, but different
451                 # (shouldn't happen)
452                 fullname = classname + '.' + prefix + name
453             else:
454                 # class name is not given in the signature
455                 fullname = classname + '.' + name
456         else:
457             add_module = True
458             if prefix:
459                 classname = prefix.rstrip('.')
460                 fullname = prefix + name
461             else:
462                 classname = ''
463                 fullname = name
464 
465         signode['module'] = modname
466         signode['class'] = classname
467         signode['fullname'] = fullname
468 
469         sig_prefix = self.get_signature_prefix(sig)
470         if sig_prefix:
471             signode += addnodes.desc_annotation(sig_prefix, sig_prefix)
472 
473         if prefix:
474             signode += addnodes.desc_addname(prefix, prefix)
475         elif modname and add_module and self.env.config.add_module_names:
476             nodetext = modname + '.'
477             signode += addnodes.desc_addname(nodetext, nodetext)
478 
479         signode += addnodes.desc_name(name, name)
480         if arglist:
481             try:
482                 signode += _parse_arglist(arglist, self.env)
483             except SyntaxError:
484                 # fallback to parse arglist original parser.
485                 # it supports to represent optional arguments (ex. "func(foo [, bar])")
486                 _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode, arglist)
487             except NotImplementedError as exc:
488                 logger.warning("could not parse arglist (%r): %s", arglist, exc,
489                                location=signode)
490                 _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode, arglist)
491         else:
492             if self.needs_arglist():
493                 # for callables, add an empty parameter list
494                 signode += addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
495 
496         if retann:
497             children = _parse_annotation(retann, self.env)
498             signode += addnodes.desc_returns(retann, '', *children)
499 
500         anno = self.options.get('annotation')
501         if anno:
502             signode += addnodes.desc_annotation(' ' + anno, ' ' + anno)
503 
504         return fullname, prefix
505

537     def before_content(self) -> None:
538         """Handle object nesting before content
539 
540         :py:class:`PyObject` represents Python language constructs. For
541         constructs that are nestable, such as a Python classes, this method will
542         build up a stack of the nesting hierarchy so that it can be later
543         de-nested correctly, in :py:meth:`after_content`.
544 
545         For constructs that aren't nestable, the stack is bypassed, and instead
546         only the most recent object is tracked. This object prefix name will be
547         removed with :py:meth:`after_content`.
548         """
549         prefix = None
550         if self.names:
551             # fullname and name_prefix come from the `handle_signature` method.
552             # fullname represents the full object name that is constructed using
553             # object nesting and explicit prefixes. `name_prefix` is the
554             # explicit prefix given in a signature
555             (fullname, name_prefix) = self.names[-1]
556             if self.allow_nesting:
557                 prefix = fullname
558             elif name_prefix:
559                 prefix = name_prefix.strip('.')
560         if prefix:
561             self.env.ref_context['py:class'] = prefix
562             if self.allow_nesting:
563                 classes = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:classes', [])
564                 classes.append(prefix)
565         if 'module' in self.options:
566             modules = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:modules', [])
567             modules.append(self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
568             self.env.ref_context['py:module'] = self.options['module']
569 
570     def after_content(self) -> None:
571         """Handle object de-nesting after content
572 
573         If this class is a nestable object, removing the last nested class prefix
574         ends further nesting in the object.
575 
576         If this class is not a nestable object, the list of classes should not
577         be altered as we didn't affect the nesting levels in
578         :py:meth:`before_content`.
579         """
580         classes = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:classes', [])
581         if self.allow_nesting:
582             try:
583                 classes.pop()
584             except IndexError:
585                 pass
586         self.env.ref_context['py:class'] = (classes[-1] if len(classes) > 0
587                                             else None)
588         if 'module' in self.options:
589             modules = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:modules', [])
590             if modules:
591                 self.env.ref_context['py:module'] = modules.pop()
592             else:
593                 self.env.ref_context.pop('py:module')

1039 class PythonModuleIndex(Index):
1040     """
1041     Index subclass to provide the Python module index.
1042     """
1043 
1044     name = 'modindex'
1045     localname = _('Python Module Index')
1046     shortname = _('modules')
1047 
1048     def generate(self, docnames: Iterable[str] = None
1049                  ) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[str, List[IndexEntry]]], bool]:
1050         content: Dict[str, List[IndexEntry]] = {}
1051         # list of prefixes to ignore
1052         ignores: List[str] = self.domain.env.config['modindex_common_prefix']
1053         ignores = sorted(ignores, key=len, reverse=True)
1054         # list of all modules, sorted by module name
1055         modules = sorted(self.domain.data['modules'].items(),
1056                          key=lambda x: x[0].lower())
1057         # sort out collapsable modules
1058         prev_modname = ''
1059         num_toplevels = 0
1060         for modname, (docname, node_id, synopsis, platforms, deprecated) in modules:
1061             if docnames and docname not in docnames:
1062                 continue
1063 
1064             for ignore in ignores:
1065                 if modname.startswith(ignore):
1066                     modname = modname[len(ignore):]
1067                     stripped = ignore
1068                     break
1069             else:
1070                 stripped = ''
1071 
1072             # we stripped the whole module name?
1073             if not modname:
1074                 modname, stripped = stripped, ''
1075 
1076             entries = content.setdefault(modname[0].lower(), [])
1077 
1078             package = modname.split('.')[0]
1079             if package != modname:
1080                 # it's a submodule
1081                 if prev_modname == package:
1082                     # first submodule - make parent a group head
1083                     if entries:
1084                         last = entries[-1]
1085                         entries[-1] = IndexEntry(last[0], 1, last[2], last[3],
1086                                                  last[4], last[5], last[6])
1087                 elif not prev_modname.startswith(package):
1088                     # submodule without parent in list, add dummy entry
1089                     entries.append(IndexEntry(stripped + package, 1, '', '', '', '', ''))
1090                 subtype = 2
1091             else:
1092                 num_toplevels += 1
1093                 subtype = 0
1094 
1095             qualifier = _('Deprecated') if deprecated else ''
1096             entries.append(IndexEntry(stripped + modname, subtype, docname,
1097                                       node_id, platforms, qualifier, synopsis))
1098             prev_modname = modname
1099 
1100         # apply heuristics when to collapse modindex at page load:
1101         # only collapse if number of toplevel modules is larger than
1102         # number of submodules
1103         collapse = len(modules) - num_toplevels < num_toplevels
1104 
1105         # sort by first letter
1106         sorted_content = sorted(content.items())
1107 
1108         return sorted_content, collapse

1217     def find_obj(self, env: BuildEnvironment, modname: str, classname: str,
1218                  name: str, type: str, searchmode: int = 0
1219                  ) -> List[Tuple[str, ObjectEntry]]:
1220         """Find a Python object for "name", perhaps using the given module
1221         and/or classname.  Returns a list of (name, object entry) tuples.
1222         """
1223         # skip parens
1224         if name[-2:] == '()':
1225             name = name[:-2]
1226 
1227         if not name:
1228             return []
1229 
1230         matches: List[Tuple[str, ObjectEntry]] = []
1231 
1232         newname = None
1233         if searchmode == 1:
1234             if type is None:
1235                 objtypes = list(self.object_types)
1236             else:
1237                 objtypes = self.objtypes_for_role(type)
1238             if objtypes is not None:
1239                 if modname and classname:
1240                     fullname = modname + '.' + classname + '.' + name
1241                     if fullname in self.objects and self.objects[fullname].objtype in objtypes:
1242                         newname = fullname
1243                 if not newname:
1244                     if modname and modname + '.' + name in self.objects and \
1245                        self.objects[modname + '.' + name].objtype in objtypes:
1246                         newname = modname + '.' + name
1247                     elif name in self.objects and self.objects[name].objtype in objtypes:
1248                         newname = name
1249                     else:
1250                         # "fuzzy" searching mode
1251                         searchname = '.' + name
1252                         matches = [(oname, self.objects[oname]) for oname in self.objects
1253                                    if oname.endswith(searchname) and
1254                                    self.objects[oname].objtype in objtypes]
1255         else:
1256             # NOTE: searching for exact match, object type is not considered
1257             if name in self.objects:
1258                 newname = name
1259             elif type == 'mod':
1260                 # only exact matches allowed for modules
1261                 return []
1262             elif classname and classname + '.' + name in self.objects:
1263                 newname = classname + '.' + name
1264             elif modname and modname + '.' + name in self.objects:
1265                 newname = modname + '.' + name
1266             elif modname and classname and \
1267                     modname + '.' + classname + '.' + name in self.objects:
1268                 newname = modname + '.' + classname + '.' + name
1269         if newname is not None:
1270             matches.append((newname, self.objects[newname]))
1271         return matches

1273     def resolve_xref(self, env: BuildEnvironment, fromdocname: str, builder: Builder,
1274                      type: str, target: str, node: pending_xref, contnode: Element
1275                      ) -> Optional[Element]:
1276         modname = node.get('py:module')
1277         clsname = node.get('py:class')
1278         searchmode = 1 if node.hasattr('refspecific') else 0
1279         matches = self.find_obj(env, modname, clsname, target,
1280                                 type, searchmode)
1281 
1282         if not matches and type == 'attr':
1283             # fallback to meth (for property; Sphinx-2.4.x)
1284             # this ensures that `:attr:` role continues to refer to the old property entry
1285             # that defined by ``method`` directive in old reST files.
1286             matches = self.find_obj(env, modname, clsname, target, 'meth', searchmode)
1287         if not matches and type == 'meth':
1288             # fallback to attr (for property)
1289             # this ensures that `:meth:` in the old reST files can refer to the property
1290             # entry that defined by ``property`` directive.
1291             #
1292             # Note: _prop is a secret role only for internal look-up.
1293             matches = self.find_obj(env, modname, clsname, target, '_prop', searchmode)
1294 
1295         if not matches:
1296             return None
1297         elif len(matches) > 1:
1298             canonicals = [m for m in matches if not m[1].aliased]
1299             if len(canonicals) == 1:
1300                 matches = canonicals
1301             else:
1302                 logger.warning(__('more than one target found for cross-reference %r: %s'),
1303                                target, ', '.join(match[0] for match in matches),
1304                                type='ref', subtype='python', location=node)
1305         name, obj = matches[0]
1306 
1307         if obj[2] == 'module':
1308             return self._make_module_refnode(builder, fromdocname, name, contnode)
1309         else:
1310             # determine the content of the reference by conditions
1311             content = find_pending_xref_condition(node, 'resolved')
1312             if content:
1313                 children = content.children
1314             else:
1315                 # if not found, use contnode
1316                 children = [contnode]
1317 
1318             return make_refnode(builder, fromdocname, obj[0], obj[1], children, name)

1320     def resolve_any_xref(self, env: BuildEnvironment, fromdocname: str, builder: Builder,

1348     def _make_module_refnode(self, builder: Builder, fromdocname: str, name: str,

1370                 else:

291     def _eval_extract(self, rowsList, colsList):
292         urow = list(uniq(rowsList))
293         ucol = list(uniq(colsList))
294         smat = {}
295         if len(urow)*len(ucol) < len(self._smat):
296             # there are fewer elements requested than there are elements in the matrix
297             for i, r in enumerate(urow):
298                 for j, c in enumerate(ucol):
299                     smat[i, j] = self._smat.get((r, c), 0)
300         else:
301             # most of the request will be zeros so check all of self's entries,
302             # keeping only the ones that are desired
303             for rk, ck in self._smat:
304                 if rk in urow and ck in ucol:
305                     smat[(urow.index(rk), ucol.index(ck))] = self._smat[(rk, ck)]
306 
307         rv = self._new(len(urow), len(ucol), smat)
308         # rv is nominally correct but there might be rows/cols
309         # which require duplication
310         if len(rowsList) != len(urow):
311             for i, r in enumerate(rowsList):
312                 i_previous = rowsList.index(r)
313                 if i_previous != i:
314                     rv = rv.row_insert(i, rv.row(i_previous))
315         if len(colsList) != len(ucol):
316             for i, c in enumerate(colsList):
317                 i_previous = colsList.index(c)
318                 if i_previous != i:
319                     rv = rv.col_insert(i, rv.col(i_previous))
320         return rv

345     def _eval_matrix_mul(self, other):
346         """Fast multiplication exploiting the sparsity of the matrix."""
347         if not isinstance(other, SparseMatrix):
348             return self*self._new(other)
349 
350         # if we made it here, we're both sparse matrices
351         # create quick lookups for rows and cols
352         row_lookup = defaultdict(dict)
353         for (i,j), val in self._smat.items():
354             row_lookup[i][j] = val
355         col_lookup = defaultdict(dict)
356         for (i,j), val in other._smat.items():
357             col_lookup[j][i] = val
358 
359         smat = {}
360         for row in row_lookup.keys():
361             for col in col_lookup.keys():
362                 # find the common indices of non-zero entries.
363                 # these are the only things that need to be multiplied.
364                 indices = set(col_lookup[col].keys()) & set(row_lookup[row].keys())
365                 if indices:
366                     val = sum(row_lookup[row][k]*col_lookup[col][k] for k in indices)
367                     smat[(row, col)] = val
368         return self._new(self.rows, other.cols, smat)

419     def _LDL_solve(self, rhs):

421         # having difficulties, try uncommenting to make sure that the
422         # input matrix is symmetric
423 
424         #assert self.is_symmetric()
425         L, D = self._LDL_sparse()
426         Z = L._lower_triangular_solve(rhs)

430     def _LDL_sparse(self):
431         """Algorithm for numeric LDL factization, exploiting sparse structure.
432         """
433         Lrowstruc = self.row_structure_symbolic_cholesky()
434         L = self.eye(self.rows)
435         D = self.zeros(self.rows, self.cols)
436 
437         for i in range(len(Lrowstruc)):
438             for j in Lrowstruc[i]:
439                 if i != j:
440                     L[i, j] = self[i, j]
441                     summ = 0
442                     for p1 in Lrowstruc[i]:
443                         if p1 < j:
444                             for p2 in Lrowstruc[j]:
445                                 if p2 < j:
446                                     if p1 == p2:
447                                         summ += L[i, p1]*L[j, p1]*D[p1, p1]
448                                 else:
449                                     break
450                         else:
451                             break
452                     L[i, j] -= summ
453                     L[i, j] /= D[j, j]
454                 elif i == j:
455                     D[i, i] = self[i, i]
456                     summ = 0
457                     for k in Lrowstruc[i]:
458                         if k < i:
459                             summ += L[i, k]**2*D[k, k]
460                         else:
461                             break
462                     D[i, i] -= summ
463 
464         return L, D
465 
466     def _lower_triangular_solve(self, rhs):
467         """Fast algorithm for solving a lower-triangular system,
468         exploiting the sparsity of the given matrix.
469         """
470         rows = [[] for i in range(self.rows)]
471         for i, j, v in self.row_list():
472             if i > j:
473                 rows[i].append((j, v))
474         X = rhs.copy()
475         for i in range(self.rows):
476             for j, v in rows[i]:
477                 X[i, 0] -= v*X[j, 0]
478             X[i, 0] /= self[i, i]
479         return self._new(X)

487     def _upper_triangular_solve(self, rhs):
488         """Fast algorithm for solving an upper-triangular system,
489         exploiting the sparsity of the given matrix.
490         """
491         rows = [[] for i in range(self.rows)]
492         for i, j, v in self.row_list():
493             if i < j:
494                 rows[i].append((j, v))
495         X = rhs.copy()
496         for i in range(self.rows - 1, -1, -1):
497             rows[i].reverse()
498             for j, v in rows[i]:
499                 X[i, 0] -= v*X[j, 0]
500             X[i, 0] /= self[i, i]
501         return self._new(X)

556     def cholesky(self):
557         """
558         Returns the Cholesky decomposition L of a matrix A
559         such that L * L.T = A

561         A must be a square, symmetric, positive-definite
562         and non-singular matrix

564         Examples

567         >>> from sympy.matrices import SparseMatrix
568         >>> A = SparseMatrix(((25,15,-5),(15,18,0),(-5,0,11)))

574         >>> A.cholesky() * A.cholesky().T == A
575         True
576         """
577 
578         from sympy.core.numbers import nan, oo
579         if not self.is_symmetric():
580             raise ValueError('Cholesky decomposition applies only to '
581                 'symmetric matrices.')

583         if M.has(nan) or M.has(oo):

585                 'positive-definite matrices')

613     def LDLdecomposition(self):
614         """
615         Returns the LDL Decomposition (matrices ``L`` and ``D``) of matrix
616         ``A``, such that ``L * D * L.T == A``. ``A`` must be a square,
617         symmetric, positive-definite and non-singular.
618 
619         This method eliminates the use of square root and ensures that all
620         the diagonal entries of L are 1.
621 
622         Examples
623         ========
624 
625         >>> from sympy.matrices import SparseMatrix
626         >>> A = SparseMatrix(((25, 15, -5), (15, 18, 0), (-5, 0, 11)))
627         >>> L, D = A.LDLdecomposition()
628         >>> L
629         Matrix([
630         [   1,   0, 0],
631         [ 3/5,   1, 0],
632         [-1/5, 1/3, 1]])
633         >>> D
634         Matrix([
635         [25, 0, 0],
636         [ 0, 9, 0],
637         [ 0, 0, 9]])
638         >>> L * D * L.T == A
639         True
640 
641         """
642         from sympy.core.numbers import nan, oo
643         if not self.is_symmetric():
644             raise ValueError('LDL decomposition applies only to '
645                 'symmetric matrices.')
646         L, D = self.as_mutable()._LDL_sparse()
647         if L.has(nan) or L.has(oo) or D.has(nan) or D.has(oo):
648             raise ValueError('LDL decomposition applies only to '
649                 'positive-definite matrices')
650 
651         return self._new(L), self._new(D)
652 
653     def liupc(self):
654         """Liu's algorithm, for pre-determination of the Elimination Tree of
655         the given matrix, used in row-based symbolic Cholesky factorization.
656 
657         Examples
658         ========
659 
660         >>> from sympy.matrices import SparseMatrix
661         >>> S = SparseMatrix([
662         ... [1, 0, 3, 2],
663         ... [0, 0, 1, 0],
664         ... [4, 0, 0, 5],
665         ... [0, 6, 7, 0]])
666         >>> S.liupc()
667         ([[0], [], [0], [1, 2]], [4, 3, 4, 4])
668 
669         References
670         ==========
671 
672         Symbolic Sparse Cholesky Factorization using Elimination Trees,
673         Jeroen Van Grondelle (1999)
674         http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/summary?doi=10.1.1.39.7582
675         """
676         # Algorithm 2.4, p 17 of reference
677 
678         # get the indices of the elements that are non-zero on or below diag
679         R = [[] for r in range(self.rows)]
680         for r, c, _ in self.row_list():
681             if c <= r:
682                 R[r].append(c)
683 
684         inf = len(R)  # nothing will be this large
685         parent = [inf]*self.rows
686         virtual = [inf]*self.rows
687         for r in range(self.rows):
688             for c in R[r][:-1]:
689                 while virtual[c] < r:
690                     t = virtual[c]
691                     virtual[c] = r
692                     c = t
693                 if virtual[c] == inf:
694                     parent[c] = virtual[c] = r
695         return R, parent
696

715

724     def row_structure_symbolic_cholesky(self):
725         """Symbolic cholesky factorization, for pre-determination of the
726         non-zero structure of the Cholesky factororization.
727 
728         Examples
729         ========
730 
731         >>> from sympy.matrices import SparseMatrix
732         >>> S = SparseMatrix([
733         ... [1, 0, 3, 2],
734         ... [0, 0, 1, 0],
735         ... [4, 0, 0, 5],
736         ... [0, 6, 7, 0]])
737         >>> S.row_structure_symbolic_cholesky()
738         [[0], [], [0], [1, 2]]
739 
740         References
741         ==========
742 
743         Symbolic Sparse Cholesky Factorization using Elimination Trees,
744         Jeroen Van Grondelle (1999)
745         http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/summary?doi=10.1.1.39.7582
746         """
747 
748         R, parent = self.liupc()
749         inf = len(R)  # this acts as infinity
750         Lrow = copy.deepcopy(R)
751         for k in range(self.rows):
752             for j in R[k]:
753                 while j != inf and j != k:
754                     Lrow[k].append(j)
755                     j = parent[j]
756             Lrow[k] = list(sorted(set(Lrow[k])))
757         return Lrow
758 
759     def scalar_multiply(self, scalar):
760         "Scalar element-wise multiplication"
761         M = self.zeros(*self.shape)
762         if scalar:
763             for i in self._smat:
764                 v = scalar*self._smat[i]
765                 if v:
766                     M._smat[i] = v
767                 else:
768                     M._smat.pop(i, None)
769         return M

771     def solve_least_squares(self, rhs, method='LDL'):
772         """Return the least-square fit to the data.
773 
774         By default the cholesky_solve routine is used (method='CH'); other
775         methods of matrix inversion can be used. To find out which are
776         available, see the docstring of the .inv() method.
777 
778         Examples
779         ========
780 
781         >>> from sympy.matrices import SparseMatrix, Matrix, ones
782         >>> A = Matrix([1, 2, 3])
783         >>> B = Matrix([2, 3, 4])
784         >>> S = SparseMatrix(A.row_join(B))
785         >>> S
786         Matrix([
787         [1, 2],
788         [2, 3],
789         [3, 4]])
790 
791         If each line of S represent coefficients of Ax + By
792         and x and y are [2, 3] then S*xy is:
793 
794         >>> r = S*Matrix([2, 3]); r
795         Matrix([
796         [ 8],
797         [13],
798         [18]])
799 
800         But let's add 1 to the middle value and then solve for the
801         least-squares value of xy:
802 
803         >>> xy = S.solve_least_squares(Matrix([8, 14, 18])); xy
804         Matrix([
805         [ 5/3],
806         [10/3]])
807 
808         The error is given by S*xy - r:
809 
810         >>> S*xy - r
811         Matrix([
812         [1/3],
813         [1/3],
814         [1/3]])
815         >>> _.norm().n(2)
816         0.58
817 
818         If a different xy is used, the norm will be higher:
819 
820         >>> xy += ones(2, 1)/10
821         >>> (S*xy - r).norm().n(2)
822         1.5
823 
824         """
825         t = self.T
826         return (t*self).inv(method=method)*t*rhs
827 
828     def solve(self, rhs, method='LDL'):
829         """Return solution to self*soln = rhs using given inversion method.
830 
831         For a list of possible inversion methods, see the .inv() docstring.
832         """
833         if not self.is_square:
834             if self.rows < self.cols:
835                 raise ValueError('Under-determined system.')
836             elif self.rows > self.cols:
837                 raise ValueError('For over-determined system, M, having '
838                     'more rows than columns, try M.solve_least_squares(rhs).')
839         else:
840             return self.inv(method=method)*rhs
841

58 """
59 An mpf value tuple is a tuple of integers (sign, man, exp, bc)
60 representing a floating-point number: [1, -1][sign]*man*2**exp where
61 sign is 0 or 1 and bc should correspond to the number of bits used to
62 represent the mantissa (man) in binary notation, e.g.
63 
64 >>> from sympy.core.evalf import bitcount
65 >>> sign, man, exp, bc = 0, 5, 1, 3
66 >>> n = [1, -1][sign]*man*2**exp
67 >>> n, bitcount(man)
68 (10, 3)
69 
70 A temporary result is a tuple (re, im, re_acc, im_acc) where
71 re and im are nonzero mpf value tuples representing approximate
72 numbers, or None to denote exact zeros.
73 
74 re_acc, im_acc are integers denoting log2(e) where e is the estimated
75 relative accuracy of the respective complex part, but may be anything
76 if the corresponding complex part is None.
77 
78 """

81 def fastlog(x):
82     """Fast approximation of log2(x) for an mpf value tuple x.
83 
84     Notes: Calculated as exponent + width of mantissa. This is an
85     approximation for two reasons: 1) it gives the ceil(log2(abs(x)))
86     value and 2) it is too high by 1 in the case that x is an exact
87     power of 2. Although this is easy to remedy by testing to see if
88     the odd mpf mantissa is 1 (indicating that one was dealing with
89     an exact power of 2) that would decrease the speed and is not
90     necessary as this is only being used as an approximation for the
91     number of bits in x. The correct return value could be written as
92     "x[2] + (x[3] if x[1] != 1 else 0)".
93         Since mpf tuples always have an odd mantissa, no check is done
94     to see if the mantissa is a multiple of 2 (in which case the
95     result would be too large by 1).
96 
97     Examples
98     ========
99 
100     >>> from sympy import log
101     >>> from sympy.core.evalf import fastlog, bitcount
102     >>> s, m, e = 0, 5, 1
103     >>> bc = bitcount(m)
104     >>> n = [1, -1][s]*m*2**e
105     >>> n, (log(n)/log(2)).evalf(2), fastlog((s, m, e, bc))
106     (10, 3.3, 4)
107     """
108 
109     if not x or x == fzero:
110         return MINUS_INF
111     return x[2] + x[3]

114 def pure_complex(v, or_real=False):
115     """Return a and b if v matches a + I*b where b is not zero and
116     a and b are Numbers, else None. If `or_real` is True then 0 will
117     be returned for `b` if `v` is a real number.
118 
119     >>> from sympy.core.evalf import pure_complex
120     >>> from sympy import sqrt, I, S
121     >>> a, b, surd = S(2), S(3), sqrt(2)
122     >>> pure_complex(a)
123     >>> pure_complex(a, or_real=True)
124     (2, 0)
125     >>> pure_complex(surd)
126     >>> pure_complex(a + b*I)
127     (2, 3)
128     >>> pure_complex(I)
129     (0, 1)
130     """
131     h, t = v.as_coeff_Add()
132     if not t:
133         if or_real:
134             return h, t
135         return
136     c, i = t.as_coeff_Mul()
137     if i is S.ImaginaryUnit:
138         return h, c

141 def scaled_zero(mag, sign=1):
142     """Return an mpf representing a power of two with magnitude ``mag``
143     and -1 for precision. Or, if ``mag`` is a scaled_zero tuple, then just
144     remove the sign from within the list that it was initially wrapped
145     in.
146 
147     Examples
148     ========
149 
150     >>> from sympy.core.evalf import scaled_zero
151     >>> from sympy import Float
152     >>> z, p = scaled_zero(100)
153     >>> z, p
154     (([0], 1, 100, 1), -1)
155     >>> ok = scaled_zero(z)
156     >>> ok
157     (0, 1, 100, 1)
158     >>> Float(ok)
159     1.26765060022823e+30
160     >>> Float(ok, p)
161     0.e+30
162     >>> ok, p = scaled_zero(100, -1)
163     >>> Float(scaled_zero(ok), p)
164     -0.e+30
165     """
166     if type(mag) is tuple and len(mag) == 4 and iszero(mag, scaled=True):
167         return (mag[0][0],) + mag[1:]
168     elif isinstance(mag, SYMPY_INTS):
169         if sign not in [-1, 1]:
170             raise ValueError('sign must be +/-1')
171         rv, p = mpf_shift(fone, mag), -1
172         s = 0 if sign == 1 else 1
173         rv = ([s],) + rv[1:]
174         return rv, p
175     else:
176         raise ValueError('scaled zero expects int or scaled_zero tuple.')

185 def complex_accuracy(result):
186     """
187     Returns relative accuracy of a complex number with given accuracies
188     for the real and imaginary parts. The relative accuracy is defined
189     in the complex norm sense as ||z|+|error|| / |z| where error
190     is equal to (real absolute error) + (imag absolute error)*i.
191 
192     The full expression for the (logarithmic) error can be approximated
193     easily by using the max norm to approximate the complex norm.
194 
195     In the worst case (re and im equal), this is wrong by a factor
196     sqrt(2), or by log2(sqrt(2)) = 0.5 bit.
197     """
198     re, im, re_acc, im_acc = result
199     if not im:
200         if not re:
201             return INF
202         return re_acc
203     if not re:
204         return im_acc
205     re_size = fastlog(re)
206     im_size = fastlog(im)
207     absolute_error = max(re_size - re_acc, im_size - im_acc)
208     relative_error = absolute_error - max(re_size, im_size)
209     return -relative_error

258 def finalize_complex(re, im, prec):
259     if re == fzero and im == fzero:
260         raise ValueError("got complex zero with unknown accuracy")
261     elif re == fzero:
262         return None, im, None, prec
263     elif im == fzero:
264         return re, None, prec, None
265 
266     size_re = fastlog(re)
267     size_im = fastlog(im)
268     if size_re > size_im:
269         re_acc = prec
270         im_acc = prec + min(-(size_re - size_im), 0)
271     else:
272         im_acc = prec
273         re_acc = prec + min(-(size_im - size_re), 0)
274     return re, im, re_acc, im_acc

277 def chop_parts(value, prec):
278     """
279     Chop off tiny real or complex parts.
280     """
281     re, im, re_acc, im_acc = value
282     # Method 1: chop based on absolute value
283     if re and re not in _infs_nan and (fastlog(re) < -prec + 4):
284         re, re_acc = None, None
285     if im and im not in _infs_nan and (fastlog(im) < -prec + 4):
286         im, im_acc = None, None
287     # Method 2: chop if inaccurate and relatively small
288     if re and im:
289         delta = fastlog(re) - fastlog(im)
290         if re_acc < 2 and (delta - re_acc <= -prec + 4):
291             re, re_acc = None, None
292         if im_acc < 2 and (delta - im_acc >= prec - 4):
293             im, im_acc = None, None
294     return re, im, re_acc, im_acc

305 def get_integer_part(expr, no, options, return_ints=False):
306     """
307     With no = 1, computes ceiling(expr)
308     With no = -1, computes floor(expr)
309 
310     Note: this function either gives the exact result or signals failure.
311     """
312     from sympy.functions.elementary.complexes import re, im
313     # The expression is likely less than 2^30 or so
314     assumed_size = 30
315     ire, iim, ire_acc, iim_acc = evalf(expr, assumed_size, options)
316 
317     # We now know the size, so we can calculate how much extra precision
318     # (if any) is needed to get within the nearest integer
319     if ire and iim:
320         gap = max(fastlog(ire) - ire_acc, fastlog(iim) - iim_acc)
321     elif ire:
322         gap = fastlog(ire) - ire_acc
323     elif iim:
324         gap = fastlog(iim) - iim_acc
325     else:
326         # ... or maybe the expression was exactly zero
327         return None, None, None, None
328 
329     margin = 10
330 
331     if gap >= -margin:
332         ire, iim, ire_acc, iim_acc = \
333             evalf(expr, margin + assumed_size + gap, options)
334 
335     # We can now easily find the nearest integer, but to find floor/ceil, we
336     # must also calculate whether the difference to the nearest integer is
337     # positive or negative (which may fail if very close).
338     def calc_part(expr, nexpr):
339         from sympy.core.add import Add
340         nint = int(to_int(nexpr, rnd))
341         n, c, p, b = nexpr
342         is_int = (p == 0)
343         if not is_int:
344             # if there are subs and they all contain integer re/im parts
345             # then we can (hopefully) safely substitute them into the
346             # expression
347             s = options.get('subs', False)
348             if s:
349                 doit = True
350                 from sympy.core.compatibility import as_int
351                 for v in s.values():
352                     try:
353                         as_int(v)
354                     except ValueError:
355                         try:
356                             [as_int(i) for i in v.as_real_imag()]
357                             continue
358                         except (ValueError, AttributeError):
359                             doit = False
360                             break
361                 if doit:
362                     expr = expr.subs(s)
363 
364             expr = Add(expr, -nint, evaluate=False)
365             x, _, x_acc, _ = evalf(expr, 10, options)
366             try:
367                 check_target(expr, (x, None, x_acc, None), 3)
368             except PrecisionExhausted:
369                 if not expr.equals(0):
370                     raise PrecisionExhausted
371                 x = fzero
372             nint += int(no*(mpf_cmp(x or fzero, fzero) == no))
373         nint = from_int(nint)
374         return nint, fastlog(nint) + 10
375 
376     re_, im_, re_acc, im_acc = None, None, None, None
377 
378     if ire:
379         re_, re_acc = calc_part(re(expr, evaluate=False), ire)
380     if iim:
381         im_, im_acc = calc_part(im(expr, evaluate=False), iim)
382 
383     if return_ints:
384         return int(to_int(re_ or fzero)), int(to_int(im_ or fzero))
385     return re_, im_, re_acc, im_acc

402 def add_terms(terms, prec, target_prec):
403     """
404     Helper for evalf_add. Adds a list of (mpfval, accuracy) terms.
405 
406     Returns
407     -------
408 
409     - None, None if there are no non-zero terms;
410     - terms[0] if there is only 1 term;
411     - scaled_zero if the sum of the terms produces a zero by cancellation
412       e.g. mpfs representing 1 and -1 would produce a scaled zero which need
413       special handling since they are not actually zero and they are purposely
414       malformed to ensure that they can't be used in anything but accuracy
415       calculations;
416     - a tuple that is scaled to target_prec that corresponds to the
417       sum of the terms.
418 
419     The returned mpf tuple will be normalized to target_prec; the input
420     prec is used to define the working precision.
421 
422     XXX explain why this is needed and why one can't just loop using mpf_add
423     """
424 
425     terms = [t for t in terms if not iszero(t)]
426     if not terms:
427         return None, None
428     elif len(terms) == 1:
429         return terms[0]
430 
431     # see if any argument is NaN or oo and thus warrants a special return
432     special = []
433     from sympy.core.numbers import Float
434     for t in terms:
435         arg = Float._new(t[0], 1)
436         if arg is S.NaN or arg.is_infinite:
437             special.append(arg)
438     if special:
439         from sympy.core.add import Add
440         rv = evalf(Add(*special), prec + 4, {})
441         return rv[0], rv[2]
442 
443     working_prec = 2*prec
444     sum_man, sum_exp, absolute_error = 0, 0, MINUS_INF
445 
446     for x, accuracy in terms:
447         sign, man, exp, bc = x
448         if sign:
449             man = -man
450         absolute_error = max(absolute_error, bc + exp - accuracy)
451         delta = exp - sum_exp
452         if exp >= sum_exp:
453             # x much larger than existing sum?
454             # first: quick test
455             if ((delta > working_prec) and
456                 ((not sum_man) or
457                  delta - bitcount(abs(sum_man)) > working_prec)):
458                 sum_man = man
459                 sum_exp = exp
460             else:
461                 sum_man += (man << delta)
462         else:
463             delta = -delta
464             # x much smaller than existing sum?
465             if delta - bc > working_prec:
466                 if not sum_man:
467                     sum_man, sum_exp = man, exp
468             else:
469                 sum_man = (sum_man << delta) + man
470                 sum_exp = exp
471     if not sum_man:
472         return scaled_zero(absolute_error)
473     if sum_man < 0:
474         sum_sign = 1
475         sum_man = -sum_man
476     else:
477         sum_sign = 0
478     sum_bc = bitcount(sum_man)
479     sum_accuracy = sum_exp + sum_bc - absolute_error
480     r = normalize(sum_sign, sum_man, sum_exp, sum_bc, target_prec,
481         rnd), sum_accuracy
482     return r

485 def evalf_add(v, prec, options):
486     res = pure_complex(v)
487     if res:
488         h, c = res
489         re, _, re_acc, _ = evalf(h, prec, options)
490         im, _, im_acc, _ = evalf(c, prec, options)
491         return re, im, re_acc, im_acc
492 
493     oldmaxprec = options.get('maxprec', DEFAULT_MAXPREC)
494 
495     i = 0
496     target_prec = prec
497     while 1:
498         options['maxprec'] = min(oldmaxprec, 2*prec)
499 
500         terms = [evalf(arg, prec + 10, options) for arg in v.args]
501         re, re_acc = add_terms(
502             [a[0::2] for a in terms if a[0]], prec, target_prec)
503         im, im_acc = add_terms(
504             [a[1::2] for a in terms if a[1]], prec, target_prec)
505         acc = complex_accuracy((re, im, re_acc, im_acc))
506         if acc >= target_prec:
507             if options.get('verbose'):
508                 print("ADD: wanted", target_prec, "accurate bits, got", re_acc, im_acc)
509             break
510         else:
511             if (prec - target_prec) > options['maxprec']:
512                 break
513 
514             prec = prec + max(10 + 2**i, target_prec - acc)
515             i += 1
516             if options.get('verbose'):
517                 print("ADD: restarting with prec", prec)
518 
519     options['maxprec'] = oldmaxprec
520     if iszero(re, scaled=True):
521         re = scaled_zero(re)
522     if iszero(im, scaled=True):
523         im = scaled_zero(im)
524     return re, im, re_acc, im_acc

527 def evalf_mul(v, prec, options):
528     res = pure_complex(v)
529     if res:
530         # the only pure complex that is a mul is h*I
531         _, h = res
532         im, _, im_acc, _ = evalf(h, prec, options)
533         return None, im, None, im_acc
534     args = list(v.args)
535 
536     # see if any argument is NaN or oo and thus warrants a special return
537     special = []
538     from sympy.core.numbers import Float
539     for arg in args:
540         arg = evalf(arg, prec, options)
541         if arg[0] is None:
542             continue
543         arg = Float._new(arg[0], 1)
544         if arg is S.NaN or arg.is_infinite:
545             special.append(arg)
546     if special:
547         from sympy.core.mul import Mul
548         special = Mul(*special)
549         return evalf(special, prec + 4, {})
550 
551     # With guard digits, multiplication in the real case does not destroy
552     # accuracy. This is also true in the complex case when considering the
553     # total accuracy; however accuracy for the real or imaginary parts
554     # separately may be lower.
555     acc = prec
556 
557     # XXX: big overestimate
558     working_prec = prec + len(args) + 5
559 
560     # Empty product is 1
561     start = man, exp, bc = MPZ(1), 0, 1
562 
563     # First, we multiply all pure real or pure imaginary numbers.
564     # direction tells us that the result should be multiplied by
565     # I**direction; all other numbers get put into complex_factors
566     # to be multiplied out after the first phase.
567     last = len(args)
568     direction = 0
569     args.append(S.One)
570     complex_factors = []
571 
572     for i, arg in enumerate(args):
573         if i != last and pure_complex(arg):
574             args[-1] = (args[-1]*arg).expand()
575             continue
576         elif i == last and arg is S.One:
577             continue
578         re, im, re_acc, im_acc = evalf(arg, working_prec, options)
579         if re and im:
580             complex_factors.append((re, im, re_acc, im_acc))
581             continue
582         elif re:
583             (s, m, e, b), w_acc = re, re_acc
584         elif im:
585             (s, m, e, b), w_acc = im, im_acc
586             direction += 1
587         else:
588             return None, None, None, None
589         direction += 2*s
590         man *= m
591         exp += e
592         bc += b
593         if bc > 3*working_prec:
594             man >>= working_prec
595             exp += working_prec
596         acc = min(acc, w_acc)
597     sign = (direction & 2) >> 1
598     if not complex_factors:
599         v = normalize(sign, man, exp, bitcount(man), prec, rnd)
600         # multiply by i
601         if direction & 1:
602             return None, v, None, acc
603         else:
604             return v, None, acc, None
605     else:
606         # initialize with the first term
607         if (man, exp, bc) != start:
608             # there was a real part; give it an imaginary part
609             re, im = (sign, man, exp, bitcount(man)), (0, MPZ(0), 0, 0)
610             i0 = 0
611         else:
612             # there is no real part to start (other than the starting 1)
613             wre, wim, wre_acc, wim_acc = complex_factors[0]
614             acc = min(acc,
615                       complex_accuracy((wre, wim, wre_acc, wim_acc)))
616             re = wre
617             im = wim
618             i0 = 1
619 
620         for wre, wim, wre_acc, wim_acc in complex_factors[i0:]:
621             # acc is the overall accuracy of the product; we aren't
622             # computing exact accuracies of the product.
623             acc = min(acc,
624                       complex_accuracy((wre, wim, wre_acc, wim_acc)))
625 
626             use_prec = working_prec
627             A = mpf_mul(re, wre, use_prec)
628             B = mpf_mul(mpf_neg(im), wim, use_prec)
629             C = mpf_mul(re, wim, use_prec)
630             D = mpf_mul(im, wre, use_prec)
631             re = mpf_add(A, B, use_prec)
632             im = mpf_add(C, D, use_prec)
633         if options.get('verbose'):

641 def evalf_pow(v, prec, options):
642 
643     target_prec = prec
644     base, exp = v.args
645 
646     # We handle x**n separately. This has two purposes: 1) it is much
647     # faster, because we avoid calling evalf on the exponent, and 2) it
648     # allows better handling of real/imaginary parts that are exactly zero
649     if exp.is_Integer:
650         p = exp.p
651         # Exact
652         if not p:
653             return fone, None, prec, None
654         # Exponentiation by p magnifies relative error by |p|, so the
655         # base must be evaluated with increased precision if p is large
656         prec += int(math.log(abs(p), 2))
657         re, im, re_acc, im_acc = evalf(base, prec + 5, options)
658         # Real to integer power
659         if re and not im:
660             return mpf_pow_int(re, p, target_prec), None, target_prec, None
661         # (x*I)**n = I**n * x**n
662         if im and not re:
663             z = mpf_pow_int(im, p, target_prec)
664             case = p % 4
665             if case == 0:
666                 return z, None, target_prec, None
667             if case == 1:
668                 return None, z, None, target_prec
669             if case == 2:
670                 return mpf_neg(z), None, target_prec, None
671             if case == 3:
672                 return None, mpf_neg(z), None, target_prec
673         # Zero raised to an integer power
674         if not re:
675             return None, None, None, None
676         # General complex number to arbitrary integer power
677         re, im = libmp.mpc_pow_int((re, im), p, prec)
678         # Assumes full accuracy in input
679         return finalize_complex(re, im, target_prec)
680 
681     # Pure square root
682     if exp is S.Half:
683         xre, xim, _, _ = evalf(base, prec + 5, options)
684         # General complex square root
685         if xim:
686             re, im = libmp.mpc_sqrt((xre or fzero, xim), prec)
687             return finalize_complex(re, im, prec)
688         if not xre:
689             return None, None, None, None
690         # Square root of a negative real number
691         if mpf_lt(xre, fzero):
692             return None, mpf_sqrt(mpf_neg(xre), prec), None, prec
693         # Positive square root
694         return mpf_sqrt(xre, prec), None, prec, None
695 
696     # We first evaluate the exponent to find its magnitude
697     # This determines the working precision that must be used
698     prec += 10
699     yre, yim, _, _ = evalf(exp, prec, options)
700     # Special cases: x**0
701     if not (yre or yim):
702         return fone, None, prec, None
703 
704     ysize = fastlog(yre)
705     # Restart if too big
706     # XXX: prec + ysize might exceed maxprec
707     if ysize > 5:
708         prec += ysize
709         yre, yim, _, _ = evalf(exp, prec, options)
710 
711     # Pure exponential function; no need to evalf the base
712     if base is S.Exp1:
713         if yim:
714             re, im = libmp.mpc_exp((yre or fzero, yim), prec)
715             return finalize_complex(re, im, target_prec)
716         return mpf_exp(yre, target_prec), None, target_prec, None
717 
718     xre, xim, _, _ = evalf(base, prec + 5, options)
719     # 0**y
720     if not (xre or xim):
721         return None, None, None, None
722 
723     # (real ** complex) or (complex ** complex)
724     if yim:
725         re, im = libmp.mpc_pow(
726             (xre or fzero, xim or fzero), (yre or fzero, yim),
727             target_prec)
728         return finalize_complex(re, im, target_prec)
729     # complex ** real
730     if xim:
731         re, im = libmp.mpc_pow_mpf((xre or fzero, xim), yre, target_prec)
732         return finalize_complex(re, im, target_prec)
733     # negative ** real
734     elif mpf_lt(xre, fzero):
735         re, im = libmp.mpc_pow_mpf((xre, fzero), yre, target_prec)
736         return finalize_complex(re, im, target_prec)
737     # positive ** real
738     else:
739         return mpf_pow(xre, yre, target_prec), None, target_prec, None
740

747 def evalf_trig(v, prec, options):
748     """
749     This function handles sin and cos of complex arguments.
750 
751     TODO: should also handle tan of complex arguments.
752     """
753     from sympy import cos, sin
754     if isinstance(v, cos):
755         func = mpf_cos
756     elif isinstance(v, sin):
757         func = mpf_sin
758     else:
759         raise NotImplementedError
760     arg = v.args[0]
761     # 20 extra bits is possibly overkill. It does make the need
762     # to restart very unlikely
763     xprec = prec + 20
764     re, im, re_acc, im_acc = evalf(arg, xprec, options)
765     if im:
766         if 'subs' in options:
767             v = v.subs(options['subs'])
768         return evalf(v._eval_evalf(prec), prec, options)
769     if not re:
770         if isinstance(v, cos):
771             return fone, None, prec, None
772         elif isinstance(v, sin):
773             return None, None, None, None
774         else:
775             raise NotImplementedError
776     # For trigonometric functions, we are interested in the
777     # fixed-point (absolute) accuracy of the argument.
778     xsize = fastlog(re)
779     # Magnitude <= 1.0. OK to compute directly, because there is no
780     # danger of hitting the first root of cos (with sin, magnitude
781     # <= 2.0 would actually be ok)
782     if xsize < 1:
783         return func(re, prec, rnd), None, prec, None
784     # Very large
785     if xsize >= 10:
786         xprec = prec + xsize
787         re, im, re_acc, im_acc = evalf(arg, xprec, options)
788     # Need to repeat in case the argument is very close to a
789     # multiple of pi (or pi/2), hitting close to a root
790     while 1:
791         y = func(re, prec, rnd)
792         ysize = fastlog(y)
793         gap = -ysize
794         accuracy = (xprec - xsize) - gap
795         if accuracy < prec:
796             if options.get('verbose'):
797                 print("SIN/COS", accuracy, "wanted", prec, "gap", gap)
798                 print(to_str(y, 10))
799             if xprec > options.get('maxprec', DEFAULT_MAXPREC):
800                 return y, None, accuracy, None
801             xprec += gap
802             re, im, re_acc, im_acc = evalf(arg, xprec, options)
803             continue
804         else:
805             return y, None, prec, None

808 def evalf_log(expr, prec, options):
809     from sympy import Abs, Add, log
810     if len(expr.args)>1:
811         expr = expr.doit()
812         return evalf(expr, prec, options)
813     arg = expr.args[0]
814     workprec = prec + 10
815     xre, xim, xacc, _ = evalf(arg, workprec, options)
816 
817     if xim:
818         # XXX: use get_abs etc instead
819         re = evalf_log(
820             log(Abs(arg, evaluate=False), evaluate=False), prec, options)
821         im = mpf_atan2(xim, xre or fzero, prec)
822         return re[0], im, re[2], prec
823 
824     imaginary_term = (mpf_cmp(xre, fzero) < 0)
825 
826     re = mpf_log(mpf_abs(xre), prec, rnd)
827     size = fastlog(re)
828     if prec - size > workprec and re != fzero:
829         # We actually need to compute 1+x accurately, not x
830         arg = Add(S.NegativeOne, arg, evaluate=False)
831         xre, xim, _, _ = evalf_add(arg, prec, options)
832         prec2 = workprec - fastlog(xre)
833         # xre is now x - 1 so we add 1 back here to calculate x
834         re = mpf_log(mpf_abs(mpf_add(xre, fone, prec2)), prec, rnd)
835 
836     re_acc = prec
837 
838     if imaginary_term:
839         return re, mpf_pi(prec), re_acc, prec
840     else:
841         return re, None, re_acc, None

915 def do_integral(expr, prec, options):
916     func = expr.args[0]
917     x, xlow, xhigh = expr.args[1]
918     if xlow == xhigh:
919         xlow = xhigh = 0
920     elif x not in func.free_symbols:
921         # only the difference in limits matters in this case
922         # so if there is a symbol in common that will cancel
923         # out when taking the difference, then use that
924         # difference
925         if xhigh.free_symbols & xlow.free_symbols:
926             diff = xhigh - xlow
927             if not diff.free_symbols:
928                 xlow, xhigh = 0, diff
929 
930     oldmaxprec = options.get('maxprec', DEFAULT_MAXPREC)
931     options['maxprec'] = min(oldmaxprec, 2*prec)
932 
933     with workprec(prec + 5):
934         xlow = as_mpmath(xlow, prec + 15, options)
935         xhigh = as_mpmath(xhigh, prec + 15, options)
936 
937         # Integration is like summation, and we can phone home from
938         # the integrand function to update accuracy summation style
939         # Note that this accuracy is inaccurate, since it fails
940         # to account for the variable quadrature weights,
941         # but it is better than nothing
942 
943         from sympy import cos, sin, Wild
944 
945         have_part = [False, False]
946         max_real_term = [MINUS_INF]
947         max_imag_term = [MINUS_INF]
948 
949         def f(t):
950             re, im, re_acc, im_acc = evalf(func, mp.prec, {'subs': {x: t}})
951 
952             have_part[0] = re or have_part[0]
953             have_part[1] = im or have_part[1]
954 
955             max_real_term[0] = max(max_real_term[0], fastlog(re))
956             max_imag_term[0] = max(max_imag_term[0], fastlog(im))
957 
958             if im:
959                 return mpc(re or fzero, im)
960             return mpf(re or fzero)
961 
962         if options.get('quad') == 'osc':
963             A = Wild('A', exclude=[x])
964             B = Wild('B', exclude=[x])
965             D = Wild('D')
966             m = func.match(cos(A*x + B)*D)
967             if not m:
968                 m = func.match(sin(A*x + B)*D)
969             if not m:
970                 raise ValueError("An integrand of the form sin(A*x+B)*f(x) "
971                   "or cos(A*x+B)*f(x) is required for oscillatory quadrature")
972             period = as_mpmath(2*S.Pi/m[A], prec + 15, options)
973             result = quadosc(f, [xlow, xhigh], period=period)
974             # XXX: quadosc does not do error detection yet
975             quadrature_error = MINUS_INF
976         else:
977             result, quadrature_error = quadts(f, [xlow, xhigh], error=1)
978             quadrature_error = fastlog(quadrature_error._mpf_)
979 
980     options['maxprec'] = oldmaxprec
981 
982     if have_part[0]:
983         re = result.real._mpf_
984         if re == fzero:
985             re, re_acc = scaled_zero(
986                 min(-prec, -max_real_term[0], -quadrature_error))
987             re = scaled_zero(re)  # handled ok in evalf_integral
988         else:
989             re_acc = -max(max_real_term[0] - fastlog(re) -
990                           prec, quadrature_error)
991     else:
992         re, re_acc = None, None
993 
994     if have_part[1]:
995         im = result.imag._mpf_
996         if im == fzero:
997             im, im_acc = scaled_zero(
998                 min(-prec, -max_imag_term[0], -quadrature_error))
999             im = scaled_zero(im)  # handled ok in evalf_integral
1000         else:
1001             im_acc = -max(max_imag_term[0] - fastlog(im) -
1002                           prec, quadrature_error)
1003     else:
1004         im, im_acc = None, None
1005 
1006     result = re, im, re_acc, im_acc
1007     return result
1008

1010 def evalf_integral(expr, prec, options):
1011     limits = expr.limits
1012     if len(limits) != 1 or len(limits[0]) != 3:
1013         raise NotImplementedError
1014     workprec = prec
1015     i = 0
1016     maxprec = options.get('maxprec', INF)
1017     while 1:
1018         result = do_integral(expr, workprec, options)
1019         accuracy = complex_accuracy(result)
1020         if accuracy >= prec:  # achieved desired precision
1021             break
1022         if workprec >= maxprec:  # can't increase accuracy any more
1023             break
1024         if accuracy == -1:
1025             # maybe the answer really is zero and maybe we just haven't increased
1026             # the precision enough. So increase by doubling to not take too long
1027             # to get to maxprec.
1028             workprec *= 2
1029         else:
1030             workprec += max(prec, 2**i)
1031         workprec = min(workprec, maxprec)
1032         i += 1
1033     return result

1036 def check_convergence(numer, denom, n):
1037     """
1038     Returns (h, g, p) where
1039     -- h is:
1040         > 0 for convergence of rate 1/factorial(n)**h
1041         < 0 for divergence of rate factorial(n)**(-h)
1042         = 0 for geometric or polynomial convergence or divergence
1043 
1044     -- abs(g) is:
1045         > 1 for geometric convergence of rate 1/h**n
1046         < 1 for geometric divergence of rate h**n
1047         = 1 for polynomial convergence or divergence
1048 
1049         (g < 0 indicates an alternating series)
1050 
1051     -- p is:
1052         > 1 for polynomial convergence of rate 1/n**h
1053         <= 1 for polynomial divergence of rate n**(-h)
1054 
1055     """
1056     from sympy import Poly
1057     npol = Poly(numer, n)
1058     dpol = Poly(denom, n)
1059     p = npol.degree()
1060     q = dpol.degree()
1061     rate = q - p
1062     if rate:
1063         return rate, None, None
1064     constant = dpol.LC() / npol.LC()
1065     if abs(constant) != 1:
1066         return rate, constant, None
1067     if npol.degree() == dpol.degree() == 0:
1068         return rate, constant, 0
1069     pc = npol.all_coeffs()[1]
1070     qc = dpol.all_coeffs()[1]
1071     return rate, constant, (qc - pc)/dpol.LC()
1072

1074 def hypsum(expr, n, start, prec):
1075     """
1076     Sum a rapidly convergent infinite hypergeometric series with
1077     given general term, e.g. e = hypsum(1/factorial(n), n). The
1078     quotient between successive terms must be a quotient of integer
1079     polynomials.
1080     """
1081     from sympy import Float, hypersimp, lambdify
1082 
1083     if prec == float('inf'):
1084         raise NotImplementedError('does not support inf prec')
1085 
1086     if start:
1087         expr = expr.subs(n, n + start)
1088     hs = hypersimp(expr, n)
1089     if hs is None:
1090         raise NotImplementedError("a hypergeometric series is required")
1091     num, den = hs.as_numer_denom()
1092 
1093     func1 = lambdify(n, num)
1094     func2 = lambdify(n, den)
1095 
1096     h, g, p = check_convergence(num, den, n)
1097 
1098     if h < 0:
1099         raise ValueError("Sum diverges like (n!)^%i" % (-h))
1100 
1101     term = expr.subs(n, 0)
1102     if not term.is_Rational:
1103         raise NotImplementedError("Non rational term functionality is not implemented.")
1104 
1105     # Direct summation if geometric or faster
1106     if h > 0 or (h == 0 and abs(g) > 1):
1107         term = (MPZ(term.p) << prec) // term.q
1108         s = term
1109         k = 1
1110         while abs(term) > 5:
1111             term *= MPZ(func1(k - 1))
1112             term //= MPZ(func2(k - 1))
1113             s += term
1114             k += 1
1115         return from_man_exp(s, -prec)
1116     else:
1117         alt = g < 0
1118         if abs(g) < 1:
1119             raise ValueError("Sum diverges like (%i)^n" % abs(1/g))
1120         if p < 1 or (p == 1 and not alt):
1121             raise ValueError("Sum diverges like n^%i" % (-p))
1122         # We have polynomial convergence: use Richardson extrapolation
1123         vold = None
1124         ndig = prec_to_dps(prec)
1125         while True:
1126             # Need to use at least quad precision because a lot of cancellation
1127             # might occur in the extrapolation process; we check the answer to
1128             # make sure that the desired precision has been reached, too.
1129             prec2 = 4*prec
1130             term0 = (MPZ(term.p) << prec2) // term.q
1131 
1132             def summand(k, _term=[term0]):
1133                 if k:
1134                     k = int(k)
1135                     _term[0] *= MPZ(func1(k - 1))
1136                     _term[0] //= MPZ(func2(k - 1))
1137                 return make_mpf(from_man_exp(_term[0], -prec2))
1138 
1139             with workprec(prec):
1140                 v = nsum(summand, [0, mpmath_inf], method='richardson')
1141             vf = Float(v, ndig)
1142             if vold is not None and vold == vf:
1143                 break
1144             prec += prec  # double precision each time
1145             vold = vf
1146 
1147         return v._mpf_

1159 def evalf_sum(expr, prec, options):

1168         return mpf(0), None, None, None

1170     try:

1173             raise NotImplementedError

1180     except NotImplementedError:
1181         # Euler-Maclaurin summation for general series
1182         eps = Float(2.0)**(-prec)
1183         for i in range(1, 5):

1188             if err <= eps:
1189                 break
1190         err = fastlog(evalf(abs(err), 20, options)[0])
1191         re, im, re_acc, im_acc = evalf(s, prec2, options)
1192         if re_acc is None:
1193             re_acc = -err
1194         if im_acc is None:

200     def _needs_brackets(self, expr):
201         """
202         Returns True if the expression needs to be wrapped in brackets when
203         printed, False otherwise. For example: a + b => True; a => False;
204         10 => False; -10 => True.
205         """
206         return not ((expr.is_Integer and expr.is_nonnegative)
207                     or (expr.is_Atom and (expr is not S.NegativeOne
208                                           and expr.is_Rational is False)))

210     def _needs_function_brackets(self, expr):
211         """
212         Returns True if the expression needs to be wrapped in brackets when
213         passed as an argument to a function, False otherwise. This is a more
214         liberal version of _needs_brackets, in that many expressions which need
215         to be wrapped in brackets when added/subtracted/raised to a power do
216         not need them when passed to a function. Such an example is a*b.
217         """
218         if not self._needs_brackets(expr):
219             return False
220         else:
221             # Muls of the form a*b*c... can be folded
222             if expr.is_Mul and not self._mul_is_clean(expr):
223                 return True
224             # Pows which don't need brackets can be folded
225             elif expr.is_Pow and not self._pow_is_clean(expr):
226                 return True
227             # Add and Function always need brackets
228             elif expr.is_Add or expr.is_Function:
229                 return True
230             else:
231                 return False
232 
233     def _needs_mul_brackets(self, expr, first=False, last=False):
234         """
235         Returns True if the expression needs to be wrapped in brackets when
236         printed as part of a Mul, False otherwise. This is True for Add,
237         but also for some container objects that would not need brackets
238         when appearing last in a Mul, e.g. an Integral. ``last=True``
239         specifies that this expr is the last to appear in a Mul.
240         ``first=True`` specifies that this expr is the first to appear in a Mul.
241         """
242         from sympy import Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum
243 
244         if expr.is_Mul:
245             if not first and _coeff_isneg(expr):
246                 return True
247         elif precedence_traditional(expr) < PRECEDENCE["Mul"]:
248             return True
249         elif expr.is_Relational:
250             return True
251         if expr.is_Piecewise:
252             return True
253         if any([expr.has(x) for x in (Mod,)]):
254             return True
255         if (not last and
256             any([expr.has(x) for x in (Integral, Product, Sum)])):
257             return True
258 
259         return False
260

262     def _needs_add_brackets(self, expr):
263         """

265         printed as part of an Add, False otherwise.  This is False for most
266         things.
267         """
268         if expr.is_Relational:
269             return True
270         if any([expr.has(x) for x in (Mod,)]):
271             return True
272         if expr.is_Add:
273             return True
274         return False

324     def _print_Cycle(self, expr):
325         from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
326         if expr.size == 0:
327             return r"\left( \right)"
328         expr = Permutation(expr)
329         expr_perm = expr.cyclic_form
330         siz = expr.size
331         if expr.array_form[-1] == siz - 1:
332             expr_perm = expr_perm + [[siz - 1]]
333         term_tex = ''
334         for i in expr_perm:
335             term_tex += str(i).replace(',', r"\;")
336         term_tex = term_tex.replace('[', r"\left( ")
337         term_tex = term_tex.replace(']', r"\right)")
338         return term_tex
